**BOOK OF THE MENAION**  
**MONTH OF SEPTEMBER**

To the glory of the Holy, Consubstantial, Life-Creating, and Undivided Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; under the reign of the Great King Augustus the Third;[^1]  
By the blessing of His Excellency, the Lord Sylvester Lubieniecki-Rudnytsky,[^2] Exarch of the Metropolia of Kyiv, Halych, and all Rus', Bishop of Lutsk and Ostroh;  
By the resolve of the Most Reverend Lord Father Hieromonk Hypatius Bilynsky,[^3] Protoarchimandrite of the Order of Saint Basil the Great;  
Through the diligence and at the expense of the monks of the same Order in the Holy Miraculous Lavra of Pochaiv, issued in print.  
In the year from the creation of the world according to the Greek chronographers: 7269; and from the Nativity of Christ: 1761.[^4]

# MONTH OF SEPTEMBER

*September 1. Beginning of the Indiction, That Is, the New Year:*

*On the 1st day, the Beginning of the Indiction, that is, the New Year; and the memory of our venerable father Symeon the Stylite and Archimandrite; and of his mother Martha; and the Synaxis of the Most Holy Mother of God in Miasena;[^5] and of the holy martyr Aeithalas; and of the holy forty women martyrs; and of the holy deacon Ammon, their teacher; and of the holy martyrs Callista, Evodius, and Hermogenes, brothers of the same mother; and the memory of righteous Joshua, son of Nun.*

*At Vespers, "Blessed is the man," the 1st antiphon. If it be on a Saturday, we recite the whole kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 verses, and sing 3 stichera of the Indiction:*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Ranks" (Небныхъ чинѡвъ):*

Having learned the prayer of the personal and divine teaching of Christ, let us cry daily unto the Creator: Our Father, Who dwellest in the heavens, give us our daily bread, overlooking our transgressions.

Thou Who of old didst write the tablets on Mount Sinai, Thyself also now in the city of Nazareth according to the flesh, didst receive the prophetic book to read, O Christ God; and having closed it, Thou didst teach the people that the Scripture concerning Thee was fulfilled.

Even as of old the bodies of the Hebrews who in truth were not obedient unto Thee, the Master of all, fell worthily in the wilderness: so also now, as the Psalmist says, scatter by Hades the bones of the impious and infidel Agarenes, O Christ.[^6]

*Other stichera of the Venerable One, Tone 5, Podoben: "O Venerable Father" (Преподобне ѻтче):*

O venerable father, if it were possible for the pillar to speak, it would not cease crying aloud of thy pains, thy labors, and thy lamentations;

But it was rather borne by thee than bore thee, watered like a tree by thy tears. The Angels were amazed, men marveled, and demons trembled at thy patience, O venerable Symeon; pray that our souls may be saved.

O venerable father, by the power of the Holy Spirit, imitating thy Master, thou didst ascend the pillar as upon a Cross. But He tore up the handwriting of debt against all, while thou didst destroy the assaults of passions; He was as a sheep, but thou as a slaughter; He ascended the Cross, and thou the pillar: O venerable Symeon, pray that our souls may be saved.

O venerable father, having bedewed thy body with tears and cleansed thy soul, thou didst ascend to the height of virtues, having thy pillar as a sensible dwelling, but as thy spiritual and heavenly city the Zion on high. Thou didst amaze the Angels, terrify men, and put demons to shame by thy virtues, O venerable Symeon; pray that our souls may be saved.

*Other stichera of the Saint, Tone 2. Idiomela:*

From a good root, a good fruit sprouted forth: the consecrated Symeon from infancy was nourished by grace rather than by milk. And having elevated his body upon a stone, and exalted his mind toward God, he built a heavenly habitation by his virtues; and walking in choir with the divine powers, he became the dwelling of Christ, the God and Savior of our souls.

Thy memory abides unto ages, O venerable father Symeon, and the meekness of thy heart, O blessed servant of Christ; for though thou hast departed from us in the flesh, O good one, yet hast thou not withdrawn from us in spirit, standing in love before God and dancing in choir with the Angels in the heavens, with whom do thou pray that our souls may be saved.

The reliquary of thy relics, O all-praised father, pours forth healings, and thy holy soul, joined with the Angels, worthily rejoices. Having boldness before the Lord, O venerable one, and dancing in choir with the bodiless powers in the heavens, with whom do thou pray that our souls may be saved.

Thou didst love the highest philosophy, O God-bearer, and didst become outside the world, living higher than visible things; and thou didst divinely show thyself an undefiled mirror of God; and being ever united unto the Light, thou didst receive light, and didst obtain a most radiant end, O blessed one. Pray for our souls, O wise Symeon.

*Glory... Tone 6. By Germanus:*

Divine grace overshadows the shrine of thy relics, O consecrated Symeon; therefore, running unto the fragrance of the myrrh of thy miracles, we draw forth healing of diseases. But O venerable father, pray unto Christ God for our souls.

*Both now... Of the Indiction, the same Tone. By Byzantios:*

O Thou Who art united with the Holy Spirit, unoriginate Word and Son, Maker and Creator of all things visible and invisible: bless the crown of the year, preserving in peace the assemblies of the Orthodox, by the prayers of the Mother of God and of all Thy saints.

*Then the Entrance, the Prokeimenon of the day, and the Readings.*  
*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 61):*[^7]

The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He hath anointed Me; He hath sent Me to preach good tidings unto the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind; to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of recompense of our God; to comfort all that mourn; to give unto the mourners of Zion glory instead of ashes, the oil of gladness to the mourners, the garment of glory instead of the spirit of despair; and they shall be called generations of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glory. And they shall build the old waste places, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall renew the desert cities, waste from generation to generation. And strangers shall come and feed your sheep, and aliens shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers. But ye shall be named priests of the Lord, ministers of your God; it shall be said unto you: Ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their wealth shall ye be admired. Instead of your double shame, and instead of confusion, their portion shall rejoice; therefore in their land they shall possess the double, and everlasting joy shall be upon their head. For I am the Lord Who loves righteousness, and hates robbery of injustice; and I will give their labor unto the righteous, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them. And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples; every one that sees them shall acknowledge them, that these are the seed blessed by God. And with gladness they shall rejoice in the Lord.

*Reading from the Book of Leviticus (Chapter 26):*[^8]

The Lord spoke unto the children of Israel, saying: If ye walk in My ordinances, and keep My commandments, and do them: then I will give you rain in its season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit. And your threshing shall overtake the vintage, and the vintage shall overtake the sowing; and ye shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell safely in your land. And I will give peace in your land, and ye shall sleep, and none shall make you afraid; and I will destroy the wild beasts out of your land, and the sword shall not go through your land. And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you slain. And five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall put ten thousands to flight; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword. And I will look upon you, and bless you, and make you increase, and multiply you, and establish My covenant with you. And ye shall eat the old store, and the old of the old, and clear out the old because of the new. And I will set My covenant among you, and My soul shall not abhor you. And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be My people. But if ye will not give ear unto Me, and will not do these My commandments; but disobey them, and if your soul loathe My judgments, so that ye will not do all My commandments, and so that ye break My covenant: I also will do this unto you: I will bring upon you scarcity, and ye shall sow your seed in vain, and your enemies shall eat your labors. And I will set My face against you, and ye shall fall before your enemies, and they that hate you shall chase you, and ye shall flee when none pursues you. And I will break the pride of your power; and I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass. And your strength shall be spent in vain, and your land shall not yield her seed, neither shall the trees of the field yield their fruit. And I will send wild beasts of the earth upon you, which shall devour you, and destroy your cattle, and make you few in number, and the coming sword shall destroy you. And your land shall be desolate, and your courts shall be waste; because ye walk contrary unto Me, I also will walk contrary unto you in fury: says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel.

*For the Venerable One:*  
*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 4):*[^9]

Though the righteous happen to die early, yet shall he be in rest; for honorable age is not that which consists in length of time, nor is it measured by number of years. But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. He pleased God, and was beloved of Him; so that living among sinners he was translated, he was caught away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.

For the fascination of wickedness darkens that which is good, and the wandering of desire perverts the innocent mind. Being made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years; for his soul pleased the Lord, therefore hasted He to take him away from among the wicked. And the people saw it, and understood it not, neither laid they this up in their minds: that His grace and mercy is with His venerable ones, and that He hath visited His chosen.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Indiction, Tone 1. Idiomela. By John the Monk:*

The beginning of the year has arrived, summoning us to honor those who have shone forth therein: Callista, Evodius, and Hermogenes, brothers of one mother and sufferers; Symeon equal to the Angels; and Joshua son of Nun; and the seven youths in Ephesus; and the choir of the forty-two holy women. Partaking in their memory, O feast-lovers, let us cry aloud in piety: O Lord, bless the works of Thy hands, and grant that we may worthily pass through the cycle of the year.

*Verse: Praise is due unto Thee, O God, in Zion, and unto Thee shall the vow be performed in Jerusalem [LXX Ps. 64:2].*

O Christ our God, Who by wisdom hast made all things, and brought them from non-existence into being: bless the crown of the year, and preserve our cities unharmed; and make glad our right-believing King by Thy power, granting him victories over adversaries, for the sake of the Mother of God, granting great mercy unto the world.

*Tone 2. Verse: We shall be filled with the good things of Thy house; holy is Thy temple, wonderful in righteousness [LXX Ps. 64:5b–c].*  
*By Cyprian:*

Wonderful art Thou, O God, and marvelous are Thy works, and Thy paths are past finding out; for Thou art the Wisdom of God, and perfect Hypostasis, and Power: co-unoriginate and co-eternal, and by Thy creative almighty power Thou didst come into the world, thereby to adorn Thy creation, ineffably born of a Mother that knew not man, without changing Thy Godhead, ordaining seasons and years unchangeably for our salvation. Therefore we cry unto Thee: O Good Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:12].*  
*By Damascene:*

O Thou Who in wisdom hast fashioned all things, eternal Word of the Father, and Who by Thine almighty word hast framed every creature: bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, and cast down heresies for the sake of the Mother of God, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind.

*Glory... Of the Saint, Tone 5:*

O venerable father, thou didst finely find a ladder whereby thou didst ascend to the height, which Elijah found as a fiery chariot; yet he left no ascent for others, but thou even after death hast thy pillar: O heavenly man, earthly angel, sleepless light of the universe, venerable Symeon, pray that our souls may be saved.

*Both now... Of the Indiction, Tone 5. By John the Monk:*

O King Who art ever and abidest unto endless ages, receive the supplication of sinners asking for salvation; and grant, O Lover of mankind, fertility unto Thy land, bestowing seasonable weather; fight alongside our right-believing King against godless barbarians, even as of old Thou didst for David, for they have entered into Thine habitations and defiled the all-holy place, O Savior; but do Thou grant victories, O Christ God, by the prayers of the Mother of God: for Thou art the victory and boast of the Orthodox.

*Troparion of the Indiction, Tone 2:*

O Creator of all creation, Who hast placed the times and seasons in Thine own power: bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, O Lord, preserving in peace the King and Thy city, by the prayers of the Mother of God, and save us.

*Glory... Of the Venerable One, Tone 1:*

Thou wast a pillar of endurance, rivaling the Forefathers, O venerable one: Job in sufferings, Joseph in temptations, and the life of the bodiless powers while in the body, O Symeon our father; pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Both now... To the Mother of God, Tone 1:*

Rejoice, O full of grace, Virgin Mother of God, haven and intercession of the human race; for from thee was incarnate the Redeemer of the world: for thou alone art Mother and Virgin, ever-blessed and all-glorified; pray unto Christ God to grant peace unto all the universe.

*At Matins, "God is the Lord," the troparion of the Indiction twice; Glory... of the Venerable One; Both now... to the Mother of God. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn of the Indiction, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph Marveled" (Оудивися Їѡсифъ):*

As unto the Creator of all and Giver of good things, we fall down before Thee in faith, crying diligently: by the compunction and bowels of Thy compassions, O Savior, and by the prayers of her who bore Thee, and of all who ever please Thee, vouchsafe as Thou art good that a year acceptable unto Thee may come, granting abundance unto those who hono r Thee, and faithfully glorify Thee.

*Glory... Of the Venerable One, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премудрости):*

Having directed thy mind to higher things, O wise one, and followed Christ unto the end, thou didst not in mind return unto the world, O God-wise one; by self-mastery and labors having put passions to death, thou didst prepare a temple for thy Lord. Therefore thou didst receive the recompense of gifts, to heal the diseased and drive away spirits, O most venerable Symeon; pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who feast with love thy holy memory.

*Both now... Of the Indiction: "As unto the Creator of all..." (see fol. 3v).[^10]*  
*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премудрости и Слова):*

Having divinely enriched thy soul with self-mastery, labors, and prayers, thou didst become a partaker with the martyrs, O blessed one; and in truth thou didst receive the gift of miracles to heal the diseases of those who faithfully honor thee. Therefore, also driving away the demon hosts by the grace given thee from on high, pray for us, O most blessed Symeon; pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who feast with love thy holy memory.

*Glory... Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily Anticipate" (Скоро предвари):*

Thou didst attain unto the contest of martyrdom, faithfully proclaiming Christ, O Callista, with thy two brothers; for nurtured by desire for our God, thou didst make them in truth spiritual vessels of the Church of Christ. Therefore also thou wast united with them, O martyr, in the life on high.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Speedily receive our supplications, O Sovereign Lady, and bring them unto thy Son and God, O all-pure Lady; dispel the tribulations of those who run unto thee; dispel the plots and insolence, O Virgin, of those who now take up arms against thy servants.

*(If it be a temple of Venerable Symeon.) After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn of the Venerable One, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премудрости):*

Thou didst surpass in faith, O wise father, and having despised all temporal things, thou didst follow Christ by the power of the Spirit. By self-mastery thou didst waste away thy body, O venerable one, ever foreseeing the heavenly glory. Therefore also thou didst find the ladder of the pillar for a divine ascent, answering to thy desire, O most sacred Symeon; pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who feast with love thy holy memory.

*Glory... Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-Unoriginate" (Собезначалное):*

By self-mastery thou didst adorn thy life, and having put thy body to death, thou didst turn to naught the assaults of the enemy, O blessed father; and thou hast departed unto God into everlasting life, as a worthy heir. Therefore cease not to pray, that our souls may find mercy.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

O Most Holy Virgin, have mercy upon us who flee with faith unto thee, compassionate one, and who ask for thy fervent protection; for thou art able as good to save all, being the Mother of God the Most High, ever entreating Him with thy maternal supplications, O full of the grace of God.

*The 1st Antiphon of the Songs of Ascents, Tone 4. Prokeimenon, Gospel, and Sticheron of the Temple. Then Psalm 50. Canons, 3: of the Indiction, Tone 1, with the Heirmos on 6, the composition of the Lord John the Monk; the Heirmos twice, the Troparia on 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Let us all people sing a song of victory unto Him Who delivered Israel from bitter bondage to Pharaoh, and led them dryshod through the depth of the sea: for He is glorified.

*Troparia:*

Let us all sing a song of victory unto Christ, by Whom all things were framed, and in Whom they were made indivisible, as unto the hypostatic Word born of the unoriginate Father: for He is glorified.

Let us all sing a song of victory unto Christ, Who by the Father's good pleasure appeared from the Virgin, and proclaimed the acceptable year of the Lord for our redemption: for He is glorified.

Having come to Nazareth, the Giver of the Law taught on the Sabbath day, ordaining for the Hebrews His ineffable coming, whereby as compassionate He saves our race.

*Theotokion:*

Hymning the all-marvelous Maiden, who caused Christ to shine forth unto the universe and filled all things with the joy of eternal life, let us all faithful praise her: for He is glorified.

*Another Canon of the Holy Women, Tone 4, whose Acrostic is: "I sing the pangs of the steadfast women martyrs." Tone 4:*[^11]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother; and I shall be seen radiantly keeping festival, and rejoicing I shall sing her wonders.

*Troparia:*

Having steadfastly set themselves against the adversary, O women martyrs, first by fasting, and secondly by blood-shedding suffering: therefore with faith we honor your memory.

Wounded with love for Him Who for our sake endured the Cross and death, the holy women followed His footsteps, forgetting the weakness of the flesh.

Ye cast down the Hellenic sacrifices and demonic mad frenzies by the weapon of the faith, and brought yourselves as a living temple, O all-honored women martyrs.

*Theotokion:*

Strengthened by the grace of Him Who shone forth from thy womb, O all-immaculate Virgin Maiden, the young maidens crushed the urge of torments and were brought after thee, rejoicing.

*Another Canon of the Venerable Father, on 4. Whose Acrostic is: "Receive the singing, O Symeon all-blessed." The composition of John the Monk, Tone 8:*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Let us all people sing unto the Lord, Who drowned Pharaoh in the Red Sea, singing a song of victory, for He is glorified.

*Troparia:*

Grant unto me who with corrupt organ of tongue weave a hymn unto thee, O God-bearing Symeon, by Thy supplications, the God-taught light of knowledge.

The Persians, Ethiopians, Indians, Scythians, and the multitude of the Arabs came to know thy wisdom, O father, and glorified Christ Who is glorified through thee.

Filled with spiritual grace, from the fold of sheep like Jacob, David, and Moses, thou didst appear as a leader of rational flocks, O blessed one.

*Theotokion:*

O all-pure and honored one, again rejoice, who didst contain in thy womb the uncontainable God; [entreat Him] that they who confess thee may be delivered from grievous afflictions.

*Katavasia, Tone 8:*[^12]

Moses inscribed the Cross, cutting the Red Sea directly with his rod for Israel traveling on foot; and striking it again reversely, he joined it together upon the chariots of Pharaoh, having drawn transversally the invincible weapon; therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He is glorified.

*We sing [this Katavasia] until the Apodosis of the Precious Cross.*[^13]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Establish me, O Christ, upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, and enlighten me with the light of Thy countenance; for there is none holy above Thee, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

Establish, O Good One, the fruitful vineyard which Thy right hand hath planted in love upon the earth, preserving Thy Church, O Almighty One.

Adorned in God-comely spiritual works, conduct through this present year, O Lord and Master, those who with faith hymn Thee, [the Master] of all things.

Grant me a tranquil cycle of the year, O compassionate Christ, and fill me with Thy divine words, which Thou wast seen speaking unto the Jews on the Sabbaths.

*Theotokion:*

As the only one who above man supernaturally received grace into thy womb and ineffably gavest birth to our Christ, we ever glorify thee.

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Heirmos:*

The bow of the mighty hath grown weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength: therefore my heart is established in the Lord.

*Troparia:*

Strengthened by the almighty power, ye trampled down the might of the adversaries: therefore as victors ye were crowned by Christ.

The gaping jaws of the beasts were shown to be powerless by the divine power of Christ, and ye were delivered unharmed, O God-bearers, honoring God.

Deified by looking unto God, ye cast away the cold of polytheism, and reached unto the warmth of the sublime glory, O passion-bearers.

*Theotokion:*

Knowing thee piously, we proclaim thee to be truly the Mother of God, O all-immaculate one; for through thee the Creator vouchsafed to communicate with us.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*

Plant Thy fear, O Lord, in the hearts of Thy servants, and be Thou our establishment, who in truth call upon Thee.

*Troparia:*

Having swiftly escaped the worldly perils of the spirits, thou didst hasten unto the saving habitation, O Symeon, from which also thou didst receive the unaging life.

Having rejoiced, thou didst bend [thy neck], subjecting thy spirit, O all-blessed one, unto the Master and God, and didst find the blessed life.

Having received the seeds of the Word in the furrows of thy heart, and by the waterings of tears, thou didst reap for Christ an abundant ear of virtue.

*Theotokion:*

Having ineffably conceived, O Bride of God, the Savior and Lord Who delivers us from grievous afflictions, who truly acknowledge thee.

*Katavasia:*

The rod is accepted as a figure of the mystery, for by its budding it chooses the priest; and for the Church that before was barren, now hath blossomed the tree of the Cross, for her power and establishment.

*Kontakion of the Indiction, Tone 2:*

Dwelling in the highest, O Christ King, Creator and Builder of all things visible and invisible, Who didst make the days and nights, the times and the years: bless now the crown of the year; protect and preserve in peace the Orthodox King,[^14] and Thy city, and Thy people, O Thou Who art plenteous in mercy.

*Then the Sessional Hymn of the Indiction, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Thou Who dost grant fruitful seasons and rains from heaven unto those on earth, receiving now the supplications of Thy servants, deliver Thy city from every necessity; for Thy compassions are truly upon all Thy works. Therefore bless our entrances and our exits, direct the works of our hands among us, and grant us forgiveness of sins, O God; for Thou, as powerful, didst bring all things from non-being into being.

*Another Sessional Hymn of the Venerable Father, Tone and Podoben the same:*

Having forsaken all earthly things, and being in the world in the body, in spirit thou wast a heavenly angel. For having put to death by the flesh the passions that assail, thou didst appear as a pleasing servant of the Trinity, O blessed one. Therefore thou healest the ailments of the suffering, and by a word drivest away spirits by grace. O all-blessed Symeon, entreat Christ God to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto those who honor thy holy memory with love.

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn of the Holy Women, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy Tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*

Spiritual ewe-lambs, ye were faithfully brought unto the Lamb and Shepherd by martyrdom, having finished the course and kept the faith. Therefore with joy today we praise your sacred memory, O richly-marvelous ones, magnifying Christ.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Guide us into the way of repentance, who ever turn aside unto evil pathless ways and provoke the all-good Lord to wrath, O unwedded, blessed Mary, refuge of desperate men, habitation of God.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

I understood Thy dispensation, O Almighty One, and with fear I glorified Thee, O Savior.

*Troparia:*

The beginning of the year Thy people offer unto Thee, glorifying Thee with angelic songs, O Savior.

As Lover of mankind, vouchsafe unto those who have begun the year also to finish it well-pleasing unto Thee, O Christ.

O only Ruler over all, Lord, having calmed the revolutions of the years, grant peace unto the world.

*Theotokion:*

As our refuge now and firm hope, let us all hymn the Mother of God.

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Heirmos:*

Seated in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, in a light cloud Jesus the Most Divine came, with incorrupt palm, and saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparia:*

Having endured torments and the breaking of the body in manifold ways, the crushing of limbs and burning, ye inherited the heavenly mansions, delighting in the tree of life, O richly-marvelous ones.

The heavenly powers marveled at the contest of the blessed maidens, how in woman's nature they conquered the enemy, being strengthened by the power of Him Who shone forth from a woman.

Having fled from all the vanity of the world, ye cleaved unto God alone with your whole soul; therefore ye endured the toils of self-mastery and the sufferings, O patient brides of Christ.

Bearing the Cross as a most mighty weapon, ye stood against the opposing battle-arrays; and with Christ ye bore away the victory, with Him Who conquered the world by the power of the Godhead.

*Theotokion:*

He came down as rain upon the fleece into thy womb, as of old the God-proclaiming prophet said, O all-immaculate one; Whom thou didst bear in two natures, unto Whom we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*

I heard, O Lord, the report of Thee and was afraid; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy dominion, O Lord.

*Troparia:*

Not upon the sand, O all-blessed one, but upon thy deepest labors having laid the foundation of self-mastery, thou didst build an unshakable pillar of virtues.

Having settled thy body in a harsh dwelling, thou didst nail thy spirit with fear, and didst find the habitation of the divine inheritance, O venerable father.

Thou didst subdue the hidden passions of the flesh, O richly-gifted one; in the rot of the worm-eaten wound, O father, thou didst find sweet fragrance.

According to His voluntary passion, assimilating thyself unto the life-creating Dead Man, as into a tomb thou didst surrender thyself alive into the dark pit.

*Theotokion:*

The God Whom thou didst bear, O all-pure Mary, entreat ever to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto thy servants.

*Katavasia:*

I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Early in the morning from the night waking we sing unto Thee, O Christ, Co-Unoriginate with the Father, and Savior of our souls: grant peace unto the world, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

Filling all things with goodness, O Christ, do Thou, by good temperature and fruitful yield, crown with blessings, grant unto Thy servants a year of many cycles.

Show unto us the yearly recompense, an orientation toward better things, and peaceful establishment unto those who know Thee, O Word of God, Who didst assimilate Thyself unto men.

Thou didst come upon the earth, O Co-Unoriginate with the Father, proclaiming from the Father remission unto the captives, sight unto the blind, and the acceptable year.

*Theotokion:*

Our hope, O pure Mother of God, and our desire we place upon thee; grant that He Whom thou didst bear be merciful unto us.

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Heirmos:*

The ungodly shall not see Thy glory, O Christ; but we, waking early in the morning from the night, hymn Thee, O Only-begotten, Radiance of the Father's glory of the Godhead, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

As immaculate ewe-lambs, as acceptable sacrifices, unto the true Lamb and Shepherd ye were offered, O women martyrs, all-rich offerings and acceptable whole burnt-offerings.

Being put to death in the body, ye were made alive in the soul, O women martyrs, having assimilated yourselves unto Him Who put to death the power of death, and unto His Cross, and death, and voluntary passion.

Having one mind in many bodies, confessing the one Lord Jesus, while scraped with manifold wounds and burned with fire, O God-wise women.

*Theotokion:*

Raise me up who am fallen into the pit of temptations, and guide me, who didst bear the Pilot God, O only all-immaculate one, Who first united the divided by His goodness.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*

Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant Thy peace unto us, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

A new Daniel Christ showed thee forth, O Symeon; for from the beasts' pit by His appearance He returned thee unharmed.

Commending all thyself unto the Lord, against sleet, and frost, and scorching heat, by contradictory assaults, thou didst strip thyself naked.

A new Moses and Elijah thou wast shown to be, taking food once throughout the entire Forty Days in all thy life, O venerable father.[^15]

*Theotokion:*

As with a golden-beaming necklace, O venerable Symeon, encircled with a rope, thou wast shown to be a heaven-walker on divine wings.

*Theotokion:*

Pray ever unto thy Son and our God, O unwedded, pure Mary, to send down great mercy upon us faithful.

*Katavasia:*

O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon was crucified Christ, the King and Lord, whereby fell he who deceived through the tree, being himself deceived by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Thou didst save the prophet from the whale, O Lover of mankind; and bring me up, I pray, from the depth of transgressions.

*Troparia:*

Vouchsafe us, O Master, to begin our life well-pleasing unto Thee, along with the beginning of the year.

Show the days of those who hymn Thee, O compassionate Savior, filled with spiritual learning in the meditation of Thy law.

*Theotokion:*

O all-immaculate Mother of God, who didst bear the Lord: deliver from perils those who hymn thee with faith, O all-pure one.

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Heirmos:*

Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried out, praying in the whale: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers!

*Troparia:*

Beholding him who first through deceit cast her out of Paradise now infuriated and trampled under women's feet, the foremother divinely rejoices.

Having zealously united self-mastery unto suffering, ye have now joined yourselves incorruptibly unto the souls of women [saints], and in the divine bridal chamber with joyful soul ye take up your abode.

The surging wild billows of torments could not submerge the ships of the women martyrs; for by a mighty hand they reached the divine harbors.

*Theotokion:*

Beholding the fulfillment of thy words, magnify exceedingly, O Mother of God, Him Who magnified thee; for all generations now truly call thee blessed.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*

Grant me a radiant robe, Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O plenteous in mercy, Christ our God.

*Troparia:*

Christ showed thee forth as an author of signs and wonders, O blessed one, an acceptable habitation of divine energy.

Thou didst lift up thy body, O Symeon, as upon a cross upon the pillar; therefore thou wast glorified together with Christ, Who was lifted up upon the Tree for thy sake.

Having found the sublime ascent, O marvelous Symeon: unto the unending height those who faithfully hymn thee lead up.

*Theotokion:*

The mountain which Daniel foresaw, from which the cut-off stone of faith, Christ, was cut: we know Thee to be.

*Katavasia:*

In the womb of the water-beast, Jonah stretching forth his palms cross-wise clearly prefigured the saving Passion; therefore coming forth after three days, he portrayed the transcendent resurrection of Christ God Who was nailed in the flesh and by His three-day resurrection enlightened the world.

*Kontakion of the Venerable Father Symeon, Tone 2:*

Seeking the highest, being joined with the highest, and having made thy pillar a chariot of fire: therefore thou wast a converser with the angels, O venerable father, with them entreating Christ God unceasingly for us all.

*Ikos:*

What human tongue shall ever suffice to recount in praise the blameless life of Symeon? Yet by the wisdom of God I shall sing: the suffering and the struggles of this valiant man on earth have fulfilled it; for he appeared as a luminary unto all men, shining forth with great patience in angelic rank. For with them singing unceasingly unto Christ, by self-mastery he acquired purity, entreating unceasingly for us all.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Children brought up together in piety, having disdained the ungodly command, were not afraid of the threatening of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*

Beginning the year, let us, the Orthodox people, make a beginning of songs unto Christ Who reigns with an unending kingdom, singing piously: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Being before the ages, and unto the age and still the Lord, O Christ, Fountain of goodness, fill this year with Thy good gifts for those who hymn Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

As servants unto the Mother of God for prayer, we offer Thy pure Mother unto Thee, O Christ, to deliver Thy people from every adversity, O Good One, who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Heirmos:*

He Who saved Thy Children of Abraham in the fire and slew the Chaldeans, whom justice righteously snared: All-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*

How invincible is thy wisdom, O God-bearing Ammon, who as leader of the choir of virgins didst not fear torments, finishing thy course with them, as a deacon and initiate of divine glory, thou didst sing: All-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

As a wise bridal-escort, with words of courage thou didst anoint the calling women martyrs to look unto the Bridegroom and to endure bodily pains: All-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Let us not be slothful, O virgins, the arena is opened, let us stand manly; Christ stretches forth the crowns, let us not spare our body, cried the valiant women in the arena: All-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*

Blessed is the fruit of thy blessed womb, Whom the heavenly powers and human assemblies bless, Who delivered us from the ancient curse, O blessed one.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*

The pious Children in Babylon bowed not down unto the golden image, but bedewed in the midst of the fiery furnace, sang a hymn, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, Who art exalted above all!

*Troparia:*

Thou didst loose drought for those who were in perplexity, and didst open for them the gates of rain, and by thy prayers didst stay the shaking earth, and didst teach the people to cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

As the greatest luminary of the Church, and a multi-radiant sun, O Symeon, emitting rays everywhere thou didst enlighten, and didst teach the people to cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

The waters gathered round about, O servant of Christ; a multitude of men assembled in the enclosure of thy self-mastery, instructed by thee to cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Of old in the arms of the Elder, but now upon the tablets of thy heart, O father, by invisible power Christ rested, O Symeon; therefore thou didst cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

It was fitting for Him Who was seedlessly incarnate of thee to come forth, O pure Virgin; for thou wast shown forth by purity to be greater than all; unto Whom crying out in hymns we say: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Katavasia:*

The senseless command of the ungodly tyrant shook the people, breathing threatening and God-hated blasphemy; yet the three Children the beast-like rage terrified not, nor the devouring fire; but in the dewy spirit counter-blowing, being with the fire, they sang: All-hymned God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Ye hymn-singers, praise Christ God, Who saved the children in the furnace, and changed the thunderous flame into dew, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

As unto the Author of salvation, O Christ, the venerable Church offers Thee the beginning of the year, crying: Praise and exalt Christ above all unto the ages.

Praise and exalt Him above all unto the ages, the Creator Who wisely renewed all things from non-being, and Who brings forth the cycles of times by His will.

Unto God Who brings forth all things and changes times for the manifold governance of men, let us sing: Praise and exalt Christ above all unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*

O pure Virgin Mother of God, in the cycles and revolutions of the years, we, the Orthodox assemblies of men, sing unto thee as Mother of God and salvation of all.

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Heirmos:*

The Children of piety in the furnace the offspring of the Mother of God saved; then prefigured, but now in energy, it raises all the inhabited world to sing unto Thee: Praise the works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

Ye wrapped radiant robes around yourselves from the blood of martyrdom, having stripped off in truth the man that corrupts with sins, and singing: Praise the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

Illuminated with the light-pourings of the abundant light, with the divine radiances of the noetic Sun, O women martyrs, ye traversed the night of godlessness, singing with one accord of soul: Praise the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

As ewe-lambs, as unblemished heifers, as divine doves, as voluntary slaughterings, ye were brought, O women martyrs, unto the Creator, and as blameless sacrifices, harmonious singing: Praise the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

By the command of the most lawless tyrants ye underwent an unjust death, being cut limb by limb, crushed with clubs, beaten unmercifully, burned with fire, cut down with the sword: therefore with joy ye received immortal, rich recompenses.

*Theotokion:*

Women ran in thy train, knowing the sweet-smelling myrrh, O all-honored Bride of God, only unwedded one, the Only-begotten Son Who shone forth from thy womb, and with thee they reign, truly reigning, singing unto Christ unto the ages.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*

Unto Him Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and in the bush through fire revealed the mystery of the Ever-Virgin unto Moses: praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

Having separated thyself from all passion, and having had compassion on thy mother's weakness, as living thou didst appear after death: praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

Thou didst raise up the paralyzed youth, and didst command the phylarch to carry his bed upon his shoulders, most sacredly crying: Praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

Stricken with the passion of Job, the rot of thy decaying flesh Christ turned into most precious pearl, O servant Symeon, praising Him unto all ages.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Receiving joy from the angel, and having borne the Lord of glory, and having shone light upon the world, we all sing unto thee, O Virgin Mother of God, unto all ages.

*Then:*

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him above all unto all ages.*

*Katavasia:*

Bless, O Children, equal in number to the Trinity, God the Father, the Creator; hymn the Word Who descended and changed the fire into dew; and exalt above all the All-Holy Spirit, Who gives life unto all, unto the ages.

*And the Priest, having censed the Holy Table, exclaims:*

*The Mother of God and the Mother of the Light let us magnify in songs.*

*And having censed the Holy Altar, and the entire church and the brethren, which is never omitted at the 9th Ode of Matins. And we chant the 9th Ode, singing aloud, in Tone 6:*

*My soul doth magnify the Lord:*

*And we sing the refrain:*

*More honorable than the Cherubim:*

*(This 9th Ode, as long as it is not a Feast of the Lord, is always chanted, even if it be the Great Doxology, or the Temple of whichever Saint it may be.)*[^16]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

A figure of thy pure childbearing the fiery burning bush showed unburned; and now we pray to extinguish the furnace of perils raging against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Mother of God.

*Troparia:*

The Word of God, and Power, and true and hypostatic Wisdom, Who upholds and directs all things wisely: do Thou now also conduct the present time for Thy servants in quiet arrangement.

*Troparia:*

All Thy works, O Lord: heavens, earth, light, and sea, waters and all fountains, sun, moon, and darkness, stars, fire, men, and beasts, together with angels praise Thee.

Thou alone art pre-eternal, as Creator of the ages, and reigning tri-hypostatic one undivided Godhead: by the supplications of His pure Mother, show the year fruitful unto Thine inheritance.

*Theotokion:*

O Savior of all, and Disposer, and Creator and Ruler of creation: by the supplications of her who seedlessly bore Thee, grant peace unto Thy world, preserving the Church ever untroubled.

*Another [Canon of the Holy Women]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Eve, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Mother of God, through the budding of thy childbearing, didst cause blessing to blossom forth unto the world. Therefore we all magnify thee.

*Troparia:*

Streams of healings the all-blessed women pour out unto those in need, as from a fountain; they halt the ruin of diseases, and drive away the burning heat of passions, watering the hearts of lovers of God unto the fruitful yield of divine deeds.

The divine deacon Ammon, and Celsina, and with them the forty divine and God-wise women, having suffered lawfully were crowned; and now they dance with the angels, whom worthily we call blessed.

Ye were lifted up, having received power against the enemies, and were likened unto angels; ye enjoy without hindrance the Tree of Life in Paradise, O brides of God, and having received a fountain of good things, pray for the world.

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast revealed as a receptacle of Wisdom surpassing transcendent mind, O immaculate Maiden, an ensouled throne and door; therefore the virgins, having loved the King, were brought after thee, O Maiden of God.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Prefigured on the mountain unto the Lawgiver in the fire and the burning bush, the childbearing of the Ever-Virgin for the salvation of us faithful, with unceasing hymns we magnify.

*Troparia:*

Thou didst reign over passions through endurance; Christ received Thee, O God-bearing Symeon, as a partaker of His kingdom. Therefore we honor Thee with hymns.

Having been accounted worthy of healing grace from the unstolen treasures of the Spirit, O God-bearing Symeon, thou grantest healings unto those who celebrate thy memory.

Having mounted up, O venerable one, from the temporal course into the air of virtue, girded with sufferings, having flown up unto the heavenly tabernacles, pray that our souls may be saved.

*Theotokion:*

The bush burning with fire and unconsumed thou wast revealed to be, O Virgin Maiden, having seedlessly conceived God and the Savior of the world, Whom unceasingly we magnify.

*Katavasia:*

Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Mother of God, who untilled didst bud forth Christ, by Whom the life-bearing Tree of the Cross was planted on earth; therefore as it is now exalted, worshipping Him, we magnify thee.

*Another [Katavasia]:*

Through the eating from the tree, death came unto our race, but by the Cross it is abolished today; for the ancestral all-generic curse is destroyed by the offspring of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly powers magnify.

*Exapostilarion of the Indiction,*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "With the Disciples" (Оу҆чн҃кѡ́мъ):*

O God of gods and Lord, tri-hypostatic Nature, unapproachable, ever-existing, uncreated, and Creator and Ruler of all: unto Thee we all fall down and Thee we entreat: as Thou art good, bless this present year, preserve in peace the king,[^17] and all Thy people, O Compassionate One.

*Glory... of the Venerable Father, in the same melody:*

Even as a luminary, O venerable one, thy light-bearing life, having shone forth, enlightened all under the sun with the rays of wonders; for by a pillar, O father, thou didst ascend as by a ladder unto God, where is the ultimate true reception of all desires, O Symeon, praying for us who honor thee, O blessed one.

*Both now... of the Indiction, in the same melody:*

Being the Creator and Governor of all creation, Who hast set the times and years in Thine own power: crown the cycle of the year with the blessings of Thy goodness, O Compassionate One, preserving in peace Thy people unharmed and whole, we pray Thee, by the supplications of her who bore Thee and of the divine angels.

*At the Praises, Stichera Idiomela of the Indiction, on 4. Tone 3. By John the Monk:*

Pre-eternal Word of the Father, Who art in the form of God, and didst establish creation from non-being into being, Who hast set the times and years in Thine own power: bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, granting peace unto Thy churches, and victories unto the most faithful king, and fruitful yield unto the earth, and unto us great mercy.

*Tone 4. By the same [John the Monk]:*

Thy kingdom, O Christ God, is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy dominion is unto every generation and generation; for all things Thou didst make in wisdom, having set forth times and seasons unto us. Therefore, giving thanks for all things and concerning all things, we cry: Bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, and vouchsafe us uncondemned to cry unto Thee: O Lord, glory be to Thee!

*By Andrew of Pyrgos:*[^18]

Thy goings, O God, Thy goings are great and marvelous; therefore we magnify the power of Thy dispensation, that Light from Light Thou didst come into Thy miserable world, and didst destroy the former curse of the ancient Adam, as Thou wast well-pleased, O Word. And in wisdom Thou hast set the times and years for us, that we may glorify Thine all-working goodness: O Lord, glory be to Thee!

*Of the Holy Women, Tone 2. By Germanus:*

When by Thy Passion, O Lord, Thou didst establish the universe, then also the infirm were girded with power. The women acted manfully against the proud tormentor, and having set right their mother's defeat, were again in the sweetness of Paradise, unto the glory of Thee Who wast born of a woman, and didst save the human race.

*Glory... of the Venerable Father, in the same tone:*

From a good root sprouted a good fruit, Symeon, who from infancy was consecrated, nourished with grace rather than with milk; and having raised his body upon a stone, and exalted his mind unto God, he built a heavenly dwelling by virtues. And he walked in choir with the divine powers, having become a dwelling of Christ, the God and Savior of our souls.

*Both now... of the Indiction, Tone 8. By Germanus:*

With unutterable wisdom having established all things, O Word, Christ God: Who hast set forth the times and years for us, bless the works of Thy hands. And make glad the faithful king by Thy power, granting him strength against barbarians, as Thou art alone good and Lover of mankind.

*Then, the Great Doxology.*

*And after the Trisagion, the troparion of the Indiction: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... "Rejoice, thou who art full of grace." Litanies, and the dismissal. And the First Hour: At the First Hour, the troparion of the Indiction: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the kontakion of the Indiction and of the Saint, we recite alternating; and the rest, and the complete dismissal.*

*At the Beatitudes, from the Canon of the Indiction, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Venerable one, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance, the troparion, first of the Indiction, and of the Mother of God: "Rejoice, thou who art full of grace"; and of the Venerable one: Glory... the kontakion of the Saint: Both now... the kontakion of the Indiction. (If it be a Temple of the Mother of God: Both now... of the Temple of the Mother of God; but the kontakion of the Indiction say at the beginning.) Prokeimenon of the Indiction, Tone 3: "Great is our Lord, and great is His power, and His understanding is without number." Verse: "Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good." And of the Venerable one: Prokeimenon, Tone 7: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones." Epistle to Timothy: section 282 [1 Tim. 2:1–7]: "Child Timothy, I exhort therefore first of all"; and of the Venerable one, to the Colossians: section 258 [Col. 3:12–16]: "Brethren, put on therefore." Alleluia, Tone 4: "Unto Thee song is due, O God, in Zion." Verse: "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, O Lord." And of the Venerable one: "Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, in His commandments he shall desire greatly." Gospel according to Luke: section 13 [Luke 4:16–22]: "At that time, Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up." And of the Venerable one, according to Matthew: section 43 [Matt. 11:27–30]: "All things are delivered unto Me." Communion Hymn: "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of Thy goodness, O Lord." Another: "In everlasting remembrance." The daily Epistle and Gospel we read beforehand.*

*One should know:*[^19]

*If the first day of the month of September fall on a Sunday: the service of the holy women is omitted, and is chanted when the Ecclesiarch shall judge. But the Sunday service is chanted with the sequence of the Indiction and of the Venerable Symeon as follows:*

*At Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera, and of the Mother of God, according to custom. Troparion of the Resurrection: Glory... Both now... Theotokion.*

*At Great Vespers: We chant "Blessed is the man," the entire kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Sunday stichera 3, and Anatolian 1, and of the Indiction 3, and of the Saint 3: Glory... of the Indiction: Both now... Theotokion of the tone. And readings of the Indiction 2, and of the Saint 1. At the Litiya, the sticheron of the Temple, and the stichera of the Indiction from the Aposticha: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... of the Indiction, written at the Praises. At the Aposticha, the Sunday stichera, according to the alphabet, with their refrains: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... of the Indiction. At the blessing of the loaves, "O Virgin Mother of God, rejoice," twice, and of the Indiction once. And a reading in the Epistles of the Apostles. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the troparion of the Resurrection, twice: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... of the Indiction. After the kathismata: the Sunday sessional hymns with their theotokia. And a reading in the Gospel commentaries, that which is in order. After the Evlogitaria, the troparia, and the Hypakoe; and a reading. The Hymns of Ascents, and the Prokeimenon of the tone. And "Let every breath." The Sunday Matins Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. The Sunday Sticheron. The Sunday Canon with the Heirmos on 4, and of the Mother of God on 2, and of the Indiction on 4, and of the Saint on 4. Katavasia: "Having traced the Cross." After Ode 3, the kontakion of the Indiction, and of the Saint; and sessional hymn of the Saint, 2: Glory... Both now... of the Indiction; and a reading of the Life of Saint Symeon. After Ode 6, the kontakion of the Resurrection, and the Ikos. And we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, we chant "More honorable than the Cherubim." The Sunday Exapostilarion: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... of the Indiction. At the Praises, Sunday stichera 4, and of the Indiction 3, Tone 3: "Pre-eternal Word," with the refrain of the Indiction. Then the idiomelon of the Saint, Tone 2, with the refrain: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones," "From a good root": Glory... the Gospel Sticheron: Both now... "Most blessed art thou." The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the troparion of the Resurrection only. Litanies. And the dismissal. And the catechesis. And the customary procession. And the First Hour in the narthex. And the final dismissal. At the First Hour, we recite the troparion of the Resurrection: Glory... of the Indiction: Both now... the Theotokion of the Hour. After the "Our Father," the kontakion of the Indiction. At the Third Hour, the troparion of the Resurrection: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... the Theotokion of the Hour; after the "Our Father," the kontakion of the Saint. Likewise at the other Hours, the kontakia of the Resurrection, and of the Indiction, and of the Saint, we recite alternating. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Resurrection of the tone, on 4; and from the Canon of the Indiction, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance, the troparion of the Resurrection, and of the Indiction, and of the Saint. Kontakion of the Resurrection: Glory... of the Saint: Both now... of the Indiction. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel, first of the Indiction, but the Sunday one under the section; then of the Saint. Communion Hymn of the Indiction; after that, of the Saint.*

*ON THE SECOND DAY OF THE SAME MONTH:*
*Memory of the Holy Martyr Mamas.*[^20]

*At Vespers, the customary kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," stichera, Tone 8, Podoben: "O Most Marvelous Wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесе):*

While thy blood was dripping, unto Christ the Life-giver, Who shed His own blood for thy sake, thou didst offer thyself, O blessed one; Who also made thee a partaker of glory and a fellow-partaker of His kingdom, because thou didst act valiantly against the deceiver, and didst quench his fierce wiles unto the end.

A pillar of piety thou wast, firmly founded upon the rock of faith, unmoved by temptations and perils, O blessed one. For the waves that dashed against thee with great storm and surging did not cast down thine unbending fortitude; for thou didst desire to be adorned with the martyrs' crown.

Following the life-bearing footsteps of our incarnate God, Who by the passion of the Cross cast down the tormentor, O passion-bearer, rejoicing thou didst enter into the tribunal of martyrdom, and being torn with wounds, him who boasted to dry up the sea, having courage along with the flesh, thou didst wound, and cast down to the earth.

*Glory... of the Martyr, Tone 6. By Byzantios:*[^21]

As a new plant, like an olive tree, thou wast set upon the table of God, as a son of those who walk in the ways of the Lord; because of thy martyrdom the Lord blessed thee, and thou seest the good things of the Zion on high, enjoying divine gladness together with thy parents, O blessed Mamas, worthy of praise; make us partakers with them by thy supplications.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

When the immaculate Ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb led voluntarily as a man to the slaughter, weeping she said: Dost Thou hasten now to make me childless, O Christ, who bore Thee? What is this that Thou hast done, O Deliverer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thine extreme goodness surpassing mind and word, O Lover of mankind.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos:*

*Glory... of the Martyr, Tone 4:*

Let us, the faithful, celebrate in harmony the memory of the martyr Mamas; for this new Abel appeared unto us. For even as he was a shepherd of sheep, and was the first to offer a lamb as a sacrifice, and the first to receive the crown of suffering: so also the glorious passion-bearer, having excelled with the flocks he fed, offered himself as an acceptable sacrifice unto Christ through martyrdom; and having boldness before Him, he asks peace for the world, and great mercy for our souls.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, in the tone of the day,*
*Podoben: "As One Valiant among the Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ въ мꙋ́нцѣхъ):*

Beholding Christ, the Lover of mankind, crucified and pierced in the ribs with a spear, the all-pure one wept, crying out: What is this, O my Son? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee in return for the good things that Thou didst do for them? And art Thou making haste to leave me childless, O most beloved One? I marvel, O Compassionate One, at Thy voluntary crucifixion.

*Troparion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*

Thy martyr Mamas, O Lord, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the tormentors and crushed the powerless boldness of demons. By his supplications, save our souls.

*Both now... Theotokion, in the tone of the day, or Stavrotheotokion.*

*At Matins, both canons from the Octoechos, and of the Saint on 4. The composition of Theophanes, Tone 8:*[^22]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

He who drove the chariot, Pharaoh, was submerged of old by the wonder-working rod of Moses, which struck in the form of a cross and divided the sea; and it saved Israel the fugitive, the wayfarer on foot, as he sang a hymn unto God.

*Troparia:*

Having departed unto God as a chosen martyr, and being filled with the three-sunned radiant beam, O glorious one: vouchsafe divine enlightenment unto those on earth who honor the honorable and light-bearing day of thy demise.

Foreknowing the nobility and in all things the perfection of thy mind, O Mamas, the Word from swaddling bands filled thee with understanding, and with the sweetnesses of good things manifoldly adorned thee, O all-praised martyr and passion-bearer.

Thy parents, holding fast unto the immaculate faith in the exile of deception, being shut up in prisons, by the divine command budded thee forth, who didst break the bond of polytheism.

*Theotokion:*

Most glorious things were spoken of thee throughout generations of generations, who didst contain God the Word in thy womb, and dost remain pure, O Mother of God and Virgin; therefore we all honor thee, our mediatress after God.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

O Lord, Supreme Builder of the heavenly vault and Architect of the Church: do Thou establish me in Thy love, O Summit of desires, Firmness of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

As a light-beaming star Christ set the passion-bearer Mamas upon the height of His Church, enlightening all under the sun with the radiances of his sufferings and marvelous wonders.

Having ascended the mountain of true knowledge, and shone with the purity of the mind's visions, by divine commands, O blessed one, thou didst raise the irrational brute creation unto rational hymnody.[^23]

A youth fair in beauty thou wast; therefore unto those lawlessly seeking to seize thee, thou wast revealed unapproachable, having come unto suffering, even as He was brought, the Lord of all.

*Theotokion:*

He Who spread out the heaven, O all-pure one, and by the nature of His Godhead holds the whole terrestrial sphere, was held in the flesh upon thine arms, and showed thee forth as the firm foundation of all the faithful.

*Sessional Hymn of the Martyr, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

A son of piety, an honorable offspring, thou wast revealed as a destroyer of impiety, O all-praised Mamas, by the power of the Spirit; for in the stadium thou didst expose the idol-deception, and with good courage didst proclaim the Trinity in song. Therefore, having been cast unto wild beasts, O saint-bearer, thou didst tame the beasts and the author of evil, the serpent; therefore we cry unto thee: Entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor thy holy memory with love.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, O only all-pure Virgin Mother, who in purity didst surpass the angels: cleanse me who above all have become dust, defiled with carnal transgressions, by the divine waters of thy prayers, granting great mercy, O pure one.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

The immaculate Ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, beholding Him Who sprouted painlessly from her suspended upon the Cross, maternally lamenting cried aloud: Woe is me, O my Child! How dost Thou suffer, desiring to deliver man from the passions of dishonor?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who without leaving the bosom of the Father didst visit our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*

Voluntarily thou didst set thyself apart for struggles, unskilled in worldly cunning, O glorious one, yet wise; for thou didst have Christ helping thee with divine power, confirming thy weakness, and showing thee forth as a witness of His sufferings, and a partaker of the brightness on high.

As a helper, he who was from God thy fellow-traveler was shown to be, even as the most rational wild beasts; for by divine love thou didst tame the most irrational passions, appearing fair through the wisest understanding, overcoming the irrationality of the enemies.

Before the tribunals of the tormentors thou didst stand, O blessed one, manifestly proclaiming the incarnation of the Word, and casting down the fierceness of godlessness, teaching all without doubting to sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*

By the supernatural birth of thy childbearing, the pain of sin was loosed, and the nature of the earthborn was changed from the curse, O all-immaculate Mother of God; and the things on high were opened for those below because of thee, and men dance together with angels.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O Never-setting Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my ways, I pray Thee.

*Troparia:*

Being scraped with iron combs, the glorious Mamas took no care for his body, resolving that the grossness of corruption be torn away, and stripping off the coats of skin, receiving the garment of incorruption.

Thou didst sing a thankful praise unto thy Creator when scraped in the ribs, O all-blessed one; and thou didst hear a voice from heaven confirming thy mind the more unto the better, and lightening the pain of thy sufferings.[^24]

Shut up in prison, there appeared unto thee from heaven a most glorious vision, O all-blessed, much-suffering passion-bearer, a most fair dove bearing the food of incorruption; for thou didst pass beyond the bounds of corruption.[^25]

*Theotokion:*

Of the divine incarnation and the unutterable transformation thou wast the mediatress, having borne Him Who was born of the Father before the sun; for through thee the nature of the earthly was united unto God and was seated upon the throne of glory.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my transgressions, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation.

*Troparia:*

Kindled with zeal for God, O most sacred one, Thou didst take no thought for the kindling flame, being bedewed with divine rain from heaven, O most valiant sufferer.

He Who for the three youths transformed the furnace into dew visibly, O God-wise and all-blessed one, snatched thee from the flame, and showed thee forth marvelously stronger than fire.

Enduring the greatest struggles, thou wast revealed greatest among sufferers, marvelous and experienced in torments. Therefore the Umpire of the contest accounted thee worthy of the greatest rewards.

*Theotokion:*

We have become partakers of the divine nature, O all-pure one, through thy divine childbearing; and we have inherited heavenly rest in Christ, praising thee with angelic ranks.

*Kontakion of the Holy Martyr, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*

With the staff given thee from God, O holy one, shepherd thy people upon the life-bearing pastures; and crush beneath the feet of those who hymn thee the invisible and untamed beasts; for all who are in perils have thee, O Mamas, as a fervent protector.

*Ikos:*

Let us sing of the martyr who is most glorious throughout all the earth, and dances with the angels in heaven, O Mamas: who of old milked the hinds in the wilderness, and now as a good shepherd pastures the rich people of the Lord with the rod of strength, guiding them unto a place of green pasture, where is truly the delight of Paradise; for on this account thou didst leave the world, that all may have thee, O Mamas, as a fervent protector.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The condescension of God the fire was ashamed of in Babylon of old; on this account the Children in the furnace, dancing with joyful foot as in a meadow, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*

The appearance of the furnace fulfilled for thee what was needed, even as coolness; for enclosed in it for many days, O Mamas, thou wast not burned, crying unto Him Who made thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Blessed is the God of our Fathers.

*Troparia:*

Thou hadst angels as fellow-recipients, fellow-choristers, and partakers of unutterable songs in the midst of the flame, O martyr; with whom thou didst cry unto the Master of all: Blessed is the God of our Fathers.

As an unfading rose, as a bridegroom going forth exceedingly fair in truth from the bridal chamber, having burned up the foolish from the furnace, and having enlightened those who behold and cry: Blessed is the God of our Fathers.

*Theotokion:*

Lo, now is fulfilled the prophecy of the God-proclaimer; for in thy womb, O Virgin, thou didst hold God the Word, and didst bear the Giver of life, unto Whom we all cry: Blessed is the God of our Fathers.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The Chaldean tyrant frantically kindled sevenfold the furnace for the godly; but having seen them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

As Daniel thou didst shut the mouths of the beasts, O glorious one, by the divine calling on the Master; thou didst put the dragon to death, thou didst put the wicked to shame, and as a victor in the heavens thou dwellest in gladness: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

They stoned thee with stones, O blessed one, they who serve stones and are petrified in soul, the transgressors; as thou didst raise thy holy hands, O martyr, unto the unbroken and immovable Rock, and didst fervently sing: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

The Bestower of the contest from on high stretching forth the crown unto thee as victor, and having traversed the good contest, O exceedingly rich one, proclaims unto thee to hasten unto Him, a venerable and sweetest journey, as thou dost fervently sing: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

Above nature thou didst conceive Him Who is from the Father without mother, having remained a Virgin and pure after childbirth; for the divine union renews nature in thee, and the boundaries of essence are renewed. Therefore, orthodoxly as having truly given birth to God, we hymn thee as Mother of God unto ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Heaven was astonished at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the ranks of angels and of men magnify thee, the Mother of God.

*Troparia:*

Thou didst commit thy soul unto the Deliverer, and unto Him thou didst fervently run, brightly adorned with the beauties of thy sacred contests, and of marvelous roots, O all-praised warrior, luminary of the universe, adornment of the Church.

Thou wast joined with the angels, having acquired angelic citizenship on earth; and with them thou singest in praise joyfully the sacred hymnody, O Mamas, unto the Trinity, all-praisedly, being deified by divine partakings, and being enriched with unending glory.

As thou hast boldness toward God, remember, O all-blessed one, those who joyfully celebrate this thy divine festival, O martyr, and who praise thy honorable and sacred suffering with pure faith; and save us from tempest, misfortunes, and distress.

*Theotokion:*

Who among those upon earth ever heard of an unwedded mother giving birth to an infant, and the Born One being God without beginning, and co-essential with the pre-beginning Father, and born of her above nature? O marvelous mystery! O divine communion, whereby we have been united unto God!

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos. Glory... of the Martyr, Tone 2, Podoben: "With the Disciples" (Оу҆чн҃кѡ́мъ):*

Thou wast nourished with the milk of deer, living in the mountains, O martyr Mamas; but thou didst appear again in the arena, having suffered most fervently, and having taken the crown of victory, thou didst depart unto the Lord.

*Theotokion:*

He who was envious of my divine and blessed life of old in Paradise, the most deceitful and all-wicked enemy, and caused me to be driven out of Eden, is put to death by thy childbirth, O Virgin.

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him. *Verse:* Hear, O God, my voice, when I make supplication unto Thee [LXX Ps. 63:11, 2].
*Epistle to the Romans: section 94 [Rom. 8:28–39].*
*Alleluia, Tone 4:* The righteous man shall flourish like a palm tree, and like a cedar in Lebanon shall he be multiplied [LXX Ps. 91:13].
*Gospel according to John: section 50 [John 15:17–16:2].*
*Communion Hymn:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous: praise is seemly for the upright [LXX Ps. 32:1].[^26]

*On the Third Day of the Same Month: The Holy Hieromartyr Anthimus, Bishop of Nicomedia; and our Venerable Father Theoctistus, Fellow-Ascetic of Euthymius the Great.*[^27]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "O All-Praised Martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи му́нцы):*

*Stichera of the Hieromartyr:*

O blessed one, wise in God, by the crimsonings of thine own blood thou didst make radiant thy sacred and divine vesture; for thou didst pass piously from strength to strength, and from glory to glory. And now pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

First offering unto God an unbloody sacrifice, as a most lawful priest, afterwards as a whole burnt offering and an acceptable sacrifice by thine own blood, as a most true martyr, thou didst bring thyself unto Christ, O all-honored speaker of God; Whom pray thou for those who sing of thee.

The armies of the martyrs, O father, thou didst bring unto Christ by thy teachings, O Anthimus, and by instructions, teaching and instructing, and openly offering thyself as an example, O wise in God; with whom pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

*Other Stichera of the Venerable One, in the same Tone and Podoben:*

O father Theoctistus, thy radiant memory makes glad the assemblies of monks with the beauties of thy life, and with the graces of miracles, and with the splendors of gifts. Pray Christ that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

O father Theoctistus, the demons were terrified of thy patient temperance, and were brought to naught by thine unceasing prayers, O all-praised one; for thou didst acquire Christ working together with thee, Whom now pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

O father Theoctistus, thou wast God's building; for having preserved that which is according to His image, true in life, thou didst show forth the calling of thine honorable image, O all-marvelous one. Pray Christ that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

and great mercy.

*Glory... Tone 6. Idiomelon:*

Thou wast a most lawful priest, even unto thy departure, O blessed Anthimus; for performing the sacred celebration of the divine and unutterable mysteries, thou didst pour out thy blood for Christ God, and didst bring thyself as an acceptable sacrifice. Therefore, having boldness toward Him, fervently pray for those who with faith and love celebrate thy most pure memory, and who honor it, that they may be delivered from assaults, and all misfortunes, and distresses.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the Third Day" (Тридне́венъ):*[^28]

Standing of old by the Tree at the time of the Crucifixion, the Virgin, weeping with the virgin disciple, cried: Woe is me! How dost Thou suffer, O Christ, Son of all impassibility?

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Glory... of the Venerable One, Tone 6:*

O venerable father, into all the earth went out the proclamation of thy righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors. Thou didst destroy the demonic legions, and didst attain unto the angelic ranks, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness toward Christ God, entreat peace for our souls.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the Third Day" (Тридне́венъ):*

Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who bore Thee cried: What strange mystery is this which I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die upon the Tree, suspended in the flesh, O Giver of life?

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Both a sharer in the ways and a successor to the thrones of the Apostles, thou didst find the practice, O God-inspired one, as an ascent to contemplation; therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, thou didst also suffer for the faith even unto blood, O hieromartyr Anthimus: pray Christ God that our souls be saved.

*Glory... of the Venerable One, Tone 8:*

With the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and with sighings from the depths thou didst make thy labors fruitful an hundredfold; and thou becamest a luminary to the universe, shining with miracles, O Theoctistus our father: pray Christ God that our souls be saved.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion.*

*At Matins, one Canon of the Octoechos, and two of the Saints. Canon of the Hieromartyr, whose Acrostic is:*[^29]

The bloom of pastors and martyrs I sing.

*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:* Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone is gloriously glorified.

*Troparia:*

Having received an interwoven crown of piety, high priesthood, and suffering, thou art blessed by Christ, O most glorious one.

Unto Thee, the Chief Pastor, Thy sacred celebrant, as an innocent and pure lamb, was brought by the hands of lawless men.

Thou didst tear down the fortresses of the heretics, O hierarch, with pious boldness, having preached the uncreated Trinity.

*Theotokion:*

O all-pure Mother of God, who above nature didst bear the incarnate, co-eternal, and transcendent Word: we hymn thee.

*Another Canon of the Venerable One, in the same Tone. Whose Acrostic is: Thy struggles, O Theoctistus, I recount. By Theophanes:*[^30]

*Ode 1. Heirmos: He cut through the uncuttable water with that which had been cut, and the sun saw land which it had not seen; the water drowned the fierce enemy, and Israel traversed the impassable. And a song was sung: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.*

*Troparia:*

Having encountered the desire for dispassion, O father, thou didst wither the wantonness of the flesh, O wise Theoctistus, aided by God. And now pray that we who sing unto the Lord may be filled with noetic light: For He is gloriously glorified.

The great Euthymius, joined unto thee with divine love, O father, and firmly abiding with thee, O Theoctistus, traversed the path of temperance in true action, and called out together with thee: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.

Thou didst mortify the body, O all-blessed one, and didst enslave the passions of the flesh, O father Theoctistus; for thou didst receive the brightness of grace, and enlightened thereby, didst divinely cry: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.

*Theotokion:*

Having thee as the hope of salvation, O Virgin Mother of God, as having borne the Word, the all-wise men with divine understanding, who blossomed in temperance, Euthymius beloved by all and divine Theoctistus, cried unto the Lord: For He is gloriously glorified.

*Ode 3. Heirmos: Thou art the establishment of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee.*

*Troparia:*

Thou wast revealed as a hieromartyr, first performing the sacred celebration acceptably unto the Deliverer; thereafter thou didst offer thyself as a sacrifice.

Thou wast not a hireling, but a most faithful shepherd, O venerable one, pouring out thy blood in godly fashion for thy flock.

Thou didst pre-eminently shepherd the flock of thy Master, O hierarch; therefore thou hast dwelt in a place of green pastures.

*Theotokion:*

Grant us help by thy supplications, O all-pure one, driving away the assaults of grievous distresses.
