*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 3. Heirmos: Thou art the establishment of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee.*

*Troparia:*

Thou didst mortify thy flesh by temperance, O venerable one, and didst enlighten thy soul with the gifts of divine graces.

Thou didst turn all desire unto thy Master, and with wrath didst arm thyself against the demons, O God-bearer.

*Theotokion:*

Chanting hymns, those taught of God piously glorified thee as the true Mother of God, O Mother of God, as having given birth to God.

*Sessional Hymn of Anthimus, Tone 4, Podoben: "The Angelic Choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):* Thy blood, O wise one, mystically cried from the earth unto God, like Abel's, O wise in God; for thou didst openly preach the uncreated Trinity. Therefore, O Anthimus, having walked as a shepherd, thou didst drive away the beasts of heresy, as a guardian of the faith.

*Glory... of the Venerable One, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Hast Appeared Today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):* Thou wast named leader of the sheep, and becamest a most radiant luminary unto the world, O venerable father Theoctistus; therefore unceasingly we honor thy memory.

*Both now... Theotokion:* O Virgin Mother, stretching forth thy most pure hands, cover those who place their hope in thee and cry unto thy Son: Grant Thy mercies unto all, O Christ.

*Stavrotheotokion:* Beholding Thy Son lifted up upon the Tree, O all-pure one, torn in thy maternal heart, thou didst sorrowfully cry: Woe is me! How hast Thou set, O my timeless Light?

*Ode 4. Heirmos: I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have understood Thy works, and I have glorified Thy Divinity.*

*Troparia:*

Having crushed the wolves with the word for thy lambs, O blessed one, thou wast put to death in body, but didst surrender thy spirit unto the Lord.

As a fragrant and all-honored sacrifice acceptable unto the King of all was thy sacrifice, and of him who offered it in wisdom of God, and of him who was offered by lawless hands.

Thou wast anointed, O venerable one, with priestly chrism first; and thou wast perfected secondly by thy suffering blood, O father.

*Theotokion:*

Grant us purification of our inadvertent sins, as Thou art sinless; and pacify Thy world, O God, through the supplications of her who bore Thee.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^31]

Thou didst mount upon horses, Thine Apostles, O Lord, and didst take their reins into Thy hands, and Thy riding became salvation unto those who faithfully sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

*Troparia:*

Thou wast revealed as a lover of the primal Wisdom, O all-wise one; for thou didst live a blameless life, pre-eminently purified in soul and mind, singing in concord: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

Having purified thy mind from passionate turmoil, O glorious one, and having guided thy senses wisely, thou didst hasten unto untroubled stillness, O father, fervently singing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

Having ascetically shaken off earthly sorrows, thy servant acquired heavenly hopes, O Master, even the divine Theoctistus, singing with Euthymius: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

*Theotokion:*

As Thou didst appear in the world from the Virgin as man, Thou didst grant victory unto Thy venerable ones; for by Thy Cross they drove away the demons, crying in faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Rising early from the night we cry unto Thee, O Lord: Save us, for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know none other.

*Troparia:*

An unbloody sacrifice thou didst offer unto the Lord, and thyself by thine own blood thou didst offer as fruit, O Anthimus.

The Divine Spirit enlightened thee, O hierarch; therefore we celebrate thy most glorious memory.

Thy divine tongue dripped salvation, and the stream of thy blood, spiritual joy.

*Theotokion:*

Still the unstable storm of my passions, O thou who didst give birth to God the Helmsman and Lord.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant us Thy peace, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

Mortify our earthly thoughts, O Lover of mankind, and the wanton impulses of the flesh, by the acceptable prayers of Thy venerable one.

From on high thou watchest over us, O all-blessed one, and guidest the life of us who celebrate thy memory with love.

*Theotokion:*

The co-dwelling pair, pre-eminent and called of God, preaches God incarnate from the pure Virgin, Who has ineffably shone forth unto us.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Grant me a robe of light, Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O most merciful Christ our God.

*Troparia:*

Thou didst baptize the people with water and the Holy Spirit, even as thou wast baptized; and thou wast baptized also by thine own blood, O father.

As a branch of the living Vine, chosen and honorable, thou didst yield the most abundant fruit unto thy Master, O all-blessed one.

Cease not to make supplication unto Christ, O blessed one, for thy flock, having presented thy supplicating blood.

*Theotokion:*

As a temple of God, and an ark, and an ensouled chamber, and the heavenly gate, O Mother of God, we the faithful proclaim thee.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*

I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows, for my soul is full of evils, and my life has drawn near unto Hades; and like Jonah I pray: O God, lead me up from corruption.

*Troparia:*

As a sun thou didst shine forth unto those upon earth, enlightening them with the light of piety, and sowing the radiance of virtues, and teaching the splendors of chastity, O Theoctistus: by thy prayers even now pacify the universe.

Delighted with God-wise contemplation, thou didst despise all things on earth, and didst beforehand judge heaven to be thine inheritance, O all-blessed father, wise in God, O Theoctistus; and now thou dwellest there in the heavens, rejoicing.

*Theotokion:*

Ye were drawn by the beauty of the love of Christ, comely and divine, Who appeared in the flesh in the world from the holy, pure Mother of God, delineations of the sure life of the monastic habit.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who Wast Raised Up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*

Having lived piously among the priests, and having finished the course of martyrdom, thou didst extinguish the idolatrous services, having become a champion for thy flock, O wise in God. Therefore it honors thee now mystically crying: From misfortunes deliver us by thy prayers, O ever-memorable Anthimus.

*Ikos:*

Having granted me divine knowledge, drive away the gloom of ignorance from my heart by thy prayers, that I may faithfully sing of thy holy memory; wherein the angelic choirs together with those of the martyrs rejoice divinely today, and men with songs of praise worthily crown thy head as with flowers, asking to receive from thee remission of transgressions and release from the evils of life, and to be delivered from enemies visible and invisible by thy prayers, O our father Anthimus.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Children who went down from Judea in Babylon of old, by faith in the Trinity trampled down the flame of the furnace, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers.

*Troparia:*

Both good and fat was thy sacrifice shown forth, O all-blessed Anthimus; for by thine own blood thou didst bring thyself unto the Master Himself, offering the unbloody sacrifices, and crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers.

Feeding and having fed the flock, thou didst gather wealth from all sides, O father; and having guarded this, thou didst preserve it with the seal of martyrdom, singing unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers.

In the midst of the Church of the faithful thou didst speak theology of the tri-hypostatic nature; and slain before it by the judgment of the unjust, O God-bearer, thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers.

*Theotokion:*

Having become incarnate from the virginal womb, Thou didst appear for our salvation; therefore knowing thy Mother as Mother of God, thankfully we cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Hebrew Children in the furnace trampled upon the flame with boldness, and turned the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.

*Troparia:*

Having cleaved unto thy Master with all desire through steadfast temperance, thou art nourished now by His splendors, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.

A divine fruit unto the Master thou didst bring thy life, O thrice-blessed one, and an acceptable and blameless sacrifice, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.

An end of sicknesses thou hast found, O father, even the delight which is in Paradise; for from the narrow path thou hast attained unto the spaciousness of the Kingdom of heaven, O all-wise one, blessing Christ unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*

Behold, the Virgin bore the divine Infant, Whom the God-bearers now knowing as God and Lord, cried: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The King of heaven, Whom the angelic hosts hymn: praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

In the memory of the glorious hieromartyr, rejoice, ye faithful, crying: We supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto the ages.

Beholding the hierarch comely adorned with the crown of martyrdom, we hymn the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto the ages.

Let us honor the servant of the Trinity, who poured out his blood for Its sake, hymning the Lord and supremely exalting Him unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

The unapproachable Light that dwelt within thee, O Virgin, showed thee forth unto all ages as a candle-stand and a radiant golden lamp.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The Chaldean tyrant frantically kindled sevenfold the furnace for the godly; but having seen them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

Thy memory comes with praises, O God-bearer; for thou wast revealed as a fosterer of righteousness, fortitude, wisdom, and chastity, O wise father, crying unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

Let us all honor the God-bearer with goodly praises, as one evidently full of grace, and pre-eminently enlightened with divine splendors, crying unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

In the tomb a saint buried thy body, one who was bright namesake of good cheer; while angels bore thy soul unto the heavens, joyfully singing unto the Creator: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^32]

*Theotokion:*

Having desired to philosophize by longing for hypostatic Wisdom, the God-wise hermits planted the virtues in godly fashion, which through thee, O Maiden, were revealed unto the world, O all-immaculate one; whom children bless, priests hymn, and people supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

The birthgiving of the Ever-Virgin, prefigured on the mountain unto the Lawgiver in the fire and the bush for the salvation of us the faithful, with unceasing hymns we magnify.

*Troparia:*

Thou indeed wast shown forth as a faithful shepherd unto the sheep, and unto the Shepherd as a lamb wast thou brought unto sacrifice, and twofold glory didst thou receive; therefore honoring thee, we call thee blessed.

Having portrayed in thyself the colors of piety with the marks of temperance, O most blessed one, truly according to the image of God didst thou show forth thy soul, O blessed one.

Keeping thy traditions unharmed, O father, and honoring thy suffering, in godly fashion we unceasingly bless the Trinity in the one nature of the Godhead with hymns.

*Theotokion:*

Crush the arms of those waging war against Thy Church, O Christ, for the sake of the Theotokos, and establish our faithful king,[^33] that we may unceasingly magnify Thee.

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Heaven was astonished at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the Theotokos do the hierarchies of angels and men magnify.

*Troparia:*

Having cleansed thyself with streams of thy tears, now dost thou delight, O Theoctistus, in the thrice-radiant light; standing manifestly before It and most exceedingly enlightened by rays thence, look down from above upon us who celebrate thy memory, O all-blessed one.

Having armed thyself with love and hope, and fenced about with faith, thou didst destroy the subtleties and deceits of the enemy; and having become a victor, now dost thou live bearing a crown, with the divine choirs of angels and venerable ones around the throne of the King of all.

Having lived chastely, righteously, and piously on earth with men, in the heavens do ye shine, O God-wise fasters, with the ranks of the bodiless ones, being nourished by the divine ray, from which also ye righteously received crowns of your struggles as victors.

*Theotokion:*

O divine and God-wise and sacred pair of fathers, most radiant,[^34] by your supplications ask peace from God to be sent down upon the world, and for the churches true concord of mind and faith, through the acceptable prayers of the Theotokos, O all-blessed ones.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "With the Disciples" (Оу҆чени́кѡмъ):*

Lead forth a dance today, the whole yearly choir, O city of Nicomedia, rejoicing in thy good shepherd and leap for joy, having an overseer who preserves thee, having become an injury unto the enemies.

*Theotokion:*

With the apostles entreat thy Son and Lord, O Theotokos, that all who hymn thee and glorify thee, and honor thee in icons, and worship thee worthily, and kiss thee with love, may be shown mercy.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*
*Glory, Tone 4. Idiomelon. By Ephraim of Caria:*[^35]

With the great city of Nicomedia does every city and land celebrate today in memory of its honorable citizen; for the ends of the earth clap their hands, rejoicing in the present solemnity of the hieromartyr. Unto him let us also, weaving crowns with hymns as with flowers, cry out: Rejoice, good shepherd, who didst lay down thy life for the sheep, a sacrifice and priest, priest and lamb! We pray thee: with those who suffered with thee,[^36] pray to Christ, O Anthimus, to deliver this thy flock from alien wolves, and to make us worthy of the heavenly fold with thee.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As One Valiant among Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

Beholding Christ, the Lover of mankind, being crucified, O all-immaculate one, and His ribs pierced with a spear, weeping she cried out: What is this, O my Son? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee for the good things Thou didst do for them? And dost Thou hasten to leave me childless, O most beloved One? I marvel, O Tenderhearted One, at Thy voluntary crucifixion!

*At the Liturgy.*
*The Beatitudes of the Octoechos, on 4; and of [Saint] Anthimus, Ode 3, on 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones. *Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me? [LXX Ps. 115:6, 3].
*Epistle to the Hebrews: section 334 [Heb. 13:7–16].*
*Alleluia, Tone 2:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness. *Verse:* Blessed is the man who fears the Lord [LXX Ps. 131:9; 111:1].
*Gospel according to John: section 36 [John 10:9–16].*
*Communion Hymn:* In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be; he shall not be afraid of evil tidings [LXX Ps. 111:6].

*On the Fourth Day of the Same Month: The Holy Hieromartyr Babylas, Bishop of Great Antioch; and the Holy Prophet and God-Seer Moses.*[^37]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having Laid Aside All Earthly Hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

*Stichera of the Hieromartyr:*

Having stained thy sacred vesture with blood, thou didst enter into the Holy of Holies, having become holy, O glorious Babylas; and visibly ever delighting in deification, being adorned and shining with martyrdom, and shown to be an angel by most honorable partakings; therefore we honor thee, and with love we celebrate thy most sacred solemnity, O worthy of blessing.

Bound with iron, unswervingly didst thou walk the path leading to the heavenly city, O venerable one; with honorable wounds, O all-wise Babylas, as with an ornament adorned; having entered into it as a most true victor, and an unconquerable martyr, and a most sacred minister of sacred rites, thou singest with the angels the sacred hymnody, purely: Holy, Holy, Holy, O Consubstantial Trinity!

Presiding over the rational flock, O hierarch, with the staff of knowledge thou didst nourish it upon the pasture of faith, and didst save it from beasts, and didst make God glad Who pastures thee from on high; Whom proclaiming before the godless ruler, O blessed one, as an innocent lamb wast thou slaughtered joyfully, with innocent children; and wast brought with them, a fragrant, whole-burnt sacrifice, O all-marvelous Babylas.[^38]

*Other Stichera of the Prophet, Tone 4, Podoben: "Being Called from On High" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

Having learned the divine mysteries of ineffable beauty and the glory of marvels, O Moses, God-seer all-praised, by shadows, sketches, and types didst thou announce them. Therefore, bringing unto us that which is prefigured of the divine radiance of the Primal Source by formless forms and immaterial matters, and having acquired by promise and grace to be made a god over Pharaoh, as God, O blessed one: pray for all who honor thee.[^39]

Having surpassed in virtues, in vision thou wast near to the God of all. In the midst of the whirlwind and of tempest, darkness, and cloud having entered within, thou wast wholly glorified. Thence didst thou receive the tablets of divine scriptures; and as equal to the angels by grace, clearly dost thou shine with the eyes of the soul together with those of the body. And thou veilest evil-believing blindness, revealing a revelation unto the faithful; this thou also impartest by word: pray that we may be saved.[^40]

In the God-wrought and fire-bearing divine love, thou wast a converser as friend to friend with God, and face to face, O thrice-blessed Moses. Looking upon thy Creator, having seen His back parts, the radiance thereof clearly, and through the cleft having learned the coming Theophany unto thee through the flesh of the Word; therefore as a pillar going before, most gloriously before the God-wise people, thou goest before and savest faithfully those who praise thee.[^41]

*Glory, of the Hieromartyr, Tone 6. Idiomelon:*

A step of ascent did the Church acquire in thy sacred contests, O hieromartyr Babylas, whom also thou keepest unshaken and unharmed by powerful wolves, while she proclaims thy valiant deeds and magnifies with thee the children slaughtered with thee for Christ, O blessed one.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having Risen on the Third Day" (Тридне́венъ):*

Pondering thy seedless conception and painless childbirth, I marvel greatly: how hast Thou willed to die thus as an evildoer, O my Son? the all-immaculate one cried out.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory, of the Hieromartyr, Tone 6:*

Standing before the tribunal of the tormentors, and contending for piety, thou didst cry out: Behold, I and the children whom God hath given me![^42] With whom having been crowned in the heavens, O hieromartyr Babylas, pray unceasingly that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having Risen on the Third Day" (Тридне́венъ):*

Beholding the lawless people unjustly nailing Thee upon the Wood, O Virgin and pure Mother of Thine, even as Simeon foretold,[^43] was wounded in her heart, O Savior.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

And partaker of the habits, and successor on the thrones of the apostles having become, thou didst find action, O God-inspired one, as an ascent unto contemplation; for this cause rightly dividing the word of truth, and for the sake of the faith thou didst suffer even unto blood, hiero- martyr Babylas, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*And of the Prophet, Tone 2:*

Celebrating the memory of Thy prophet Moses, O Lord, therefore we pray Thee: save our souls.

*Or this one, in the same Tone:*

Unto the height of the virtues didst thou ascend, O prophet Moses; and for this cause wast thou counted worthy to behold the glory of God, having received the grace-filled tablets of the Law, and bearing within thyself the grace of the inscriptions; and thou wast the honorable boast of the prophets, and a great mystery of piety.

*At Matins, one Canon of the Octoechos, and two of the Saints. By John the Monk, Tone 6:*[^44]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Traversing the deep on foot as if on dry land, Israel, seeing the persecutor Pharaoh drowned, cried out: Let us sing a triumphal song unto God!

*Troparia:*

By thine own blood, as Moses through the Red Sea, having passed without pain, O blessed Babylas, thou didst cry a song of victory unto God: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously magnified!

Thou didst surpass the desire of earthly things, having subordinated the desire to live unto the divine longing, O blessed Babylas, coming to behold the beauty of Christ.

As a loving son of the Thrice-Divine Trinity, with three children didst thou die rejoicing, O blessed Babylas, ever leading these souls with desire.

*Theotokion:*

Having received thine own Creator, as He Himself willed, incarnate above understanding from thy seedless womb, O pure one, thou wast truly shown forth as Sovereign Lady of creatures.

*Another Canon, of the Prophet, whose Acrostic is:* Moses, first of the prophets, let him be praised with words. *And in the Theotokia, by Clement.*[^45] *Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Traversing the Red Sea's depth with dry feet, ancient Israel of old, by the cross-shaped hands of Moses, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.

*Troparia:*

Moses, first of the prophets, let him be praised, as having first conversed with God manifestly, face to face, not in riddles of words, but having seen Him as in the form of flesh.

As a divine leader of the people and deliverer unto thy nation Israel did God give thee, O Moses, God-seer, even as thy father prayed, announcing thy birth by the anointing of promise.

The virtues of thy kin found thee, a treasure of wisdom, hidden by the knowledge of God as in an ark, O God-seer Moses; therefore the queen and divine Providence reared thee.[^46]

*Theotokion:*

Moses was terrified, beholding the most glorious early vision, the strange mingling of the bush and the flame, which prefigured the Incorrupt One coming from the Virgin Mother; Whom having passed through times, he beheld in the flesh.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

*Troparia:*

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who didst exalt the horn of Thy faithful Babylas, and crown him with the crown of Thy confession.

Thy Cross, O Lord, was the strength of martyrs, which established the children with blessed Babylas, and by them cast down the audacity of godless deceit.

The strength of the devil hath wholly failed, O Christ; for by innocent children and by divine Babylas the strong one is conquered, and is mocked and derided by them.

*Theotokion:*

The marvel of thy divine childbirth, O pure one, surpasses every order of nature; for above nature thou didst conceive God in thy womb, and having given birth thou remainest Ever-Virgin.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*

The bow of the mighty hath grown weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord.

*Troparia:*

Thou wast filled with wholly ineffable knowledge, O God-seer; the Holy Spirit through an angel clearly taught thee the knowledge of ancient things.[^47]

With wounds of bright divine radiance, with God-given signs didst thou strike Egypt with wonder, O all-wise one, most gloriously altering the nature of the elements.

Thy luminous citizenship, radiant with divine brilliance, gazes upon the fair aspect of thy beauty, O blessed one, and insatiably drew all toward divine beauty.

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast terrified by the fearful vision, at the dreadful sight, O all-wise one; but the voice of the Lord forbade thee, Who was born of the Virgin in the flesh.

*Kontakion of the Prophet, Tone 2:*

The choir of prophets with Moses and Aaron rejoices today with gladness, for the fulfillment of their prophecy is accomplished upon us: today shines the Cross the Cross, whereby Thou hast saved us: by their prayers, O Christ God, have mercy upon us.

*Sessional Hymn of the Hieromartyr, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the Divine Faith" (Бж҃твенныѧ вѣ́ры):*

Pouring forth the confession of faith, thou didst extinguish the deceit of bad belief, having rebuked idolatrous godlessness; and having become a divine whole-burnt offering, with miracles thou dost dew the ends of the earth: O venerable father, pray Christ God to grant us great mercy.

*Glory, Another Sessional Hymn of the Prophet, Tone 4:*

Knowing thee as truly the first of all the prophets, we the faithful piously praise thee; for thou wast the first to see God, even as it was possible for man to see Him.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, Tone 4:*

Having stretched forth thy most pure hands, O Virgin Mother, shelter those who hope in thee and cry unto thy Son: Grant Thy mercies unto all, O Christ!

*Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4:*

Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Wood, O all-immaculate one, her maternal heart torn asunder, piteously cried out: Woe is me! How hast Thou set, O my ageless Light?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church in godly fashion sings, crying out from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.

*Troparia:*

Christ is my power, God and Lord! didst thou cry before the tribunal, undaunted by the threats of the tormentors, O hieromartyr Babylas, rejoicing in the Lord.

Offering unto the Lord an unblemished, fearful, unbloody sacrifice, thou didst also bring thy very self as an undefiled slaughter by blood, O hieromartyr Babylas.

Having nourished the tender understanding of the children with spiritual milk as a wise tutor of children, O venerable one, thou didst direct them unto perfection, O hieromartyr Babylas.

*Theotokion:*

Truly immaterial and incomprehensible, O Theotokos, unto those on earth and in heaven are the mysteries of thy magnificent childbirth, O Ever-Virgin.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her station, worthily crying out: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

When the slowness of thy tongue and thy voice was made clear by divine Providence, O God-seer, Thou didst appear as the words of the divine mysteries of Genesis, and with plagues didst Thou wound Egypt.[^48]

How most glorious is thy calling, O God-seer! How fearful are the works of thy marvels! For God appeared unto thee as a Son,[^49] and having exalted thee with glory, sent thee as a savior unto Israel.

Thou didst strike every firstborn of Egypt, even as Christ put to death the dominion of demons; for the things wrought by thee truly were types of what was to come, O glorious one.

*Theotokion:*

"Draw not nigh hither," heard Moses, the voice of God crying from the flame of the bush; for that place prefigured in beauty that Christ was to be born in the flesh of the pure one.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine with love the souls of those who dawn early unto Thee, I pray, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, recalling them from the darkness of sins.

*Troparia:*

Having truly received Thy divine grace from on high, O Jesus, the hieromartyr Babylas led even young children unto Thy love and unto contempt of death.

Illumined with Thy divine knowledge, the hieromartyr Babylas taught all, O Lord, to know Thee as the only God, Who art Lord, calling them from the darkness and deceit.

Marked by Thy divine election, the hieromartyr Babylas, to shepherd Thy rational flock, offers his blood unto Thee, O Word of God, wisely guiding all unto the path of salvation.

*Theotokion:*

Save those who confess thee from the soul as the Theotokos, O good Lady of the world; for we have thee as an invincible protectress, who art truly the Parent of God.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Thou, O my Lord, didst come as a light into the world, a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith from the dark gloom of ignorance.

*Troparia:*

With strokes upon the Red Sea Thou didst make many divisions with thy rod, O God-seer, that Thou mightest show therein the divine power of the Cross.

O most beloved boldness! O purity of an honorable soul! "If Thou hast known me above all," said the God-seer unto God, "manifest Thyself intelligently unto me."[^50]

Covered by the rock, thou didst not see the face of God as hidden, O God-seer, but didst know the Incarnation of the Word as His back parts.

*Theotokion:*

Sensibly thou didst go into the gloom, and didst learn ineffable things, O God-seer, that God the Savior was to be born of the Virgin in the flesh.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!

*Troparia:*

Beholding the deceitful sea of life agitated with tempest, Babylas, the most glorious sufferer, cried: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!

Imitating Christ, thou didst surrender thy life for the flock, O glorious martyr and sufferer, blessed Babylas, and thou didst tear down the walls of deceit.

The wavering mind of the children did Babylas, the ever-memorable sufferer, wisely establish by his sufferings, leading them from earth unto heavenly life, O most glorious one.

*Theotokion:*

O all-immaculate Theotokos, who didst bear the Helmsman and Lord unto mortals, calm the wavering and fierce turbulence of my passions, and grant stillness unto my heart.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.

*Troparia:*

Having acquired the mighty army of God, O Israel, thou didst destroy the seven nations of Canaanite malice; giving their land unto the people for an inheritance.[^51]

Having ineffably entered into the divine gloom, O Moses, where God was Who called thee, thou didst receive the tablets of the Law written with His finger, as His great pleaser.[^52]

God caused Moses the God-seer to give ear unto His voice, having manifested Himself unto him, that He might show His fearful mystery with glory.

*Theotokion:*

By the divine will does the glorious Moses prefigure thee, O Theotokos, as an ark, covered everywhere with the rays of the Spirit as with gold unto the glory of God.[^53]

*Kontakion of the Hieromartyr, Tone 8, Podoben: "As First-Fruits of Nature" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*

As a preacher of piety and confirmation of sufferers, the Church glorifies thee, O glorious Babylas, being enlightened today; but as having boldness toward the Lord, pray to Christ to preserve in perfect peace those who magnify and praise thee, O much-suffering one!

*Ikos:*

Meditating manifestly upon heavenly radiance, being estranged from the world, and having imitated the passions of Christ, thou didst put to death the carnal passions thou didst put to death the carnal passions, and having taken up thy cross, thou didst follow after thy Creator, O martyr. And abiding with Him now, pray for those who honor thee in truth, O much-suffering one.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The angel made the furnace a source of dew for the venerable youths, while the command of God burning the Chaldeans persuaded the tyrant to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!

*Troparia:*

The heavenly hierarchies today, seeing the young victors over deceit and marvelous Babylas, cried out, rejoicing together in Christ: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our Fathers!

The light-bearing moon has made clear the grace unto the faithful gathered together, and glorious Babylas bearing a crown bids those rejoicing together to cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our Fathers!

The perplexed design of the tormentors was to help non-existent gods; but unto the Most Holy Trinity marvelous Babylas bids us cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!

*Theotokion:*

Through thee, O Virgin Mother, light has shone forth brightly upon the universe; for thou didst bear God, the Creator of all; Whom pray, O all-pure one, to send down great mercy upon us the faithful.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*

In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, burned by love of piety rather than by the flame, cried out: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

In ineffable visions of God having become a divine writer, being wholly wise in visions, having skillfully set them in words, thou didst present thine action unto the Primal Origin of gladness, O God-seer Moses.

Having dared to perform the priesthood with thee, Korah was shown descending alive into Hades;[^54] while God preserved for thee the honorable whole portion, O Moses, of kingship and priesthood together.

Unto thee as deliverer of the Judean nation of old, O Moses, Michael the leader of the heavenly hosts appeared as the divine guardian of thy body; for he put to shame the author of evil who spoke against it.[^55]

*Theotokion:*

Aaron's divine rod showed thee forth budded, O Theotokos, remission of sins unto all;[^56] for thou wast an estrangement unto earthly ones, even as that dreadful threat was unto those who murmured against God.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

From the flame for the venerable ones didst Thou pour forth dew didst Thou pour forth dew, and the sacrifice of the righteous one didst Thou burn up with water; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, merely by willing them: Thee do we highly exalt unto all ages.

*Troparia:*

God the Father, the Creator, the consubstantial Son, and the divine Spirit do the youths in the flame command to hymn: Let all creation bless the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages.

Today, O brethren, the youths in the flame command to hymn the memory of the hieromartyr Babylas: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and highly exalt Him unto all ages.

Today the young disciples of Babylas the priest and martyr, crowned with the elder, command to sing the song of the youths in the furnace: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and highly exalt Him unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

Thou didst bear in the flesh God, Who holds all things in His hand, and in thy embraces, O Virgin, didst thou carry Him; Whom we praise as the works of the Lord, and highly exalt unto all ages.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Daniel, having stretched forth his hands, shut the lions' mouths in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of fire, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*

Truly a servant of God, as meek wast thou heard of, and in deeds wast thou such; therefore was the Lord made known unto thee above all the prophets, O Moses, and taking up His abode within thee, taught thee to sing faithfully: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

As a mystic of God, and servant, and king of Israel, O God-seer Moses, thou didst appear, and didst proclaim Christ to come in the flesh, prefiguring in thyself His fearful and divine coming; of Whom also thou appearedst unto me as a living image and a faithful prophet.

By the word of prophecy and the commands of the Law didst thou faithfully instruct the people, directing them by signs and marvels and showings of wonders; for having appeared as a leader from God, O God-seer Moses, therefore wast thou gathered unto thy fathers with great glory.

*Theotokion:*

None heard beforehand prior to thee, O glorious God-seer Moses, servant of Christ, because thou didst utter all things, prefiguring the mysteries of the divine economy of that divine childbearing; for in the flame of the bush thou didst behold the invisible aspect.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-immaculate one, the Word incarnate was made manifest unto men: Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.

*Troparia:*

God showed unto men a path easily ascended by the Cross unto heavenly height; therefore is death conquered by earthly ones, for the young children feared it not, together with marvelous Babylas, whom we call blessed.

As Thou art Light, O all-pure Christ, cleanse my soul from the dark mist of passions by the prayers of Thy passion-bearers, Babylas and the children, whose yearly memory we celebrate, keeping festival in glorious fashion.

Let us draw forth healing of passions, fleeing unto the glorious church of the sufferers; for therein are come the angelic choirs, and the spirits of all the righteous, and the good Lady, bestowing healings with marvelous Babylas.

*Theotokion:*

Thou, O pure Mother of God, Virgin most holy, having conceived in thy womb ineffably, didst bear the Son Who shone forth without beginning from the Father; pray Him for thy servants, the only Lover of mankind, to save our race.

*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*

A cornerstone uncut by hands was cut out from thee, O Virgin, from an unhewn mountain, Christ, Who united the divided natures: therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos.

*Troparia:*

Even after death wast thou an eyewitness of the Lord, O God-seer; for not in dark riddles as in the rock of old, but in human flesh didst thou behold Christ shining with Divinity.[^57]

Mount Tabor was enriched with glory above Sinai, where Moses from the dead and the Tishbite from the lands of the living beheld Christ with the apostles, transfigured as true God.[^58]

Save me by thy merciful prayer and boldness of supplications, O God-seer Moses, as guide of Israel, and fullness of Christians, deliver from fierce and dire perils and every harm those who hymn thee.

*Theotokion:*

Depicting thee beforehand, O Virgin, as the golden jar, the tablet, and the divine table, Moses clearly showed that God was to be born of thee: Whom having beheld in the flesh, we faithfully finish thy song.[^59]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "The Heavens with Stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*

Both a priest and a victim of God didst thou appear, O Babylas, sacrificing unto Him without blood; and sacrificed by thine own blood with the mature infants, with them do we now praise thee.

*Theotokion:*

Those who do not venerate thine icon, O Virgin, and that of thy Son and God, with pure faith, cast down as godless, and deliver unto Gehenna.[^60]

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*

Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made wonderful all His desires in them.[^61] *Verse:* I beheld the Lord ever before me.[^62]

*Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 301 [Heb. 10:32–38].*

*Alleluia, Tone 4:* The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them.[^63]

*Gospel according to Luke, pericope 77 [Lk. 14:16–24].*

*Communion Hymn:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.[^64]

*On the Fifth Day of the Same Month:*

*Commemoration of the Holy Prophet Zacharias, Father of the Honorable John the Forerunner.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Hast Given a Sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

Having the anointing upon thee and the holy vestment, O ever-memorable Zacharias, thou didst serve God as an angel, mediating between the Creator and the creation, O blessed one, and clearly receiving the revelations of the Holy Spirit; therefore we call thee blessed, and today perform thy holy solemnity, glorifying the Savior.

Thou didst behold a Child being born of the Maiden, O divinely inspired Zacharias, co-unoriginate with the Father; and thou didst manifestly prophesy unto thine own child: Truly thou shalt be a prophet, preparing His ways.[^65] Together with him we call thee blessed, and sacredly celebrate thine honorable solemnity, O all-rich God-bearer.

Thou wast a living and animate temple of the Holy Spirit; and in the midst of the temple, O glorious one, serving God with a pure heart, thou wast unrighteously slain, finishing thy divine course as a martyr, O worthy of glory.[^66] Therefore hast thou entered into the heavenly temple by thine own blood, entreating cleansing for our souls.

*Glory, Tone 8. Idiomelon. By John the Monk:*

Clothed truly with the garment of legal priesthood, thou didst serve according to the order of Aaron, and standing in the temple thou didst clearly see the angelic form, O most blessed one.[^67] Therefore, all of us duly singing thy translation, O Zacharias, praise thee with hymns, who in old age didst bring forth glorious John: pray the merciful God that our souls may be saved.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O Most Marvelous Wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

"What is this visible sight that is seen by mine eyes, O Master? Thou Who upholdest all creation art lifted up upon the Wood, and diest, granting life unto all!" the Theotokos weeping said, when she beheld lifted up upon the Cross Him Who ineffably shone forth from her as God and man.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory, Tone 2. By Anatolius:*

As a pure priest thou didst enter into the Holy of Holies, and clad with the sacred vestment, thou didst serve God blamelessly. Even as Aaron giving laws, and as Moses leading the tribes of Israel, in the pure signification of the bells;[^68] therefore wast thou also slain: but thy righteous blood hath become for us a saving healing, and as fragrant myrrh it opens the hearing unto the path of eternal life. O thrice-blessed Zacharias, parent of John the Baptist and spouse of Elizabeth, earnestly pray for our souls!

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

When the spotless Ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb willingly dragged unto slaughter as a man, weeping she said: "Dost Thou now hasten, O Christ, to make me childless who gave birth to Thee? What is this that Thou hast done, O Deliverer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thine extreme goodness, which surpasses mind and word, O Lover of mankind!"

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Robed with the garment of priesthood, O all-wise one, according to the Law of God Thou didst offer acceptable whole-burnt offerings in sacred beauty, O Zacharias; and Thou wast a luminary and a beholder of mysteries, bearing clearly within thee the marks of grace, O all-wise one; and slain with the sword in the temple of God, O prophet of Christ, with the Forerunner pray that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos without the martyr troparia; and that of the saint* and that of the saint on 6. Composition of Theophanes, Tone 8.

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Having traversed the water as dry land, and having escaped the evil of Egypt, the Israelite cried out: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

*Troparia:*

To praise thy memory, O prophet, I pray for the grace of the Spirit to aid me by thy mediation, crying: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

Thy life was found blameless, adorned with the garment of priesthood and the light-bearing radiance of prophecy, O divinely speaking blessed one.

Having adorned thy head with the legal crown, O Zacharias, thou didst appear divinely manifested, crying: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

*Theotokion:*

Clad in the garment of the robe of the ephod like Aaron,[^69] thou didst receive the Maiden who budded from the root of Jesse, who bare the Deliverer in her womb.[^70]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Thou art the establishment of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee.

*Troparia:*

When thou didst offer the incense of ministry, O high priest, then didst thou receive the announcement of the Forerunner.[^71]

The chrism of consecration anointed thee to minister as priest like Aaron; therefore wast thou accounted worthy of the angelic vision.

Zacharias begat John as the morning herald, announcing Thee unto the universe, O Savior, the spiritual Sun.[^72]

*Theotokion:*

Direct my conduct and life, O all-immaculate Mother of God, who didst bring light unto the house of Zacharias.[^73]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That Which Was Commanded Mystically" (Повелѣ́нное):*

Having ministered as priest unto God according to the Law, and having prophesied Christ incarnate of the Holy Spirit from the Virgin, O Zacharias, thou didst appear unto the universe as a luminous pillar; and thou didst say that the Dayspring from on high of righteousness, enlightening the whole world and guiding our feet into the way of peace, saving our race.[^74] *(Twice)*

*Glory, now and ever, Theotokion, Tone 8:*

O thou who didst bear the Unchangeable God, establish my heart, which is ever altered by sin and sloth through the assaults of the deceiver, O good Lady, by thy maternal prayers; that I also may thankfully glorify thee, O Mother of God Mary: have mercy upon thy flock which thou hast acquired, O all-spotless one.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Preserved ever by the Cross of thy Son and God, O Virgin, we conquer the assaults and cunning of demons. Hymning thee truly and properly as the Theotokos, with love all generations call thee blessed, O pure one, even as thou didst foretell; therefore grant us remission of sins by thy prayers.[^75]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity.

*Troparia:*

Thy prophet, O Master, having faithfully served Thee with the figures of the Law, was also accounted worthy to behold Thy truth in grace.

With light didst thou receive light, being brighter than the darker law, O most blessed one; for unto the Law grace hath now been added unto thee.

The divine Gabriel, standing before God, clearly announced unto thee, O blessed one, the voice of the Word and the Forerunner.

*Theotokion:*

The Creator of creation, finding thee a pure dwelling, took up His abode in thee, O Virgin, Who loosed the barrenness of Elizabeth.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Dawning early we cry unto Thee, O Lord, save us: for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know none other.

*Troparia:*

A mitre was placed upon thy head, O prophet, bearing the inscription of true divine priesthood.[^76]

Creation rejoices in thy childbearing, O high priest; for thou didst bud forth the preacher of repentance.

Adorned with holiness was thy life, for thou didst fulfill all the commandments of the Lord together with Elizabeth.[^77]

*Theotokion:*

Thy tongue is directed unto song, O divinely speaking one; for thou didst behold the unwedded one carrying God in her womb.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Grant me a robe of light, Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O Most Merciful Christ our God!

*Troparia:*

Serving the shadow of the Law, and a preacher of grace, O our Savior: for he was accounted worthy to behold Thine Incarnation.

Adorned with the words of judgment, O sacred Zacharias, thou didst receive the oblation of the Word bearing flesh.[^78]

Thou didst appear inside the temple serving God, O divinely inspired mystic, having become a wondrously honorable priest.

*Theotokion:*

Carrying in thy womb the Savior, O Virgin Mother of God, the Word without beginning without beginning, thou wast made known unto Elizabeth the prophetess.[^79]

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*

Today the prophet and priest of the Most High, Zacharias, the parent of the Forerunner, hath set forth the table of his memory, nourishing the faithful, having mingled for all the drink of righteousness; therefore is he translated, as a divine mystic of God's grace.[^80]

*Ikos:*

Bound by the silence of the Law at the voice of the angel, the hierarch received an angel, the prophet and mystic of Christ's coming, with barren and chaste Elizabeth; and by his birth grace and redemption and our universal reconciliation were renewed. He proclaimed Him as the Lamb and Creator, and the renewer of nature, Who grants fruit from a barren womb, and as the Son Who appeared from the Virgin, as a divine mystic of God's grace.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Hebrew youths in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparia:*

When the voice of the one crying came forth from the barren one above nature, he loosed the bonds of thy tongue to cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages![^81]

The friend of the Bridegroom was born of the barren one, clearly announcing beforehand the childbearing of the Virgin unto those who cry with faith: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages![^82]

Thou wast wholly a divine instrument of the Spirit, O thrice-blessed Zacharias; and thine infant proclaimed Thee a prophet, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*

Beholding thee, O Maiden, as the fulfillment of the Law and the sum of all prophecy, Zacharias recognized thee, crying: Blessed, O all-pure one, is the fruit of thy womb!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Hymn the Lord Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and Who revealed in the bush by fire the mystery of the Ever-Virgin unto Moses, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

He appeared as a prophet of truth; for John the Forerunner, coming before, prepared the ways of Christ, O blessed hierarch: Whom we highly exalt unto all ages.

Thou didst call the Master blessed as Teacher, Who hath granted salvation unto us, the Lord of glory Who shone forth unto us from David in the flesh: Whom we highly exalt unto all ages.

Thou wast accounted worthy of great gifts, O divinely manifested one, having begotten the Forerunner, who was greater than all the prophets who hymns the Lord and highly exalts Him unto all ages.[^83]

*Theotokion:*

Both a hierarch and a proclaimer of God, Zacharias, bowed down crying "Rejoice!" unto the Virgin and Mother bearing the Lord of creation, whom we highly exalt unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Truly do we confess thee to be the Theotokos, saved through thee, O pure Virgin, with the bodiless choirs magnifying thee.

*Troparia:*

Thou wast filled with the divine inspiration of the Comforter, and didst begin to bless the Lord, O sacred mystic, divinely wise and divinely blessed one.[^84]

Beholding the fulfillment of the archangel's words, O divinely speaking and all-praised one, straightway thou didst stir thy tongue unto blessing.

With the crowns of suffering and priesthood and the enlightenment of prophecy wast thou adorned, O most blessed and divinely speaking Zacharias.

*Theotokion:*

Being the receptacle of Light, O Virgin, enlighten my soul darkened by passions, and deliver me from the outer darkness by thy prayers.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Unchangeable Light" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*

At first, at the voice of the angel, thou wast struck dumb in the inner sanctuary, because of the budding of the voice of the one crying that was to come forth from thee; and now thou art silent on his account, having been slaughtered before the entrance, O Zacharias.[^85]

*Theotokion:*

Shining forth as Light from Light, O Word, timelessly before the morning star, as Light from a mother under time, Thou hast come forth unchangeably, enlightening the ends of the world with radiant beams, as the Light of the world.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory, Tone 8:*

Offering sacrifices according to the Law, O Zacharias, thou didst bring thy holy soul into the Holy of Holies unto God Who was born, in holy translation, by a voluntary offering, in the porch of the sanctuary, being slaughtered like a lamb.[^86]

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O Lord, Though Thou Didst Stand before the Tribunal" (Гдⷭи а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*

O Lord, when the sun beheld Thee, the Sun of righteousness, suspended upon the Wood, it hid its rays, and the moon turned its light into darkness; and Thine all-spotless Mother, wounded in her maternal womb...

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4, and of the prophet, Ode 3 on 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 7: The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him.[^87] Verse: Hear, O God, my voice* my prayer, when I make supplication unto Thee.[^88]

*Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 314 [Heb. 6:13–20].*

*Alleluia, Tone 7:* Light is dawned for the righteous.[^89]

*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 96 [Matt. 23:29–39].*

*Communion Hymn:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^90]

*On the Sixth Day of the Same Month:*

*Commemoration of the Miracle Wrought at Colossae, Which Is Chonae, by the Archistrategos Michael.[^91] And of the Holy Martyr Eudoxius and Those Who Suffered with Him.[^92] And of Our Venerable Father Archippus.[^93]*

*At Vespers, after the customary Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "As One Valiant among Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

Appearing as the most radiant defender of the Thrice-Sun Divinity, O Archistrategos Michael, with the heavenly powers thou criest rejoicing: Holy art Thou, O Father; holy art Thou, O co-unoriginate Word; holy art Thou also, O Holy Spirit: one glory, one kingdom, and one nature, one Godhead and power!

Thine appearance is fiery, and thy beauty marvelous, O Michael, chief among the angels; for by immaterial nature thou traversest the ends of the earth, fulfilling the commandments of the Creator of all, recognized as mighty in thy strength; and having made thy temple a fountain of healings, honored by thy holy invocation.

Thou Who makest Thine angels spirits, as it is written, and Thy ministers a flame of fire,[^94] hast shown forth the Archistrategos Michael, O Lord, pre-eminent in the midst of Thine archangelic ranks, obeying Thy nod, O Word, and with fear proclaiming the Thrice-Holy hymn unto Thy glory.

*Glory, Tone 6. Idiomelon. By Byzantios:*

Rejoice with us, all ye angelic ranks! For your leader and our protector, the great Archistrategos, on this present day in his honorable church, appearing most gloriously, doth sanctify us. Therefore, duly singing praise, let us cry aloud unto him: Shelter us under the shelter of the wings of thine immaterial glory, O Michael, greatest archangel!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Rejoice with us, all ye choirs of virgins! For our protectress, mediatress, and protection, and great refuge, on this present day in her honorable and divine festival comforts those who sorrow. Therefore, duly praising her, let us cry aloud: Shelter us by thy divine protection, O all-pure Lady Theotokos!

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory, now and ever, Tone 8. Idiomelon. By John the Monk:*

As leader of the hosts and defender, and chief captain of the angels, O Archistrategos, deliver from every necessity and affliction, from sicknesses and dire sins, those who faithfully hymn and entreat thee, O glorious one; clearly as immaterial beholding the Immaterial One, and illumined with the unapproachable light of the Master's glory. For He out of love for mankind took flesh from the Virgin for our sake, desiring to save mankind.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Archistrategos of the heavenly hosts, we the unworthy ever entreat thee that by thy prayers thou mayest surround us with the shelter of the wings of thine immaterial glory, preserving us who earnestly fall down and cry: Deliver us from perils, as leader of the hosts of the powers on high![^95]

*The service of the Martyr Eudoxius is sung at Compline. Canon of the Martyr, Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Having traversed the water as dry land, and having escaped the evil of Egypt, the Israelite cried out: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

*Troparia:*

Desiring the glory of sufferers, come, all ye, let us praise the great one among sufferers, Eudoxius, with cymbals, keeping festival in the manner of David.[^96]

An impious command went forth into all the world, not to serve the living God, but idols; but thou, O martyr, didst serve thine invisible God.[^97]

*Glory:*

True to thy name, O glory of the pious, martyr Eudoxius, thou didst confess Christ as God without beginning in the midst of unrighteous judges who tormented thee.[^98]

*Theotokion:*

The ranks of angels and of men, O unwedded Mother, praise thee unceasingly; for thou didst bear their Creator as an Infant in thine arms.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments; for there is none holy beyond Thee, O Thou Who alone lovest mankind.

*Troparia:*

As a lamb to the slaughter, thou wast led, O martyr Eudoxius, neither disputing nor crying aloud, O all-blessed one, imitating the life of Christ thy Teacher; and for this cause thou hast received unending glory.[^99]

Unto the idol-worshipers, O sufferer, thou didst proclaim: My God lives unto the ages; but your gods are the works of men's hands; having fallen, they rise not again, being graven and lifeless.[^100]

*Glory:*

Thou didst cast down the wiles of the enemy, O sufferer, thy mind having been established upon the rock of the Church of Christ. Therefore thou didst also cry aloud: I leave behind corruptible life in exchange for life that is truly eternal.[^101]

*Theotokion:*

Co-ever-existing with the Father and sharing His throne, God the Word, desiring to renew the forefather, hypostatically assumed him from thee, O pure one, having found thee, His Mother, as a rampart for all.[^102]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have understood Thy works, and I have glorified Thy Divinity.

*Troparia:*

Thou didst refute the deceit of those who compelled thee to renounce endless life and to love worldly life.[^103]

Being wounded, thou didst rejoice for the sake of the Word Who was slaughtered in the flesh for our sake; and unto the tormentors thou didst cry: Unworthy are my sufferings![^104]

*Glory:*

The gods whom ye serve, having mouths, speak not, O Eudoxius, thou didst cry aloud: let them that make them become like unto them![^105]

*Theotokion:*

Grant us cleansing of our sins of ignorance, as Thou art sinless, and give peace unto Thy world, O God, by the prayers of her that bare Thee.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant Thy peace unto us, O Thou Who lovest mankind.

*Troparia:*

Thou art my strength, Eudoxius cried aloud: O Christ God, Who didst suffer in the flesh, establish me; for behold, I suffer, being tormented.

Thou art the treasure of petitions, O Christ God; despise me not, Thou didst cry aloud in thy torments, O patient-souled Eudoxius.[^106]

*Glory:*

I fear neither sword nor fire, Eudoxius cried unto the tormentor: for behold, I have God as a mighty strength, Whom I serve.[^107]

*Theotokion:*

Heal the infirmity of my passions, O pure one, having accounted me worthy of thy visitation; and grant me health by thy supplications.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and hear me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparia:*

Neither sword nor fire shall separate me from the love of Christ, and your threats I count as childish games, Eudoxius cried aloud with faith unto those who compelled him to sacrifice.[^108]

I fear that unquenchable, tormenting fire; and I desire that life which cannot be taken away, O tormentor, Eudoxius cried: behold my body, wound it; I serve not thine idols![^109]

*Glory:*

The gods whom thou worshippest are silver and gold; they have mouths and speak not, ears and hear not, feet and walk not; but my God is the Maker of all, thou didst cry aloud.[^110]

*Theotokion:*

May we be delivered from grievous transgressions by thy prayers, O pure Mother of God, and may we attain, O all-holy one, the divine radiance of the Son of God Who was ineffably incarnate of thee.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Having gathered another wealth, and having brought it unto the poor, thou didst disperse it and gavest thy bread unto the hungry; and for this cause, having acquired incorruptible life, thou didst shine forth by the confession of Christ. Therefore, having acted manly and suffered lawfully, thou didst receive from God the crown of thy labors, O passion-bearer Eudoxius. Entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love.[^111]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Children coming from Judea in Babylon of old trampled underfoot the flame of the furnace by their faith in the Trinity, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*

Emulating the endurance of the Children, O most wise Eudoxius, thou didst not bow thy knees unto the deceptive image; but thou didst cry aloud with fervent faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^112]

Having acquired the invincible aid of grace, O martyr Eudoxius, thou didst steadfastly overthrow the armies of the enemy. And victorious, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^113]

*Glory:*

Kindled with the love of divine longing, O martyr Eudoxius, thou didst loathe the attachment to the temporal age, receiving thy recompense, and thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^114]

*Theotokion:*

Desiring to renew him who fell through deceit, the all-good God is incarnate and born of the Virgin, and deifies humanity.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Sevenfold did the Chaldean tyrant madly kindle the furnace for the godly; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

Thou didst sail across the abyss of wounds, O glorious one, and didst reach the haven of life, O Eudoxius, having received the crown of endurance, and with the angels thou criest unceasingly: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme exalt Him unto all ages![^115]

Having passed through fire and water, O blessed one, Christ brought thee out into rest; wherein rejoicing with the angels, O wise martyr, thou singest unceasingly unto the Trinity the hymn: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme exalt Him unto all ages![^116]

*Glory:*

Thou didst destroy the noetic serpent by the aid of the heavenly King, O glorious one, and having received the victory crown of endurance, with the bodiless hosts thou criest unceasingly: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme exalt Him unto all ages![^117]

*Now and ever, Triadikon:*

The Thrice-radiant Godhead shining in a single beam from one three-hypostatic nature: the unoriginate Begetter, the Word consubstantial with the Father, and the co-reigning Spirit of one essence: ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Heaven was astonished thereat, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the ranks of angels and men magnify thee as the Mother of God.

The angelic hosts were terrified and the assemblies of men marveled, that having a corruptible and fleeting nature, O sufferer, thou didst show the bodiless demons to be overthrown and impotent; and in faith thou didst cry unto the Trinity: I serve Thee; O Thrice-radiant Light, Thou art my glory![^118]

Blessed art thou, O martyr, glorified unto generations of generations, O Eudoxius; for having in no wise spared thy flesh for Christ's sake, thou didst endure torments, and didst not bow down unto graven idols. Therefore the angelic ranks, having clothed thee with the garment of incorruption, crowned thee.[^119]

*Glory:*

By thy prayers unto God, O martyr Eudoxius, snatch from every assault of the enemy those who with faith celebrate the memory of thy sufferings, that they may not boast against us; for as a martyr thou art able, having received from the Most High the reward of thy sufferings.[^120]

*Theotokion:*

Thou hast appeared, O Virgin Mother of God, having beyond nature given birth in the flesh unto God the Word, Whom the Father, being good, poured forth from His heart before all ages; Whom we now understand to be higher even than bodies, though He clothed Himself in a body.[^121]

*Stichera of the Martyr, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Ranks" (Нбⷭныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

True to thy name, O martyr Eudoxius, through virtues thou didst receive the grace of the Savior, and with noble boldness didst exchange thy life for the good glory of suffering; and dancing with the angels in the heavens, thou art now worthily glorified.[^122]

Having been beheaded for the sake of the faith, thou didst crown thy head with an incorruptible wreath, O all-blessed Eudoxius; therefore cease not by thy prayers unto Christ to remember us who celebrate thy memory, O glorious martyr.[^123]

Having despised wealth and temporary life in a martyric manner, O Eudoxius, thou didst count it a divine boast to bear the reproach of Christ rather than worldly good glory; having drawn near to torments and afflictions even unto blood, O glorious one.[^124]

*Glory, now and ever, Theotokion:*

Held fast by the abyss of transgressions, fleeing unto the quiet haven of thy most pure supplication, O Mother of God, I cry unto thee: Save me, stretching forth thy sovereign right hand unto thy servant, O all-immaculate one.

*Stavrotheotokion, Podoben:*

Standing by the Cross of thy Son and God, and beholding His longsuffering, the pure Mother wept and said:

Woe is me, my sweetest Child! What are these things? Thou sufferest unjustly, O Word of God, that Thou mayest save mankind!

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos, without the martyrs; and the Canon of the Archangel on 6, whose acrostic is: "I sing of the first of the bodiless minds: Joseph." Tone 4.*[^125]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

I will open my mouth, and it will be filled with the Spirit, and I will pour forth a word unto the Queen and Mother, and I will appear radiantly keeping festival, and I will joyfully sing her wonders.

*Troparia:*

Being ever illuminated with divine brightness, enlighten my mind to hymn thee, O Archistrategos of the hosts on high, the confirmation of all who flee unto thee.[^126]

The pre-unoriginate Mind showed thee forth, O most glorious Archistrategos, as the chief captain of the supermundane order, and a light to those in darkness, and the divine ornament of His Church.[^127]

Anticipating the heavenly minds in spirit, O Michael, thou hast been given most pre-eminently unto those below as a rampart, and a confirmation, and a weapon that slays and consumes the enemies.[^128]

*Theotokion:*

O all-immaculate Virgin, who art the majesty of angels and the help of men: do thou help me who sail upon the sea, ever falling into the tempest of sin and being in peril.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in wealth do we boast, but in Thee, the Father's hypostatic Wisdom, O Christ; for there is none holy beyond Thee, O Thou Who lovest mankind.

*Troparia:*

By divine strength, O all-praised leader of angels, thou traversest the whole earth, snatching from dire evils us who call upon thy divine name.[^129]

As a divine herald, as an unashamed defender of the faithful, thou hast been a guide and instructor of the erring, O most God-beholding Archistrategos of God.[^130]

Thou wast a most pure mirror of the divine radiance, having radiantly received the manifestations of the honorable Spirit, O Michael, worthy of wonder, chief among angels.[^131]

*Theotokion:*

He Who by His will framed the immaterial minds, by His desire took up His abode in thy material womb, O all-immaculate one: the Ineffable One seen in the flesh.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Instructor of the heavenly ranks, and servant of the divine glory, having worthily become so by the command of thy Creator, thou art an intercessor for Christians, saving and visiting earthly things by thine immaterial glory. Therefore we all duly praise thee with blessings, today hymning thy divine solemnity, O Archistrategos Michael; entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy divine miracles with love.[^132]

*Glory, Another Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "The Choir of Angels" (Ли́къ а҆́ггелскїй):*

Having the divine Michael as archistrategos, the angelic choir brings unceasing praise with him unto the Holy Trinity; for out of nothing the Maker of all brought into being the armies of fiery ranks by His Word.[^133]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O hope of Christians, all-holy Virgin, Whom beyond mind and word thou didst bear as God: unceasingly entreat Him with the powers on high to grant remission of all our sins and amendment of life unto those who ever glorify thee with faith and love.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hanging dead upon the Wood, the spotless Ewe-lamb wept and spoke, crying out maternally: How shall I endure Thy descent beyond words, O my Son, and Thy voluntary passions, O all-good God?[^134]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine, came upon a light cloud, and with an incorruptible hand saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparia:*

Being the primal Mind, Thou didst by Thy will frame the divine minds, and didst make Michael chief among them, enlightened by all-blessed participation, and shining with His noetic powers.[^135]

With the Thrones, Dominions, Powers, Authorities, and holy Principalities, thou proclaimest the holy hymn unto the Trinity, O most glorious Michael, saving us who hymn thee.[^136]

We magnify the Creator and Lord of all, Who out of compassion gave us the radiant Archistrategos Michael as a most great protection, an insurmountable wall, and a shield.[^137]

*Theotokion:*

In spirit, O Virgin, the one who was divinely manifested through the Spirit spoke of old of the most glorious wonder of thy childbirth, seeing thee most clearly as the overshadowed mountain, from which the Holy God came forth, being incarnate.[^138]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

The ungodly shall not see Thy glory, O Christ; but waking early out of the night, we hymn Thee, O Only-begotten One, the radiance of the Father's glory and of the Godhead, O Thou Who lovest mankind.

*Troparia:*

Thou didst appear leading ancient Israel, by the command of Him Who is from Jacob, Who appeared unto men in the coarseness of the body, O Michael, bodiless Archistrategos of angels.[^139]

Being ever deified by immaterial radiances, through divine-principle participation, thou dost also grant unto us a light-giving illumination, O chief among angels, being marvelously wondered at.[^140]

Adorned with grace is thy divine temple; for having come into it, O Michael, chief among angels, thou didst show it forth as an abyss of cures and a destroyer of passions.[^141]

*Theotokion:*

God showed thee to be higher than the noetic angels, having taken up His abode in thy womb, O pure and all-immaculate one; Whom do thou ever entreat to have compassion upon those who hymn thee.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah prayed in the belly of the sea monster: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers!

*Troparia:*

The multitude of the faithful rejoices, praising thee with blessings, and glorifies the all-holy Word, Who by His goodness united earthly beings with angels, O Michael.[^142]

Thou didst save the armies of Israel, appearing and imparting divine commands, O Archistrategos; thou didst overthrow the enemies and didst completely destroy them.[^143]

When Joshua the son of Nun beheld thee, he fell down in worship, inquiring of thy honorable and holy name, O leader of angels, held by reverence and fear.[^144]

*Theotokion:*

Blessed are the people who call thee blessed, O blessed one who gavest birth unto the blessed God, Who out of mercy deified earthly beings by an ineffable union.

*Kontakion, Tone 2:*

Archistrategos of God, minister of the divine glory, leader of angels and guide of men: ask for what is profitable for us, and great mercy, as Archistrategos of the bodiless hosts.[^145]

*Ikos:*

Thou hast said in Thy scriptures, O Lover of mankind, that the multitude of angels in heaven rejoices over one sinner that repents, O Immortal One.[^146] Therefore we who are in iniquities, O sinless One, Who alone knowest the heart, ever dare to pray unto Thee as compassionate, to show mercy and send down compunction unto us, the unworthy, O Master, granting us forgiveness; for on behalf of us all there prays unto Thee the Archistrategos of the bodiless hosts.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

Thou Who in the fire didst save Thy Children of Abraham, and didst slay the Chaldeans whom justice righteously snared: O highly praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*

Having observed, Daniel beheld thee standing together, O blessed one, and enlightening him at the river Chobar: the vision which lightning-visaged Gabriel saw, revealing Michael the chief captain unto him.[^147]

With loud voice let us praise in faith the guides of the angels, the God-beholding and light-bearing Michael and Gabriel, our good comforters, protectors, and guardians.[^148]

Being fair, all-comely, and God-beholding, Thou wast a leader beyond mind of the immaterial spirits, O most radiant Michael; pray with them, therefore, for all of us.[^149]

*Theotokion:*

Truly seeing the co-ever-existing Word of the great Mind ineffably and dreadfully taking up His abode in thee, O Virgin, the Archangel Gabriel cried aloud: Rejoice, blessed throne of the Most High!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Almighty Deliverer of all, having descended, Thou didst bedew those who practiced piety in the midst of the flame, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works, bless and hymn the Lord!

*Troparia:*

Leader of the noetic bodiless ones, saving intercessor of men, divine servant of God, O Michael, thou hast been shown forth, unceasingly singing: All ye works, bless and hymn the Lord![^150]

Two all-radiant beacons, the Archangels Michael and Gabriel, illuminating creation with the radiances of the Thrice-radiant Godhead, ye drive away the gloom of dire evils.[^151]

As good helmsmen, O Archangels, save my soulish ship from the storm of sins, fallen and in peril, steering it unto the haven of the divine will.

*Theotokion:*

The divine archangel, having appeared as the adorner of the bride, cried unto thee: Rejoice, unwedded Bride of God, glory of angels, and salvation and protection of men!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Eve through the disease of disobedience introduced the curse; but thou, O Virgin Mother of God, through the bud of thy pregnancy didst blossom forth blessing unto the world: therefore we all magnify thee.

*Troparion:*

Behold, the majesty of thy divine temple, O Archangel, shining with thy radiant presence, sends forth lightnings of miracles, and by divine grace ever drives away the darkness of sicknesses.[^152]

*Troparia:*

Being a fair and comely pair, by the Master's command ye serve those on earth, O Archangels, snatching them from dire evils, and sending down saving enlightenment unto all through the Divine Spirit.[^153]

Today the bodiless, divine minds rejoice with us, seeing this great and radiant Archistrategos hymned by all; and with love they celebrate with us, magnifying the Giver of life.[^154]

O divine and radiant pair, archangels, all-honorable Michael and all-glorious Gabriel: standing before the honorable Trinity, deliver from guilt of transgressions and from torments those who praise you.[^155]

*Theotokion:*

We joyfully bring unto thee the voice of divine Gabriel, and cry aloud: Rejoice, O paradise, having in thy midst the tree of life, O most pure one, most glorious palace of the Word! Rejoice, O all-immaculate Virgin!

*Exapostilarion:*

As of old thou didst submerge the disorderly courses and roarings of the rivers, O Archistrategos of glory: so now, O archangel, destroy the pride of the nations and the rages of demons, that we may worthily honor thee in hymns as is due.[^156]

*Theotokion:*

The ranks of the bodiless ones honor thy childbirth, for thou alone didst fill earthly beings with joy. Therefore we, the faithful, glorify thee, the all-immaculate one, praising thee in songs; for thou didst dawn light upon those in darkness, like the day dawning at morning.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Ranks" (Нбⷭныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

Angels celebrating in the world, * unto God sitting on the throne of glory * let us cry aloud the hymn: * Holy art Thou, O heavenly Father; * holy art Thou, O co-ever-existing Word; * holy art Thou also, O all-holy Spirit! Twice.*[^157]

Excelling the heavenly ones in great boldness, and standing before the awesome throne in glory, * O eyewitness of ineffable things: * save us, O Archistrategos Michael, * who are in the distress of perils and afflictions, * by thy prayers, we pray.[^158]

Thou art truly first of the bodiless angels, * and a minister of that divine radiance, * an eyewitness and initiate: * save us, O Archistrategos Michael, * who yearly honor thee with piety * and faithfully hymn the Trinity.[^159]

*Glory, in the Same Tone. Idiomelon:*

The Archistrategos of the powers on high, Michael, the chief captain of the divine ranks, today has summoned us to solemn festival; he who walks ever with us and preserves all from every assault of the devil. Come therefore, ye lovers of festivals and lovers of Christ, taking the flowers of virtues, with pure thoughts and upright conscience let us honor the assembly of the archangels; for standing unceasingly before God and singing the Thrice-Holy hymn, he prays that our souls may be saved.[^160]

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "All-Praised Martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*

A sword has pierced my heart, O Son, * the Virgin said, * when she beheld Christ hanging upon the Wood: * my heart is torn asunder, O Master, * even as Simeon foretold unto me of old; * but arise, and glorify together with Thyself * Thy Mother and handmaid, O Immortal One, * I pray Thee.[^161]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory, of the Archangel, Tone 5:*

Wherever thy grace overshadows, O archangel, from thence the power of the devil is driven away; for the fallen morning star cannot endure to behold thy light. Therefore we pray thee: quench his fiery darts that are moved against us by thine intercession, delivering us from his scandals, O praiseworthy Archistrategos Michael![^162]

*Now and ever, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*

Beholding her own Lamb of old dragged unto the slaughter, the Ewe-lamb followed earnestly, crying these things unto Him: Whither goest Thou, my sweetest Child, O Christ?
