For what cause dost Thou run this swift course with longsuffering and unsluggishness, O most-desired, sinless, most merciful Lord Jesus? Give a word unto me, Thy handmaid, O my most beloved Son; despise not in silence her that strangely bare Thee, O all-compassionate One, O God all-merciful, Who grantest great mercy unto the world.[^163]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Archangel, Ode 3 and 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: He Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.[^164] Verse: Bless the Lord, O my soul... Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 305 [Heb. 2:2–10]. Alleluia, Tone 5: Praise the Lord, all ye His angels... Verse: For He spoke, and they came to be. Gospel according to Luke, pericope 51 [Luke 10:16–21]. Communion Hymn: He Who makes His angels spirits.*[^165]

*On the Seventh Day of the Same Month: Forefeast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Birthgiver of God; and of the Holy Martyr Sozon.*[^166]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Ranks" (Нбⷭныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

The noetic rays have shone forth for the universal joy of the world, * announcing beforehand unto all * the Sun of glory, Christ God, * at thy nativity, O all-immaculate one; * for thou wast shown forth to be the mediatress * of true gladness and grace.[^167]

This thy forefestal glory, O all-immaculate one, * announces beforehand unto all * thy benefactions unto mankind which surpass speech; * for thou art now unto us the cause of gladness * and of future joy, * O Ever-Virgin Birthgiver of God.[^168]

The Maiden who contains God * and the pure Birthgiver of God, * the glory of the prophets, the daughter of David, * today is born of Joachim * and of chaste Anna; * and the curse of Adam that was upon us * is destroyed by her nativity.[^169]

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Hast Given a Sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

Strengthening by His power * thy weakness, O blessed one, * He Who willingly bare our weakness: * for His sake thou didst complete the martyr's course with joy, * and didst crush the feeble enemy with most comely feet; * therefore Jesus, the Lover of mankind * and the Savior of our souls, * has woven for thee crowns of victory.[^170]

Thou didst wound the enemies, * though wounded thyself, O glorious one, * and didst cast them down unto the earth, * having armed thyself with the Cross; * and being encompassed with invincible armor * and confirmed by love for Him Who translated thee unto the noetic kingdoms * as an invincible martyr, * as a heavenly man.[^171]

Unto fire and poison, * manifestly emulating Him Who endured grievous sufferings for thy sake, * O passion-bearer Sozon, * thou didst grievously deliver thyself unto wounds and sores, * and unto unbearable torments; * therefore He honored thee with heavenly gifts, * and showed thee forth as a fountain of healings * unto those who love thee.[^172]

*Glory:*

*Glory, now and ever, of the Forefeast, Tone 4. Idiomelon:*

Thy most honorable nativity, O most holy and pure Virgin, the multitude of angels in heaven and the human race on earth call blessed; for thou wast the Mother of the Creator of all, Christ God. Beseeching Him for us, we pray, cease not: on behalf of us who have set our hope upon thee next to God, O all-hymned and unwedded Birthgiver of God.[^173]

*If it be Friday evening: Glory, of the Forefeast; Now and ever, the Theotokion-Dogmatikon of the current Tone.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O Marvelous Wonder" (Ѡ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

O marvelous wonder! * That from a mother who bare not, * and from barren old age, * a rod bearing a flower today sprouts forth: * His Mother and unwedded bride, * from the righteous Joachim and Anna. * Therefore the choir of prophets now rejoices, * and all the solemn assembly of the patriarchs, * at her nativity.[^174]

*Verse: Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.[^175]*

Today David rejoices, * and Jesse now leaps for joy, * and Levi is magnified; * and with him the righteous Joachim rejoices, * and Anna's childlessness is loosed by thy nativity, * O most pure Mary, greeted by God with joy; * and the assembly of angels with mankind, * we all call thy divine womb blessed.[^176]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy face.[^177]*

Rejoice, assembly of mankind! * Rejoice, temple of the Lord! * Rejoice, holy mountain! * Rejoice, divine table! * Rejoice, lampstand of the Light! * Rejoice, honorable glory of the Orthodox! * Rejoice, Mary, Mother of Christ God! * Rejoice, all-immaculate one! * Rejoice, offering of the Divine Bread! * Rejoice, tabernacle! * Rejoice, unburnt bush! * Rejoice, hope of all![^178]

*Glory, now and ever, Tone 4. By Germanus:*

A universal joy has shone forth unto us from the righteous ones, from Joachim and Anna: the all-hymned Virgin, who because of her surpassing purity becomes the ensouled temple of God, and is truly acknowledged as the only Birthgiver of God. By her supplications, O Christ God, send down peace upon the world, and great mercy unto our souls.[^179]

*Troparion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*

Thy martyr Sozon, O Lord, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the tormentors and crushed the feeble audacities of the demons. By his supplications, save our souls.[^180]

*Glory:*

*Glory, now and ever, of the Forefeast, in the Same Tone:*

From the root of Jesse and from the loins of David, the Maiden of God Mary is born unto us today; for all things rejoice with joy and are renewed. Rejoice together, heaven and earth; praise her, ye families of the nations! Joachim makes merry and Anna keeps festival, crying out: The barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life![^181]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Forefeast, twice; Glory, of the Martyr; Now and ever, of the Forefeast. After the first Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "The Stone Having Been Sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*

Having been born marvelously from a barren womb, from virginal loins thou didst give birth beyond nature; for having appeared as a comely stem, thou didst blossom forth Life unto the world. Therefore the heavenly powers cry aloud unto thee, O Birthgiver of God: Glory to thy coming, O pure one! Glory to thy nativity! Glory to thy virginity, O Mother unwedded![^182]

*Glory, now and ever, the same. After the second Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word Co-Beginningless" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*

All heavenly things now rejoice, and the human race now keeps festival with them, and the prophets mystically make merry together; for she whom they foresaw in types in ancient generations—the bush, and the jar, and the rod, the cloud, the gate, and the throne, and the great mountain—is born today.[^183]

*Glory, now and ever, the same. Canon of the Forefeast with the Heirmos on 8, whose acrostic is: "I sing the Nativity of the Maiden of God, the Virgin. Joseph." Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

I will open my mouth, and it will be filled with the Spirit, and I will pour forth a word unto the Queen Mother, and I will appear radiantly keeping festival, and I will joyfully sing her wonders.

*Troparia:*

Rejoicing today, with gladness let us sing the divine nativity of the Mother of God; for she bare joy unto the universe, destroying the sorrow of the first mother.[^184]

From a barren woman comes forth the barrenness of sin, she whom the Law prefigured, and the proclamations of the divine speakers of God pre-manifested: the most pure Sovereign Lady and all-immaculate one.[^185]

She became the temple and palace of the King, in which He made a dwelling for Himself: the Super-essential One makes the faithful a dwelling of the Holy Trinity.[^186]

The most comely bridal chamber, the highest throne of God, comes forth from a barren woman, upon which the Super-essential One sat in the flesh, for by His goodness He raises up unto the knowledge of the light those who sit in the darkness of destruction.[^187]

*Another Canon, of the Saint, on 4, in the Same Tone. By Theophanes. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Having traversed the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet, ancient Israel of old, by the cruciform hands of Moses, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.

*Troparia:*

Unto those who today honor thy venerable memory, grant that they may be saved, and protect them from all assaults, tribulations, and afflictions, now beseeching the Lord and Benefactor, O most glorious one.[^188]

Christ truly showed thee forth as an all-radiant star upon the height of the Church, O martyr, illuminating the whole universe with the splendors of thy sufferings, O all-praised one.[^189]

Having troubled the sea of impiety like the Lord's steed, O martyr, by the deluge of thine honorable and holy blood, thou didst drown all the power of the adversaries, even as Pharaoh was drowned.[^190]

*Theotokion:*

Seedlessly by the Father's will from the Divine Spirit, thou didst conceive the Son of God, and didst bear in the flesh Him Who is from the Father without a mother, and for our sake from thee without a father.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

As the barren church from among the nations bare, and the congregation that was manifold in children languished, unto our marvelous God let us cry aloud: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

A fruitful land is born from a barren land, which shall bring forth the Cultivator of good things and the life-bearing Ear of corn, Who nourishes all by His divine beck.[^191]

Today the rod of virginity sprouted, from which shall blossom the Flower, God our Husbandman, cutting down the evil shoots by His extreme goodness.[^192]

Behold, the uncut mountain, hewn from the barren rock, brings forth the Noetic Stone, Who shall work the crushing of all the graven images of the deceiver.[^193]

The foreshadowings of the Law foretold thee, O Maiden; for outside the things of the Law, thou carriest in thy womb the Lawgiver, Who preserves thee beyond words, incorrupt and spotless.[^194]

*Another. Heirmos:*

Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and confirmation!

*Troparia:*

The streams of thy blood, having flowed like a river for the sake of Christ, quenched the fire of the ungodly, O martyr and ever-hymned passion-bearer.[^195]

Patiently thou didst submit unto the infliction of wounds like an invincible pillar, O glorious one, casting down the fortress of delusion.[^196]

In the manner of David, like Goliath, thou didst cast down the noetic tormentor and his host with the sling of faith, O all-glorious one.[^197]

*Theotokion:*

Thou alone hast appeared unto those on earth as the mediatress of blessings that transcend nature, O Mother of God; therefore we cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice!

*Kontakion of the Holy Sozon, Tone 2, Podoben: "The Firm" (Тве́рдыѧ):*

Having come together today, let us loudly praise the true and divinely wise martyr, the tested contender of piety, Sozon, the initiate of grace and most rich giver of healings; for he prays unto Christ God for us all.[^198]

*Ikos:*

Come, all ye, let us now earnestly praise with hymns the great contender Sozon, who shone forth manifestly in the honorable and divine Church of Christ, having offered what is worthy; for he truly cast down the ferocity of the idolaters, and ever abides granting salvation unto the faithful. Therefore we earthborn, drawn by love, now call him blessed, honoring the venerable and glorious memory of the passion-bearer, crying out: O all-blessed Sozon, pray unto Christ God for us all![^199]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily Anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предва́ри):*

Having been saved by faith, O much-suffering Sozon, by the providence of Christ God thou wast a saving haven unto those who are tempest-tossed; for thou gushest forth rivers of healings unto those who honor thee, and ever soothest diseases and burning fevers. Therefore with faith we honor thy divine memory.[^200]

*Glory, now and ever, of the Forefeast, Tone 8, Podoben: "That Which Was Mystically Commanded" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*

Let heaven rejoice, and let the earth be glad! For the heaven of God is born on earth, this Bride of God from the promise; the barren woman nurses the infant Mary, and Joachim rejoices at her birth, saying: A rod is born unto me, from which Christ blossomed forth as a flower from the root of David: truly a most marvelous wonder![^201]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine, came upon a light cloud, and with an incorruptible hand saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparia:*

She who is higher than the angels is born on earth as a Maiden, being in holiness and purity without question; who gives birth unto Christ, the cleansing of all, our sanctification and all-perfect deliverance.[^202]

Blessed was Anna's womb, for it bare a womb that was to contain the blessed and uncontainable Word, which grants regeneration unto all the faithful.[^203]

Now the malicious darkness begins to be destroyed; for the ensouled cloud of the Sun has shone forth from a barren womb, the all-immaculate one, whose radiant nativity let us celebrate.[^204]

Like a fruitful olive tree that has sprouted from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, Anna causes thee to blossom forth, sprouting the good grace of the Word, before Whom mercy and truth ever go.[^205]

*Another. Heirmos:*

Beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Kindled with the love of God, O all-blessed one, thou didst burn up all the brushwood deception of the godless by thy words, and rejoicing didst cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^206]

Being thyself a temple of the Lord built together, thou didst hasten into the temple of the godless, and didst valiantly shatter their ministrations, O all-praised passion-bearing martyr.[^207]

Thy sacred temple was shown forth as a medicine for every disease unto those who flee unto it with faith and honor thy valiant deeds therein, O most praised passion-bearer Sozon.[^208]

*Theotokion:*

In unwedded state thou didst bear the Lord, O Virgin, and after childbirth thou wast shown forth still virgin; therefore with unceasing voices, with unhesitating faith we cry aloud unto thee, O Sovereign Lady: Rejoice!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

All things were amazed at thy divine glory; for thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, Who grants peace unto all who hymn thee.

*Troparia:*

The sealed book is born today, which it is impossible to read by the law of the nature of earthly beings, preserved to be a dwelling of the Word, even as the books of the divinely speaking prophets manifested by the Spirit.[^209]

The saving vine is born today, which shall blossom forth the incorruptible and divine cluster, pouring forth sweetness, from which everyone who mystically drinks produces divine and saving gladness.[^210]

Leap for joy, ye people, making merry with the angels; today, the Virgin having been born of a barren woman, sorrow has ceased, and joy is brought in for those who celebrate her divine nativity.[^211]

The divine prophet most clearly prefigured thee as a new scroll, wherein by the Father's finger the Word shall be written, O Virgin, inscribing in the book of life all who through His goodness submit unto His dominion.[^212]

*Another. Heirmos:*

Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith from dark ignorance.

*Troparia:*

Enlightened with the light of the Trinity, O martyr, thou didst destroy the polytheistic darkness of godlessness, having appeared as an ever-radiant luminary.[^213]

Thou wast shown forth as a fair-flowering rose by the outpouring of thy blood, O blessed one, and with the fragrance of miracles thou hast perfumed the world.[^214]

Being a noetic cluster of the vine of Christ, thou didst gush forth the sweetly-contrite wine of martyrdom unto those who glorify thee with faith.[^215]

*Theotokion:*

We put thee forward as an invincible weapon against the enemies; thee we have as the foundation and hope of our salvation, O Bride of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, O ye divinely wise: come, let us clap our hands, glorifying God Who was born of her.

*Troparia:*

Today is born the bridge that leads mankind across unto the light: the heavenly ladder, the most spacious mountain of God, the Virgin Birthgiver of God, whom we call blessed.[^216]

The scarlet cloth, Anna, produced the purple robe which afterwards dipped the fleece of the King's incarnation, whom we all worthily hymn in song.[^217]

The fountain has burst forth now from a little drop, O all-immaculate one, who having given birth unto the abyss of salvation, shall dry up the immeasurable floods of polytheism.[^218]

From a barren root thou didst sprout, and by thy divine springing forth beyond nature thou didst cut down the thorns from the root of malice, O Virgin parent of God, ever-blessed one.[^219]

*Another. Heirmos:*

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from the demonic blood by the blood that flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.

*Troparia:*

Desiring to be slaughtered for the sake of the love of God, as a spotless sacrifice thou didst offer thyself unto His table; therefore with piety we honor thee, O all-praised one.[^220]

Having dryshod traversed the deep of delusion, O martyr, thou didst reach the haven of the kingdom on high, enjoying eternal tranquility, O blessed one.[^221]

The tormentor scraped thy ribs mercilessly with iron claws, but with glory thou didst commit thy spirit into the hands of God, O all-blessed and ever-memorable one.[^222]

*Theotokion:*

O wonder of all wonders, newest of all! That a Virgin, having conceived without knowing man, unconstrainedly contained Him Who holds all things in His womb!

*Kontakion of the Forefeast, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*

Today the Virgin and Birthgiver of God Mary, the unending bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom, is born from a barren woman by the counsel of God; the chariot of the Word is adorned with beauty; for unto this she was foreordained, the divine gate and Mother of the true Life.[^223]

*Ikos:*

The fruit that was given from a barren woman, the Maiden of God Mary, whom the divine prophets of old foresaw by the Spirit: seeing her today playing in Anna's bosom, with faithful Joachim let us noetically hasten unto the feast, and summon those afar off, saying: The restoration of this world has come today; for from a barren womb has sprouted the divine gate and Mother of the true Life![^224]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The divinely wise served not creation rather than the Creator, but valiantly trampling upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*

Joachim and Anna are called blessed, who gave birth unto the Mother of God, blessed and pure unto me; who bare the blessed Word, God Who makes the faithful blessed.[^225]

An honorable gift did thy parents acquire in thee, O all-immaculate one, who didst conceive God, Who enriched with better gifts those who cry aloud: O Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^226]

Thy breasts are sweeter than wine, O divinely blessed Anna; for with sacred breasts thou didst nurse her who nursed the all-good Word, the Giver of milk and the Nourisher of every breathing creature.[^227]

Leap for joy, adorn thy voice, O divinely inspired David, and make merry:

for behold, the ark which of old thou didst announce beforehand has come forth from a barren womb, preserved for the King of creation and God.[^228]

*Another. Heirmos:*

In the Persian furnace the Children of Abraham, burning with the love of piety rather than with flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Cast into the furnace of painful torments, O martyr, having received the dew of endurance from God, thou didst gratefully cry aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^229]

Having a soul truly brighter than any gold, O martyr, thou wouldst by no means sacrifice unto a gold-beaten and soulless god; but thou didst sacrifice thyself as a most fragrant offering unto the Lord.[^230]

The Great Shepherd united thee, who wast a shepherd of sheep, O martyr, unto His spiritual flock like a spotless lamb, showing thee forth, O all-praised one, to be unassailable by noetic wolves.[^231]

*Theotokion:*

Rejoice, sanctified divine dwelling of the Most High; for through thee joy was given, O Birthgiver of God, unto those who cry aloud: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The birthgiving of the Mother of God saved the pious Children in the furnace: then indeed prefigured, but now in deed accomplished, it raises up the whole universe to sing unto Thee: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

Let us move our tongue in song, honoring the divine nativity, and unto the all-hymned and super-divine Word incarnate by the Spirit, let us cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^232]

Leap for joy, ye divine prophets, honoring the nativity of the Virgin; for she fulfilled the proclamations of you all, having given birth unto Christ, the King of all, Who was declared by you, Whom we exalt above all unto all ages.[^233]

Cry out gladness, ye mountains! Apostles and martyrs, dance for joy! Ye venerable and righteous ones, now rejoice today at the nativity of the Lord's Mother, crying aloud: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^234]

A fragrant apple blossomed, taking up the divine rose, and today perfumed the ends of the earth and put an end to the foul stench of our sin, O all-pure one and Mother of the Word, whom we exalt above all unto all ages.[^235]

The barren human nature was today gladdened with the venerable gifts of the Divine Spirit, having seen the Maiden of God born from a barren woman, and it cried aloud: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^236]

*Another. Heirmos:*

Daniel, having stretched forth his hands, shut the lions' mouths in the pit; and the Children, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*

Having broken off the hand of the gold-crafted idol, O wise one, thou didst give it unto the poor, procuring for thyself inexhaustible wealth, truly the wealth of martyrdom, O ever-memorable and glorious one, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^237]

Having wrestled in the flesh with the bodiless one, by the assistance of Christ thou didst cast him down; therefore He Himself bestowed upon thee honors, O glorious one, and the working of miracles; unto Whom rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^238]

Opening thy mouth, thou didst fill it with the Spirit, O all-praised Sozon; and the mouths of the enemies blaspheming the Creator thou didst fill with all shame, and rejoicing didst cry aloud unto Christ: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^239]

*Theotokion:*

Thou alone among all generations, O pure Virgin, wast shown forth as the Mother of God; thou wast the receptacle of the Godhead, O all-immaculate one, not having been burned by the fire of the unapproachable Light; therefore we all bless thee, O Mary, Bride of God.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy in spirit, being enlightened, and let the nature of the bodiless minds keep festival, honoring the sacred solemnity of the Mother of God, and let it cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Birthgiver of God, pure Ever-Virgin!

*Troparia:*

Behold, the holy place of God has been manifestly shown forth, named the most glorious city of the King; radiant paradise has brightly blossomed, being the mediatress of paradise and mankind's adoption unto God.[^240]

The candle and lampstand appeared today, shining with the golden radiance of the pre-eternal Light; taking up His abode in her, He shall enlighten those in the night of dire evils, and shall dispel the gloom of godlessness, and make all partakers of the Day truly through faith.[^241]

Today the earth dances for joy, for it has seen a new heaven, the all-comely heaven of God brought forth; taking up His abode wherein in the flesh, He higher shall He raise mankind, and deify all by His goodness; Whom, faithfully hymning, we magnify.[^242]

The most excellent pair, Joachim and Anna, brought forth an undefiled heifer, from whom the fatted Bullock, having come forth, was slain for the world, taking away the sins of men, and destroying the sacrifices offered unto demons.[^243]

Enlighten us who in spirit celebrate thy light-bearing nativity, O thou that didst bear the Light, Mother of God, and show us forth as partakers of the future Light, O all-pure one, and grant peace and deliverance from dire evils by thy maternal prayers.[^244]

*Another. Heirmos:*

A cornerstone was cut without hands from the unhewn mountain that art thou, O Virgin: Christ, Who joined together the natures that had stood apart; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Troparia:*

Thou wast shown forth as a chosen stone of Christ the Cornerstone, O martyr, cast upon the earth and tearing down the fortress of delusion, while making firm the hearts of the faithful.[^245]

Having acquired thee as a stream of life, Christ's Church is now bedewed with the blood of thy sufferings as with waters, O martyr, and is ever adorned with the majesty of miracles.[^246]

Thou didst find the reward of thy struggles and of thy labors, O God-wise one: the Heavenly Kingdom, wherein dancing for joy, O Sozon, remember those who with faith celebrate thy sacred memory, O all-glorious one.[^247]

*Theotokion:*

Loose now the bonds of my transgressions, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, who didst bear the Spring of compassion, O only God-blessed one, and fill me with joy, that I may worthily magnify thee.

*Exapostilarion of the Martyr, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены услышите):*

Having armed himself with the weapon of Thy precious Cross, Thy passion-bearer, O Word, firmly conquered the adverse powers and put the tormentors to shame, and suffered for Thee; and with Thee, O my Christ, King of all, he reigns continually.[^248]

*Glory, both now: Of the Forefeast:*

Be renewed, O Adam, and be magnified, O Eve! Ye prophets, dance for joy with the apostles and the righteous! For the common joy of angels and of men hath shone forth today from the righteous Joachim and Anna: the Birthgiver of God Mary.[^249]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (Доме евфрафов):*

Come, ye who are descended from Adam, let us hymn the Virgin, most pure Mary, who sprouted from David and brought forth Christ.

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*[^250]

Let us offer praise unto the Redeemer, the Lord, Who from a barren woman hath given unto us the Birthgiver of God and only Ever-Virgin.

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy face.*[^251]

Today the joy of the whole universe is most gloriously born from barren loins: the Mother of the King of all.

*Glory, both now, Tone 2. Idiomelon:*

She who was foreordained Queen of all, the dwelling-place of God, has today come forth from the barren womb of glorious Anna, the divine habitation of the Ever-existing Essence; through whom shameless Hades was trampled down, and Eve with all her race is brought into steadfast life. Unto her let us worthily cry aloud: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb![^252]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Forefeast: Ode 3, on 4; and of the Saint: Ode 6, on 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him.[^253] *Verse: Hear my voice, O God, when I pray unto Thee.*[^254] *Epistle to the Ephesians, Pericope 233 [Eph. 6:10-17].*[^255] *Alleluia, Tone 4:* The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them.[^256] *Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and the Lord will deliver them out of them all.*[^257] *Gospel according to John, Pericope 52 [John 15:17-16:2].*[^258] *Communion Hymn:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^259]

*It should be known if the Forefeast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Birthgiver of God and of the Martyr Sozon falls on a Sunday:*

On Saturday at Small Vespers, the Resurrectional stichera and those of the Birthgiver of God according to custom. Resurrectional troparion; Glory, both now: its Theotokion.

At Great Vespers: After the Kathisma, on "Lord, I have cried," Resurrectional stichera, 3; and of the Anatolian, 1; and of the Forefeast, 3; and of the Martyr, 3. Glory: of the Forefeast; both now: the first Theotokion of the current Tone. At the Litiya, the sticheron of the temple, then the aposticha stichera of the Forefeast from Vespers. Glory, both now: of the Forefeast, which is written at Matins on the aposticha. At the aposticha, Resurrectional stichera; Glory, both now: of the Forefeast. At the blessing of the loaves, the troparion "O Virgin Birthgiver of God," twice; and of the Forefeast, once. And a reading from the Apostolic Epistles.

At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Resurrectional troparion, twice; Glory: of the Martyr; both now: of the Forefeast. After the Kathismata, the Resurrectional sessional hymns and their Theotokia; and a reading from the Commentary Gospel, Sunday before the Exaltation.[^260] After this, the Evlogitaria (the Blameless), and the Hypakoe. And a reading of the Sunday in order. The Gradual (Hymns of Ascent), and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath praise the Lord," and the Sunday Resurrection Gospel, and "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Then the Resurrection Canon with the heirmos, on 4; and of the Birthgiver of God, on 2; and of the Forefeast, on 4; and of the Martyr, on 4. Katavasia: "Tracing the Cross with his rod..." After Ode 3, the Kontakion of the Forefeast, and its Ikos, and of the Martyr. Glory: Sessional hymn of the Martyr; both now: of the Forefeast. After Ode 6, the Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable than the Cherubim." Resurrectional Exapostilarion; Glory: of the Martyr; both now: of the Forefeast. At the Praises, Resurrectional stichera, 4; and of the Anatolian, 1; and of the Forefeast, 3, which are the aposticha stichera of that day, with their refrains. Glory: the Gospel sticheron; both now: "Most blessed art thou." The Great Doxology. Resurrectional troparion only. Litanies, and dismissal, and catechesis. And the customary procession into the narthex; and the First Hour. At the First Hour, the Resurrectional troparion; Glory: of the Forefeast; both now: the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Forefeast, and the final dismissal. At the Third Hour, the Resurrectional troparion; Glory: of the Martyr; both now: the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," the Resurrectional Kontakion. Likewise also at the other Hours we say the Resurrectional troparion first, and those of the Forefeast and of the Martyr alternating. But the Kontakia, the Resurrectional and that of the Forefeast, we say alternating.

At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Octoechos, on 6, including the Triadikon; and of the Forefeast, Ode 3, on 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrectional troparion and that of the Forefeast; then of the holy temple, and of the Martyr. The Resurrectional Kontakion, and of the holy temple; Glory: of the Martyr; both now: of the Forefeast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel: first of the Sunday before the Exaltation, and of the order, or under one pericope; then of the Saint. The Prokeimenon of the Tone is omitted. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens." And of the Martyr: "In everlasting memory shall the righteous be."

*On the Eighth Day of the Same Month: The Nativity of our Most Holy Lady the Birthgiver of God and Ever-Virgin Mary.*[^261]

*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, on 4, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небесных чинов):*

Joachim and Anna keep festival, having brought forth the beginning of our salvation, the only Birthgiver of God; with whom we also celebrate today, blessing the pure Virgin from that root of Jesse.[^262]

Today the flower of Anna, the God-given garden, the Birthgiver of God hath blossomed forth, the salvation of mankind; from whom the Creator of all, being born beyond comprehension, as the Good One cleanses all Adam's defilement by His goodness.[^263]

Who can worthily hymn the Virgin nursing as an infant from Anna ineffably? Ye mountains and hills, drop down sweetness today! For the Life and Purification of all is nourished with milk, the pure Birthgiver of God.[^264]

The land which was formerly barren brings forth fruitful soil; and having given holy fruit from a barren womb, she is nourished with milk: a fearful wonder! The Nourisher of our life, who received the Heavenly Bread in her womb, is nourished with milk from the breasts.[^265]

*Glory, both now, Tone 4:*

Thy most honorable nativity, O most holy pure Virgin, the multitude of angels in heaven and the human race on earth bless; for thou wast the Mother of Christ God, the Creator of all; Whom cease not to implore for us, we pray thee, who after God have placed our hope in thee, O all-hymned and unwedded Birthgiver of God.[^266]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (Доме евфрафов):*

Rejoice, Joachim, and rejoice, Anna; for the mediatress of joy and salvation, the work of a barren woman, is born unto us.[^267]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*[^268]

Thou alone of earthborn mortals hast been shown forth as salvation, having borne the Word beyond word and nature; therefore we call thee blessed.

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy face.*[^269]

Put away all sorrow, O Adam and Eve! For the Mother of Joy most gloriously blossoms forth today from a barren woman.

*Glory, both now, the same Podoben:*

The temple of God, the only Birthgiver of God, comes forth from a barren and unbearing woman; and Adam rejoices, crying aloud.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Thy nativity, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, hath proclaimed joy unto the whole universe; for from thee hath shone forth the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God; and having loosed the curse, He gave blessing, and having abolished death, He granted us life eternal.[^270]

*At Great Vespers, we chant the Kathisma "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon. On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, on 8, Tone 6. Idiomela. By Patriarch Sergius:*

Today God, Who rests upon noetic thrones, hath prepared for Himself a holy throne upon the earth; He Who established the heavens by wisdom hath formed an ensouled heaven through His love for mankind; for from a barren root He hath made to bud forth for us His Mother as a life-bearing garden: the God of wonders and the Hope of the hopeless; O Lord, glory be to Thee![^271]

This is the day of the Lord: rejoice, ye people! For behold, the bridal chamber of the Light and the book of the Word of Life hath come forth from the womb; and the door that looks toward the east, being born, awaits the entrance of the Great High Priest, alone bringing the One and Only, Christ, into the universe for the salvation of our souls.[^272]

Even if bright barren women have blossomed forth by the divine will, yet Mary hath shone forth above all who were born in God-befitting manner; for having been born most gloriously from a barren mother, she bore in the flesh the God of all, beyond nature from a seedless womb: the only portal of the Only-begotten Son of God, through which having passed He preserved it shut; and having wisely ordered all things as He Himself knows, He wrought salvation for all men. *Twice.*[^273]

*By Stephen the Hagiopolite:*

Today the barren gates are opened, and the divine virginal portal proceeds forth. Today grace begins to bring forth fruit, manifesting unto the world the Mother of God, through whom earthly things are united with the heavenly, for the salvation of our souls.[^274]

Today is the proclamation of worldwide joy; today the breezes have blown, heralds of salvation: the barrenness of our nature is loosed; for the barren woman is shown to be mother of her who remains virgin even after the birth of the Creator; from whom He Who is God by nature takes what is foreign to Himself, and for the straying works salvation in the flesh: Christ the Lover of mankind and the Redeemer of our souls.[^275]

Today the barren Anna brings forth the Maiden of God, chosen out of all generations to be the habitation of Christ God, the King and Creator of all, in fulfillment of the divine dispensation, through which we earthborn mortals were refashioned and renewed, from corruption unto unending life.[^276]

*Glory, both now: The first sticheron: "Today God, Who rests upon noetic thrones..." Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*

*Reading from Genesis [Gen. 28:10-17]:*[^277]

Jacob went forth from the Well of the Oath, and went toward Haran. And he found a place, and slept there, for the sun had set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put it at his head, and slept in that place. And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, whose top reached unto heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending upon it. And the Lord leaned upon it, and said: "I am the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac; fear not: the land whereon thou sleepest, unto thee will I give it, and unto thy seed. And thy seed shall be as the sand of the earth, and it shall spread abroad unto the sea, and to the southwest, and to the north, and to the east; and in thee shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed, and in thy seed. And behold, I am with thee, keeping thee in every way whithersoever thou goest; and I will bring thee back into this land, for I will not leave thee until I have done all that I have spoken unto thee." And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and said: "Truly the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not." And he was afraid, and said: "How fearful is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven!"

*Reading from the Prophecy of Ezekiel [Ezek. 43:27; 44:1-4]:*[^278]

Thus says the Lord: "It shall come to pass from the eighth day and forward, that the priests shall offer your burnt offerings upon the altar, and your peace offerings; and I will accept you," says Adonai the Lord. And He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary which looks toward the east; and it was shut. And the Lord said unto me: "This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it; because the Lord God of Israel shall enter in by it, and it shall be shut. For the Prince, he shall sit in it to eat bread; he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and shall go forth by the way thereof." And He brought me by the way of the holy gate that is toward the north, in front of the house; and I looked, and behold, the house of the Lord was full of glory.

*Reading from Proverbs [Prov. 9:1-11]:*[^279]

Wisdom hath built for herself a house, and set up seven pillars. She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine in her bowl, and hath prepared her table. She hath sent forth her servants, calling with a loud proclamation unto the bowl, saying: "Whosoever is simple, let him turn aside unto me." And unto them that want understanding she said: "Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled for you. Forsake folly, and ye shall live; and seek wisdom, that ye may have life, and direct understanding in knowledge." He that instructs the wicked shall get to himself dishonor; and he that reproves an ungodly man shall defame himself. For reproofs unto the ungodly are wounds unto him. Reprove not the wicked, lest they hate thee; reprove a wise man, and he will love thee. Give occasion unto a wise man, and he will be yet wiser; instruct a just man, and he will increase in learning. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the counsel of saints is understanding. For to know the law is the character of a good mind. For in this way thou shalt live a long time, and years of thy life shall be added unto thee.

*At the Litiya, Stichera, Tone 1. Idiomela. By Stephen the Hagiopolite:*

The beginning of our salvation hath come to pass today, O ye people! For behold, she who was foreordained from ancient generations to be Mother and Virgin, the receptive dwelling-place of God, comes forth to be born from a barren woman: the flower from Jesse, and the rod from his root hath blossomed forth. Let Adam the forefather leap for joy, and let Eve be glad with joy! For behold, she who was fashioned from the rib of Adam openly calls her daughter blessed: "For unto me," she says, "salvation is born, for whose sake I shall be set free from the bonds of Hades." Let David dance, striking his harp, and let him bless God: for behold, the Virgin comes forth from a barren womb for the salvation of our souls.[^280]

*Tone 2:*

Come, all ye lovers of virginity and devotees of purity! Come, receive with love the praise of maidenhood, the fountain of life flowing from a hard rock, and the bush of immaterial Fire springing from an unfertile woman, which cleanses and enlightens our souls.[^281]

*By Patriarch Anatolius:*

What is this sound of those keeping festival? Joachim and Anna mystically hold celebration: "Rejoice with us today, O Adam and Eve," saying: "for she through whom of old paradise was shut by transgression, the blessed Fruit, the Maiden of God Mary, hath been given unto us, opening its entrance unto all!"[^282]

She who was foreordained Queen of all, the dwelling-place of God, hath today come forth from the barren womb of glorious Anna, the divine habitation of the Ever-existing Essence; through whom shameless Hades was trampled down, and Eve with all her race is brought into steadfast life. Unto her let us worthily cry aloud: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb![^283]

*Glory, both now, Tone 8. By Patriarch Sergius:*

On the notable day of our feast, let us blow the trumpet with the spiritual pipe! For she who is of the seed of David, the Mother of Life, is born today, loosing the darkness: the renewal of Adam, and the recalling of Eve, the fountain of incorruption, and the release from corruption; through whom we have been deified and delivered from death. And let us, the faithful, cry aloud unto her with Gabriel: Rejoice, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee, for thy sake granting us great mercy![^284]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4. Idiomela. By Patriarch Germanus:*

Worldwide joy hath shone forth unto us from the righteous ones, from Joachim and Anna: the all-hymned Virgin, who by reason of her surpassing purity becomes the ensouled temple of God, and is truly acknowledged as the only Birthgiver of God. By her prayers, O Christ God, send down peace upon the world, and upon our souls great mercy.[^285]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*

By the angelic foretelling, a most pure Fruit hath today come forth from the righteous Joachim and Anna, O Virgin: heaven and throne of God, and receptacle of purity, proclaiming joy unto the whole world: mediatress of our life, removal of the curse, bestowal of blessing. Therefore, in thy nativity, O God-called Virgin, entreat peace for the world, and for our souls great mercy.[^286]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy face.*[^287]

Let the barren and childless Anna today clap her hands brightly! Let earthly beings shine in light, let kings dance, let hierarchs be glad in blessings, let the whole world keep festival! For behold, the Queen and undefiled Bride of the Father hath blossomed from the root of Jesse! No longer shall women bear children in sorrow; for joy hath blossomed forth, and life dwells in the world for all men. And no longer are the offerings of Joachim turned away; for the weeping of Anna hath been turned into joy: "Rejoice with me," she says, "all chosen Israel! For behold, the Lord hath given unto me the ensouled palace of His divine glory, for the common gladness and joy, and the salvation of our souls!"[^288]

*Glory, both now, Tone 8. By Patriarch Sergius:*

Come, all ye faithful, let us run unto the Virgin! For behold, she is born who before conception was foreknown as the Mother of our God: the vessel of virginity, Aaron's rod that budded from the root of Jesse, the preaching of the prophets, and the offspring of the righteous Joachim and Anna. She is born, and the world is renewed with her; she is born, and the Church is adorned in her majesty: the holy temple, the receptacle of the Godhead, the virginal vessel, the royal bridal chamber, wherein the most glorious mystery of the ineffable union of the natures that came together in Christ was accomplished! Worshipping Him, we hymn the all-immaculate Virgin's nativity.[^289]

*At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion: "Thy nativity, O Virgin Birthgiver of God..." thrice. It is written at Small Vespers. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast, thrice.*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Удивися Иосиф):*

Cry aloud, O David: What did God swear unto thee? "What He swore unto me," he says, "He hath already fulfilled, having given of the fruit of my loins the Virgin Maiden, from whom the Creator Christ, the New Adam, was born King upon my throne; and He reigns today, possessing a kingdom that cannot be moved: the barren woman bears the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life.[^290]

*Glory, both now, the same.*

*And a reading of the feast.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Удивися Иосиф):*

From the root of Jesse and from the loins of David, the Maiden of God Mary is born today unto us; for all things rejoice with joy and are renewed. Rejoice together, heaven and earth! Praise her, ye families of the nations! Joachim is glad, and Anna keeps festival, crying aloud: "The barren woman bears the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life!"[^291]

*Glory, both now, the same.*

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повеленное тайно):*

Let heaven rejoice, and let the earth be glad! For the heaven of God hath been born upon the earth, this Bride of God, according to promise. The barren woman suckles the infant Mary, and Joachim rejoices at her birth: "A rod," he said, "hath been born unto me, from which the Flower Christ hath blossomed, from the root of David: truly a most glorious wonder!"[^292]

*Glory, both now, the same Tone:*

Be renewed, O Adam! Rejoice, O Eve! Be glad, O David! Be of good cheer, O Anna! For the Mother of thy Creator is born most gloriously. All the earth dances for joy, having been renewed, and rejoices, clothed in a vesture. Let every tongue, dancing for joy, cry aloud unto Mary: Blessed is the house of David, for it nourishes the nourisher of our life![^293]

*And we read the Homily of Gregory the Hieromonk.*[^294]

*Hymns of Ascent, the first antiphon of the Fourth Tone. Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.[^295] *Verse: My heart hath poured forth a good word.*[^296] *Let every breath praise the Lord.* *Verse: Praise God in His saints.*[^297] *Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 4 [Luke 1:39-49, 56]: "In those days, Mary arose..."*[^298] *After Psalm 50: Glory:* Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Merciful One, cleanse the multitude of our transgressions. *Both now, the same. Then:* Have mercy upon me, O God. *And the Sticheron of the feast, Tone 6:* This is the day of the Lord: rejoice, ye people! For behold, the bridal chamber of the Light and the book of the Word of Life hath come forth from the womb; and the door that looks toward the east, being born, awaits the entrance of the Great High Priest, alone bringing the One and Only, Christ, into the universe for the salvation of our souls.[^299]

*Two canons: the heirmoi of both canons twice, and the troparia onto twelve.*[^300]
*The first canon, the creation of Lord John. Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified.[^301]

*Troparion:*
Come, ye faithful, rejoicing in the Divine Spirit! Let us honor with hymns the Ever-Virgin Maiden who hath come forth today from the barren woman for the salvation of mankind.[^302]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, O pure one, Mother and handmaid of Christ God, who art the mediatress of the primal blessedness! All the human race worthily glorifies thee with hymns.[^303]

*Troparion:*
Today the bridge of life is born, whereby men, having found the recall from the fall of Hades, glorify Christ the Giver of life with hymns.[^304]

*Another Canon, of Lord Andrew, Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who crushed wars with His arm, and led Israel through the Red Sea, let us sing, as unto our Deliverer and God, for He hath been glorified.[^305]

*Troparion:*
Let all creation dance for joy! Let David also be glad, for from his tribe and from his seed hath come forth a rod bearing the flower, the Lord, the Creator of all.[^306]

*Troparion:*
The Holy of Holies, the infant is placed in the holy sanctuary to be nourished by an angel's hand: let us all then faithfully keep feast at her nativity.[^307]

*Troparion:*
Anna was a barren woman who bare not, yet not childless unto God; for behold, the pure Virgin Mother was fore-named from generations: therefore she sprouted forth the Fashioner of nature in the form of a servant.[^308]

*Troparion:*
Thee, the guileless ewe-lamb, who from thy womb hast brought the Lamb Christ as an infant into our essence: all of us honor thee with hymns who wast born of Anna.[^309]

*Triadicon:*
Three unoriginate Ones I glorify, three Holy Ones I sing, three co-eternal Ones in one essence I proclaim: for one God is glorified in Father and Son and Spirit.[^310]

*Theotokion:*
Who hath seen a child nourished with milk whom a father sowed not? Or where was a virgin mother seen? Truly both are beyond understanding, O pure Birthgiver of God.[^311]

*Katavasia:*
Moses, having traced the Cross directly with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel going on foot; and the same, striking across, brought it together again over Pharaoh's chariots, having inscribed the invincible weapon. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He hath been glorified.[^312]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst slay sin, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing praise unto Thee.[^313]

*Troparion:*
Having lived blamelessly unto God, O God-wise parents, ye gave birth unto the salvation of all, having brought forth the mother of the Creator and our God.[^314]

*Troparion:*
The Lord Who pours forth life unto all brought forth from a barren woman the Virgin, in whom He was pleased to dwell, preserving her incorrupt after childbearing.[^315]

*Troparion:*
Today let us sing praise unto Mary, the fruit of Anna, who bare the life-bearing cluster of grapes, as the Birthgiver of God, the mediatress of all and our helper.[^316]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God, my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies: I have rejoiced in Thy salvation.[^317]

*Troparion:*
Having been nourished in the Holy of Holies, O most pure Virgin Birthgiver of God, thou hast shown thyself higher than creation, having brought forth the Creator in the flesh.[^318]

*Troparion:*
Blessed is thy womb, O chaste Anna, for thou hast sprouted forth the fruit of virginity: her who without seed bare the Nourisher of creation and the Deliverer, Jesus.[^319]

*Troparion:*
All creation blesses thee, O Ever-Virgin, who today art born of Anna: the most pure rod from the root of Jesse that budded forth the flower, Christ.[^320]

*Troparion:*
Showing thee higher than all creation, O pure Birthgiver of God, thy Son magnifies thy nativity from Anna, and makes all glad today.[^321]

*Triadicon:*
Unto Thee we bow down, O Father unoriginate in essence; we sing praise unto Thy timeless Son, and we honor Thy co-eternal Spirit, as one God in three Persons by nature.[^322]

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the Giver of light and Author of human life, O pure Birthgiver of God, thou hast been revealed as the treasury of our life and the portal of unapproachable Light.[^323]

*Katavasia:*
The rod is taken as an image of the mystery, for by budding forth it chooses the priest; and for the Church that was previously barren, the wood of the Cross hath now blossomed forth, for power and establishment.[^324]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ Їѡ́сифъ):*
The Virgin Mary and truly Birthgiver of God, as a cloud of light, hath today shone forth unto us, and from the righteous ones comes forth unto our glory. No longer is Adam condemned, and Eve hath been set free from bonds; and therefore we cry aloud, shouting with boldness unto the only pure one: Thy nativity proclaims joy unto the whole universe![^325]

*Glory, both now, the same.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I have glorified Thee, O only Lover of mankind.[^326]

*Troparion:*
We hymn Thee, O Lord, Who hast given unto all as a saving harbor for the faithful her who bare Thee.[^327]

*Troparion:*
Christ hath shown thee, O Bride of God, as the praise and dominion of all who faithfully sing praise unto thy mystery.[^328]

*Troparion:*
O Sovereign Lady who knewest not wedlock, being delivered from transgressions by thy prayers, we all prudently call thee blessed.[^329]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
The Prophet Habakkuk with noetic eyes foresaw Thy coming, O Lord; therefore he also cried aloud: God shall come from Teman. Glory to Thy power, glory to Thy condescension![^330]

*Troparion:*
The Patriarch Jacob, having clearly foreseen, O Savior, the majesty of Thy dispensation, cried aloud in the Spirit, speaking mystically unto Judah: "From the sprout thou art gone up, my son," proclaiming Thee as God from the Virgin.[^331]

*Troparion:*
Now the rod of Aaron that budded from the root of David, now the pure Virgin comes forth; and heaven and earth dance together, and all the families of the nations, and Anna and Joachim mystically keep festival.[^332]

*Troparion:*
Now let heaven be glad, let the earth also rejoice, and let Joachim and David dance for joy: the one indeed as thy parent who truly bare God, and the other as thy forefather, proclaiming thy majesty, O pure one.[^333]

*Troparion:*
The universe rejoices with thee today, O God-wise Anna, for thou hast blossomed forth the Mother of its Deliverer: her who sprouted from the root of David, bearing for us the rod of power, the flower, Christ.[^334]

*Triadicon:*
I glorify God unoriginate, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the uncreated consubstantial Trinity, before Whom the Seraphim stand with reverence, crying: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God![^335]

*Theotokion:*
The Pre-unoriginate Principle receives a beginning from thee, O Birthgiver of God, in bodily time; and the Word of the Father remains co-unoriginate, and the Word of the Father remains co-unoriginate, and having become incarnate, and co-eternal with the Spirit, preserving the divine dignity.[^336]

*Katavasia:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I have considered Thy works, and I have glorified Thy Godhead.[^337]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Having dispersed the shadowy gloom of enigmas, and having illumined the hearts of the faithful by the coming of the truth through the Maiden of God: do Thou also guide us by Thy light, O Christ.[^338]

*Troparion:*
Let us, ye people, hymn the Cause of all, the Cause of Him Who was to be according to us; at whose prefiguration the prophets rejoiced, being counted worthy, bringing forth manifest salvation from her.[^339]

*Troparion:*
The budding of Aaron's dry rod showed forth unto Israel the pre-election; and now the radiant blossoming of those who sprouted forth shines forth most gloriously, the all-glorious birth from the barren woman.[^340]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
O Lord our God, grant us peace; O Lord our God, possess us; O Lord, beside Thee we know no other, we call upon Thy name.[^341]

*Troparion:*
Most pure is thy nativity, O spotless Virgin, ineffable; and conception unspeakable, and thy childbearing, O unwedded Bride: for He was God, wholly clothed in me.[^342]

*Troparion:*
Today let the angelic ranks be glad, with songs let those born of Adam dance for joy: for the rod hath been born that sprouted the flower, Christ, our only Deliverer.[^343]

*Troparion:*
Today Eve is loosed from condemnation, and barrenness also is loosed, and Adam from the ancient curse at thy nativity: for through thee have we been delivered from corruption.[^344]

*Troparion:*
Glory to Thee Who hast today glorified the barren woman: for from promise she bare the ever-blossoming rod, from which budded forth Christ, the flower of our life.[^345]

*Triadicon:*
Glory to Thee, O Holy Father, the Unbegottenness; glory to Thee, O timeless Son, the Only-begotten; glory to Thee, O Divine and Co-enthroned Spirit, Who proceedest from the Father and abidest in the Son.[^346]

*Theotokion:*
Thy womb became the bearer of the Sun; thy purity remained as before, unharmed, O Virgin: for Christ the Sun, as a Bridegroom from a bridal chamber, appeared from thee.[^347]

*Katavasia:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon was crucified Christ the King and Lord, whereby he who deceived by the tree fell, being himself deceived by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh Who grants peace unto our souls.[^348]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
From the whale Jonah cried aloud unto the Lord: Lead me up from the depths of Hades, I pray, that as unto my Deliverer, with the voice of praise and in the spirit of truth, I may sacrifice unto Thee.[^349]

*Troparion:*
In the affliction of barrenness, the God-wise parents of the Mother of God cried aloud unto the Lord; and they bare her unto generations of generations, for the common salvation and praise.[^350]

*Troparion:*
The God-wise parents of the Mother of God received a worthy heavenly gift from God: a carriage higher than the Cherubim themselves, the birthgiver of the Word and Creator.[^351]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
As the waters of the sea, O Lover of mankind, I am tossed by the billows of life. Therefore, as Jonah, so do I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Compassionate Lord![^352]

*Troparion:*
Since thou art the Holy of Holies, O pure one, thy chaste parents dedicated thee in the temple of the Lord to be honorably nourished and to be prepared as His Mother.[^353]

*Troparion:*
Ye barren women and mothers, dance for joy! Take courage, and leap, ye childless ones! For a childless, barren woman sprouts forth the Birthgiver of God, who shall deliver Eve from travail and Adam from the curse.[^354]

*Troparion:*
I hear David singing unto thee: "Virgins shall be brought after thee, they shall be brought into the temple of the King"; and with him I also hymn thee as the King's daughter.[^355]

*Troparion:*
We hymn thy holy nativity, we honor also thine immaculate conception, O Bride called of God and Virgin; and with us the ranks of angels and the souls of the saints glorify it.[^356]

*Triadicon:*
In thee the Trinitarian mystery is hymned and glorified, O pure one: for the Father was well pleased, and the Word took up His abode in thee, and the Divine Spirit overshadowed thee.[^357]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the golden censer, for the Fire took up His abode in thy womb, the Word from the Holy Spirit, and in human form was seen in thee, O pure Birthgiver of God.[^358]

*Katavasia:*
In the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah, having spread forth his hands in the form of a Cross, clearly prefigured the saving Passion; therefore coming forth after three days, he portrayed the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God Who was nailed in the flesh and by His three-day Resurrection hath enlightened the world.[^359]

*Kontakion, Tone 4:*
Joachim and Anna were loosed from the reproach of childlessness, and Adam and Eve from the corruption of death, were loosed, O most pure one, in thy holy nativity. This do thy people also celebrate, being delivered from the guilt of transgressions when they cry unto thee: The barren woman bears the Birthgiver of God, and the nourisher of our life![^360]

*Ikos:*
The prayer together with the sighing of Joachim and Anna over their barrenness and childlessness was acceptable, and entered into the ears of the Lord, and sprouted forth a life-bearing Fruit for the world. For the one offered prayer upon the mountain, and the other bare reproach in the garden; yet with joy: The barren woman bears the Birthgiver of God, and the nourisher of our life![^361]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The bush that was unburnt by fire on the mountain, and the dew-bearing furnace of the Chaldeans, clearly prefigured thee, O Bride of God: for thou didst receive the Divine immaterial Fire unburnt in a material womb. Therefore unto Him Who was born of thee we sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^362]

*Troparion:*
The lawgiver was restrained from understanding Thy presence in material manifestations, and the great mystery, O all-immaculate one, being instructed of old figuratively not to think on earthly-zealous things; therefore marveling at the wonder, he said: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^363]

*Troparion:*
As a mountain and a heavenly gate and a spiritual ladder did the divine choir call thee in a manner befitting God: for from thee a Stone was cut without hands of man, and a door through which the Lord passed, the God of our fathers, the God of wonders.[^364]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
The Chaldean furnace, kindled with fire, was bedewed by the Spirit at the presence of God; the children sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^365]

*Troparion:*
We celebrate, O pure one, and faithfully bow down before thy holy nativity, singing praise unto thy Son, whereby we have now been delivered from the ancient condemnation of Adam.[^366]

*Troparion:*
Now Anna rejoices, and cries aloud boasting: "Being barren, I have borne the Mother of God, for whose sake the condemnation of Eve was loosed, and the pain that was in sorrows!"[^367]

*Troparion:*
Adam hath been set free, and Eve dances for joy, and they cry aloud in the Spirit unto thee, O Birthgiver of God: Through thee have we been delivered from the primal curse, when Christ appeared![^368]

*Troparion:*
O womb that contained the dwelling-place of God! O belly that bare her who is more spacious than the heavens! The holy throne, the spiritual ark of sanctification![^369]

*Triadicon:*
Let us glorify the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, in the unity of the Godhead, the most holy Trinity, undivided, uncreated, co-eternal, and consubstantial.[^370]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone hast most gloriously given birth unto God, O Virgin; thou hast renewed nature by thy childbearing, O Mary; thou hast loosed Eve from the primal curse, O pure Birthgiver of God.[^371]

*Katavasia:*
The senseless decree of the wicked tyrant, breathing forth threats and God-hated blasphemy, shook the people; yet the three youths were not dismayed by the beast-like rage nor the consuming fire: but as the dew-bearing wind blew against it, being in the midst of the fire they sang: O supremely praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^372]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
In the furnace of the youths Thou didst of old prefigure Thy Mother, O Lord; and this image delivered them from the fire as they entered unburnt; whom we hymn, who hath appeared today unto the ends of the earth through Thee, and we supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^373]

*Troparion:*
The tabernacle foreordained for our reconciliation unto God now begins to exist, being about to give birth unto the Word Who appeared unto us in the grossness of flesh; Whom we hymn, having received existence through Him out of nothing, and we supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^374]

*Troparion:*
The transformation of barrenness hath loosed the world's barrenness of good things, and hath clearly shown forth the miracle of Christ Who came unto earthly beings; Whom we hymn, having received existence through Him out of nothing, and we supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^375]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Covering His chambers with waters, setting the sand as a boundary for the sea, and sustaining all things: the sun hymns Thee, the moon glorifies Thee, all creation offers a hymn unto Thee, as the Creator of all unto the ages.[^376]

*Troparion:*
O Thou Who didst marvelous wonders for the barren womb, Who didst open the non-bearing womb of Anna and gave her fruit: Thou art Holy God, Thou art the Son of the Virgin, Thou didst take flesh from her, the ever-blossoming Virgin and Birthgiver of God.[^377]

*Troparion:*
Shutting the deep and opening it, lifting up water in the clouds, and giving rain: Thou, O Lord, didst grant from the barren root of holy Anna a most pure fruit to bud forth and give birth unto the Birthgiver of God.[^378]

*Troparion:*
O Cultivator of our thoughts and Planter of our souls, Thou Who didst show the barren earth to be fruitful: of old Thou didst make holy Anna, who was dry, to be a fertile, rich furrow bearing good sheaves, to sprout forth the most pure Fruit, the Birthgiver of God.[^379]

*Troparion:*
Come, let us all behold the city of God now being born as from a small chamber: having an exit from the door of the womb, yet knowing no entrance of intercourse: God alone, the Creator, passed by this strange path.[^380]

*Triadicon:*
O transcendent Trinity, co-unoriginate Unity, the host of angels hymns Thee and trembles; heaven and earth and the abysses are dismayed; men bless Thee, fire serves Thee, all things in creation obey Thee with fear, O Holy Trinity.[^381]

*Theotokion:*
O newest tidings! God, the Son of a woman! O seedless childbearing! A husbandless Mother, and that which is born is God! O fearful sight! O strange conception of the Virgin! O ineffable birth! Truly all things are beyond understanding and sight![^382]

*Katavasia:*
Bless, ye youths, equal in number unto the Trinity, the Creator, God the Father; hymn the Word Who descended and transformed the fire into dew; and supremely exalt the All-Holy Spirit, Who grants life unto all, unto the ages.[^383]

*At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable than the Cherubim," but before the heirmos and troparia we sing this refrain:*[^384]
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the most glorious nativity of the Mother of God.[^385]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Her who before the sun ineffably conceived God, the Luminary Who shone forth and came bodily unto us from virginal sides: O blessed and all-immaculate one, thee, O Birthgiver of God, do we magnify.[^386]

*Troparion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the most glorious nativity of the Mother of God.
He Who for the disobedient people poured forth water from a rock, grants unto the obedient nations from barren loins a Fruit for our gladness, thee, O all-immaculate Mother of God, whom we worthily magnify.[^387]

*Troparion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the most glorious nativity of the Mother of God.
The remover of the ancient sudden condemnation and restoration of our foremother, who art the cause of our race's reconciliation unto God, the bridge unto the Creator: thee, O Birthgiver of God, do we magnify.[^388]

*Another Refrain:*
Magnify, O my soul, her who was born from a barren woman, the Virgin Mary.[^389]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Virginity is alien to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Birthgiver of God, both were accomplished. Therefore all the tribes of the earth unceasingly magnify thee.[^390]

*Troparion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, her who was born from a barren woman, the Virgin Mary.
Thou hast inherited a birth worthy of thy purity, O Mother of God, through promise: for of old thou wast given as a God-budded fruit unto a barren woman: therefore all the tribes of the earth unceasingly magnify thee.[^391]

*Troparion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, her who was born from a barren woman, the Virgin Mary.
The prophecy of the crying one hath been fulfilled; for he says: "I will raise up the fallen tabernacle of holy David," which was prefigured in thee, O pure one, for whose sake the dust of all men hath been fashioned into a body of God.[^392]

*Troparion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, her who was born from a barren woman, the Virgin Mary.
We bow down before thy swaddling clothes, O Birthgiver of God; we glorify Him Who gave fruit unto her that was previously barren, and Who most gloriously opened the womb of her that bare not: for being sovereign God, He does all things whatsoever He wills.[^393]

*Troparion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, her who was born from a barren woman, the Virgin Mary.
As a gift of song we faithfully offer unto thee, O Birthgiver of God, born of Anna: unto mothers, a Mother; and virgins, an only Virgin: praising, we bow down before thee, we sing and glorify thee.[^394]

*Triadicon:*
It is alien unto the lawless to glorify the unoriginate Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the uncreated sovereign Dominion, whereby the whole world is upheld by the nod of Its might.[^395]

*Theotokion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, her who was born from a barren woman, the Virgin Mary.
Thou didst contain in thy womb, O Virgin Mother, Christ the King, One of the Trinity, Whom all creation hymns, and before Whom the ranks on high tremble: entreat Him, O all-pure one, that our souls may be saved.[^396]

*Katavasia and festal refrains:*
Thou art a mystical paradise, O Birthgiver of God, who untilled didst sprout forth Christ, by Whom the life-bearing tree of the Cross was planted upon earth: therefore at its elevation now, worshipping Him, we magnify thee.[^397]

*And the other:*
The death that came upon our race through the eating of the tree is abolished today by the Cross; for the primal ancestral curse is destroyed by the blossoming of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly hosts magnify.[^398]

*Exapostilarion:*
Today from the barren Anna hath come forth the flower, the Birthgiver of God, filling all the ends of the world with divine fragrance, and filling all creation with joy; whom singing we worthily praise, as being higher than the earthborn.[^399]

*Glory, both now:*
Adam, be renewed! And Eve, be magnified! Ye prophets, dance for joy with the apostles and the righteous: for common joy hath shone forth unto angels and men from the righteous Joachim and Anna today: the Birthgiver of God Mary.[^400]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ ди́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
O marvelous wonder! The fountain of life is born of a barren woman, and grace begins to bear fruit radiantly! Be glad, O Joachim, having become the parent of the Birthgiver of God! There is none other among earthborn parents like unto thee, O God-pleasing one: for the Maiden who contained God, the dwelling-place of God, the all-holy mountain, was granted unto us through thee.[^401]

*Troparion:*
O marvelous wonder! Fruit hath shone forth from the barren woman by the nod of the Creator of all and Almighty Ruler! Nobly hath it loosed the barrenness of good things in the world: ye mothers, dance for joy with the Mother of the Birthgiver of God, crying: Rejoice, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee, Who through thee grants great mercy unto the world![^402]

*Troparion:*
The blessed Anna, having appeared, bare an ensouled pillar of chastity and a radiant receptacle glistening with grace: in truth the rampart of virginity, the divine blossoming, which is granted unto all virgins and those desiring virginity: clearly granting the beauty of virginity, and bestowing great mercy upon all the faithful.[^403]

*Glory, both now, Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
This is the day of the Lord: rejoice, ye people! For behold, the bridal chamber of the Light and the book of the Word of Life hath come forth from the womb; and the door that looks toward the east, being born, awaits the entrance of the Great High Priest, alone bringing the One and Only, Christ, into the universe for the salvation of our souls.[^404]

*The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the feast, first litanies, and Dismissal.*[^405]
*And the brethren are signed with the holy oil by the priest; and we sing the idiomelon sticheron of the feast, whichever the ecclesiarch desires.*[^406]

*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes from the canon: of the Second Tone, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Eighth Tone, Ode 6, on 4.*[^407]
*After the Entrance, Troparion of the feast; Glory, both now, Kontakion.*[^408]
*Prokeimenon, Song of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 3:* My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Savior.[^409]
*Verse: Because He hath regarded the low estate of His handmaid; for behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.*[^410]
*Epistle to the Philippians, Pericope 240 [Phil. 2:5-11].*[^411]
*Alleluia, Tone 8:* Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.[^412]
*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance.*[^413]
*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 54 [Luke 10:38-42; 11:27-28].*[^414]
*Instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos: "Virginity is alien to mothers..." and until the Apodosis, with the refrain of the feast.*[^415]
*Communion Verse:* I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord [LXX Ps. 115:4].[^416]
*And there is consolation for the brethren at the refectory, sufficient and spiritual.*[^417]

*It should be known if the Nativity of the Most Holy Birthgiver of God occurs on a Sunday:*[^418]
*On Saturday evening at Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," resurrectional stichera of the Tone, on 4; Glory, both now, of the feast.*[^419]
*At the Aposticha, one resurrectional sticheron; and the aposticha of the feast from Great Vespers, with the refrains of the feast. Glory, both now, of the feast. Resurrectional Troparion; Glory, both now, of the feast. Little Litany, and Dismissal.*[^420]
*At Great Vespers: After the customary Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," resurrectional stichera 3, and one Anatolian, and of the feast 6. Glory, both now, of the feast. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. And three readings of the feast. At the Litiya, stichera; and Glory, both now, of the feast. At the Aposticha, resurrectional stichera; Glory, both now, of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast, thrice. And a reading in the Epistles, or of the feast.*[^421]
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," resurrectional Troparion twice; Glory, both now, of the feast. After the customary Kathismata, resurrectional sessional hymns with their Theotokia. And a reading in the Commentary Gospel for the Sunday before the Exaltation. Then the Polyeleos, and the troparia "The Angelic Council." And the Hypakoe of the Tone. And both sessional hymns of the feast, once each: Glory, the sessional hymn that follows the Polyeleos; and both now, the other one. And the reading of the feast. The Songs of Ascents of the Tone. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the feast. Then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," Psalm 50, and the kissing of the Gospel according to custom. Thereafter, Glory: "Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God;" Both now, the same. Sticheron of the feast. Resurrectional canon with the heirmos on 4, and of the Birthgiver of God on 2, and both canons of the feast on 8. Katavasia: "Moses, having traced the Cross." After Ode 3, resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, and sessional hymn of the feast twice. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, we do not sing the refrains, but we sing "More honorable." Resurrectional Exapostilarion; Glory, both now, of the feast. At the Praises, resurrectional stichera 4, and of the feast 4, with the refrains of the feast; Glory, of the feast; Both now: "Most blessed art thou;" and the Great Doxology. Trisagion. And the resurrectional Troparion only. Litanies, and Dismissal. Oil is also given from the lamp of the feast. Then Glory, both now, the Gospel Sticheron; and the Catechesis; and the customary procession; and the First Hour in the narthex. At the First Hour, resurrectional Troparion; Glory, of the feast; Both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," resurrectional Kontakion, and Dismissal. Likewise at the other Hours, resurrectional Troparion; Glory, of the feast; and both now, Theotokion of the Hours. Kontakion of the feast, and the resurrectional, we say alternating.*[^422]
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes resurrectional of the Tone, on 6; and of the feast, Ode 3, on 4. After the Entrance, resurrectional Troparion, and of the feast; Glory, resurrectional Kontakion; and both now, of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel, we read first of the Sunday before the Exaltation, then the regular sequence; thereafter, of the Birthgiver of God. But the Prokeimenon of the Tone is omitted. Communion Verse: "Praise the Lord from the heavens;" and of the feast: "I will take the cup of salvation."*[^423]
*If the Afterfeast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Birthgiver of God occurs on a Sunday:*[^424]
*On Saturday at Small Vespers, resurrectional stichera, and of the Birthgiver of God, according to custom.*[^425]
*At Great Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried," resurrectional stichera 3, and one Anatolian; and of the feast for that day in order, 3; and of the saint from the Menaion, 3. Glory, of the feast, or of the saint; and both now, the first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day; and the litanies. At the Litiya, stichera of the feast, the evening aposticha of that day; Glory, both now, of the feast. At the Aposticha, resurrectional stichera; Glory, of the saint; but if not, Glory, both now, of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion: "Birthgiver of God and Virgin, rejoice," twice; and of the feast, once. And a reading in the Apostolic Epistles.*[^426]
*At Matins: Resurrectional Troparion, twice; Glory, of the saint; but if not, Glory, both now, of the feast. After both Kathismata, resurrectional sessional hymns, with their Theotokia. And a reading in the Commentary Gospel for the Sunday before the Exaltation. Then the Evlogitaria, and the troparia "The Angelic Council;" and the Hypakoe of the Tone; and a reading in the Commentary Gospel for the regular Sunday. The Songs of Ascents, and Prokeimenon of the Tone. Resurrection Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," and Psalm 50, and the rest as on a Sunday. Resurrectional canon with the heirmos on 4, and of the Birthgiver of God on 2, and of the feast on 4, and of the saint on 4. Katavasia: "Moses, having traced the Cross." After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the feast; and of the saint, if he have one, and the sessional hymn: Glory, both now, of the feast. After Ode 6, resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos.
