At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable." Resurrectional Exapostilarion; Glory, of the saint; but if not, Glory, both now, of the feast. At the Praises, resurrectional stichera 4, and of the feast 4: the aposticha of that day, with its doxasticon, with the refrains of the feast: Glory, the Gospel Sticheron; Both now: "Most blessed art thou." After the Great Doxology, the resurrectional Troparion only; and litanies, and Dismissal; and Catechesis; and procession into the narthex, and the First Hour. At the First Hour, resurrectional Troparion; Glory, of the feast; and both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," Kontakion of the feast, and the final Dismissal. At the Third Hour, resurrectional Troparion; Glory, of the saint; but if not, Glory, of the feast. After the Trisagion, Kontakion of the feast, and the resurrectional, we say alternating.*[^427]
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and of the feast from the canon, the regular Ode, on 4. After the Entrance, resurrectional Troparion, and of the feast; and of the temple of the saint [male], or of the saint [female]; and of the saint of the day, if there is one. Then resurrectional Kontakion, and of the temple of the saint [male], or of the saint [female]; Glory, of the saint of the day, if there is one; but if not, Glory, of the temple of the saint; and both now, of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel, first of the Sunday before the Exaltation; then the regular pericope combined together; and of the saint. Communion Verse: "Praise the Lord from the heavens;" and of the saint, if there is one; but if not, of the feast.*[^428]
*Saturday before the Exaltation:*[^429] *(Note: See)*
*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 3:* Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises unto our King, sing praises [LXX Ps. 46:6].[^430] *Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations [LXX Ps. 46:1].*[^431] *Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 126 [1 Cor. 2:6-9]: "Brethren, we speak wisdom..."*[^432] *Alleluia, Tone 5:* Thy mercies, O Lord, I will sing unto ages, unto generation and generation [LXX Ps. 88:1].[^433] *Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 34 [Matt. 10:37-11:1]: "The Lord said: He that loves father or mother..."*[^434] *The Epistle and Gospel of the regular Saturday are read combined under one pericope; then of the saint, if he have any. Communion Verse of the day.*[^435]
*It should be known: If the Apodosis of the Nativity of the Birthgiver of God occurs on the Saturday before the Exaltation: Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Verse of the feast. Epistle and Gospel, first of the Saturday before the Exaltation, then of the feast; but the Prokeimenon of the Saturday before the Exaltation is omitted.*[^436]
*Sunday before the Exaltation:*[^437]
*At Matins, we read in the commentary the Gospel of John, and of the day.*[^438]
*At the Liturgy: Prokeimenon, Tone 6:* Save, O Lord, Thy people [and bless Thine inheritance.] *Verse: Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry [LXX Ps. 27:1].[^439] Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 215 [Gal. 6:11-18]: "Brethren, see with how large letters..."[^440] Alleluia, Tone 1:* I have exalted one chosen out of My people [LXX Ps. 88:20].[^441] *Gospel according to John, Pericope 9 [John 3:13-17]: "The Lord said: No man hath ascended up to heaven..."[^442] Then the regular sequence. Communion Verse of the day.*[^443]
*On the Ninth Day of the Same Month:*[^444]
*The Holy and Righteous Ancestors of God, Joachim and Anna; and the Holy Martyr Severian:*[^445]
*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the feast, 3, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинẃвъ):*[^446]
Joachim and Anna keep festival, having given birth to the first-fruits of our salvation, the only Birthgiver of God: with them we also keep feast today, blessing the pure Virgin from that root of Jesse.[^447]

The Maiden who contained God, the pure Birthgiver of God, the glory of the prophets, the daughter of David: today is born of Joachim and chaste Anna; and the curse of Adam which was upon us is abolished by her nativity.[^448]

She that was previously a barren land brings forth a fruitful earth; and having given a holy fruit from a barren womb, she nourishes it with milk: a fearful wonder, the nourisher of our life, who having received the heavenly God in her womb, is nourished with milk from the breasts.[^449]

*Other Stichera of the Saints, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^450]
Come now, let us dance with songs, O feast-lovers, and faithfully celebrate, honoring the memory of Joachim and Anna, the honorable pair: for they bare unto us the Mother of God, the pure Virgin; therefore, having also departed from temporal things unto the incorruptible and ever-living dwellings, they pray that we may be saved.[^451]

All creation is brightly adorned today, chanting unto the Birthgiver of God, bringing with one mind the yearly memorial of thy parents: of marvelous Joachim, and together celebrating with Anna,[^452] for they mediated joy, having sprouted forth beyond hope her that flashed forth light, and the nourisher of our life.[^453]

Today Anna rejoices, leaping in spirit, and is glad, rejoicing, having obtained the desire of goodly children which she desired of old: for the divine fruit of promise and blessing sprouted forth, the all-blameless Mother who bare our God, and made the Sun to shine upon those sleeping in darkness.[^454]

*Glory, both now, Tone 5. Of Ephraim of Caria:*[^455]
O blessed pair, ye have surpassed all parents, in that ye have sprouted forth her that is superior to all creation! Truly blessed art thou, O Joachim, having become the parent of such a Maiden! Blessed is thy womb, O Anna, for thou hast sprouted forth the Mother of our Life! Blessed are the breasts with which thou didst suckle her that nourished with milk Him Who nourishes all breath! Whom we beseech you, O all-blessed ones, to pray that our souls may be mercied.[^456]

*Note: If it occur on Friday evening: Glory, of the feast; Both now, the first Theotokion of the current Tone.*[^457]
*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^458]
The God-wise Anna in truth, having previously seen a bird's nest in a tree, remembering her childlessness, cried: Woe is me, O Lord, Lord! I alone, a sinner, have been deprived of fruitfulness by Thee. Then God the Lover of mankind gave her as a fruit the Virgin, more honorable than all creation.[^459]
*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [LXX Ps. 44:11].*[^460]
The God-wise Anna in truth, childless grief and barrenness did know at first; therefore praying, she cried unto God: Loose my grievous and barren bond; and grant her to bear the holy offspring that is to bear Thee, the Word, which Thou, O Master Christ, Giver of life, bestowest upon her: for she shall bear Thee, the Savior of all men.[^461]
*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [LXX Ps. 44:13].*[^462]
In truth the Master and God, having heard thy prayer, as Sarah's of old: when she heard the angel's voice proclaiming joy unto thee: Thou shalt bear the Mother of God; and thou didst cry out in gladness of soul: The Master and Lord, my God and Creator, in truth hath removed reproach from me who have given birth unto the Ever-Virgin![^463]
*Glory, both now, Tone 8:*
Ye who from barren loins have sprouted forth the holy rod, the Birthgiver of God, from whom salvation shone forth unto the world,[^464] Christ God: the holy pair and holy union, Joachim and Anna, having departed unto the heavenly mansions, with their daughter, the most pure Virgin, dance with the angels, making supplication for the world. With them we also, having assembled piously, singing say: Ye who through the Maiden of God and most pure Mary were named the Ancestors of Christ, pray for our souls![^465]

*Troparion of the Saints, Tone 2:*
Celebrating the memory of Thy righteous ones, O Lord, through them we beseech Thee: save our souls.[^466]

*Or this, Tone 4:*
Having been righteous under the grace of the Law, Joachim and Anna bare unto us a God-given Child. Therefore today the divine Church brightly triumphs, joyfully celebrating your honorable memory, glorifying God Who hath raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David.[^467]

*Glory, both now, of the feast:*
Thy Nativity, O Virgin Birthgiver of God... *Written on the feast.*[^468]

*The service of the martyr is sung at Compline.*[^469]
*Canon, Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the water as dry land, and having escaped the malice of Egypt, the Israelite cried: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God![^470]

*Troparion:*
The impious command prevailed, to sacrifice unto idols soulless and deaf; but Christ conquered by the martyr's steadfast and noble resistances.[^471]

*Troparion:*
He loosed from bonds those that denied Christ, and whomsoever He found honoring Him as God He began to torment in every way; but when He encountered thee, O God-wise one, He was put to shame.[^472]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst astonish the impious tormentor, having rushed valiantly unto the judgment seat; and with boldness thou didst expose the weakness, rot, and feebleness of the false gods.[^473]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone, O Maiden, didst contain in thy womb in God-befitting manner Him Whom the heavens cannot contain, Who dwelt within thee and received human nature from thee.[^474]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou art the establishment of them that run unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the Light of the darkened, and my spirit sings praise unto Thee.[^475]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst rejoice being beaten for Christ, O wise one; for Thou didst have the assured recompense for sufferings.[^476]

Being cut with sinews, through the frequent changing of the torturers, O glorious one: even this thou didst not feel, as though in another's body.[^477]

Thou hast found recompense from Christ, O wise one, having received the crown of victory, and unending joy.[^478]

*Theotokion:*
My neighboring one is all good and unblemished: beholding thee of old, Solomon cried in the Songs.[^479]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have understood Thy works, and I have glorified Thy Divinity.[^480]

*Troparion:*
Flattering to soften thy strength, O martyr, and hoping to conquer thee, the tormentor thought to shoot at the sky.[^481]

*Troparion:*
Thou dost not perceive, O senseless one, Christ's power that strengthens me against sicknesses and labors: thou didst cry unto the tormentor, O most glorious one.[^482]

*Troparion:*
Unless power had been given me from on high, Severian cried unto the tormentor, how could I, being flesh, have endured the severing of my limbs?[^483]

*Theotokion:*
O most holy Bride of God, grant me help by thy supplications, to be delivered from the deceitful one, that I may glorify thee, my hope.[^484]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Rising early, we cry unto Thee, O Lord: Save us! For Thou art our God; besides Thee we know none other.[^485]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast lifted upon a tree, O glorious one, and scraped over thy body with iron claws of him that raged wickedly.[^486]

*Troparion:*
My God, Thou didst cry: strengthen this contest, that I may finish the torments, being scraped.[^487]

*Troparion:*
When the tormentor saw thee, O glorious one, enduring torments without weakening, the wretched one was astonished.[^488]

*Theotokion:*
My hope and protectress, and my shelter, O Birthgiver of God, save me by thy supplications from the snares of the serpent.[^489]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Grant me a radiant robe, Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O most merciful Christ our God.[^490]

*Troparion:*
The fierce one shut thee up in prison, and forced thee with hunger to deny Christ, Whom thou didst love, O blessed one, from thy youth.[^491]

*Troparion:*
Led into prison, O wise one, thou didst instruct with boldness all that saw thee, teaching them not to fall away from Christ.[^492]

The fierce and senseless tormentor commanded thee, O martyr, to be beheaded with the sword, because thou didst not sacrifice unto the idols; but thou didst disregard it.[^493]

*Theotokion:*
Cause me to be clothed in a robe of light by thy prayers, O Bride of God, doing good, in the day of judgment, singing praise unto thee.[^494]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):*[^495]
Armed with nobility of soul, O God-wise one, thou didst surrender thyself unto diverse torments, ignited with love for the Master, O most richly endowed. Therefore thou didst expose the frenzy of the tormentors, and didst receive from God the incorruptible crown of victory.[^496]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Thou Who in the beginning didst found the earth, and establish the heavens by Thy Word: Blessed art Thou unto ages, O Lord, the God of our fathers.[^497]

*Troparion:*
With sharp stones the impious one crushed thy mouth, which with boldness proclaimed Christ in the midst of the transgressors. Having obtained His glory, thou now dancest there.[^498]

*Troparion:*
Suspended on a wall, O passion-bearer, by the great wrath of the tormentor, tied unto a heavy stone, thou didst not deny Christ, the highly exalted God of our fathers.[^499]

*Troparion:*
O thy steadfast resistance, O blessed one! O thy fervent love toward the Creator! For the sake whereof He adorned thee with an incorruptible crown, having suffered nobly.[^500]

*Theotokion:*
Thou art my light, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, thou art my joy and shelter, and my haven, O blessed one; and I glorify thee, as having given birth unto the God of our fathers.[^501]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The King of heaven, Whom the hosts of angels sing: praise and exalt Him above all unto all ages.[^502]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst endure wounds unto the end, O soldier of Christ, and didst pass over, rejoicing, unto the supreme Kingdom, O all-blessed one.[^503]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast not put to shame for the sake of Christ, O valiantly wise one, having endured diverse torments; therefore thou art also glorified unto all ages.[^504]

*Troparion:*
Crown-bearer, now truly dancing with the sufferers under the roof of the King: remember them that with faith keep thy memory.[^505]

*Theotokion:*
Birthgiver of God, protectress of Christians: deliver us from every distress, that we may sing praise unto thee unto all ages.[^506]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Truly we confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God, we who have been saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs.[^507]

By the hands of them that love thee, O blessed one, thy body was shrouded and buried as holy, and it pours forth streams of healings unto the glory of God.[^508]

O wonder, how the dead youth arose and met thy body on the way, being borne to burial, O all-marvelous martyr![^509]

Having obtained the eternal Kingdom, O blessed one, and standing honorably before the Birthgiver of God, pray fervently for them that sing praise unto thee.[^510]

*Theotokion:*
The chief ranks of the angels were amazed, beholding the Incarnate One, and seeing thee who barest the Creator of the ages, O Ever-Virgin.[^511]

*Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^512]
Being cut with sinews for Christ's sake, O glorious one, and suspended on a tree, and ruthlessly scraped on Thy flesh with iron scrapers; and being commanded to sacrifice unto idols, O wise one, Thou didst not deny the Lord of all; but by Thy sufferings Thou didst expose the weakness and vanity of idols, and Thou becamest a companion of the angels.[^513]

Rejoicing, thou didst gird thyself for the contest, as a lawful athlete, O right-marvelous one; with noble mind, disregarding torments, O martyr, and striving to be likened unto Christ by death, O marvelous one; therefore[^514] Jesus the Lover of mankind, the Savior of our souls, adorned thee with the crown of the Kingdom.[^515]

*Glory, in the same Tone:*
Led as a prisoner and glorying in wounds, thou didst command those that looked on to imitate thy disposition, looking unto the heavenly recompenses, O blessed one; which grant great and high beauty, as being incorruptible and enduring unto ages, making them that abide in them heirs through the Spirit.[^516]

*Both now, of the feast:*
Today the divine wealth of the grace of the Master is poured out unto all the ends of the world from a barren source, truly pouring forth gifts, and announcing her procession, unto them that with love honor her nativity, and cry out: O all-powerful Jesus, Thou art the Savior of our souls![^517]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast twice; Glory, of the Ancestors of God; Both now, of the feast.*[^518]
*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*[^519]
Today the Virgin and Birthgiver of God Mary, the indestructible chamber of the Heavenly Bridegroom, is born of barren Anna by the will of God, having prepared herself as the chariot of the Word of God: for unto this was she fore-ordained to be the Maiden and the Mother of Life.[^520]
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*[^521]
O David, He that swore unto thee of old, having anointed thee, hath fulfilled the fruit of thy loins upon thy throne, having given Mary: for thou seest her that is of marvelous Anna, and thou rejoicest: from whom Christ was incarnate, the Savior of all, by boundless goodness saving our race.[^522]
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 6, and of the saints on 6.*[^523]
*Canon of the feast, Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified.[^524]

*Troparion:*
Come, ye faithful, rejoicing in the Divine Spirit! Let us honor with hymns the Ever-Virgin Maiden who hath come forth today from the barren woman for the salvation of mankind.[^525]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, O pure one, Mother and handmaid of Christ God, who art the mediatress of the primal blessedness! All the human race worthily glorifies thee with hymns.[^526]

*Troparion:*
Today the bridge of life is born, whereby men, having found the recall from the fall of Hades, glorify Christ the Giver of life with hymns.[^527]

*Another Canon of the Saints. Whose acrostic is: "Thy parents, O all-pure one, I sing chaste-mindedly." Tone 2.*[^528]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
In the deep of old, the overwhelming power laid low the whole host of Pharaoh; and the Incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin: the pre-eminently glorified Lord, for gloriously hath He been glorified.[^529]

*Troparion:*
Having shone forth with the splendors of virtues, O God-wise Anna and ever-blessed Joachim, ye were counted worthy to give birth unto the lamp that made the noetic Sun to flash forth, Who shone from her in the flesh.[^530]

*Troparion:*
With God-like vision toward God, truly God-accepted Joachim and divine Anna, praying unswervingly, bare the most pure Birthgiver of God, surpassing all creation in holiness.[^531]

*Troparion:*
Possessing a transcendent life and the brightness of conversation, ye were higher than all earthly parents together: having given birth unto the incorruptible Virgin, and for her sake having truly become the Ancestors of God.[^532]

*Theotokion:*
[Of salvation...][^533] The originators of the salvation of all, most blessed Joachim and glorious Anna, bare the honorable and spotless and all-pure Birthgiver of God, having received her as the recompense of piety.[^534]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death; and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us that sing praise unto Thee.[^535]

*Troparion:*
Having lived blamelessly before God, ye bare the salvation of all, O God-wise parents, having given birth unto her who bare the Creator and our God.[^536]

*Troparion:*
The Lord, Who pours forth life unto all, brought forth from a barren woman the Virgin, in whom He was pleased to dwell, and after childbirth preserved her incorrupt.[^537]

*Troparion:*
Today let us praise in song Anna's fruit, Mary, who bare the life-bearing Cluster, as the Birthgiver of God, and the protectress and helper of all.[^538]

*Another Canon. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit rejoiced in singing: There is none holy as our God, and there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord.[^539]

*Troparion:*
Being barren and bereft of children, and imploring the Creator with tears, thou wast counted worthy to give birth unto the only blessed one, O God-accepted Anna, crying aloud: For there is none holy besides Thee, O Lord.[^540]

*Troparion:*
Having enriched his spouse with divine grace, divine and God-proclaiming Joachim was counted worthy to give birth unto the mediatress of salvation for men; unto whom we cry aloud: For there is none blameless above thee, O Sovereign Lady.[^541]

*Troparion:*
Let us sing praise unto the all-honorable pair, from whom the Virgin shone forth unto us, being higher than all creatures, for she bare God; unto Whom let us cry aloud: For there is none holy above Thee, O Lord.[^542]

*Theotokion:*
Having escaped the reproach of barrenness, Anna bare the Birthgiver of God, who gloriously abolished the reproach of Eve; unto whom we cry aloud: For there is none blameless above thee, O Sovereign Lady.[^543]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Joachim and Anna were freed from the reproach of childlessness, and Adam and Eve from the corruption of death, O all-pure one, in thy holy nativity. This do thy people also celebrate, having been delivered from the guilt of transgressions, when they cry unto thee: The barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God, and the nourisher of our life.[^544]

*Ikos:*
The acceptable prayer together with the sighing of barrenness and childlessness of Joachim and Anna entered into the ears of the Lord, and brought forth a life-bearing fruit for the world: for the one offered prayer upon the mountain, and the other bore her reproach in the garden; yet with joy the barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God, and the nourisher of our life.[^545]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate" (Собезна́чальное):*[^546]
Joachim and Anna keep festival, for after God they worthily found grace, and bare a fruit, a God-acceptable temple, the Virgin and pure Mother of God, the only blessed one, who unceasingly prays that our souls may be saved.[^547]
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, O only Lover of mankind.[^548]

*Troparion:*
We praise Thee in song, O Lord, Who hast given her that bare Thee as a saving haven unto all the faithful.[^549]

*Troparion:*
Christ revealed thee, O Bride of God, as the praise and strength of all who faithfully sing praise unto thy mystery.[^550]

*Troparion:*
O unblemished Sovereign Lady, delivered from transgressions by thy prayers, with prudent mind we all call thee blessed.[^551]

*Another Canon. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou didst come from the Virgin, not a mediator, nor an angel, but Thyself, O Lord, being incarnate, and Thou didst save me, all of man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^552]

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing, God-wise and God-accepted Joachim receives from the barren woman the maiden Virgin, for whose sake the barrenness of the world was loosed by her nativity.[^553]

*Troparion:*
Joachim, as the divine fruit, now offers us a most rich spiritual banquet; for he hath given birth unto the Mother of God, the all-incorrupt Maiden.[^554]

*Troparion:*
Grace offers her that saved mankind from death and corruption, who was destined to be the Mother of God, having received the co-essential Word, Who was ineffably incarnate.[^555]

*Troparion:*
From the root of Jesse shone forth a pair, from whom sprang the rod bearing the flower, sweetening me, all of man, with the fragrance of the myrrh of the Godhead.[^556]

*Theotokion:*
Direct my life, O Birthgiver of God, guiding me by the divine commandments of the Word Who was incarnate of thee; and lead me unto the light, O Virgin Mother Mary, Bride of God.[^557]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Having dispelled the shadow-traced darkness of enigmas, and enlightened the hearts of the faithful by the arrival of truth through the Maiden of God: do Thou also guide us by Thy light, O Christ.[^558]

*Troparion:*
Let us sing, ye peoples, the Cause of all, the Cause of our being according to us: in whose type the prophets rejoiced, being counted worthy, bringing forth the manifest salvation from her.[^559]

*Troparion:*
The budding of the dry rod of the priest showed unto Israel the forechosen judgment; and now the brightness of those that budded forth shines gloriously, the all-glorious birth from the barren woman.[^560]

*Another Canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Enlightenment of them that lie in darkness, O Salvation of the despairing, Christ my Savior: unto Thee do I rise early, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy radiance, for besides Thee I know no other God.[^561]

*Troparion:*
The chaste pair, shining with the dawn of purity, Anna and God-accepted Joachim, bare for us the barren human nature, which virginity adorned with divine radiance.[^562]

*Troparion:*
Anna and all-praised Joachim, the honorable couple and God-wise pair of chastity, bare the virginal, God-adorned throne, who is higher than all by the divine hand.[^563]

*Troparion:*
Having lived in a God-wise manner, divine Joachim and Anna, the seers of God, were clearly counted worthy to give birth unto the light-bearing door for the Dayspring from on high that appeared for the guidance of the wandering.[^564]

*Troparion:*
The tablet of the New Law inscribed by God, upon which is the remission of the sins of the Old Law, the Divine Word prefigured of old, as now from a rock the Almighty by His nod hath hewn her from a barren woman.[^565]

*Theotokion:*
By thy dawn, O Mother of God, command my mind, darkened by sin, to be enlightened, O Virgin, destroying the darkness of ignorance and transgressions; for I know no other protectress above thee.[^566]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
From the whale Jonah cried unto the Lord: Do Thou lead me up from the depth of Hades, I pray; that unto Thee as Deliverer, with the voice of praise and the spirit of truth, I may sacrifice.[^567]

*Troparion:*
Unto the Lord in the sorrow of barrenness the God-wise parents of the Mother of God cried aloud; and they bare her unto generations of generations, for the common salvation and praise.[^568]

*Troparion:*
The God-wise parents of the Mother of God received a worthy heavenly gift from God: the chariot higher than the Cherubim themselves, the birthgiver of the Word and Creator.[^569]

*Another Canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion; lead me up from corruption, O God.[^570]

*Troparion:*
Having of old received a fruitful seed from divine illumination, barren Anna was counted worthy to give birth unto the Maiden who is piously honored by all creatures.[^571]

*Troparion:*
Now having given birth by the will of God, the barren woman was counted worthy in obedience to receive the Virgin, who bare without carnal will, when God Himself manifestly willed it.[^572]

*Troparion:*
Illumined in spirit, Isaiah beheld the offspring of Joachim and Anna as a new scroll, wherein was inscribed the incarnate Word.[^573]

*Theotokion:*
Mystery runs before mystery: for the grace that formerly was barren bare the mediatress of salvation, revealed unto us through the birth of virginity.[^574]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Anna now rejoices, loosed from the bonds of barrenness, and nourishes the all-pure one, calling together all to praise Him Who granted from her womb unto mankind the only Mother who knew not man.[^575]

*Ikos:*
She that formerly was delivered from the bonds of childlessness by prayer invites us to celebrate together the miracle, and to offer gifts unto her that is born, praying before her with love; whom of old the virgins ran before, leaping with joy and crying aloud: Behold, the recall of all is come! Behold, Adam is set free, for Anna hath brought forth fruit, the only Mother who knew not man.[^576]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The bush unburnt by fire upon the mountain, and the Chaldean furnace dropping dew, clearly prefigured thee, O Bride of God; for in a material womb thou didst receive the immaterial Divine Fire unconsumed. Therefore we sing unto Him that was born of thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^577]

*Troparion:*
The lawgiver was hindered from comprehending thy great mystery in material manifestations, O all-pure one, being typically instructed of old not to mind earthly zealous things; therefore, amazed at the miracle, he said: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^578]

*Troparion:*
The divine choir divinely named thee the Mountain and the Heavenly Door and the Spiritual Ladder; for from thee a stone was cut without hands of man, and the door through which passed the Lord, the God of wonders of our fathers.[^579]

*Another Canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The contrary command of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame; but Christ spread spiritual dew over the pious children: He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^580]

*Troparion:*
Having budded from the root of God-wise David, O holy pair, ye bare for the world the all-sacred rod, the pure Virgin, who seedlessly made Christ to shine forth unto us as the most sacred flower.[^581]

*Troparion:*
Bearing the Birthgiver of God as a radiant candle, divine Anna, like a gold-gleaming lampstand, enlightened the whole world with divine light and the bright splendors of virginity.[^582]

*Troparion:*
O glorious ancestors, most richly endowed, of God the Almighty, Who was incarnate through your God-wise daughter for His ineffable mercy: entreat now remission of transgressions for me who flee unto you.[^583]

*Theotokion:*
As being greater than all parents, ye bare her who has dominion over all creatures, most pure Mary, who bare God clothed in flesh, made like unto us for His manifold tender compassion.[^584]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
In the children's furnace of old Thou didst prefigure Thy Mother, O Lord; and this image delivered from the fire them that entered unburnt; whom we sing as revealed by Thee today unto the ends of the earth, and we supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^585]

*Troparion:*
The tabernacle foreordained for our reconciliation unto God now begins to be, being destined to give birth unto the Word Who appeared unto us in the thickness of the flesh; Whom we sing, having received through Him our being from non-existence, and we supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^586]

*Troparion:*
The transformation of barrenness loosed the worldly barrenness of good things, and clearly showed the miracle of Christ Who came unto earthly men; Whom we sing, having received through Him our being from non-existence, and we supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^587]

*Another Canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and transformed the flame into dew, praise God, O ye works, as Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^588]

*Troparion:*
Abounding in the wealth of virtues, honorable Joachim and chaste Anna bare the Queen and Virgin, adorned with divine glory; whom all creation sings as the Birthgiver of God.[^589]

*Troparion:*
The all-spotless Bride was sent as a rod of strength unto us through you, O friends of God; through whom, in the midst of enemies, we prevail over the godless, trampling upon their crafts.[^590]

*Troparion:*
A weapon of good-pleasure was granted unto us from God through you, O most sacred couple; whereby we, the faithful, are now ever fair-crowned, O pure Virgin Mother who barest God.[^591]

*Troparion:*
The power of God by fruitbearing opened the barren womb, and guards beforehand the door of the splendor of virginity, for whose sake the Word came unto earthly men, being incarnate by an ineffable word.[^592]

*Theotokion:*
Enlightened by the light-pourings of Him Who was incarnate of thee for our sake, O all-spotless Sovereign Lady, may the excellent pair of thy parents be an intercession for us of heavenly blessings.[^593]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thee who ineffably didst incarnate from virginal loins God, the Luminary Who shone forth before the sun, Who came unto us in the flesh, O blessed, all-honorable Birthgiver of God, we magnify.[^594]

*Troparion:*
He Who poured forth water from the rock for an intractable people grants from barren loins unto the well-obedient nations a fruit for our joy, even thee, O all-pure Mother of God, whom worthily we magnify.[^595]

*Troparion:*
The abolisher of the unjust ancient condemnation and the restoration of the ancestral mother, the cause of our race's adoption unto God, the bridge unto the Creator: thee, O Birthgiver of God, we magnify.[^596]

*Another Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, having become incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten the darkened and to gather together the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Birthgiver of God do we magnify.[^597]

*Troparion:*
Being of one mind and of one soul in virtue, O honorable parents of the all-pure Virgin, O most sacred ones: pray that they may be saved who fervently celebrate your all-praised and glorious memory.[^598]

*Troparion:*
Ye destroyed the pasture of death, O glorious ones, having radiantly given birth unto the Mother of Life, who abolished its assault, and mediated immortal life as hope by reason of faith.[^599]

*Troparion:*
Fair as the sun, Joachim, uniting with the light-bearing moon Anna, bare the ray of virginity, through whom the radiance of the Divine Essence, united hypostatically unto flesh, shone forth unto us.[^600]

*Troparion:*
Having lived chastely and piously, O blessed ones, ye were now counted worthy of ineffable sweetness, having obtained the manifestation of God Who appeared unto the world from you: Whom implore, that our souls may be saved.[^601]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "He hath visited us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀ є҆́сть):*[^602]
She that abolished the curse of Eve is now born of barren elders, from Anna and Joachim; whom with the angels let all of us, the faithful, praise in hymns as is due.[^603]

*Glory, both now:*
As a sun from the sun, and as a moon from the moon, from Anna and Joachim was born the all-spotless Maiden, and she enlightened the ends of the world with her radiance; whom singing, let us worthily call blessed, celebrating their honorable memory.[^604]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^605]
*Sticheron:*
Now dance, O prophet David, for behold: from thy loins the Virgin Maiden of God, Mary, is born gloriously, through whom earthly men have divinely found the recall from their fall.[^606]

*Verse: Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [Ps. 44:11].*[^607]
*Sticheron:*
Adam together with Eve is stripped of the deadness of corruption by grace, and all mortals are quickened; for having truly been born of a barren woman, she loosed the barrenness of the world.[^608]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [Ps. 44:13].*[^609]
*Sticheron:*
Thy most honorable nativity we celebrate radiantly with the angels, O pure Virgin Mother; but, O Mother of God, cease not to protect the Christians who sing praise unto thee.[^610]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast, Tone 2:*
Today the all-spotless, pure one came forth from the barren woman. Today all creation rejoices in her nativity. Adam is loosed from bonds, and Eve is freed from the curse. All heavenly things rejoice, and peace is granted unto men. And we, glorifying, cry aloud: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men![^611]

*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 1, of the Second Tone, on 4; and of the Saints, Ode 6, on 4.*[^612]
*Prokeimenon of the Feast, and until the Apodosis. Then of the Saints, Tone 7: God is marvelous in His saints [Ps. 67:36].*
*Verse: In congregations bless ye God [Ps. 67:27].*
*Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 210 from the half [Gal. 4:22–31].*[^613]
*Alleluia* Tone 1: The salvation of the righteous is of the Lord [Ps. 36:39].*[^614]
*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 36 [Lk. 8:16–21].*[^615]
*Communion Hymn of the Feast, and of the Saints: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous [Ps. 32:1].*[^616]

*On the Tenth Day of the Same Month: The Holy Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora.*[^617]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, 3; Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^618]
*Sticheron:*
O most marvelous wonder! For from a childless bed and a barren womb, the rod bearing the flower buds forth today: the Mother of God, who knew not wedlock, from righteous Joachim and Anna. Therefore the prophetic gatherings and the whole assembly of the patriarchs rejoice in her nativity.[^619]

*Sticheron:*
Today David rejoices, and Jesse leaps with joy, and Levi is magnified, and righteous Joachim dances in spirit, and Anna's childlessness is manifestly loosed by thy nativity, O pure Mary. O thou who knewest not wedlock, the assembly of angels together with all earthly men bless thy divine womb.[^620]

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, gathering of earthly men; rejoice, temple of the Lord! Rejoice, unwedded Mother, who didst gloriously loose the barrenness of Anna, and didst pour forth remission of sins unto earthly men by thy nativity! Rejoice, all-spotless one; rejoice, divine temple; rejoice, tabernacle wherein the Creator and Lord took up His abode![^621]

*Other Stichera of the Saints, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^622]
*Sticheron:*
Adorned with the purple dye of blood, fair in the beauty of virginity, O maidens, ye were incorruptibly united unto Christ our God, Who preserved your virginity undefiled in the immortal heavenly incorruption, in the heavenly mansions, in the chamber not made with hands, O martyrs.[^623]`

*Sticheron:*
Though imperfect in body, yet perfect in mind, ye conquered the ancient serpent, the author of evil, O glorious ones, by the power of the Spirit, and demonstrated his strength to be powerless. Therefore ye received crowns of victory, Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora, servants of the Trinity.[^624]

*Sticheron:*
Neither when dismembered in your limbs, nor when consumed by fire, nor when torn by iron claws, nor when suspended on a tree, nor when cut with the sword, did ye deny Christ, O all-praised passion-bearers. Therefore ye received the crown of victory, Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora, servants of the Trinity.[^625]

*Glory, both now, Tone 2:*
What is this noise of them that keep festival? Joachim and Anna feast mystically. Rejoice with us today, saying, O Adam and Eve: for unto us who of old closed paradise by transgression, a blessed fruit hath been given, the Maiden of God Mary, opening its entrance unto all.[^626]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*[^627]
*Sticheron:*
Let the door of the God-receiving temple be opened: for today Joachim, having received within with glory the temple and throne of the King of all, dedicated her, having sanctified her unto the Lord, who from him was chosen to be the Mother of God.[^628]

*Verse: Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [Ps. 44:11].*[^629]
*Sticheron:*
The spiritual rays of universal joy have shone forth unto the world, announcing beforehand unto all the Sun of Glory, Christ God, in thy nativity, O all-pure one. For thou hast been revealed as the mediatress of true gladness and grace.[^630]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [Ps. 44:13].*[^631]
*Sticheron:*
This thine all-honorable glory, O pure one, announces unto all peoples the benefits of thy tender compassion. For thou art the mediatress of present gladness and the pure cause of future joy: appear unto us through thy prayer.[^632]

*Glory, both now, Tone 2, Idiomelon:*[^633]
She that was foreordained Queen of all, the dwelling-place of God, came forth today from the barren womb of glorious Anna, the divine habitation of the Ever-Existing Essence; through whom shameless Hades was trampled down, and Eve, the mother of all, is introduced into steadfast life. Unto her let us worthily cry aloud: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb![^634]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
*Thy nativity, O Virgin Birthgiver of God...*[^635]

*At Matins, after the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*[^636]

Magnify the wonder, and let David be glad; O Adam, be renewed, and let Levi be strengthened: from whom Christ was born unto me. Stir up the harp, O hymnographer, and say: Who is she that is born, whom thou callest daughter? She is the nourisher of our life, the Mother of Christ God.[^637]
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded secretly" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*[^638]
Be renewed, O Adam; rejoice, O Eve; make glad, O David; take good courage, O Anna: for the Mother of thy Creator is born most gloriously. All the renewed earth leaps for joy, and rejoices, robed in a garment. Let every tongue, leaping with joy, now cry unto Mary: Blessed is the house of David, for it nourishes the nourisher of our life![^639]
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*Canon of the Feast with the heirmos on 8, and of the Martyrs on 4.*[^640]
*Canon of the Feast, Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who crushed wars with His arm, and led Israel through the Red Sea, let us sing as unto our Deliverer and God, for He hath been glorified.[^641]

*Troparion:*
The Holy of Holies, an infant, is presented in the holy sanctuary to be nurtured by the hand of an angel: let us all therefore faithfully celebrate together at her nativity.[^642]

*Troparion:*
Let all creation dance, and let David also be glad; for from his tribe and from his seed came forth the rod, bearing as a flower the Lord, the Creator of all.[^643]

*Troparion:*
The barren Anna bare not, yet was she not childless unto God: for behold, the pure Virgin Mother was forenamed from generations. Therefore she budded forth the Creator of nature in the form of a servant.[^644]`

*Troparion:*
Thee, the gentle ewe-lamb, who broughtest forth the Lamb Christ as an infant from Thy womb into our nature: all of us honor thee in hymns as born of Anna.[^645]

*Triadikon:*
Three unoriginate Persons I glorify, three Holy Ones I sing, three Co-ever-existing Ones in one essence I proclaim: for one God is glorified in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.[^646]

*Theotokion:*
Who hath seen a Child nourished with milk, Whom no father begat? Or where was a Virgin Mother seen? Truly beyond understanding are both, O pure Mother of God![^647]

*Another Canon of the Holy Women, whose acrostic is: "The sufferings of the three true sisters I honor." By Joseph.*[^648]

*Joseph. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother, and I shall be seen radiantly keeping festival, and rejoicing I shall sing her wonders.[^649]

*Troparion:*
The uncreated Trinity, Whom ye piously proclaimed, make propitious unto us, O glorious martyrs, who now honor your divine sufferings and achievements, O divinely blessed ones.[^650]

*Troparion:*
The maidens disregarded the words of the tormentor, being shielded by the divine weapon of faith, and they surrendered to the demand of tortures and to an unjust death for the sake of the Life of all.[^651]

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the all-powerful might of the Creator, the all-honorable maidens took on a manly spirit, and with their feet they trampled upon the crooked and haughty serpent, and cast him down unto the ground.[^652]

*Theotokion:*
As an animate temple, as an incorrupt tabernacle, as the heavenly gate, as the divine table, as the palace and throne of the Master, let us honor the pure Mary with hymns.[^653]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God, my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies, I have rejoiced in Thy salvation.[^654]

*Troparion:*
Nurtured in the Holy of Holies, O Virgin all-pure Birthgiver of God, thou hast been revealed higher than creation, having given birth unto the Creator in the flesh.[^655]

*Troparion:*
Blessed is thy womb, O chaste Anna, for thou didst sprout the Virgin as fruit, who seedlessly gave birth unto Jesus, the Nourisher of creation and the Deliverer.[^656]

*Troparion:*
Let all creation bless the Ever-Virgin, who today is born of Anna: who sprouted as the most pure flower, Christ, from the root of Jesse.[^657]

*Troparion:*
Showing thee higher than all creation, O pure Birthgiver of God, Thy Son magnifies thy nativity from Anna, and makes all glad today.[^658]

*Triadikon:*
Thee do we worship, O Father unoriginate in essence; we sing Thy co-eternal Son, and we honor Thy co-ever-existing Spirit, as one God in three Persons by nature.[^659]

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the Giver of Light and the Author of human life, O pure Birthgiver of God, thou hast been revealed as the treasury of our life and the door of unapproachable light.[^660]

*Another Canon. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Not in wisdom, and power, and riches do we boast, but in Thee, the hypostatic Wisdom of the Father, O Christ: for there is none holy above Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^661]

*Troparion:*
Deadened in mind, the most lawless tormentor fiercely urged thee to deny Christ, our Life, wounding thee, O martyr Menodora.[^662]

*Troparion:*
The tormentor spared not her who looked unto God, but mercilessly broke thy limbs with rods, weaving for thee an eternal crown, though he knew it not, O martyr.[^663]

*Troparion:*
Through tortures the thrice-rich holy martyrs found a treasure in the heavens and everlasting glory, having drawn nigh unto God.[^664]

*Theotokion:*
Deliver me: drive away the darkness of my soul, and rend asunder the bonds of sins, O pure Virgin, and save me, who barest the All-Bountiful.[^665]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*[^666]
Having patiently suffered for the sake of the Trinity, ye conquered the multi-scheming enemy, being brotherly clothed in the Spirit. Therefore ye dwell with the five virgins in the heavenly bridal chamber, O passion-bearers, and with the angels ye stand unceasingly before the King of all in gladness.[^667]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou wast amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ):*[^668]
The heavenly ranks of the bodiless powers were amazed at your manifold endurance. For as though another were suffering, ye remained steadfast while your legs and joints were broken, enduring a bitter death, and with a woman's body crushing the apostate serpent, O virgin brides of the Giver of Life, defenders of the faith![^669]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast, the same Tone:*
From the root of Jesse and from the loins of David, the Maiden of God Mary is born unto us today; for all things rejoice with gladness and are renewed. Rejoice together, heaven and earth; praise her, ye families of the nations! Joachim is glad and Anna keeps festival, crying aloud: The barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life![^670]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
The prophet Habakkuk with spiritual eyes foresaw Thy coming, O Lord; therefore he also cried aloud: God shall come from Theman! Glory to Thy power, glory to Thy condescension![^671]

*Troparion:*
The patriarch Jacob, clearly foreseeing the majesties of Thy dispensation, O Savior, cried aloud in the Spirit, speaking secretly unto Judah: From a tender sprout Thou hast ascended, O my son!—proclaiming Thee as God from the Virgin.[^672]

*Troparion:*
Now the rod of Aaron, which budded from the root of David; now the pure Virgin comes forth, and heaven and earth dance together, and all the families of the nations, and Anna and Joachim mystically.[^673]

*Troparion:*
Now let heaven be glad, and let earth rejoice, and let Joachim and David dance: the one indeed as thy parent who truly barest God; and the other as thy forefather, proclaiming thy majesties, O pure one.[^674]

*Troparion:*
The inhabited earth rejoices together with thee today, O God-wise Anna; for thou didst blossom forth the Mother of its Deliverer: who, having budded from the root of David, bears for us the rod of power, the flower Christ.[^675]

*Triadikon:*
I glorify God unoriginate, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the uncreated consubstantial Trinity, before Whom the seraphim stand with reverence, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God![^676]

*Theotokion:*
The Origin beyond origin takes an origin from thee, O Parent of God, by a bodily burden; and the Father's Word, co-unoriginate and co-ever-existing with the Spirit, having become incarnate, remains, preserving the divine dignity.[^677]

*Another Canon. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus, the God supreme, came upon a light cloud with an incorrupt hand, and saved them that cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^678]

*Troparion:*
Shining with the rays of the Cross, the ever-blessed Metrodora, tied to a tree, endured fiery torture, extinguishing the coals of delusion with the dew of the love of Christ.[^679]

*Troparion:*
Reaching out her thoughts in clear vision, beholding the inscrutable beauties of the Bridegroom, the ever-blessed Metrodora, beaten with rods, endured pains valiantly.[^680]

*Troparion:*
Ye were adorned, O maidens, and radiantly glorified, having loved the supremely glorified Word in every way. Wounded by His love, ye steadfastly endured the onsets of passions.[^681]

*Theotokion:*
Slain by the malice of the deceiver, O all-spotless one who barest Life, quicken me, for unto thee have I fled; and having fallen into the depth of sin, lead me up, as thou art merciful, O all-immaculate one.[^682]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Lord our God, grant us peace; O Lord our God, possess us; O Lord, besides Thee we know none other we know none other: Thy Name do we name.[^683]

*Troparion:*
Thy most pure nativity, O blameless Virgin, is ineffable, and Thine unuttered conception and thy childbirth, O unwedded Bride: for He was God, Who was wholly clothed in me.[^684]

*Troparion:*
Today let the angelic ranks be glad, let those of Adam's race dance with songs: for the rod is born that sprouted forth Christ alone, our Deliverer.[^685]

*Troparion:*
Today Eve is loosed from condemnation, childlessness also is loosed, and Adam from the ancient curse, at thy nativity: for through thee we have been delivered from corruption.[^686]

*Troparion:*
Glory to Thee Who hast glorified the barren woman today: for according to the promise she bare the ever-blossoming rod, from whom Christ sprouted forth, the Flower of our life.[^687]

*Triadikon:*
Glory to Thee, O Holy Father, unbegotten God! Glory to Thee, O co-eternal Son, Only-Begotten! Glory to Thee, O divine and co-enthroned Spirit, Who proceedest from the Father and abidest in the Son![^688]

*Theotokion:*
Thy womb became the bearer of the Sun; thy purity remained unharmed as before, O Virgin: for Christ the Sun, like a Bridegroom from a bridal chamber, came forth from thee.[^689]

*Another Canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, didst come as Light into the world, the Holy Light Who turnest from gloomy ignorance them that sing Thy praise in faith.[^690]

*Troparion:*
Having shown a patient disposition and an unconquerable mind before the judgment-seat, the martyrs wove for themselves the crown of victory.[^691]

*Troparion:*
Now Nymphodora steadfastly suspended endures the tearings of iron claws, having loved the immortal Bridegroom.[^692]

*Troparion:*
Let the thrice-radiant lamps, the three-roofed chamber, the dwelling-place of the Trinity, the God-wise virgins, be praised with hymns.[^693]

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee alone chosen and fair and spotless, the God-supreme Word is incarnate of thee, O thou full of God's grace![^694]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Like the waters of the sea, O Lover of mankind, I am tossed by the waves of this life; therefore like Jonah, so cry I unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O compassionate Lord![^695]

*Troparion:*
Thee being the Holy of Holies, thy chaste parents, O pure one, dedicated thee in the temple of the Lord to be nurtured honorably, and to prepare and to be prepared to be His Mother.[^696]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, ye barren women and mothers; take courage, and leap for joy, ye childless! For the childless barren woman sprouts forth the Birthgiver of God, who shall deliver Eve from travail and Adam from the curse.[^697]

*Troparion:*
I hear David singing unto thee: The virgins shall be brought after thee, they shall be brought into the King's temple; and together with him I also praise thee as the King's Daughter.[^698]

*Troparion:*
We sing thy holy nativity, we honor also thine immaculate conception, O Bride called by God and Virgin; and the ranks of angels and the souls of the saints glorify with us.[^699]

*Triadikon:*
In thee the mystery of the Trinity is sung and glorified, O pure one: for the Father was well-pleased, the Word took up His abode in thee, and the divine Spirit overshadowed thee.[^700]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the golden censer: for the Fire took up His abode in thy womb, the Word from the Holy Spirit, and in human form was seen in thee, O pure Parent of God.[^701]

*Another Canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries out unto Thee, cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed from Thy side for mercy's sake.[^702]

*Troparion:*
Desiring to behold Thine inscrutable beauty, wounded by Thy sweetest love, O unoriginate Word, they valiantly endured the ferocity of tortures.[^703]

*Troparion:*
Like lilies in the garden of sufferers the most glorious maidens blossomed forth, and perfumed the Church with the fragrances of various tortures by the grace of the Spirit.[^704]

*Troparion:*
Desiring the immortal Bridegroom alone, strengthened by invisible power, the virgin maidens visibly despised visible death.[^705]

*Theotokion:*
The Lord Who took up His abode in thy womb, having found thee holier and purer than all creation, O Mother of God named after the Lord, all-pure Birthgiver of God![^706]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Joachim and Anna were freed from the reproach of childlessness, and Adam and Eve from the corruption of death, O all-pure one, in thy holy nativity. This do thy people also celebrate, having been delivered from the guilt of transgressions, when they cry unto thee: The barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life![^707]

*Ikos:*
The prayer together with the sighing over the barrenness and childlessness of Joachim and Anna was well- pleasing: it entered into the ears of the Lord, and sprouted forth a life-bearing fruit for the world. For the one offered prayer on the mountain, and the other bore reproach in the garden, yet with joy: The barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life![^708]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Chaldean furnace, kindled with fire, was bedewed by the Spirit at the presence of God; the children sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^709]

*Troparion:*
We celebrate, O pure one, and faithfully worship thy holy nativity, singing praise unto Thy Son, through Whom we have now been delivered from the ancient condemnation of Adam.[^710]

*Troparion:*
Now Anna is glad and cries aloud, boasting: Though barren, I have given birth unto God's Mother, for whose sake the condemnation of Eve is loosed, and the pain in griefs.[^711]

*Troparion:*
Adam is freed, and Eve dances, and in the Spirit they cry aloud unto thee, O Birthgiver of God: Through thee we have been delivered from the ancestral curse, now that Christ has appeared.[^712]

*Troparion:*
O womb that contained God's dwelling-place! O belly that bore her who is wider than the heavens! Holy throne, spiritual ark of sanctification![^713]

*Triadikon:*
Let us glorify the Father, the Son, and the Spirit in the unity of the Godhead, the All-Holy Trinity, undivided, uncreated, co-ever-existing, and consubstantial.[^714]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone didst give birth unto God most gloriously, O Virgin; thou didst renew nature by thy childbirth, O Mary; thou didst loose Eve from the ancestral curse, O pure Parent of God.[^715]

*Another Canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Abrahamic children in Babylon of old trampled down the flame of the furnace, crying aloud in hymns: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^716]

*Troparion:*
When the wicked tormentor commanded you to sacrifice unto deaf idols, ye spat upon him, O maidens, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^717]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened in mind with the rays of the Divine Source, ye blackened the idolatrous gloom, O all-praised ones, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^718]

*Troparion:*
Neither the severance of limbs, nor persecution, nor tribulation was able in any way to separate from Christ those who cried aloud while being tortured: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^719]

*Theotokion:*
Supernaturally wast thou counted worthy, O Virgin, to give birth from thy womb unto the Creator, Who builds up earthly men who builds up earthly men who sing in faith: Blessed art Thou, O God![^720]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
He Who covers His chambers with waters, Who sets the sand as a bound to the sea and upholds all things: Thee the sun sings, Thee the moon glorifies, unto Thee all creation offers a hymn, as the Creator of all unto the ages.[^721]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who hast wrought marvelous things for a barren womb, Who didst open the childless womb of Anna and gave her fruit: Thou, O Holy God, Thou, O Son of the Virgin, Thou from her didst take flesh, from the ever-blossoming Virgin and Birthgiver of God.[^722]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who shuttest the abyss and openest it, Who liftest up the water in the clouds and givest rain: Thou, O Lord, didst grant a most pure fruit to sprout forth from the barren root of holy Anna, and to give birth unto the Birthgiver of God.[^723]

*Troparion:*
O Cultivator of our thoughts and Planter of our souls, Thou Who didst show forth barren earth as fruitful: Thou of old didst make holy Anna, who was dry, to be a fertile furrow bearing good ears of corn, bringing forth fruit, to sprout forth the most pure fruit, the Birthgiver of God.[^724]

*Troparion:*
Come, let us all behold the city of God now being born from a small chamber as it were: having an outgoing from the door of the womb, yet knowing no incoming of union: God the Creator alone passed by this marvelous path.[^725]

*Triadikon:*
O Trinity beyond essence, Unity co-unoriginate: Thee the multitude of angels sings and trembles before; heaven and earth and the abysses are dismayed; men bless Thee, the fire serves Thee; all things that are in creation obey Thee with fear, O Holy Trinity![^726]

*Theotokion:*
O most new hearing! God, the Son of a woman! O seedless childbirth! A mother without husband, and the One born is God! O fearful sight! O strange conception of a Virgin! O ineffable childbirth! Truly all things are beyond understanding and sight![^727]

*Another Canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
O almighty Deliverer of all, having descended into the midst of the flame, Thou didst bedew them that were pious, and taughtest them to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works, sing praise unto the Lord![^728]

*Troparion:*
Sharpened by love of the Creator, ye blunted the serpent's stings; having taken on manly struggles in a woman's body, ye were crowned with heavenly crowns.[^729]

*Troparion:*
Engaging in combat in the midst of the contest, the God-wise maidens with flesh conquered the bodiless, invisible enemies, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, praise ye the Lord![^730]

*Troparion:*
Strengthened in God our Savior, prevailing in Christ Jesus, ye destroyed the powerless dominion of the enemy, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^731]

*Troparion:*
Ye obtained the Kingdom on high, reigning with Christ Jesus, variegated with the wounds of tortures, adorned with beauty, O praiseworthy maidens![^732]

*Theotokion:*
As the undefiled dwelling-place of God, Whom thou didst receive becoming incarnate, and known in two natures, O Maiden; unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^733]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Alien unto mothers is virginity, and strange unto virgins is childbearing: in thee, O Birthgiver of God, both were accomplished. Therefore all the tribes of the earth unceasingly magnify thee.[^734]

*Troparion:*
A nativity worthy of thy purity, O Mother of God, hast thou inherited through promise: for unto a woman once barren thou wast given as a divinely sprouted fruit. Therefore all the tribes of the earth unceasingly magnify thee.[^735]

*Troparion:*
The prophecy of him that cried aloud was fulfilled, for he says: I will raise up the fallen tabernacle of holy David, which was prefigured in thee, O pure one; for whose sake the dust of all men was fashioned into the Body of God.[^736]

*Troparion:*
We venerate thy swaddling-bands, O Birthgiver of God; we glorify Him Who gave fruit to her that was previously barren, and Who opened the childless womb most gloriously: for He does all that He wills, being God sovereign in power.[^737]

*Troparion:*
As a gift unto thee, O Birthgiver of God, born of Anna, do we faithfully bring hymnody: Mother and Virgin, the only Virgin: glorifying we worship thee, we sing and praise thee.[^738]

*Triadikon:*
Alien is it unto the lawless to glorify the unoriginate Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the uncreated all-sovereignty, by Whom the whole world is upheld through the nod of Her might.[^739]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst contain in thy womb, O Virgin Mother, One of the Trinity, Christ the King, Whom all creation sings, and before Whom the ranks on high tremble: Him implore, O all-blameless one, that our souls may be saved.[^740]

*Another Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A corner-stone unhewn by hands was cut out from thee, O Virgin, the unquarried mountain, even Christ, Who joined together the sundered natures: therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.[^741]

*Troparion:*
Desiring to behold the beauty of the Bridegroom, drawn unto Him by every kind of beckoning, O God-bearers, ye were counted worthy of immortality in a mortal body; therefore ye are worthily called blessed.[^742]

*Troparion:*
Ye appeared in the midst of the tormentors like undefiled lambs among savage wolves, reproaching their beast-like nature, and ye offered yourselves unto Christ as an acceptable sacrifice.[^743]

*Troparion:*
Together ye wove an unfading crown, O virgins, having obtained divine glory, and as martyrs ye were counted worthy to receive the truly unshakable Kingdom with the martyrs.[^744]

*Troparion:*
Pray that they who celebrate your memory with love may obtain the glory whereof ye were counted worthy, and the gladness which ye received, since ye have boldness before the Master, O honorable virgins.[^745]

*Theotokion:*
Spare me, O Christ, when Thou shalt come to judge the world with glory; dispel the gloom of my passions through the prayers of her that bare Thee and of Thy honorable martyrs, for Thou art good and the Lover of mankind.[^746]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Changeless Light" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*[^747]
The Sun whence the spiritual Sun came forth according to the flesh, today hath shone upon the world from a barren womb. Therefore dancing we cry aloud: Rejoice, O Mary, deliverance of our ancestors![^748]
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^749]
*Sticheron:*
The house of God, the only Birthgiver of God, comes forth from a barren and childless couple, and Adam rejoices, being renewed.[^750]

*Verse: Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [Ps. 44:11].*[^751]
*Sticheron:*
Today joy is born of Anna, announcing unto the world the loosing of the curse: rejoice, all ye creation![^752]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [Ps. 44:13].*[^753]
*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, O Joachim, and thou, O God-wise Anna, for having given birth unto the joy and gladness of the world, and the mediatress of salvation.[^754]

*Glory, both now, Tone 4:*
Universal joy hath shone forth unto us from the righteous ones, from Joachim and Anna: the all-hymned Virgin, who for the sake of her surpassing purity becomes the living temple of God, and alone is truly recognized as the Birthgiver of God. Through her prayers, O Christ God, send down peace upon the world, and upon our souls great mercy![^755]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 4 and 6, on 8.*[^756]

*On the Eleventh Day of the Same Month: Our Venerable Mother Theodora of Alexandria.*[^757]
*Here also is sung the Service of the Holy Hieromartyr Autonomus.*[^758]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Venerable Mother, 3, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^759]
*Sticheron:*
In a woman's body and in a man's form, thou didst accomplish manly struggles, having settled in the midst of men, condemning passions, and utterly bridling the surgings of lusts by fasting and unceasing prayers, O Theodora, and by thy divine and unwavering gazes toward God.[^760]

*Sticheron:*
When the sun set beneath the earth, it saw thee not buried; but the Unsetting Sun, the Searcher of hearts and Lord, Who sees hidden things, recognized thee, and enlightened the eyes of thy heart with the light of repentance. Therefore thou didst hasten to be well-pleasing unto Him by painful abstinence and the perfection of virtues.[^761]

*Sticheron:*
In no way understanding the enemy's scheming, thou didst love the child whom thou barest not, and with a father's tender compassion didst nourish him, O glorious one, enduring human reproach with pious thoughts, an innocent interdict in truth, O Theodora: therefore do we celebrate thine honorable festival.[^762]

*Other Stichera of Autonomus, the same Tone and Podoben:*[^763]
*Sticheron:*
Enlightened by virtues, adorned with piety, thou wast a divine hierarch, and like a multi-radiant sun thou didst traverse the world, instructing everywhere the preaching of the faith; and thou didst uproot delusion with the sickle of thy tongue, O God-wise hierarch, great preacher Autonomus![^764]

*Sticheron:*
Unto painful sufferings with a manly contest, unto bruises and wounds didst thou hasten; for showered with a multitude of stones, O Autonomus, thou didst make them as steps and a ladder: thou didst ascend unto God as a crown-bearer, and wast joined unto the army of the bodiless powers, praying for the world.[^765]

*Sticheron:*
Having accomplished thy vesture most brightly with the blood of martyrdom by the grace of the Holy Spirit, Thou didst hierarchically ascend into the Holy of Holies on high whither Jesus our Forerunner has entered: having received from God the crown of victory, together with all that have been perfected by precious blood, O Autonomus.[^766]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast, the same Tone [Tone 4], Idiomelon:*
By the angel's foretelling, the most pure fruit, from Joachim and Anna the righteous, today came forth: the Virgin, the heaven and throne of God, and the receptacle of purity, announcing joy unto all the world, the mediatress of our life, the removal of the curse, the granting of blessing. Therefore at thy nativity, O Virgin called by God, ask peace for the world, and for our souls great mercy![^767]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
*Sticheron:*
Thou didst weep from thy soul, lamenting as one childless, desiring a child; but thou hast given birth unto a child, the boast of our whole race.[^768]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [Ps. 44:11].*
*Sticheron:*
The honorable nativity of the all-pure Virgin, for whose sake the world was renewed, let us honor with hymnodic voices.[^769]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [Ps. 44:13].*
*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, ye wise, divinely-speaking prophets: for the Virgin is born, from whom the Salvation of the world is about to be born.[^770]

*Glory, both now, Tone 4:*
Let childless Anna the barren today clap her hands brightly; let earthly things wear radiance; let kings dance; let hierarchs make merry in blessings; let the whole world celebrate! For behold, the Queen and immaculate Bride of the Father hath budded forth from the root of Jesse. No longer do women bear children in sorrows: for joy hath blossomed forth, and Life lives among all men in the world. And no longer are the gifts of Joachim turned away, for Anna's lamentation is turned into joy: Rejoice with me, she says, all the chosen Israel! For behold, the Lord hath given me the living palace of His divine glory, unto common gladness and joy, and the salvation of our souls.[^771]

*Troparion of the Venerable Mother, Tone 8:*[^772]
In thee, O mother, was preserved with certainty that which is according to the image; for taking up the cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thy deeds didst teach to overlook the flesh, for it passes away, but to care for the soul, a thing immortal: therefore also with the angels rejoices thy spirit, O venerable Theodora![^773]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast of the Feast, twice; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Feast. And the usual Kathismata.*[^774]

*After the First Kathisma-Verse-Reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*[^775]
Having been born most gloriously from a barren womb, from virginal loins thou didst give birth supernaturally: for having appeared as a fair stem, thou didst sprout forth Life for the world. Therefore the heavenly powers cry unto thee, O Birthgiver of God: Glory to thy procession, O pure one! Glory to thy nativity! Glory to thy virginity, O unwedded Mother![^776]

*Glory, both now, the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma-Verse-Reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*[^777]
The rays of universal joy of thy nativity, O Virgin Mother Mary, shone forth upon the earth, and enlightened the minds of them that sing praise unto thee with love.[^778]

*Glory, both now, the same.*

*Canon of the Feast, with the Heirmos, on 6; and of the Venerable Mother, on 4; and of Autonomus, on 4.*[^779]

*Canon of the Feast, Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a hymn unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought out of Egyptian bondage: for He hath been glorified![^780]

*Troparion:*
Come, ye faithful, rejoicing in the Divine Spirit: her that today hath come forth from the barren woman for the salvation of mankind, the Ever-Virgin Maiden, let us honor with hymns.[^781]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, O pure one, Mother and handmaid of Christ God, who art the mediatress of the primal blessedness: all we of the human race worthily glorify thee with hymns.[^782]

*Troparion:*
Today is born the bridge of Life, whereby men, having found the restoration from the fall into hades, glorify Christ the Giver of life with hymns.[^783]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother, Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen Mother: and I will appear celebrating radiantly, and rejoicing I will sing her wonders.[^784]

*Troparion:*
Fill Thou my mouth with Thy praise, O Lord, as I sing Thy much-hymned glory, and honor the pains of Theodora, who was well-pleasing unto Thee by the radiance of her life.[^785]

*Troparion:*
Today Thy sacred solemnity shines forth brighter than the sun, for it enlightens souls that are in darkness, and ever drives away the demonic gloom, O right marvelous one.[^786]

*Troparion:*
The sun knew not thy setting when thou wast hidden, but the Unsetting Sun alone recognized thee as all-knowing, and enlightened the eyes of thy soul with the rays of repentance, O divinely-blessed one![^787]

*Troparion:*
Thy sin was written down, O all-honorable one, even as the gospels related; but having made haste, by the sweats of abstinence and by streams of tears thou didst blot it out.[^788]

*Theotokion:*
As an animate bridal chamber, as an incorrupt tabernacle, as the heavenly gate, as the divine table, as the palace and Master's throne, let us honor pure Mary with hymns.[^789]

*Another Canon, of the Martyr, the Acrostic whereof is: "Lawfully, O God-wise one, hast thou finished thy course." Tone 8.*[^790]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having passed through the water as if it were dry land, and escaped the Egyptian evil, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God![^791]

*Troparion:*
Brought up from infancy in the laws of the Creator, thou didst grow up in the law of virtues and the prime of piety; therefore lawfully, O father, didst thou suffer.[^792]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst arm thy mind with the weapon of patience and courage, O wise one, taking the field against the warfare of delusion, and irrecoverably conquering it.[^793]

*Troparion:*
Having appeared as a teacher of the laws of piety and of dogmas, O father, and a preacher of truth, thou wast resounded throughout all creation like an apostle, O Autonomus.[^794]

*Theotokion:*
Having known God Who appeared on earth incarnate, and having been deified by Him through grace, we sing unto thee, O Virgin, having enjoyed His gifts.[^795]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us that sing praise unto Thee.[^796]

*Troparion:*
Having lived blamelessly before God, ye gave birth unto the Salvation of all, O divinely-wise parents, having begotten her that bare the Creator and our God.[^797]

*Troparion:*
The Lord Who gushes forth life unto all brought forth the Virgin from a barren woman; in whom He was pleased to take up His abode, and after childbearing preserved her incorrupt.[^798]

*Troparion:*
Anna's fruit, Mary, who today bare the life-bearing cluster, let us sing as the Birthgiver of God, and the protectress and helper of all.[^799]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O Birthgiver of God, living and plentiful fountain: establish spiritually the band of them that sing thy praise, who have gathered themselves together, and vouchsafe unto them crowns of glory in thy divine glory.[^800]

*Troparion:*
Clothed in men's apparel, thou didst wisely hasten with diligence; and thou didst join thyself unto the honorable assembly of monks, struggling against the principalities of the evil ruler of this world.[^801]

*Troparion:*
Womanly weakness thou didst change manfully by thy calling in truth and by a new manner, showing thyself, O venerable one, through deeds to be an honorable gift desired of God.[^802]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show forth a bodiless life in a mortal body, O glorious one, maintaining unremitting abstinence, unceasing vigil, and continual prayer, O Theodora![^803]

*Theotokion:*
The storm of sin and the turmoil of unfitting thoughts trouble me. Have compassion, O all-immaculate one, and as thou art merciful stretch forth unto me a helping hand, that being saved I may magnify thee.[^804]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou art the establishment of them that run unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the Light of them that are darkened, and my spirit sings praise unto Thee.[^805]

*Troparion:*
With the showers of thy words thou didst drown the mire of passion-fraught godlessness, O hierarch, and didst refresh the faithful.[^806]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a teacher and servant of Christ, O venerable one, and a companion and partaker of His divine sufferings.[^807]

*Troparion:*
With the weapon of preaching, O venerable one, thou didst establish them that were obedient, and didst preserve unharmed them that resisted.[^808]

*Theotokion:*
A marvelous and most astounding hearing in heaven and on earth: for thou, O Birthgiver of God, didst ineffably give birth unto the Creator of all that exist.[^809]

*After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Saint [Theodora], Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Having exhausted thy body with fasts, by vigilant prayers thou didst entreat the Creator concerning thy sin, that thou mightest receive perfect forgiveness: and thou didst receive remission, having shown forth the path of repentance.[^810]

*And the Kontakion of the Saint [Autonomus], Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ):*
Blamelessly didst thou initiate into divine mysteries, O all-wise one, and wast an acceptable sacrifice, O divinely-blessed one: for thou didst drink of Christ's cup, O most glorious one, luminary of the universe, praying unceasingly for us all.[^811]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*
Having manfully endured the struggles of abstinence, thou didst cast down the crafty one, having piously lived thy life among men, O Theodora and now thou hast passed over unto God, praying for all who sacredly celebrate thy holy dormition.[^812]

*Glory, of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
A radiant crown of incorruption hath Christ granted thee, O all-blessed one, as a sufferer and honorable hierarch, O Autonomus: for unto Him thou didst offer bloodless sacrifices, unfeignedly imitating His divine holiness; and of His ageless sweetness, O blessed one, hast thou tasted.[^813]

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезна́чальное):*
Joachim and Anna keep festival, for worthily did they find grace after their affliction, and gave birth unto the fruit that was an acceptable temple of God, the Virgin and pure Mother of God, the only blessed one, who unceasingly prays that our souls may be saved.[^814]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, Who alone art the Lover of mankind.[^815]

*Troparion:*
We sing praise unto Thee, O Lord, Who hast given her that bare Thee as a saving haven unto all the faithful.[^816]

*Troparion:*
Christ showed thee forth, O Bride of God, as the boast and dominion unto all that faithfully sing thy mystery.[^817]

*Theotokion:*
O unwedded Sovereign Lady, being delivered from transgressions through thy prayers, we all prudently call thee blessed.[^818]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Perceiving the unsearchable divine counsel of Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Thou Most High, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^819]

*Troparion:*
For many days, O glorious one, thou didst valiantly endure fasting as if bodiless, while Christ strengthened thy weakness by His almighty will and nourished thee with divine grace.[^820]

*Troparion:*
Look upon my humility and weeping, behold my affliction, and lighten the heavy burden of my sin! cried Theodora unto Him Who alone is able to save.[^821]

*Troparion:*
