Having drowned with the showers of thy tears him that craftily tripped thee with ensnarement, by valor thou didst conquer the hunter of souls, sheltered by divine grace in the haven, O glorious one.[^822]

*Theotokion:*
O all-marvelous Mother of God, shine forth upon me the ray of repentance; dispel the gloom of mine immeasurable evils, and drive away from my heart the evil thoughts, O Virgin![^823]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead.[^824]

*Troparion:*
Having the Lord as an assisting champion in the divine warfare, by thy struggles, O father, thou didst conquer the ancient enemy of earthly men.[^825]

*Troparion:*
Bowing down in diligent searching, O father, into the depths of the divine hidden treasures, from thence thou didst learn His ineffable mysteries.[^826]

*Troparion:*
At the catechizing of thy words, the idol shrines fell down, O wise one, and the schools of delusion were consumed by the fire of thy commands.[^827]

*Troparion:*
The flame of thy teachings was lifted up unto an exalted life, O wise one, revealing thee unto the ends of the earth as an unerring guide unto God.[^828]

*Theotokion:*
Cleanse with thy prayers them that have been defiled by passions, O Birthgiver of God, and count us worthy with pure thoughts to sing thy nativity.[^829]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Having dispersed the shadow-written gloom of enigmas, and having enlightened the hearts of the faithful through the divine Maiden at the arrival of truth: do Thou also guide us by Thy light, O Christ![^830]

*Troparion:*
Let us, O ye peoples, sing praise unto the Cause of all, the Author of that which has come to pass for our sake: in whose prefiguration the prophets rejoiced when they were counted worthy, bringing forth the manifest salvation from her.[^831]

*Troparion:*
The budding from the dry priest's rod showed forth the fore-discernment unto Israel; and now the radiance of them that have budded forth shines most gloriously: the all-glorious birth from a barren woman.[^832]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
All things were amazed at thy divine glory: for thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in thy womb the God Who is over all, and gavest birth unto the timeless Son, Who grants peace unto all that sing praise unto thee.[^833]

*Troparion:*
The ranks of the bodiless were astonished, beholding thee in an earthly body imitating their life and honorable conversation, and surmounting the enemy who of old tripped thee with deceit, O Theodora.[^834]

*Troparion:*
God subjected unto Thee the attacks of wild beasts, having given Thee the grace of healings: this she proclaims who was delivered by thy hand from being devoured by a savage beast, which having been crushed thou didst heal, O glorious one.[^835]

*Troparion:*
With a mature mind thou didst nurse the babe, enduring cruel calumny, giving thanks unto the Almighty Who gave thee *Troparion:*
...power, and Who made thee marvelous, O all-praised Theodora![^836]

*Theotokion:*
The strength and establishment of my infirm heart art thou, O unwedded Virgin, an insurmountable rampart against the face of the enemy, saving me from all perils and conquering the regiments of the fierce adversary.[^837]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and with Thy lofty arm grant us Thy peace, O Lover of mankind![^838]

*Troparion:*
The noetic Light enlightened thee, O Autonomus, and having the word of life, revealed thee as a lamp unto all the ends of the earth.[^839]

*Troparion:*
Having drawn forth the voice of God as a sword, thou didst cut down the host of falsely named wisdom, O father Autonomus.[^840]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst exhaust the enemy's whole quiver of arrows, and didst make a show of all that armed themselves against thee, O blessed Autonomus.[^841]

*Theotokion:*
New and most glorious things have come to pass, O all-honorable one: for through thee God appeared in the flesh upon earth, and we earthly ones have been deified.[^842]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
From the sea monster Jonah cried unto the Lord: Lead me up, I pray, from the depth of hades, that as unto my Deliverer I may sacrifice unto Thee in the voice of praise and the spirit of truth![^843]

*Troparion:*
In the grief of childlessness the divinely-wise parents of the Mother of God cried unto the Lord: and they gave birth unto her for generations of generations, unto common salvation and praise.[^844]

*Troparion:*
A worthy heavenly gift did the divinely-wise parents of the Mother of God receive from God: a carriage exalted above the Cherubim themselves, the mother who bare the Word and Creator.[^845]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, O ye divinely-wise, come, let us clap our hands, and glorify God Who was born of her![^846]

*Troparion:*
Offering a fountain of tears unceasingly, afflicting thyself and groaning, with thanksgiving didst thou endure the monks' interdict and separation, O divinely-blessed one.[^847]

*Troparion:*
Having thy drink from the sea and nourishing thyself with wild herbs, dwelling with wild beasts in the desert, thou didst live as if in heaven, O right marvelous one.[^848]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst endure the burning of the sun and the chill of the night, warmed by the grace of the Divine Spirit; therefore dost thou enjoy the blessedness on high.[^849]

*Theotokion:*
The divine jar and table the divine jar and table, which carried the Bread of life, the untilled field, the holy mountain, the Virgin Birthgiver of God, let us glorify with hymns.[^850]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray: for unto Thee have I cried, and hear me, O God of my salvation![^851]

*Troparion:*
The power of the Comforter strengthened thee, O wise one, even as the disciples of old, and armed thee with a fiery tongue, O Autonomus, to enlighten earthly men and to consume ungodliness with fire.[^852]

*Troparion:*
Though infantile in soul-directed wisdom, O venerable father, in bodily infirmity thou didst with valiant power receive supernatural struggles and unslackening labor for the preaching.[^853]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst lay beneath the feet of the pious the head of the enemy that was lifted up against the Creator, having by grace armed them against him through faith in thy words.[^854]

*Theotokion:*
Desiring through thee to heal the crushings of nature, the Creator and Maker, O Birthgiver of God, gave thee as divine medicine unto them that flee unto thee in infirmities.[^855]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Joachim and Anna were freed from the reproach of childlessness, and Adam and Eve from the corruption of death, O all-pure one, in thy holy nativity. This do thy people also celebrate, having been delivered from the guilt of transgressions, when they cry unto thee: The barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life![^856]

*Ikos:*
The prayer together with the sighing over the barrenness and childlessness of Joachim and Anna was acceptable unto God, and entered into the ears of the Lord, and sprouted forth a life-bearing fruit for the world. For the one offered prayer on the mountain, and the other bore reproach in the garden; yet with joy the barren woman gives birth unto the Birthgiver of God and the nourisher of our life.[^857]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The bush unconsumed by fire upon the mountain, and the dew-bearing Chaldean furnace, manifestly prefigured thee, O Bride of God: for thou didst unconsumed receive the divine immaterial Fire in a material womb. Therefore unto Him Who was born of thee do we sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^858]

*Troparion:*
The lawgiver was forbidden to comprehend that which concerns thee in material visions, and the great mystery, O all-pure one, being typically instructed of old not to mind earthly zeal *Troparion:*
...therefore amazed at the wonder, he said: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^859]

*Troparion:*
A mountain and heavenly gate and noetic ladder did the divine choir divinely call thee: for from thee a stone was cut out without hands of men, and a door through which passed the Lord, the God of wonders of our fathers.[^860]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The divinely-wise served not the creature rather than the Creator, but manfully trampling down the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, the all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers![^861]

*Troparion:*
With intolerable wounds did the crafty enemy afflict thee, fancying himself in apparitions; but thou didst cast down his fierce rage, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^862]

*Troparion:*
Dry ditches didst thou fill with water by thy prayers, O glorious one, manifestly working wonders and magnifying God Who glorified thee, unto Whom we cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^863]

*Troparion:*
Them that celebrate thy memory, O glorious one, do thou ever remember with great boldness, entreating God the All-Compassionate, unto Whom we call: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^864]

*Theotokion:*
O Virgin who barest Christ the King: have compassion and save me who am shaken by passions; establish me in faith and guide me unto the saving path, O Salvation of the faithful![^865]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Having arrived from Judea in Babylon of old, by faith in the Trinity the children trampled down the flame of the furnace, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^866]

*Troparion:*
Having gathered together into one the choirs of piety, O father Autonomus, them that were enlightened through faith by thy words, thou didst teach to cry unceasingly: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^867]

*Troparion:*
With unslackening courage, O martyr, thou didst endure the commands of the godless that were established in the souls of the unbelievers; and from their foundations didst thou uproot them, O wise one, establishing grace in their hearts.[^868]

*Troparion:*
Muffled together with the anointing of thy priesthood, O father Autonomus, was divine suffering: for thy blood showed thee forth as a radiant hierarch unto them that faithfully cry: Blessed art Thou, O Christ![^869]

*Theotokion:*
He Who fashioned human nature from the earth, as Creator and God, renews it when corrupted *Theotokion:*
...taking it from thee, O Mother of God, and vouchsafes unto it mystical adoption as sons, O pure one.[^870]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
In the children's furnace Thou didst of old prefigure Thy Mother, O Lord: and this image snatched them out of the fire as they entered unburnt; her do we sing, who through Thee hath appeared today unto the ends of the earth, and we highly exalt Him unto all ages.[^871]

*Troparion:*
The predestined tabernacle of our reconciliation unto God now begins her being, as she is about to give birth unto the Word Who appeared unto us in the grossness of the flesh: Whom we sing, having received through Him existence out of non-existence, and we highly exalt Him unto all ages.[^872]

*Troparion:*
The transformation of barrenness loosed the worldly barrenness of good things, and manifestly showed forth the wonder of Christ, Who came unto earthly men: Whom we sing, having received through Him existence out of non-existence, and we highly exalt Him unto all ages.[^873]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The childbirth of the Birthgiver of God saved the pious children in the furnace: then prefigured, but now accomplished, it moves the whole world to sing unto Thee: Sing unto the Lord, all ye works, and highly exalt Him unto all ages![^874]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened with a pure mind, thy leader was caught up and beheld the good things which the Lord had prepared for Thee: the light-resembling paradise and the ineffable bridal chamber, O Theodora, wherein the Bridegroom, the Bestower of awards, settled Thee.[^875]

*Troparion:*
The choirs of angels, martyrs, and venerable saints, leading thy soul, bore it unto the heavenly mansions, unto the resting-place of them that make merry, wherein is the dwelling of them that cry out and highly exalt Christ unto the ages.[^876]

*Troparion:*
The multitude of monks, having assembled, bury thy blessed body in faith: for having seen most glorious things, they recognized what was extraordinary: that though a woman in body, thou wast well-pleased to live in the midst of men, sheltered by the hand of the Almighty, O divinely-wise Theodora.[^877]

*Troparion:*
Enduring in all-night prayers, thou didst lull to sleep the stirrings of passions, and didst fall asleep with a sleep like unto the righteous, and passed over unto the unwaning dawn, singing: Sing unto the Lord, all ye works, and highly exalt Him unto the ages![^878]

*Theotokion:*
After thee ran the women, perceiving sweet-scented myrrh, O all-pure Bride of God, unwedded Maiden[^879] unwedded: truly reigning together with thee and with Thy only-begotten Son Who shone forth from thy womb, singing of Christ unto the ages.[^880]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Who is the Heavenly King, Whom the angelic hosts hymn: praise and highly exalt Him unto all ages![^881]

*Troparion:*
As thou wast strengthened in Christ, the might of the tormentors fell, O divinely-wise one; for unto them thou wast fearsome in the Spirit.[^882]

*Troparion:*
With valiance of mind thou didst expose the rottenness of delusion, O all-blessed one, showing forth strength in the deeds of piety.[^883]

*Troparion:*
The rivers of thy wonders poured forth, and showed thee to be an abyss of healings in the world, O father, pouring forth grace.[^884]

*Theotokion:*
Thy grace, O Virgin, hath truly been pre-eminently glorified in signs upon the earth: for marvelous is the wonder of thy childbirth.[^885]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thee who ineffably didst give flesh from virginal loins unto God Who shone forth before the sun as a luminary, and came in the flesh unto us: O blessed, all-pure one, thee, O Mother of God, do we magnify.[^886]

*Troparion:*
He Who poured forth water from the rock for an intractable people, grants unto the well-submissive nations from barren loins a fruit for our gladness, thee, O all-pure Mother of God, whom we worthily magnify.[^887]

*Troparion:*
The remover of the ancient unjust condemnation and restoration of the foremother; who art the cause of our race's reconciliation unto God, the bridge unto the Creator: thee, O Mother of God, do we magnify.[^888]

*Canon of the Venerable Mother. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened in spirit; and let the nature of immaterial minds celebrate, honoring the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and let it cry: Rejoice, O all-blessed Birthgiver of God, pure Ever-Virgin![^889]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst set as a star from the world, O all-praised one, and didst shine forth in otherworldly life, leaving as beams unto us the virtues and corrections of thy life, enlightening the hearts of all that faithfully celebrate thy memory.[^890]

*Troparion:*
The heavenly gates were brightly opened, receiving thee, and the Church of the firstborn now holds thy sacred soul, keeping festival with the elect, O ever-memorable Theodora, where is the voice of them that feast and the unwaning light.[^891]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast found the recompense of thy labors as thou didst hope for heavenly honor; thou didst bring desire to rest, having found the fountain of good things wherein thou delightest, beholding the Bridegroom more clearly and purely, O Theodora, even as the angels were vouchsafed to behold Him.[^892]

*Troparion:*
Loosing of hardships, deliverance from passions, and correction of life, do thou ask, O ever-memorable one, to be sent down upon them that praise thee and celebrate thy honorable memory, having boldness before the Lord, O honorable and glorious Theodora.[^893]

*Theotokion:*
Save me, O pure one, who didst bear the Savior and the All-Compassionate; have compassion on thy servant and direct me unto the paths of repentance; drive far away the temptations of the evil one from my midst, and deliver me from his ensnarement, O Mother of God, helper of the faithful.[^894]

*Canon of the Martyr. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Truly do we confess thee as the Mother of God, who are saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs.[^895]

*Troparion:*
Flying unto the height of piety, borne aloft by virtues, O Autonomus, by suffering thou didst ascend unto Christ, O father.[^896]

*Troparion:*
Thy labors sown with tears, O divinely-wise one, multiplied unshakeable fruits of joy and glory, and of sweetness which is in Christ Jesus.[^897]

*Troparion:*
Lawfully vouchsafed crowns and divine gifts, O hierarch Autonomus, by thy prayers thou dost establish us in divine laws.[^898]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth unto Life and incorruption, O Virgin, Who made victors over death them that truly magnify thee as Mother of God.[^899]

*Exapostilarion of the Feast, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃или́щи):*
From the barren and aged, advanced in years Anna, the Life and divine Light, the all-immaculate Maiden, the gate of the East, who ineffably shone forth Light unto the ends of the earth, forming a choir, let us call her blessed as higher than earthly mortals.[^900]

*Glory, both now: The same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Нбⷭ҇ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
*Sticheron:*
From Anna today hath blossomed forth the flower, the divinely-given garden, the Mother of God, the salvation of mankind; from whom beyond understanding is born the Creator of all, Who, being good, in His goodness cleanses all the defilement of Adam.[^901]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear [Ps. 44:11].*
*Sticheron:*
Who is able worthily to hymn the Virgin who ineffably is an infant from Anna? Let the mountains therefore and hills drop sweetness today; for the Life and Cleansing of all, the pure Mother of God, is nourished with milk.[^902]

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance [Ps. 44:13].*
*Sticheron:*
She that was formerly childless and barren gives birth unto the Life of all, the only Mother of God, and is filled with gladness; and earthly human nature now rejoices, glorifying the true Mother of the Deliverer, Jesus, the only Lord.[^903]

*Glory, both now, Tone 8:*
On the notable day of our feast, let us sound the trumpet on the spiritual pipe; for she who is of the seed of David is born today, the Mother of Life, dispelling darkness: the renewal of Adam and calling back of Eve, the fountain of incorruption, the release from corruption; through whom we have been deified and delivered from death. And let us cry aloud unto her with Gabriel, O ye faithful: Rejoice, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee, for thy sake granting us great mercy![^904]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 7 and 8, on 8.*[^905]

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
*God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel [Ps. 67:36].*
*Verse: In the congregations bless ye God [Ps. 67:27].*[^906]

*Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 208 (Gal. 3:23–29):*
*Brethren: Before faith came...*[^907]

*Alleluia, Tone 4:*
*With patience I waited for the Lord, and He inclined unto me [Ps. 39:2].*[^908]

*Gospel according to John, Pericope 28 (Jn. 8:3–11):*
*At that time, the scribes and Pharisees brought...*[^909]

*Communion Hymn:*
*In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be [Ps. 111:6].*[^910]

*(Conclusion of the Twelfth Day: Decorative woodcut tailpiece with floral rosette) In the Same Month, on the Twelfth Day: Holy Hieromartyr Autonomus:*[^911]
*On this day the Feast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Mother of God is given leave, and the entire service is of the Feast.*[^912]
*In the evening, the usual Kathisma chanting. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, on 6. Glory, both now, of the Feast. (If it be on Friday evening: Glory, of the Feast; Both now, the Dogmatic Theotokion of the current Tone.) The Prokeimenon of the day, without Entrance and without Old Testament readings. Then "Vouchsafe, O Lord," and the litany "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha, Stichera, and Glory, both now, of the Feast. After "Our Father," Troparion of the Feast. Then litany, and dismissal. At Compline, the Kontakion of the Feast. At Midnight Office we chant according to custom, with the Kathisma, and the usual troparia, and not of the Feast. And we say the prayer: "Remember, O Lord, in hope..."*[^913]
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, twice; Glory, both now, the same. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Feast, and reading. Psalm 50. Canon of the Feast, the first with the Heirmos on 8, and the second with the Heirmos on 6. And we chant the Heirmoi of both canons twice. Katavasia: "Tracing the cross..." After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast, twice. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast. At Ode 9, we do not chant the "More honorable," but we chant the refrains of the Feast. At the Katavasia gathering: "Thou art a mystical [paradise]..." and the other, "Through the eating of the tree..." with the refrains of the Feast. Exapostilarion of the Feast, twice. At the Praises, Stichera of the Feast on 4. Glory, both now, of the Feast. Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Feast, once. And the litanies, and dismissal. And the exit into the narthex. And the First Hour. At the Hours, Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.*[^914]
*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes of both canons, Ode 4, on 8. After the Entrance, Troparion of the Feast. Glory, both now, Kontakion of the Feast. Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel of the day and of the Feast.*[^915]
*It is fitting to know: If the Apodosis of the Nativity of the Mother of God happen on a Sunday:*[^916]
*On Saturday at Little Vespers, the Sunday Stichera according to custom. At the Aposticha, one Sunday Sticheron, and the Aposticha of the Feast with their own refrains from Great Vespers. Glory, both now, of the Feast.*[^917]

*Sunday Troparion. Glory, both now, of the Feast.*[^918]
*At Great Vespers: After the usual Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Sunday Stichera, 3; and Anatolian [Eastern], 1; and of the Feast, 6, which are sung on the Feast itself. Glory, of the Feast; Both now, the first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. At the Litiya, Stichera, and Glory, both now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Sunday Stichera; Glory, both now, of the Feast. At the Blessing of the Loaves, Troparion: "Birthgiver of God and Virgin," twice; and of the Feast, once. And a reading from the Epistles of the Apostles.*[^919]
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Sunday Troparion, twice; Glory, both now, of the Feast. After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia. And a reading from the Commentary Gospel, Sunday before the Exaltation. Then the Polyeleos [Amomos]. And the Hypakoe of the Tone. And a reading, Sunday in order. The Hymns of Ascent [Stepénna], and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath." The Sunday Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. The Sunday Sticheron. And the rest according to custom. Canon: Sunday with the Heirmos on 4; and of the Mother of God on 2; and of the Feast, both canons on 8. Katavasia: "Tracing the cross..." After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and Sessional Hymn of the Feast, twice. After Ode 6, Sunday Kontakion and Ikos. And the Prologue [Synaxarion]. At Ode 9 we sing the "More honorable." Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory, both now, of the Feast. At the Praises, Sunday Stichera on 4; and of the Feast with the Doxasticon on 4, with the refrains of the Feast. Glory: the Gospel Sticheron; Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday Troparion only. Litanies, and dismissal, and the Catechesis of St. Theodore the Studite, and the usual exit into the narthex. And the First Hour. And the final dismissal. At the Hours, the Sunday Troparion; Glory, of the Feast; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," Kontakion of the Feast and the Sunday Kontakion, saying them alternately.*[^920]
*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6, and of the Feast, Ode 9 on 4. After the Entrance, the Sunday Troparion and of the Feast. Glory: the Sunday Kontakion; Both now: of the Feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Sunday before the Exaltation, and the Sunday in course under one pericope. Then of the Mother of God. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens." Another, of the Feast: "I will take the cup of salvation."*[^921]

*In the Same Month, on the Thirteenth Day:*[^922]
*The Commemoration of the Dedication of the Holy Church of the Resurrection of Christ our God; and the Forefeast of the Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross; and the Holy Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion:*[^923]
*In the evening, the usual Kathisma chanting. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6: of the Dedication, 3, Tone 6, Idiomela:*
*Sticheron:*
To honor dedications is an ancient law and one well-established, and rather to honor new things by renewals. For the isles are renewed unto God, as Isaiah says [Isa. 41:1], which are to be understood as the churches from the Gentiles, now established and receiving firm maintenance from God. Therefore let us also spiritually celebrate the present dedication.[^924]

*Sticheron:*
Be renewed, brethren, and having put off the old man, live in newness of life, placing a bridle on all things whence comes death; let us chastise all our members, hating all evil eating of the tree, and remembering this only, that we may flee the things of old. So let man be renewed; thus is the day of dedication honored.[^925]

*Sticheron, by Anatolius:*
Thou didst place Thy Church as a pillar of strength, O Christ, O Pre-eternal Word, for Thou didst found her upon the rock of the faith; therefore she abides unshaken unto the age, having Thee Who for her sake in the last times didst immutably become man. Giving thanks therefore, we hymn Thee, saying: Thou art before the ages, and unto the age, and still further, our King: glory to Thee![^926]

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
*Sticheron:*
Christ, having looked down upon thy good deeds and divine prayers, O Cornelius, sent unto thee a holy angel who enlightened thee wholly, and the supreme of the sacred Apostles [Peter], renewing thee with all thy house with water and the Spirit, O glorious one, and instructing thee in better things by the grace of the Spirit.[^927]

*Sticheron:*
Anointed with the chrism of the priesthood, thou didst run to proclaim the saving preaching unto the nations; and thou didst uproot the thorns of delusion, O divinely-wise one, planting unbeguiling doctrine in souls in souls by the Spirit; therefore we call thee blessed, as a God-pleasing hierarch and unconquered martyr, rejoicing, O Cornelius.[^928]

*Sticheron:*
Following the pattern of thy goodness, the unwise showed themselves to be prudent; and though dead and dwelling in the tomb according to the law of nature, O blessed one, thou makest it a fountain of many wonders, O wise Cornelius, healing the sick and driving away the spirits of wickedness by the Holy Spirit, O divinely-inspired one.[^929]

*Glory, of the Dedication, Tone 6, Idiomelon, by John the Monk:*
Celebrating the memory of the Dedication, O Lord, glorifying Thee the Giver of holiness, we pray: let the senses of our souls be sanctified through the prayers of the glorious passion-bearers, O Good One, Almighty![^930]

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone:*
Today the Tree hath appeared; today the Hebrew race is perished; today the faith is made manifest by faithful kings; and Adam fell through the tree, and again through the Tree demons trembled: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee![^931]

*If it be on Friday evening: Both now, the first Dogmatic Theotokion of the current Tone.*
*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and readings.*[^932]
*Reading from the Third Book of Kings (1 Kings 8:22–23, 27–30):*
Solomon stood before the presence of the altar of the Lord, before all the congregation of Israel, and having spread forth his hands unto heaven, he said: O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like Thee, in heaven above and upon earth beneath. If indeed the heaven and the heaven of heavens will not suffice Thee, how much less this house which I have built unto Thy name? Yet look upon my prayer, O Lord God of Israel, to give ear unto the supplication and prayer wherewith Thy servant prays before Thee toward Thee today; that Thine eyes may be open upon this house day and night, upon this place whereof Thou saidst: My name shall be there; to give ear unto the prayer wherewith Thy servant prays in this place, day and night; and to give ear unto the supplication of Thy servant and of Thy people Israel. Whatsoever things they shall pray toward Thee in this place, do Thou also hear in the place of Thy dwelling in heaven, and do, and be merciful unto them.[^933]

*Reading from Proverbs (Prov. 3:19–26):*
God by wisdom founded the earth, and prepared the heavens by understanding. By His knowledge the depths were broken up, and the clouds dropped dew. My son, let them not pass from thee, but keep my counsel and understanding thought, that thy soul may live and grace may be upon thy neck; and it shall be healing unto thy flesh, and care unto thy bones. That thou mayest walk trusting in peace in all thy ways, and thy foot shall not stumble. For if thou sit down, thou shalt be without fear; and if thou sleep, thou shalt sleep sweetly. And thou shalt not fear sudden terror, neither the rushing onslaught of the ungodly when it comes. For the Lord shall be in all thy ways, and He shall establish thy foot that thou be not shaken. Refuse not to do good unto him that has need, whenever thy hand is able to help. Say not: Go and come again, and tomorrow I will give, when thou art able to do good; for thou knowest not what the coming day will bring forth. Devise not evil against thy friend who dwells beside thee and trusts in thee. Contend not with a man without cause, lest he do some evil unto thee. Gain not the reproaches of evil men, neither emulate their ways. For every transgressor of the law is unclean before the Lord, and does not associate with the righteous. The curse of the Lord is in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed. The Lord resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.[^934]

*Reading from Proverbs (Prov. 9:1–11):*
Wisdom hath built for herself a house, and hath set up seven pillars. She hath slaughtered her sacrifice, and mingled her wine in her bowl, and prepared her table. She hath sent forth her servants, calling with a lofty proclamation unto the bowl, saying: Whosoever is foolish, let him turn aside unto me. And unto them that lack understanding she said: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled for you. Forsake folly, and ye shall live, and seek understanding that ye may live, and rectify understanding in knowledge. He that instructs the evil shall receive dishonor unto himself, and he that reproves an ungodly man gets himself a blot. For reproof unto an ungodly man is wounds unto him. Reprove not evil men, lest they hate thee; reprove a wise man, and he will love thee. Give occasion unto a wise man, and he will be yet wiser; instruct a righteous man, and he will add to receiving it. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of the saints is understanding. For to know the Law is the property of a good mind. For by this means thou shalt live a long time, and years of life shall be added unto thee.[^935]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, life-bearing Cross" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ живоно́сный крⷭ҇тъ):*
*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, life-bearing Cross, unconquerable victory of piety the gate of paradise, the establishment of the faithful, the rampart of the Church; whereby corruption was destroyed and brought to nought, and the power of death was trampled down, and we were raised up from earth unto heavenly things. An invincible weapon, adversary of demons, glory of martyrs, truly the ornament of the venerable, haven of salvation: grant unto the world great mercy![^936]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy [Ps. 98:5].*
*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, O Cross of the Lord, whereby mankind was released from the curse, token of true joy; who drivest away enemies at thine exaltation, O all-honorable one, helper unto us, might of kings, strength of the righteous, majesty of priests; which being depicted, deliverest from cruel evils; rod of strength whereby we are shepherded, weapon of peace, which angels surround with fear; divine glory of Christ, Who grants unto the world great mercy![^937]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages, He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [Ps. 73:12].*
*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, guide of the blind, physician of the infirm, resurrection of all the dead, who didst raise up us that were fallen into corruption, O precious Cross; whereby the curse was destroyed, and incorruption blossomed forth, and we on earth were deified, and the devil was utterly cast down. Today beholding thee exalted by the hands of the hierarch, we exalt Him Who was exalted upon thee, and we worship thee, drawing abundantly great mercy![^938]

*Glory, of the Dedication, Tone 2, by Anatolius:*
Celebrating the Dedication of the all-sacred temple of Thy Resurrection, we glorify Thee, O Lord, Who didst sanctify it and perfect it by Thine all-perfect grace, and Who adornest it with the mystical and sacred sacrifices offered by the faithful; Who acceptest from the hands of Thy servants the bloodless and all-pure sacrifices, and grantest unto them that rightly offer them the cleansing of sins and great mercy.[^939]

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone:*
The divine treasure hidden in the earth, the Cross of the Life-Giver, was shown forth in the heavens unto the pious Emperor [Constantine], and spiritually reveals the inscription of victory over enemies. Having joyfully ascended unto the height of vision with faith and love, by his zeal he brought it forth from the bowels of the earth for the redemption of the world of the world, and the salvation of our souls.[^940]

*Troparion of the Dedication, Tone 4:*
As Thou didst show forth the splendor of the firmament above, so hast Thou also shown the beauty of the holy tabernacle of Thy glory below, O Lord; establish it unto ages of ages, and accept our supplications continually offered unto Thee therein, through the Mother of God, O Life and Resurrection of all![^941]

*Glory, of the Martyr, Tone 4:*
As a sharer of the apostolic ways and a successor to their thrones, thou didst find action as an ascent unto divine vision, O God-inspired one; therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, thou didst also suffer for the faith even unto blood, O hieromartyr Cornelius: entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved![^942]

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone:*
The life-giving Cross of Thy goodness, which Thou hast granted unto us unworthy ones, O Lord, we offer unto Thee in supplication: save Thy people and Thy city that entreat Thee through the Mother of God, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind![^943]

*At Matins, after the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Behold, Christ hath enlightened by His coming, He hath renewed the world by His divine Spirit; souls are renewed, for the house is now dedicated unto the glory of the Lord, wherein Christ our God also renews the hearts of the faithful, unto the salvation of mankind.[^944]

*Glory, both now: The same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Today the festal day of the dedication hath overtaken us, the faithful, commanding all of Christ's flock pre-eminently to be renewed, and with radiant countenance faithfully to hymn a song from the depths of the heart unto the Good One: as unto our Deliverer and the One Who renews us.[^945]

*Glory, both now: The same.*

*Three Canons: of the Dedication with the Heirmos on 6; of the Forefeast on 4; and of the Saint on 4.*
*Canon of the Dedication, the composition of John the Monk, Tone 4:*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the watery deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet of old, ancient Israel conquered the might of Amalek in the wilderness by Moses' hands stretched out in the form of a cross.[^946]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who of old didst guide chosen Israel by a pillar, O Christ, hast planted the Church in Zion through the bath of baptism, as she cries: Let us sing a hymn unto our God![^947]

*Troparion:*
Today the coming of Thine unapproachable glory made the temple erected unto Thee on earth as heaven, wherein with one accord we sing a hymn unto our God.[^948]

*Troparion:*
The Church of the Lord is adorned not by the law, nor by the stretching forth of slavish hands, but glorying in the grace of the Cross, she sings unto Thee: Let us sing a hymn unto our God![^949]

*Theotokion:*
Without seed, by the Father's will, from the Divine Spirit thou didst conceive the Son of God, and didst bear Him in the flesh: Him Who from the Father is without mother, and for our sake from thee without father.[^950]

*Another Canon of the Forefeast, alphabetical, without Theotokia, the composition of Joseph, the same Tone:*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, drown the three parts of my soul in the deep of passionlessness, I pray Thee, like the mighty captains, that unto Thee as on a timbrel, in the mortification of the body, I may sing a triumphal hymn.[^951]

*Troparion:*
Let heaven be glad and let the earth rejoice, for the all-holy Cross comes forth, sanctifying by grace us that kiss it as a fountain of holiness and the cause of the deification of all.[^952]

*Troparion:*
Strengthen us, O all-holy Cross, that faithfully worship thee, to tread piously upon the heavenly path, that turning away from the abysses of the adversaries, we may become partakers of divine glory.[^953]

*Troparion:*
Having become known unto the Creator through thee, O all-honorable Cross, with heart and soul we ever embrace thee, beholding thee lying before us, and we are enlightened in mind, glorifying the Word, the Cause of all.[^954]

*Theotokion:*
O City of God the Universal King, honorable treasure acceptable unto God, O all-immaculate Mother of God: preserve thine inheritance that ever praises thee and honors thy nativity with faith.[^955]

*Another Canon to the Saint, the acrostic whereof is: "I sing the glory of thy wonders, O blessed one." The composition of Joseph. Tone 2:*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Christ, Who shatters wars with a high arm, shook off horse and rider into the Red Sea, and He saved Israel, as they sang a song of victory.[^956]

*Troparion:*
Enlighten by thy prayers, O divinely-blessed hierarch, those that celebrate this thy light-bearing and divine dormition, and all-radiant memory, and sacred solemnity.[^957]

*Troparion:*
Even before being perfectly instructed in the mysteries, O wise Cornelius, thou didst show thyself occupied in almsgiving and prayers, O all-blessed one, seeking the Lord of all in uprightness of mind occupied in almsgiving and prayers, O all-blessed one, seeking the Lord of all in uprightness of mind.[^958]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast manifestly taught the saving laws of Him Who united Himself unto flesh through surpassing goodness, when the chief of the Apostles, by the Master's nod, taught thee, O blessed one.[^959]

*Theotokion:*
Thou dost inflame the hearts of the faithful ever to glorify thee with insatiable love, O Sovereign Birthgiver of God: for thou art the glory of mankind, having given birth unto the Lord of glory, O pure one.[^960]

*Katavasia: Having traced a cross...*[^961]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and refuge, and establishment![^962]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast sanctified Thy Church on earth by the Spirit, O Christ, anointing her today with the oil of Thy rejoicing.[^963]

*Troparion:*
Today, O Lord, beyond understanding, Thou hast shown forth the handmade tabernacle to be the house of Thy glory, fashioned with divine economy.[^964]

*Troparion:*
Having Thee, O Christ, as an indestructible foundation, the Church is crowned with Thy Cross as with a royal diadem.[^965]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone on earth, O Mother of God, hast been the mediatress of blessings that transcend nature; therefore we offer unto thee: Rejoice![^966]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast, but in Thee, the Father's hypostatic Wisdom, O Christ: for there is none holy besides Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^967]

*Troparion:*
Glorifying in Thee the glory of Christ that hath come to pass, we glorify Him with faith, O most glorious Cross of the Lord, by the honorable embracing of Thee, and we are enlightened.[^968]

*Troparion:*
Having come with gladness, O faithful, let us draw as from a pure fountain the waters of the Cross that quicken again, and being saved, let us praise God.[^969]

*Troparion:*
Jesus, Who is Life, was suspended and put to death upon the tree of the Cross; embracing it now with faith, we drive away the passions, the ministers of death.[^970]

*Theotokion:*
Drive away outer darkness from my soul, break the bonds of sin, O pure Virgin, and save me, who didst bear the All-Merciful One.[^971]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing by Thy command, and didst suspend what was uncontrollably heavy, establish Thy Church upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind.[^972]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst receive the illumination of the Holy Spirit and divine grace from divine lips, receiving it all with thine entire household at the coming of the divine chief of the Apostles, who proclaimed the saving teachings.[^973]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast exalted in virtues like a high-grown cedar, and didst bring forth sweet-smelling fruits for us: the dispensing of teachings, the grace of wonders, and the working of healings, O blessed hierarch Cornelius.[^974]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast deemed worthy of greatest glorious renown, O Cornelius; with the chief [Apostle] and many others thou didst run, preaching everywhere the divine proclamation, whereby being enlightened, we were delivered from the darkness of ignorance.[^975]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the radiant dwelling-place of purity, bearing the Giver of light incarnate, Who appeared as man like unto us because of His love for mankind, and Who destroyed corruption, O all-pure Virgin, Bride of God, the incorruptible restoration of men.[^976]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Яви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
The Church is shown to be a heaven of many lights, enlightening all the faithful, wherein standing we cry: Establish this house, O Lord![^977]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded" (Повелѣ́нное):*
Christ showed forth the tabernacle of testimony, and divine Moses pitched it on earth, and Solomon renewed the temple with sacrifices; and we, fleeing with faith unto the new Jerusalem, let us give Davidic divine praise unto Him Who was crucified for our sake, asking forgiveness of all wherein we have sinned.[^978]

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Яви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
The holy Church received thee as firstfruits from the Gentiles, enlightening her by thy virtuous deeds, O sacred initiate of mysteries, divinely-wise Cornelius.[^979]

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆дивле́нїе І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Moses stretched forth his hands unto the height of heaven, prefiguring the Cross, the divine weapon of the faithful, whereon Christ nailed sins. Therefore the enemy wept in suffering, painfully crying with his senses: The wooden spear pierced me in the midst of my heart; Christ looses all from the bonds of hades![^980]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^981]

*Troparion:*
Not with sacrifices of irrational beasts, but with Thy precious, life-bearing blood from Thy side is the Church sprinkled, fittingly crying: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^982]

*Troparion:*
The beloved dwellings of the Lord, unto those that desire to behold openly the glory of His countenance, cry with one accord: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^983]

*Troparion:*
Prefiguring the anointing of Thy chosen people, the Church is anointed today with precious myrrh, invisibly receiving the divine grace of the Spirit.[^984]

*Theotokion:*
Without experience of wedlock thou didst give birth, O Virgin, and after childbirth thou didst appear still a virgin; therefore with unceasing voices we cry unto thee with undoubted faith, O Lady: Rejoice![^985]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
For the sake of love of Thine image, O Merciful One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away: for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise.[^986]

*Troparion:*
The Cross of the Lord, which is worshipped by faithful men, appears radiant as the sun; kissing it, we are enlightened in soul.[^987]

*Troparion:*
The Lord God appeared incarnate, and being lifted up upon the Tree, He enlightens those that worship Him, ever delivering them from cruel evils.[^988]

*Troparion:*
Grant unto us cleansing and remission of sins, O Word of God, who faithfully worship today Thy precious Cross lying before us.[^989]

*Theotokion:*
Without leaving the Father's bosom, the Word reclined in thy bosom as an infant, O Maiden, wishing to renew me who was subject to corruption.[^990]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Perceiving with foresight Thy divine emptying, Habakkuk cried unto Thee with trembling, O Christ: Thou art come for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed.[^991]

*Troparion:*
Having received the grace of the Spirit, like the light-radiant sun thou didst traverse the earth, O Cornelius, driving away the darkness of the madness of idols, O most praised one.[^992]

*Troparion:*
Going forth like a great river, thou dost water all the face of the earth with divine teachings, choking the tares of polytheism, O Cornelius.[^993]

*Troparion:*
Having become dead unto the whole world, for the sake of Him Who was put to death for us, O all-blessed Cornelius, thou didst proclaim the divine resurrection unto all that were dead in passions all-blessed Cornelius, thou didst proclaim the divine resurrection unto all that were dead in passions.[^994]

*Theotokion:*
O pure Virgin, thou wast supernaturally the pure dwelling-place of the Father's Wisdom, through whom we are now delivered from the malice of the crafty one.[^995]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, art come as light into the world, a holy light turning those that hymn Thee with faith from gloomy ignorance.[^996]

*Troparion:*
Of old on Sinai, Thou didst show forth the tabernacle not made with hands unto Moses who beheld God, prefiguring Thy Church, O Christ.[^997]

*Troparion:*
Thou, O Lord, hast established a tabernacle on earth: Thou dost unite the choirs of men with the heavenly ranks by Thy power.[^998]

*Troparion:*
We know Thee, O Lord, as the fountain of life: Thou, O Holy One, having come, hast proclaimed peace, O Christ, unto Thy Church.[^999]

*Theotokion:*
We set thee forth as a firm weapon against enemies; we have acquired thee as the strength and hope of our salvation, O Bride of God.[^1000]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
Send down Thine illumination upon us, O Lord, and loose us from the gloom of transgressions, O Good One, granting Thy peace.[^1001]

*Troparion:*
Strengthen us against corrupting passions, who honor and kiss thee, O precious Cross, the most holy sign of the holy Passion.[^1002]

*Troparion:*
Being enlightened today in hearts and souls with good virtues, let us draw near, O faithful, and worship the sacred and divine tree of the Cross.[^1003]

*Troparion:*
Sweetening of old the waters of Marah, Moses prefigured thee, O precious Cross, whereby Thou didst pour out saving sweetness unto men.[^1004]

*Theotokion:*
Pray for us unto Christ, Who from thy pure blood was clothed in material flesh, O all-pure Maiden, and Who renewed earthly beings.[^1005]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, unto Thee I rise early and unto Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, for Thou alone art compassionate.[^1006]

*Troparion:*
Having committed thyself wholly unto the Almighty, thou didst not offer honor unto deaf idols, O sacred initiate of mysteries, though compelled by defiled, murderous men.[^1007]

*Troparion:*
Having called upon the most high, invisible God in prayers, O Cornelius, greatly admired, thou didst cast down the temple of abominable idols having called upon the most high, invisible God in prayers, O Cornelius, greatly admired, thou didst cast down the temple of abominable idols.[^1008]

*Troparion:*
Keeping the commandments of the Almighty, thou didst endure bonds in prison, and didst loose foolish men from the bonds of evil belief, O divinely-wise one.[^1009]

*Theotokion:*
Rain down upon me remission of sins, O all-pure one; visit me who am infirm and tempest-tossed by worldly temptations and bodily passions.[^1010]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed from Thy side for mercy's sake.[^1011]

*Troparion:*
Christ the King desired the beauty of the chosen Church today, and showed her forth as mother of the nations, made sons by the Spirit from servitude.[^1012]

*Troparion:*
The ranks of hostile demons tremble at Christ's Church, which is signed with the sign of the Cross and sanctified by the consecrating illumination of the Spirit.[^1013]

*Troparion:*
Having not sand, but Christ as foundation, the Church from the Gentiles is crowned with unapproachable beauty and adorned with a royal diadem.[^1014]

*Theotokion:*
O wonder newer than all wonders! For the Virgin, having conceived without knowledge of man Him Who contains all things, did not constrain Him in her womb.[^1015]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
I am come into the depths of the sea, and the tempest of many sins hath overwhelmed me; but as God, lead up my life from the abyss, O Most Merciful One.[^1016]

*Troparion:*
Pierced in His side upon thee, O Cross, voluntarily suspended, the Creator pours forth blood and water, wherewith we that faithfully kiss thee are edified.[^1017]

*Troparion:*
Life-giving tree of the Lord, fountain of immortality, redemption of all the world: save us that kiss thee, as our saving guardian.[^1018]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast been shown unto us as a mighty weapon whereby we conquer all the assaults of the adversaries, O divine Cross, who sacredly kiss thee in uprightness of soul.[^1019]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the holy temple of Him Who rests in the saints, O Birthgiver of God; therefore thou dost sanctify us that faithfully hymn thee, O Virgin Mother.[^1020]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
By the raging, soul-corrupting tempest, O Master Christ, calm the sea of passions, and lead me up from corruption, for Thou art compassionate.[^1021]

*Troparion:*
Purely offering thy prayers, thou didst manifestly behold the angel of God praising thee, having [thine alms and fasting] pleasing unto God.[^1022]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by the Spirit, thou wast shown forth as a light-giving star enlightening the ends [of the earth] with light-radiant rays, O sacred initiate of mysteries, Cornelius.[^1023]

*Troparion:*
Having come to know the Lord of glory, who wast formerly darkened by delusion, thou dost gain sight by thy prayer, O blessed one, and receivest divine cleansing with thine entire household.[^1024]

*Theotokion:*
The Lord of glory became incarnate from thy virginal blood as He alone knows, O all-hymned one, saving us by His goodness.[^1025]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The firm and divinely-bearing" (Тве́рдыѧ):*
Grant the renewal of the Spirit in hearts, and illumination unto the inner man, for those that celebrate with faith the sacred dedication of the temple of Thy house, which Thou wast well-pleased to have built in Thy divine name, O Thou Who alone art glorified in the saints.[^1026]

*Ikos:*
Celebrating the memory of the dedication of old unto God, wisest Solomon offered whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices of irrational beasts; but now when truth and grace came upon the earth, He immediately transformed the sacrifices, offering a sacrifice for our salvation in Himself, as Lover of mankind. Sanctify the Church and show her forth unshakable, O Thou Who alone art glorified in the saints.[^1027]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, the children of Abraham, burned more by the love of piety than by the flame, cried: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1028]

*Troparion:*
The flame of the furnace was shown forth of old as bedewing; and now the spiritual anointing with oil illumines those that cry: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1029]

*Troparion:*
As in a furnace acceptable unto God, in this new tabernacle, we, all that are of spiritual Israel, being bedewed, cry: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1030]

*Troparion:*
Wounded with sweetest divine desire, come, in this royal bridal chamber let us be united unto the Bridegroom Christ, crying: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1031]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, sanctified divine dwelling-place of the Most High: for through thee joy was given, O Mother of God, unto those that cry: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady![^1032]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
The three youths in Babylon, having turned the tyrant's command into foolishness, cried out in the midst of the flame: Blessed art Thou Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of our fathers![^1033]

*Troparion:*
Of old in the blessings of the children, Jacob prefigured thee, O precious Cross; but we now worshipping thee honor thee, drawing enlightenment.[^1034]

*Troparion:*
The words of the divine prophets have now received fulfillment, O most sacred Cross: for the Lord of all was lifted up upon Thee, delivering all from corruption.[^1035]

*Troparion:*
Embracing thee now with lips and heart, O all-honorable Cross, we ever draw sanctification, health, and salvation of both soul and body.[^1036]

*Theotokion:*
O blessed Virgin, pray for us that pray unto thee, for in thee we all place our hope, and unto thee we cry: O Mother of God, despise not thy servants![^1037]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
The supremely exalted Lord of the fathers extinguished the flame and bedewed the children who sang with one accord: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1038]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast the firstfruits of the Gentiles, O Cornelius, for thou wast the first to receive holy baptism and the grace of the Spirit, like the God-proclaimers of old.[^1039]

*Troparion:*
Performing greatest wonders by divine grace, of old thou didst catch those of evil mind unto the faith, teaching them to sing: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1040]

*Troparion:*
Hidden in the earth and covered with briars, through divine revelations, O wise one, thou wast revealed, pouring forth the grace of wonders and driving away illnesses.[^1041]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown forth as a pipe sweetly singing saving teachings and sweetening the souls of all, O Cornelius, as thou sangest: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1042]

*Triadikon:*
Let us glorify this three-hypostatic Unity: the Father without beginning, the co-essential Son, and the Holy Spirit, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1043]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst appear, having deified the commingling of man by thy divine childbirth, O all-immaculate Virgin; therefore as is due, we, the faithful, glorify thee.[^1044]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Daniel stretched forth his hands and shut the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the children, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1045]

*Troparion:*
Today with a noetic robe, woven from above by divine grace, Thy Church, O Lord, is adorned like a bride, and she calls her people unto gladness to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord calling her people unto gladness to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1046]

*Troparion:*
Today Christ the second Adam hath shown forth this new tabernacle as a noetic paradise, bearing the life-bearing weapon of the Cross instead of the tree of knowledge, unto those that sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1047]

*Triadikon:*
Honoring Thee, the Father without beginning, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one Godhead, perfect, unoriginate, indivisible, co-essential, unconfused, in three Hypostases, we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1048]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone in all generations, O all-pure Virgin, wast shown forth as the Mother of God; thou wast the dwelling-place of the Godhead, O all-immaculate one, not burned by the fire of unapproachable Light. Therefore we all bless thee, O Mother, Bride of God.[^1049]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
O Almighty Deliverer of all, having descended, Thou didst bedew those that lived piously in the midst of the flame, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works, bless and hymn the Lord![^1050]

*Troparion:*
Let us now worship the saving weapon and indestructible ready help of the faithful, the mighty protection, the Cross of the Lord, as it lies before all.[^1051]

*Troparion:*
Lifting up on high the serpent upon the tree before the Hebrews, as it is written, Moses prefigured thee, O all-honorable tree, whereby we are delivered from the deceit of noetic serpents.[^1052]

*Troparion:*
Thou art the illumination of our souls, O light-giving and all-honorable Cross: for embracing thee, we drive back the principalities and powers of darkness by thy divine power.[^1053]

*Theotokion:*
Let us honor the pure Virgin who supernaturally gave birth unto the unoriginate and uncreated Word for our salvation, crying in song: O Virgin, we bless thy childbirth![^1054]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee, Creator of all, the children in the furnace, having woven a universal choir, sang: All ye works, hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1055]

*Troparion:*
With uprightness of mind thou didst seek from the soul the one God Who appeared on earth; therefore, O God-bearer, thou wast the honorable firstfruits of the Gentiles and the receptacle of the Spirit.[^1056]

*Troparion:*
With the coal of thy fiery words, O blessed hierarch, thou didst burn up the matter [of error]; therefore thou hast passed over unto the never-setting Light, enlightening all that hymn thee with love with the coal of thy fiery words, O blessed hierarch, thou didst burn up the matter [of error]; therefore thou hast passed over unto the never-setting Light, enlightening all that hymn thee with love.[^1057]

*Troparion:*
The Word, Who calls all things into being out of nothing, became unto thee an inheritance, a portion, help, deliverer, strength, praise, light, and guidance, O divinely-wise Cornelius.[^1058]

*Triadikon:*
Holy Father, Holy Word, All-Holy Uncreated Spirit, Indivisible Trinity: save those that hymn Thy dominion, kingdom, and majesty with love.[^1059]

*Theotokion:*
Pour out upon us thy customary mercies, O Mother and Maiden, and entreat for us, O pure one, forgiveness of all transgressions, both in knowledge and in ignorance, and that have happened unto us through heedlessness.[^1060]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin, even Christ, Who united the separated natures. Therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God.[^1061]

*Troparion:*
Come with a pure heart and sober eyes of the mind, daughters of the King, beholding the beauty of the Church shining more than gold, let us magnify it![^1062]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice and be glad, bride of the Great King, beholding the radiant beauty of thy Bridegroom, crying with thy people: We magnify Thee, O Giver of life![^1063]

*Troparion:*
Grant from on high Thy protection unto Thy Church, O Savior: for she knows no other besides Thee, magnifying Thee in knowledge, Who of old didst lay down Thy life for her.[^1064]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, thou who art full of grace, bride of the Great King: for through thee, O pure one, we were all delivered from the curse of Eve, and found life in thy childbirth, O unwedded one.[^1065]

*Another [Canon of the Forefeast]. Heirmos:*
Thy childbirth was shown forth incorrupt: God came forth from thy womb, appearing on earth as a bearer of flesh, and dwelt among men. Therefore we all magnify thee, O Mother of God.[^1066]

*Troparion:*
Christ suspended upon Thee, O Cross of the Lord, truly lifted up the world fallen into the abyss of perdition; therefore we now worship Thee with love, and honor and glorify Thee.[^1067]

*Troparion:*
Let us cleanse our souls and hearts with good deeds alone, and beholding the saving tree of the Cross lying before us in our midst, let us worship it with faith and love, with divine wisdom.[^1068]

*Troparion:*
Like a great sun, with thy flashes thou dost illumine those that are in darkness, and dost burn demons, O most beautiful Cross. Therefore we cry: Enlighten all that worship thee with faith.[^1069]

*Theotokion:*
Illumine me with divine light, O Virgin receptacle of the Light, driving away the gloom of my passions, and the truly deepest night of pleasures, O all-pure Birthgiver of God.[^1070]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Rejoice, O Isaiah: a Virgin hath conceived in her womb, and bare a Son, Emmanuel, both God and Man, the Orient is His name: Whom magnifying, we call the Virgin blessed.[^1071]

*Troparion:*
The Church gathers all unto a sacred solemnity in thine honorable memory, O preacher of Christ; for thou wast shown forth as an equal in station unto the holy disciples, having inherited the Holy Spirit even as they.[^1072]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast adorned with the dogmas of piety as a sacred celebrant; thou wast made like unto the divine ministers of God; and thou ever pourest forth rivers of healings, O blessed one, driving away the infirmities of men, O most sacred Cornelius.[^1073]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with the robe of salvation which Christ wove by becoming incarnate, thou now traversest the heavenly realms with exceeding joy, purely beholding the incomprehensible beauty of the Bridegroom, O right glorious Cornelius.[^1074]

*Troparion:*
Thine honorable shrine, like a fountain, abundantly pours forth healings unto the faithful, and drives away evil spirits, O Cornelius, and enlightens the eyes of all who praise thee with faith.[^1075]

*Theotokion:*
Ask enlightenment for me, O thou who didst give birth unto the Light that shone forth from the Light, driving far away from me the darkening of pleasures and temptations, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, unfailing protectress.[^1076]

*Exapostilarion of the Dedication, Tone 2, Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*
Renew by the Spirit, O Good Word, the all-hymned, all-honorable, and holy Church which Thou hast redeemed with Thy most pure Blood, and adorn her with most divine rays, glorifying with glory those that worthily celebrate the dedication of Thy temple.[^1077]

*Glory, now and ever, of the Forefeast, the same Podoben:*
With light-giving splendors the Cross of the Lord, lying before us, calls all by divine love unto its exaltation: come, let us all kiss it faithfully with joy, love, and fear, and let us glorify the one Creator and Master.[^1078]

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Dedication on 6, Tone 4:*

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Today the divine, sacred, and honorable light-bearing house of Christ's Resurrection is radiantly renewed; and the tomb gives divine life unto the world; and the immortal fountain wells forth, pouring out streams of the grace of miracles, washing away afflictions, and granting healings unto those that hymn Him with faith.[^1079]

*Sticheron:*
Light-bearing rays have shone from on high, shining and enlightening all; let us faithfully honor Christ the Creator! Let us all celebrate in hymns the Resurrection, and the life-bearing, divine solemnity of the sacred dedications, and let us cry aloud in psalms, that we may find the Savior and Lord merciful.[^1080]

*Sticheron:*
Desiring to behold beforehand the holy scepter of the Cross lifted up in the midst of the earth, let us pre-cleanse our souls and illumine our mind, being enlightened with the light; and shining with divine power, let us hymn Christ Who grants sanctification through His honorable Wood unto those that cry out with faith and fervently hymn Him.[^1081]

*Other Stichera, Tone 4. Idiomela by John the Monk:*
Be renewed, be renewed, O New Jerusalem! For thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! This house the Father created; this house the Son established; this house the Holy Spirit renewed, Who enlightens, strengthens, and sanctifies our souls.[^1082]

*Sticheron:*
Of old, indeed, when dedicating the temple, Solomon offered sacrifices of irrational animals and burnt offerings unto Thee, O Lord. But when Thou wast pleased, O Savior, that types should be abolished and truth made known, the human races offer bloodless sacrifices unto Thy glory: for ruling over all, Thou sanctifiest all things by the Holy Spirit.[^1083]

*Tone 4. By John the Monk:*
Today the Church from the Gentiles is renewed by the honorable and life-flowing Blood from the most pure and incorruptible side of Christ our God, Who was incarnate of the Holy Virgin. Therefore, ye choirs of the faithful, having gathered together, let us glorify the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one Godhead upholding all things.[^1084]

*Glory, Tone 3. Idiomelon:*
Ascend unto thyself, O man! Be new instead of old, and celebrate the renewal of thy soul as long as there is time of life, that the way of thy whole life may be renewed for thee: for the ancient things are passed away, behold, all things are become new. Bring forth this fruit unto the feast, being changed with a good change: thus is man renewed, thus is the day of dedication honored.[^1085]

*Now and ever, of the Forefeast, the same Tone. By John the Monk:*
O Christ our God, Who didst accept Thy voluntary Crucifixion for the common resurrection of the human race, and with the reed of the Cross, dyeing Thy fingers in crimson blood, wast pleased in Thy love for mankind to sign our pardon like a King: despise not us who are in distress, and again estranged from Thee; but O Thou Who alone art longsuffering, have compassion upon Thy people who are in adversity, and arise, subdue those that war against us, for Thou art almighty.[^1086]

*Great Doxology.*
*And the Dismissal.*
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the canon of the Dedication, Odes 3 and 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* Holiness befits Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.[^1087]
*Verse:* The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty.[^1088]
*Epistle: To the Hebrews, Section 307 [Heb. 9:1–7].*[^1089]
*Alleluia, Tone 2:* His foundations are in the holy mountains.[^1090]
*Verse:* Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.[^1091]
*Gospel according to Matthew, Section 97.*[^1092]
*Communion Hymn:* Lord, I have loved the beauty of Thine house, and the place where Thy glory dwells.[^1093] *Alleluia, thrice.*

*Be it also known:* (Mark this)[^1094]
*If the Exaltation of the Precious Cross falls on a Sunday: on the Saturday before the Exaltation:*
*At the Liturgy: The Prokeimenon and Alleluia of the Dedication alone; and that of the Saturday before the Exaltation is omitted. The Epistle and Gospel are read first of the Dedication, and then of the Saturday before the Exaltation. Communion Hymn of the Dedication. But the Epistle and Gospel of the day are read beforehand. And of the Sunday before the Exaltation, the Epistle and Gospel are read on the preceding Sunday.*

*It should be known:*
*That if the Dedication, the 13th day, falls on a Sunday: The service of the Holy Cornelius is omitted, and is sung whenever the ecclesiarch decides. And the Sunday service is sung with the Dedication, and with the Forefeast of the Precious Cross.*[^1095]

*At Small Vespers: Resurrection Stichera and of the Birthgiver of God, according to custom. Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory, now and ever, Theotokion.*
*At Great Vespers: Blessed is the man, the entire kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried", 3 Resurrection Stichera; 1 Anatolian; 3 of the Dedication; and 3 of the Cross: Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (written at the Aposticha). Glory, of the Dedication; Now and ever, Dogmatic Theotokion of Tone 1. Entrance; and the 3 readings of the Dedication. At the Litiya, the Sticheron of the Temple, and of the Dedication from the Praises, Tone 1: "Be renewed, be renewed"; and of Tone 4: "Today is renewed"; the same Tone: "Lifting up in the midst of the earth". Glory, Tone 5:* O Word Who restest in the bosom of the Father, by Thy Holy Spirit renew the temple erected unto Thy name.[^1096] *Now and ever, Tone 6: "Today the Tree is deemed". At the Aposticha, Resurrection Stichera of the Tone. Glory, Tone 2: "Celebrating the Dedication"; Now and ever, of the Cross, the same Tone: "The divine treasure". At the Blessing of the Loaves, Troparion: "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin", twice; and of the Dedication, once. And a reading from the Apostolic Epistles.*[^1097]
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord", Troparion of the Resurrection, twice; Glory, of the Dedication; Now and ever, of the Cross. After the kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Resurrection; Glory, now and ever, of the Dedication; the Theotokia are omitted. And a reading from the Gospel commentary for the Sunday before the Exaltation. After the Evlogitaria: Hypakoe; and we read from the Gospel commentary for the Sunday in course. The Graduals, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath"; Gospel of the Resurrection. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; and Psalm 50. Sticheron of the Resurrection. Canon of the Resurrection with its Heirmos on 4; and of the Birthgiver of God on 2; and of the Dedication on 4; and of the Cross on 4. Katavasia: "Inscribing the Cross". After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the Dedication, and the Sessional Hymn; Glory, now and ever, of the Cross; and a reading. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection; and the Prologue. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable". Exapostilarion of the Resurrection; Glory, of the Dedication; Now and ever, of the Cross. At the Praises, 4 Resurrection Stichera; and of the Dedication, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign", 2; and 2 Idiomela, Tone 3: "Ascend unto thyself, O man"; the other: "O Christ our God". First verse:* Holiness befits Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days. *The other:* The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty. *Glory, the Gospel Sticheron; Now and ever:* Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Birthgiver of God. *Great Doxology. Troparion of the Resurrection; the Litanies; Dismissal; and Catechesis*[^1098] *and the customary procession into the narthex; and the First Hour. At the Hours, Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory, of the Dedication; Now and ever, the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father", Kontakion of the Resurrection and of the Dedication, saying them alternately. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Resurrection of the Tone on 6; and of the Dedication, Ode 3 on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion of the Resurrection, of the Dedication, and of the Cross. Kontakion of the Resurrection; Glory, now and ever, of the Dedication. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel: first of the Sunday before the Exaltation, and the daily under one section; then of the Dedication. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens"; and of the Dedication.*[^1099]

*(Woodcut Headpiece: The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross)*

*On the 14th Day of the Same Month: The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross; and the Falling Asleep of our Father among the Saints John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople.*[^1100]

*Be it known: That the office of Chrysostom is not sung on this most radiant day, neither in the City of Constantine nor anywhere, because of the Exaltation of the Precious Cross, a Feast of the Lord; and it was transferred unto the 13th day of the month of November.*[^1101]

*At Small Vespers, Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Нбⷭ҇ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
The Cross is lifted up, and demons are driven away; the thief opens the gates of Eden; death is slain and is now shown forth desolate; Christ is magnified! Therefore rejoice, all ye born of earth: the curse is dissolved! *(Twice)*[^1102]

*Sticheron:*
Come, all ye lovers of God, beholding the precious Cross lifted up, let us magnify it together and give glory unto the one Deliverer and God, crying aloud: O Thou Who wast crucified upon the wood of the Cross, despise not us who pray unto Thee![^1103]

*Sticheron:*
Moses of old, sweetening the bitter water, delivered Israel, prefiguring the Cross in a type; and we, all the faithful, mystically portraying it divinely in our hearts at all times, are saved by its power.[^1104]

*Glory, now and ever, Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
Today the plant of life comes forth from the hidden depths of the earth; it confirms the Resurrection of Christ nailed upon it; and lifted up by priestly hands, it proclaims His ascension into the heavens, whereby our mortal compound, having fallen unto earth, now has its dwelling in the heavens. Therefore let us cry aloud in thanksgiving: O Lord Who wast lifted up upon it, and thereby didst raise us up together with Thyself, vouchsafe us Thy heavenly joy, as Lover of mankind![^1105]

*Prokeimenon of the day.*
*And "Vouchsafe, O Lord".*
*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
With the God-flowing water and with Thy Blood, O Word, the Church is radiantly adorned as a bride, singing the glory of the Cross.[^1106]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.[^1107]

*Sticheron:*
Lifting up the lance with the Cross, the nails, and the other instruments wherewith the life-bearing Body of Christ was pierced, let us worship.[^1108]

*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages; He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^1109]

*Sticheron:*
When Moses conquered Amalek, holding his hands aloft in the form of a cross, he prefigured the most pure Passion of Christ.[^1110]

*Glory, now and ever, Tone 6:*
Today the Tree is shown forth; today the Hebrew race is perished; today by faithful kings the faith is manifested; and Adam fell away because of a tree, and again by the Tree the demons trembled: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee![^1111]

*Troparion, Tone 1:*
Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance, granting victories unto our right-believing King over adversaries, and by Thy Cross preserving Thy habitation.[^1112]

*After the dismissal of Small Vespers:*
*The ecclesiarch enters into the prothesis with the priest, deacon, and paraecclesiarch, with candles; and the priest and deacon vest. And having censed the precious Cross, he says:* "Blessed is our God". *Then the Trisagion; and after "Our Father", the Troparion of the Cross:* "Save, O Lord, Thy people"; *Glory, now and ever, the Kontakion. And the priest takes the precious Cross upon his head with the platter*[^1113] head, and brings it into the holy altar, two lamps preceding him. And he places the precious Cross upon the holy table in the place of the Gospel, and they kindle a candle before it for the whole night; and he places the Gospel in the high place.[^1114]

*It should be known:*
*That if this Feast falls on a Sunday, nothing of the Resurrection is sung: neither Resurrection Stichera, nor the Evlogitaria, nor the Graduals of the Tone, nor is the Resurrection Gospel read; we only say "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ". "Holy is the Lord our God" is not sung either, but we sing the entire service of the Feast.*
*At Great Vespers: If on Saturday evening, we sing "Blessed is the man", the entire kathisma. If on Sunday evening, we sing "Blessed is the man", the first antiphon. But if on another day, we do not sing "Blessed is the man", but after the introductory Psalm we sing "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 6. And we sing Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having set aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^1115]
The Cross is lifted up, commanding all creation to hymn the most pure Passion of Him Who was lifted up thereon; for having slain upon it him that had slain us, He made alive those that were dead, and adorned them, and vouchsafed them to dwell in the heavens as the Merciful One, by the abundance of His goodness. Therefore rejoicing, let us exalt His name, and let us magnify His extreme condescension! *(Thrice)*[^1116]

*Sticheron:*
Moses prefigured thee, stretching forth his hands on high, and he conquered Amalek the tormentor, O precious Cross, the boast of the faithful, the confirmation of sufferers, the adornment of the Apostles, the champion of the righteous, the salvation of all the venerable. Therefore creation, beholding thee lifted up, rejoices and celebrates, glorifying Christ Who through thee gathered together the things that were separated, by His extreme goodness! *(Thrice)*[^1117]

*Sticheron:*
O most precious Cross, around which stand the angelic ranks rejoicing, today being lifted up, by divine nodding thou liftest up all who were driven out by the theft of food, and had slipped into death. Therefore, embracing thee with hearts and lips, we, the faithful, draw sanctification, crying aloud: Exalt Christ, the all-good God, and worship His divine footstool! *(Twice)*[^1118] *Glory, now and ever, Tone 2:*
Come, all ye nations, let us worship the blessed Tree, whereby eternal righteousness has come to pass! For he who deceived forefather Adam by a tree is deceived by the Cross, and falls cast down with a strange fall, who held the royal creation by tyranny; by the Blood of God the serpent's poison is washed away, and the curse of righteous condemnation was dissolved when the Righteous One was condemned by an unrighteous judgment: for it was fitting that a tree should heal a tree, and that by the Passion of the Impassible One upon the Tree the passions of the condemned one should be loosed. But glory, O Christ the King, unto Thy wise dispensation toward us, whereby Thou hast saved all, as Good and Lover of mankind![^1119]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*
