*(If this Feast falls on a Saturday: On Friday evening the Prokeimenon of the day is omitted, and the Great Prokeimenon is sung, Tone 7:* Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He pleased, He hath done.[^1120] *Because on Saturday evening the Prokeimenon is sung:* The Lord is King.) *And the readings.*

*Reading from Exodus [15:22–16:1]:*
Moses led the sons of Israel away from the Red Sea, and led them into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water to drink. And they came to Marah, and were not able to drink water from Marah, for it was bitter; therefore the name of that place was called Bitterness. And the people murmured against Moses, saying: "What shall we drink?" And Moses cried unto the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree; and he cast it into the water, and the water was made sweet. There God set for him ordinances and judgments, and there He proved him, and said: "If thou wilt indeed hear the voice of the Lord thy God, and do that which is pleasing before Him, and give ear unto His commandments, and keep all His ordinances, no disease which I brought upon the Egyptians will I bring upon thee; for I am the Lord Who heals thee." And they came to Elim, and there were twelve springs of water, and seventy date palms; and they encamped there beside the waters. And they set out from Elim, and all the congregation of the sons of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.[^1121]

*Reading from Proverbs [3:11–18]:*
My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord, neither faint when thou art rebuked of Him rebuked of Him: for whom the Lord loves He chastens, and scourges every son whom He receives. Blessed is the man that finds wisdom, and the mortal that knows understanding. For to purchase her is better than the treasures of gold and silver. And she is more precious than costly stones; no evil thing can oppose her, she is easily known unto all that love her; and all precious things are not worthy of her. For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory. Out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and she bears law and mercy upon her tongue. Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are peace. She is a tree of life unto all that lay hold on her, and lean upon her as upon the Lord steadfastly.[^1122]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah [60:11–16]:*
Thus says the Lord: thy gates shall be opened continually, O Jerusalem; they shall not be shut day or night, that men may bring unto thee the strength of the Gentiles, and their kings led captive. For the nations and the kings that will not serve thee shall perish, and those nations shall be utterly desolated. And the glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, with the cypress, the pine, and the cedar together, to glorify My holy place; and I will glorify the place of My feet. And the sons of them that afflicted thee, that provoked thee, shall come bending unto thee; and all they that provoked thee shall worship at the steps of thy feet; and thou shalt be called the City of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, and there was no helper for thee, I will make thee an eternal joy, a gladness unto generations of generations. And thou shalt suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt eat the wealth of kings; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord That saves thee, and God of Israel That delivers thee.[^1123]

*At the Litiya, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 1. By Andrew of Jerusalem:*
Today, truly, the holy-acting word of David hath received fulfillment; for behold, manifestly we worship the footstool of Thy most pure feet, and hoping in the shadow of Thy wings, O All-Compassionate One, we cry unto Thee: Let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us! Exalt the horn of Thy Orthodox people by the elevation of Thy precious Cross, O Christ, plenteous in mercy![^1124]

*Sticheron:*
Planted in the Place of the Skull, the wood of the sacred Life, whereon the Pre-Eternal King wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, being lifted up today, sanctifies the ends of the world, and the house of the Resurrection is renewed; the angels in heaven rejoice, and men upon earth are glad, crying Davidically and saying: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy: granting great mercy unto the world![^1125]

*Sticheron:*
Prefiguring Thy Cross, O Christ, the Patriarch Jacob, giving a blessing unto his grandsons, made his hands crosswise upon their heads. Lifting it up today, O Savior, we cry aloud: Grant victories unto our Christ-loving King, even as triumph unto Constantine![^1126]

*Tone 2. By Theophanes:*
The divine treasure hidden in the earth, the Cross of the Life-Giver, was shown in the heavens unto the pious king, and noetically manifested the title of victory over enemies; whereat rejoicing with faith and love, he divinely ascended unto the height of vision, and with diligence brought it forth from the bowels of the earth, for the redemption of the world and the salvation of our souls.[^1127]

*By Cyprian:*
The crossing of the hands of the Patriarch Jacob in blessing his children handed down the mighty sign of Thy Cross. Holding it as a steadfast guardian, we all-powerfully drive away the demonic legions, and through it cast down the pride of Belial, and conquer the all-destructive power of the hostile Amalek. Lifting it up now in pious mindfulness, we, the faithful, cry out for the cleansing of sins unto Thy goodness in exceeding manifold voices, offering: Lord, have mercy! O Thou Who wast incarnate of the Virgin, have compassion, O Good One, upon the wise creation of Thy hands![^1128]

*By Leo the Despot:*
Thou art my mighty protection, O three-part Cross of Christ! Sanctify me by thy power, that with faith and love I may worship and glorify thee![^1129]

*Tone 4:*
Today let us sing a festal hymn, and with radiant countenance and clear tongue let us cry aloud: For our sake Christ accepted judgment, spitting, and wounds, and was robed in purple, and mounted the Cross; seeing Whom, the sun and the moon hid their light, and the earth was shaken with fear, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain. Do Thou also now grant unto us Thy precious Cross, as guardian, keeper, and driver-away of demons, that we all kissing it may cry aloud unto it: Save us, O Cross, by thy power; sanctify us by thy brightness, O precious Cross, and strengthen us by thine elevation![^1130]

[thou art] granted unto us as light, and the salvation of our souls.

*By Anatolios:*
A sign radiant with stars prefigured the victory of triumph unto the great pious king, O Cross, which his mother Helen having found, made manifest unto the world; and lifting thee up today, we the choirs of the faithful cry aloud: Enlighten us by thy brightness, O life-bearing Cross! Sanctify us by thy power, O all-precious Cross, and establish us by thine elevation, being lifted up against the array of the enemies![^1131]

*Glory, Both now, the same Tone. By Anatolios:*
Prefiguring the action of the precious Cross, O Christ, Moses conquered the opposing Amalek in the Sinai desert; for when he stretched out his hands, making the sign of the Cross, the people were strengthened; and now the fulfillment of these things has been accomplished in us: today the Cross is lifted up, and demons flee; today the whole creation is set free from corruption, for all gifts have shone forth unto us for the sake of the Cross. Therefore, all rejoicing, we fall down before Thee, saying: How magnified are Thy works, O Lord! Glory to Thee![^1132]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5. Automelon:*
Rejoice, O life-bearing Cross, invincible victory of piety, gate of paradise, confirmation of the faithful, rampart of the Church! Whereby corruption was destroyed and brought to nought, and the power of death was trampled down, and we were raised from earth unto the heavenly: invincible weapon, adversary of demons, glory of the martyrs, truly the adornment of the venerable, haven of salvation, granting great mercy unto the world![^1133]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.[^1134]

Rejoice, O Cross of the Lord, whereby mankind was released from the curse, token of true joy! Who drivest away enemies at thine elevation, O all-precious helper unto us: dominion of kings, strength of the righteous, majesty of priests, who art prefigured and dost deliver from cruel evils; rod of power whereby we are pastured; weapon of peace, about which the angels stand in fear; divine glory of Christ, Who grants great mercy unto the world![^1135]

*Verse:* God is our King before the ages, He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^1136]

Rejoice, O guide of the blind, physician of the infirm, resurrection of all the dead: who hast raised us who had fallen into corruption, O precious Cross! Whereby the curse was dissolved, and incorruption flourished, and we of the earth were deified, and the devil was utterly cast down. Seeing thee lifted up today by the hands of hierarchs, we exalt the One Who was lifted up in the midst of thee, and worship thee, drawing richly great mercy![^1137]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 8. By John the Monk:*
Him Whom Moses of old, prefiguring in himself, cast down Amalek and conquered; and David the psalmist, crying aloud, commanded to worship at Thy footstool, Thy precious Cross, O Christ God: today we sinners worship with unworthy lips, singing unto Thee Who wast pleased to be nailed upon it, we pray: O Lord, with the thief vouchsafe us Thy Kingdom![^1138]

*Then:* Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart...

*At the Blessing of the Loaves, Troparion, Tone 1:*
Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance, granting victories unto our right-believing King [name][^1139] over adversaries, and by Thy Cross preserving Thy commonwealth.

*Thrice.*

*And we read the Homily concerning the Precious Wood.*[^1140]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion, thrice.*

*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
No sooner was the wood of Thy Cross set up, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for him whom Hades eagerly swallowed, it let go in trembling; Thou hast shown us Thy salvation, O Holy One, and we glorify Thee: O Son of God, have mercy on us![^1141]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4, Podoben: "When the Stone Was Sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*
We worship the wood of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind, for upon it Thou, the Life of all, wast nailed; Thou didst open paradise, O Savior, unto the thief who approached Thee with faith, and who was accounted worthy of delight, confessing unto Thee: Remember me, O Lord! Receive us also, who cry like him: We all have sinned, in Thy tender compassion despise us not![^1142]

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
Today the prophetic word is fulfilled; for behold, we worship in the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord; and having received the tree of salvation, we have obtained freedom from sinful passions, by the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind![^1143]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*
Joshua the son of Nun of old mystically prefigured the image of the Cross, when he stretched out his hands crosswise, O my Savior, and the sun stood still until he cast down the enemies opposing Thee, O God; for now it set upon the Cross, seeing Thee, and having destroyed the dominion of death, Thou hast raised the whole world with Thyself![^1144]

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*
Of old in paradise the tree stripped me bare, the enemy bringing mortification through tasting; but the Tree of the Cross, bearing the garment of life unto men, was planted upon earth, and the whole world was filled with all joy; seeing it exalted, O people, let us with faith cry out in concord unto God: Thy house is full of glory![^1145]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*The Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of the 4th Tone. Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.[^1146]

*Verse:* Sing unto the Lord a new song, for the Lord hath done marvelous things.[^1147]

*Let every breath.*

*Verse:* Praise God in His saints.

*Gospel according to John, section 42 [12:28–36]: from the half.*

*Then:* Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ...

*Psalm 50.*

*And the Sticheron, Tone 6:*
O Cross of Christ, hope of Christians, guide of the erring, haven of the storm-tossed, victory in battles, confirmation of the universe, physician of the sick, resurrection of the dead: have mercy on us![^1148]

*The Canon of the Cross, whose acrostic is: Relying upon the Cross, I utter song. A work of Lord Cosmas. The Heirmoi twice, and the Troparia to 12. Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Tracing the Cross with his rod, Moses directly divided the Red Sea for Israel who went on foot; and striking it transversely, brought it together again over Pharaoh's chariots, writing the invincible weapon. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He is glorified![^1149]

*Troparion:*
Of old Moses in himself prefigured the image of the most pure Passion, standing in the midst of the consecrated ones; and forming the Cross, he lifted up victory with outstretched palms, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He is glorified![^1150]

Moses placed upon a pillar the remedy, deliverance from the destructive and venomous bite; and crosswise unto the wood he bound the serpent that creeps upon the earth, exposing the malicious harm in this. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He is glorified![^1151]

*Troparion:*
The heavens showed the victory of the Cross unto the ruler of piety and God-wise King; wherein the fierceness of the evil-hearted enemies was cast down, deceit was overthrown, and the divine faith was spread abroad unto the ends of the earth. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He is glorified![^1152]

*Katavasia, both choirs together:* Tracing the Cross with his rod...

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The rod is taken as a figure of the mystery, for by budding it designates the priest; and for the Church that formerly was barren, now the Tree of the Cross has blossomed forth, for her strength and confirmation.[^1153]

*Troparion:*
As the flinty rock struck poured forth water for a disobedient and hard-hearted people, it made manifest the mystery of the God-called Church, whereof the Cross is the strength and confirmation.[^1154]

*Troparion:*
From His most pure side pierced by a spear, water with blood flowed forth, renewing the Covenant and washing away sin; for the Cross is the boast of the faithful, and the strength and confirmation of kings.[^1155]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
In thee, O thrice-blessed and life-giving Cross, the people rejoicing keep festival together with the bodiless choirs; the ranks of hierarchs reverently sing; the multitude of monks and fasters worship; and we all glorify Christ Who was crucified.[^1156]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity.[^1157]

*Troparion:*
Moses of old changed the bitter springs in the wilderness with a tree, prefiguring the transition of the Gentiles unto piety through the Cross.[^1158]

*Troparion:*
Jordan gave back to the wood the axe that had sunk into the depth, signifying by the Cross and Baptism the cutting down of deception.[^1159]

*Troparion:*
Sacredly the people encamp in four divisions, marching in advance in the pattern of the Tabernacle of Witness, glorified in cruciform ranks.[^1160]

*Troparion:*
Marvelously stretched out, the Cross emitted sunbeams and the heavens declared the glory of our God.[^1161]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ was crucified, the King and Lord: through which he who deceived by the tree has fallen, being deceived by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1162]

*Troparion:*
O ever-hymned Tree whereon Christ was stretched out: the turning sword that guarded Eden stood in awe of thee, O Cross, and the dread Cherubim yielded unto Christ Who was nailed upon thee, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1163]

*Troparion:*
The opposing powers of the nether regions are terrified of the Cross, the sign traced in the air wherein they walk; and the generations of heaven and earth bow the knee unto Christ, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1164]`

*Troparion:*
Appearing with incorruptible rays, the divine Cross, having shone forth divine light upon the darkened Gentiles who had strayed into error, unites them unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1165]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Stretching out his hands in the form of a cross in the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah clearly prefigured the saving Passion; therefore coming forth after three days, he portrayed the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God Who was nailed in the flesh, and by His three-day Resurrection enlightened the world.[^1166]

*Troparion:*
Bowed down with age and weighed down by illness, Jacob was straightened when he crossed his hands, manifesting the operation of the life-bearing Cross; for the antiquity of the shadowy scripture of the Law he rewrote anew: God Who was nailed in the flesh upon it, and drove away the soul-destroying disease of deception.[^1167]

*Troparion:*
Laying his hands upon the youth, the divine Israel manifested heads in cruciform manner, as the elder glory, the people serving the Law; therefore, seeming thus to be mistaken, he changed not the life-bearing pattern: for the newly-established people of Christ God shall excel, they cried aloud, fortified by the Cross.[^1168]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will" (Вознесы́йсѧ на кре́стъ во́лею):*
Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will, O Christ God, bestow Thy compassions upon Thy new commonwealth named after Thee; gladden by Thy power our right-believing King,[^1169] granting him victories over adversaries: having Thine alliance, a weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy of victory.

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into Paradise, and heard unutterable and divine words, which it is not lawful for (human) tongues to speak: what writes he unto the Galatians, which ye, lovers of the Scriptures, have read and known? "Far be it from me," he says, "to glory, save only in the Cross of the Lord, whereon having suffered He slew the passions." Him therefore let us also steadfastly hold, the Cross of the Lord, as our boast, all of us; for unto us this saving Tree is a weapon of peace, an invincible victory.[^1170]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The senseless decree of the impious tyrant, breathing forth threat and God-hateful blasphemy, shook the people; yet the three youths were terrified neither by the bestial fury nor by the consuming fire; but when the dew-bearing Spirit blew against it, being with the fire, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, praised above all![^1171]

*Troparion:*
Tasting of the tree, the first among men took up his dwelling in corruption; for being condemned by a most dishonorable rejection of life, he handed down unto his whole race a certain bodily corruption, as it were a disease's harm; but we who are born of earth, having found restoration through the Tree of the Cross, cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, praised above all![^1172]

*Troparion:*
Disobedience dissolved the commandment of God, and the tree brought death unto men, having been unseasonably partaken of; and for the confirmation of the all-honorable, the Tree of Life was thenceforth barred, which He opened unto the dying thief who wisely cried: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, praised above all![^1173]

*Troparion:*
Israel, beholding things to come, grasped the tip of Joseph's staff, signifying the sovereign power of the kingdom: prefiguring the most glorious Cross; for this is the victorious boast of kings, and light unto them that cry with faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, praised above all![^1174]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Bless, ye children, equal in number unto the Trinity, God the Father, the Creator; praise ye the Word Who descended and changed the fire into dew; and highly exalt for ever the All-Holy Spirit, Who gives life unto all, unto the ages![^1175]

*Troparion:*
As the Tree is lifted up, sprinkled with the blood of the incarnate God the Word, praise Him, ye heavenly hosts; celebrating the restoration of mortals, ye peoples, worship the Cross of Christ, through which resurrection unto the ages has come unto the world![^1176]

*Troparion:*
Ye earth-born, with your palms, the stewards of grace, the Cross whereon Christ God stood: lift up sacredly, and also the spear that pierced the body of God the Word, that all nations may see the salvation of God, glorifying Him unto the ages![^1177]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, ye Christian faithful kings, forechosen by divine judgment, boast in the victorious weapon, having received from God the precious Cross; for in this the tribes of wars seeking audacity are scattered unto the ages![^1178]

*At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable", but we sing the Refrain of the Feast:*
Magnify, O my soul, the most precious Cross of the Lord.[^1179]

*Then, the Heirmos of the 1st Canon:*
Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Birthgiver of God...

*And the other choir likewise the refrain, and the heirmos.*
*And unto the remaining 6 verses we sing the same refrain.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Birthgiver of God, which untilled didst sprout forth Christ, by Whom the life-bearing Tree of the Cross was planted upon earth. Therefore, worshipping Him as it is lifted up now, we magnify thee![^1180]

*Troparion:*
Let all the trees of the forest rejoice, their nature being sanctified by Him by Whom they were planted in the beginning, when Christ was stretched out upon the Tree. Therefore, worshipping Him as it is lifted up now, we magnify thee![^1181]

*Troparion:*
The sacred horn has arisen, and the Cross is head unto all the God-wise; whereby all the horns of sinners are mentally crushed. Therefore, worshipping Him as it is lifted up now, we magnify thee![^1182]

*Second Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the elevation of the life-creating Cross of the Lord.[^1183]

*And the Heirmos:* Through the eating of the tree... *And the other choir likewise, the refrain and the heirmos. And 6 troparia with this refrain.*

*Another Heirmos:*
Death, which came upon the race through the eating of the tree, has been brought to nought today by the Cross; for the universal curse of the ancestral mother was dissolved by the offshoot of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly hosts magnify![^1184]

*Troparion:*
Leaving not the murderous bitterness which came from the tree, O Lord, for Thou didst utterly destroy it by the Cross; for this cause Thou didst of old sweeten the bitterness of the waters of Marah with a tree, prefiguring the action of the Cross, which all the heavenly hosts magnify![^1185]

Those who were continually submerged in the gloom of the forefather, O Lord, Thou hast raised up today by the Cross; for as our nature was formerly dragged down altogether unrestrainedly by deception, the light of Thy Cross has restored us again, which we, the faithful, magnify![^1186]

*Troparion:*
That Thou mightest show unto the world the worshipped image of the Cross, O Lord, Thou didst depict it most glorious of all in the heavens, illumined with immeasurable light, an invincible divine weapon unto the king. Therefore all the heavenly hosts magnify Thee![^1187]

*Katavasia:* Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Birthgiver of God... *The other:* Through the eating of the tree... *with refrains. And a prostration.*

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Unto the disciples" (Оу҆чени́кѡмъ):*
The Cross is the guardian of the whole inhabited earth; the Cross is the beauty of the Church; (the Cross is the dominion of kings); the Cross is the confirmation of the faithful; the Cross is the glory of angels, and the plague of demons.[^1188]

*Twice.*

*Glory, Both now, Podoben: "Hear, ye women" (Же́ны оу҆слы́шите):*
The Cross is lifted up today, and the world is sanctified; for He Who sits with the Father and the Holy Spirit stretched out His hands upon it, and drew the whole world unto Thy knowledge, O Christ; vouchsafe therefore divine glory unto them that hope in Thee![^1189]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 8. Automelon:*
O most marvelous wonder! The life-bearing plantation, the most holy Cross, is seen lifted up on high today. All the ends of the earth glorify, demonic legions are terrified. Oh, what a gift has been granted unto mortals, whereby, O Christ, save our souls, as Thou alone art tenderly compassionate![^1190]

*Twice.*

O most marvelous wonder! Like a cluster of grapes full of life, bearing the Most High, the Cross is seen lifted up from the earth today, whereby we all have been drawn unto God, and death has been swallowed up utterly. O most pure Tree, whereby we have received the immortal food in Eden, glorifying Christ![^1191]

O most marvelous wonder! The breadth and length of the Cross is equal unto heaven, for by divine grace it sanctifies all things. In this the barbarian nations are conquered; in this the scepters of kings are confirmed. O divine ladder, whereby we ascend unto the heavens, exalting Christ the Lord in hymns![^1192]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 6:*

Today the Cross of the Lord comes forth, and the faithful receive it with longing, and take healings of soul and body and every disease. Let us kiss it with joy and with fear: with fear, on account of sin, being unworthy; and with joy, on account of the salvation which Christ God, Who was nailed upon it and possesses great mercy, grants unto the world![^1193]

*And they sing the Great Doxology softly and in concord.*

*While the Great Doxology is being sung, the priest vests in all the sacred vestments, and takes the censer with incense, approaches the Holy Table, and censers the precious Cross crosswise; and takes it with the diskos upon his head, and goes out by the north door, two tapers preceding him, as far as the royal doors of the church; and standing there, he awaits the conclusion of the Doxology and the Trisagion. When this is finished, the deacon exclaims with a loud voice:* Wisdom! Upright! *And we begin the Troparion:* Save, O Lord, Thy people... *(straightway).*

*If there is no deacon, then the priest himself performs everything. And the priest comes, carrying the precious Cross upon his head, unto the midst of the church before the holy royal doors, where the Tetrapod has been prepared, and places the precious Cross upon the diskos atop it, and censers crosswise. Then he makes 3 prostrations unto the ground, on whatever day it may be. And taking the precious Cross with the branches of basil herb strewn upon the footstool of the Cross,[^1194] he stands before the Tetrapod, looking toward the east, and exclaims with a loud voice in the hearing of all:* Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee, give ear and have mercy. *And we begin the first hundred:* Lord, have mercy. *The priest signs at the beginning with the precious Cross, 3 times. Then he bows his head so that the head is about a span away from the ground; and little by little he rises upward until the completion of the second 50* Lord, have mercy. *And when he reaches 97* Lord, have mercy, *the ekklesiarches raises his voice, while the priest stands upright, awaiting the end of the hundred; and he signs with the Cross again, 3 times. Then, turning toward the south side, he says:* Furthermore we pray for the Most Holy Universal Hierarch [name], the Pope of Rome, and for our pious and God-preserved King [name]:[^1195] for their dominion, victory, endurance, peace, health, salvation, and remission of their sins; and that the Lord our God may especially prosper them, and aid them in all things, and subdue under their feet every enemy and adversary, let us all say. *And we begin the second hundred:* Lord, have mercy. *And the priest makes the second elevation, as written above. Then turning toward the west, he says:* Furthermore we pray for our Most Consecrated Archbishop [name], and for our God-beloved Bishop [name]; *(and monks also add: and for our most venerable fathers: our Proto-archimandrite [name], and Superior [name], or Hegumen [name]);*[^1196] and for all our brethren in Christ, for health, and salvation, and remission of their sins, let us all say. *And we begin the third hundred:* Lord, have mercy. *When this is finished, the priest turns toward the north side, and says:* Furthermore we pray for every Christian soul, for health, and salvation, and forgiveness of their sins, let us all say. *And the fourth elevation takes place. And turning toward the east, he says:* Furthermore we pray for all who serve and have served in this holy monastery, for health, and salvation, and forgiveness of their sins, let us all say. *And we begin the fifth hundred. And after the fifth elevation, we sing the Kontakion:* Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross... *Then we sing this verse in Tone 6:* Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy holy Resurrection we glorify, *thrice. While the brethren are singing, the priest places the precious Tree of the Cross upon the Tetrapod, and they begin to bow down in worship, the priest and the superior, making 3 prostrations before the precious Cross; then they kiss it. After kissing, they make again one prostration; likewise also both choirs make one prostration each. Then all the brethren approach from the right and left sides, two by two in order, and bow down in worship, and kiss the precious Cross. And we sing the Idiomelon Stichera until all the brethren have kissed it.*

*And when we kiss the precious Cross, we sing Idiomelon Stichera of the precious Cross, Tone 2:*
Come, ye faithful, let us worship the life-creating Tree, whereon Christ the King of glory, having stretched out His hands of His own will, raised us unto the first blessedness, whereof the enemy formerly having stolen through pleasure, caused us to be banished from God. Come, ye faithful, let us worship the Tree whereby we were accounted worthy to crush the heads of invisible enemies! Come, all ye lineages of the nations, [the] Cross[^1197] of the Lord let us honor in hymns! Rejoice, O Cross, complete deliverance of fallen Adam! For in thee our most faithful kings boast, as by thy power they mightily subdue the Ishmaelite peoples. Kissing thee now with fear, we Christians glorify God Who was nailed upon thee, saying: O Lord Who wast nailed thereon, have mercy on us, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind![^1198]

*Tone 5:*
Come, ye peoples, beholding the most marvelous wonder, let us worship the power of the Cross: for as the tree in Paradise brought forth death, so this one blossomed with life, having the sinless Lord nailed upon it; from Whom all the nations receiving incorruption cry out: O Thou Who by the Cross didst abolish death and set us free, glory to Thee![^1199]

*Tone 5:*
The voice of Thy prophets, Isaiah and David, has been fulfilled, O God, saying: All the nations shall come, O Lord, and shall worship before Thee. For behold, the people that have been filled with Thy grace, O Good One, in Thy courts of Jerusalem: O Thou Who didst endure the Cross for us, and by Thy Resurrection quickenest us, preserve and save us![^1200]

*Tone 6:*
The four-cornered world is sanctified today, as Thy four-part Cross is lifted up, O Christ our God, and the horn of our faithful king is exalted together with it;[^1201] whereby we shatter the horns of our enemies. Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous in Thy works; glory to Thee![^1202]

The voices of the prophets foreannounced the holy Tree, whereby Adam was set free from the ancient curse of death; and creation today, as it is lifted up, lifts up its voice together, asking of God rich mercy. But do Thou, Who alone art boundless in tender compassion, O Master, be our cleansing, and save our souls![^1203]

*Tone 8:*
The voice of Thy prophet Moses, O God, has been fulfilled, saying: Ye shall see your Life hanging before your eyes.[^1204] Today the Cross is lifted up, and the world is freed from delusion. Today the Resurrection of Christ is renewed, and the ends of the earth rejoice, offering a song unto Thee with cymbals in the manner of David, and saying: Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O God, the Cross and the Resurrection, on account whereof Thou hast saved us, O Good One and Lover of mankind; O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee![^1205]

*Tone 8:*
Today the Master of creation and Lord of glory is nailed upon the Cross, and is pierced in His side; gall and vinegar He tastes, Who is the sweetness of the Church; with a crown of thorns is He surrounded, Who covers heaven with clouds; He is clothed with the garment of mockery, and is struck with a mortal hand, Who with His hand formed man; He is scourged upon His shoulders, Who decks heaven with clouds; spitting and wounds He receives, reproaches and buffetings; and all things He endures for my sake, the condemned one, my Redeemer and God, that He may save the world from delusion, as He is tenderly compassionate![^1206]

*Glory, Both now, in the same tone:*
Today He Who is unapproachable in essence becomes approachable unto me, and suffers passions, freeing me from passions; He Who grants light unto the blind is spat upon by lawless lips, and gives His back unto wounds for the captives. The pure Virgin and Mother, beholding Him upon the Cross, cried out in anguish: Woe is me, my Child, what is this that Thou hast done? Thou Who art comely in beauty beyond all men appearest breathless, formless, having neither form nor comeliness; woe is me, my Light, I cannot bear to behold Thee sleeping, my womb is pierced, and a cruel sword passes through my heart; I hymn Thy passions, I worship Thy tender compassion: O longsuffering Lord, glory to Thee![^1207]

*Then the litanies.*

*And the rest as usual.*

*And the complete dismissal takes place.*

*At the Liturgy, Antiphon 1, Tone 2. Psalm 21:*
*Verse 1:* O God, my God, attend unto me; why hast Thou forsaken me?[^1208]
*Refrain:* Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us.
*And again, the second choir:*
*Verse 2:* Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions.
*Refrain:* Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us.
*And again, the first choir:*
*Verse 3:* O my God, I will cry by day, and Thou wilt not hear, and by night, and it shall not be unto folly for me.
*Refrain:* Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God...
*Then the second choir, Verse 4:*
But Thou dwellest in the holy place, O Praise of Israel.
*Refrain:* Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God...
*Glory, Both now:* Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God...

*Antiphon 2, Tone 2. Psalm 73:*
*Verse 1:* Why, O God, hast Thou cast us off unto the end?[^1209]
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who wast crucified in the flesh, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia.

*The second choir, Verse 2:*
Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who wast crucified in the flesh, who sing unto Thee...
*Verse 3:* This Mount Zion, wherein Thou hast dwelt.
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God...
*Verse 4:* But God is our King before the ages; He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God...
*Glory, Both now:* Only-begotten Son... *both choirs together.*

*Antiphon 3, Tone 4. Psalm 98:*
*Verse 1:* The Lord reigns, let the peoples rage.
*Then the Troparion:* Save, O Lord, Thy people... *all to the end.*
*The second choir, the same verse:*
The Lord reigns, let the peoples rage; He sits upon the Cherubim, let the earth be shaken.
*Troparion:* Save, O Lord, Thy people...
*And again the first choir, Verse 3:*
The Lord is great in Zion, and high above all peoples.
*Troparion:* Save, O Lord, Thy people...
*The second choir, Verse 4:*
Worship the Lord in His holy court.
*Troparion:* Save, O Lord, Thy people...
*Then the Entrance.*

> **Deacon:** "Wisdom! Upright!"
*And we sing the Entrance Hymn:*
Exalt the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy![^1210]
*Then the Troparion:* Save, O Lord, Thy people...
*Glory, Both now, the Kontakion:* Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will...
*Instead of the Trisagion:*
Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy holy Resurrection we glorify.[^1211]
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Exalt the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy.
*Verse:* The Lord reigns, let the peoples rage.
*Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 125 [1 Cor. 1:18-24].*[^1212]
*Alleluia, Tone 4:* Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.
*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages; He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 60 [Jn. 19:6-11, 13-20, 25-28, 30-35].*[^1213]
*Communion Hymn:*
The light of Thy countenance has been signed upon us, O Lord. Alleluia.[^1214]

*At the table there is consolation for the brethren, of oil and wine, and of other vegetable foods; but of cheese, eggs, and fish we by no means dare to partake.*[^1215]

*The 15th Day of the Same Month: The Holy Great-Martyr Nicetas.*[^1216]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast and of the Saint, on 6.*

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, life-bearing Cross" (Ра́дуйсѧ живоно́сный кр́те):*
Rejoice, life-bearing Cross, invincible victory of piety, gate of Paradise, confirmation of the faithful, rampart of the Church; whereby corruption was abolished, and the power of death was destroyed and trampled down, and we were lifted up from earth unto heaven; invincible weapon, adversary of demons, glory of martyrs, true adornment of the venerable, haven of salvation, granting great mercy unto the world![^1217]

Rejoice, Cross of the Lord, whereby mankind was released from the curse, token of true joy, who by thy lifting up, O most honorable one, drivest away enemies, helper unto us, dominion of kings, strength of the righteous, majesty of priests; prefigured, and delivering from evils; rod of strength whereby we are pastured; weapon of peace, which angels attend with fear; divine glory of Christ, Who grants great mercy unto the world![^1218]

Rejoice, guide of the blind, physician of the infirm, resurrection of all the dead, who hast raised us who had fallen into corruption, O precious Cross; whereby the curse was dissolved, and incorruption blossomed forth, and we mortals were deified, and the devil was utterly cast down. Today, beholding thee lifted up by the hands of hierarchs, we exalt Him Who was lifted up upon thee, and we bow down before thee, richly drawing forth great mercy![^1219]

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Clad in the panoply of piety, thou wast revealed as a champion of Christ the Crown-giver, O passion-bearer Nicetas, as of old the most mighty Gideon, having cast down the hosts of the aliens by thy valiant boldness.[^1220]

Thou didst strike the tormentor of alien race, O divinely wise one, through the all-powerful faith of the Savior, having endured passions; therefore, O wise one, thou didst turn the barbarians unto the Creator and Benefactor of all, and they glorify Him piously.[^1221]

Offering the firstfruits from the barbarians as a trophy unto Christ, O martyr, thou wast revealed as a divinely eloquent sufferer, and didst die for the Trinity; therefore thou didst manifestly receive a crown, and like a luminary thou shinest in godly splendor upon the world, O right-renowned one![^1222]

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 6. By Theophanes:*
We know thee as a luminary of the martyrs, O Nicetas, sufferer of Christ; for having forsaken the glory of earthly dignity, and having hated ancestral godlessness, thou didst crush their gods and put the barbarians to shame victoriously. For Christ's sake thou didst fulfill the martyrdom of confession, and becamest a soldier of the true God. Pray unto the Benefactor of all for us, that He may show tender compassion and save our souls![^1223]

*Both now, of the Feast, in the same tone:*
The voices of the prophets foreannounced the holy Tree, whereby Adam was set free from the ancient curse of death; and creation today, as it is lifted up, lifts up its voice together, asking of God rich mercy. But do Thou, Who alone art boundless in tender compassion, O Master, be our cleansing, and save our souls![^1224]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
Our God is in heaven and on earth; all whatsoever He pleased, He has done.[^1225]
*Verse:* In the going forth of Israel out of Egypt, of the house of Jacob from a barbarous people, Judea became His sanctuary.
*Verse:* The sea saw and fled, Jordan was turned back.
*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? And thou, Jordan, that thou wast turned back?
*Then the litany:* Let us all say...
*If it should be a Saturday: We sing the Prokeimenon of the day:* The Lord reigns... *The great Prokeimenon is sung on the eve of the Feast.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
The Cross being lifted up bids the whole creation to hymn the most pure passion of Him Who was lifted up upon it; for having slain thereon him that had slain us, He has quickened the dead, and adorned them, and accounted them worthy to dwell in the heavens as He is compassionate, through the surpassing abundance of goodness. Therefore, rejoicing, let us exalt His name, and let us magnify His extreme condescension![^1226]
*Verse:* Exalt the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy.
Moses prefigured thee, stretching out his hands on high, and he overcame and he overcame the tormentor Amalek, O precious Cross, boast of the faithful, confirmation of sufferers, adornment of apostles, champion of the righteous, savior of all the venerable! Therefore creation, beholding thee lifted up, rejoices and keeps festival, glorifying Christ, Who through thee has gathered together the divided by His extreme goodness.[^1227]
*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages; He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
O most precious Cross, which the ranks of angels attend rejoicing, today being lifted up, by divine nod thou liftest up all who were driven out through the theft of food and slipped into death. Therefore, kissing thee with hearts and lips, we the faithful draw forth sanctification, crying out: Exalt Christ the all-good God, and worship His divine footstool![^1228]

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 8:*
Thou hast shown thyself true to thy name of victory,[^1229] O all-honorable martyr Nicetas, having preached Christ our God in the contest, and having confessed Him before kings and tormentors. Therefore cease not to pray for the peace of the world, and for Christ-loving kings, and for all who faithfully celebrate thy memory, unto the only Lover of mankind, that we may be delivered from all wrath![^1230]

*Both now, in the same tone:*
The voice of Thy prophet Moses, O God, has been fulfilled, saying: Ye shall see your Life hanging before your eyes. Today the Cross is lifted up, and the world is freed from delusion. Today the Resurrection of Christ is renewed, and the ends of the earth rejoice, offering a song unto Thee with cymbals in the manner of David, and saying: Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O God, the Cross and the Resurrection, on account whereof Thou hast saved us, O Good One and Lover of mankind; O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee![^1231]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyr, O Lord, Nicetas, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless insolence of demons. By his prayers save our souls![^1232]

*Or this one, in the same tone:*
Having zealously taken up the Cross of Christ as a weapon, thou didst run to the root of the enemies, and having suffered for Christ, thou didst afterwards surrender thy consecrated soul unto the Lord through fire, whence also thou wast accounted worthy to receive from Him gifts of healing O great-martyr Nicetas; pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved![^1233]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast:*
Save, O Lord, Thy people...

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, twice;*
*Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast.*

*After the first Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "Being compassionate" (Бл҃гоутро́бїа су́щи):*
When Thou, O Master Christ, wast crucified, the dominion and might of death was dissolved, and all the hostile tyranny was trampled down; and we who of old died through the tree of transgression were quickened through the Tree of the Cross. Therefore we sing of Thy passions![^1234]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*After the second Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "At the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
Thou didst deign to suffer the Cross and death, having set this up in the midst of creation, when Thou wast pleased, O Savior, to have Thy body nailed; then also the sun hid its rays. Beholding these things upon the Cross, the thief also cried out unto Thee as God: Remember me, O Lord; and having believed, he received Paradise.[^1235]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*The Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos on 8, and of the Saint on 6.*

*The Canon of the Feast, Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Moses, having traced the Cross directly with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel who went on foot; and striking it reversely, he brought it together upon the chariots of Pharaoh, having inscribed the invincible weapon. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1236]

*Troparia:*
Moses of old prefigured the image of the most pure Passion in himself, standing in the midst of the sacred ones; and shaping the Cross, he raised up victory with outstretched palms, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1237]

Moses placed upon a pillar a remedy, deliverance from the venomous and deadly bite; and in the image of the Cross he bound the serpent that creeps upon the earth, exposing the harm made manifest therein. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1238]

Heaven showed forth the victory of the Cross unto the ruler of piety and divinely wise king, wherein the fury of malicious enemies was cast down, delusion was overturned, and the divine faith was spread unto the ends of the earth. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1239]

*Another Canon of the Saint, whereof the acrostic is: "I sing of thee, named after victory, Nicetas." By Theophanes, Tone 4.*[^1240]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Traversing the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet, ancient Israel of old on foot overcame the power of Amalek in the wilderness through the cross-shaped hands of Moses.[^1241]

*Troparia:*
Having put to death the carnal mind of my flesh, illumine my intellect with enlightening radiance, that I may hymn thy festival, as an all-excellent victor, pray unto Christ, O Nicetas![^1242]

Having cast off the fall that came from passions, thou didst endure wounds valiantly, and in a martyr's manner thou wast clad in an honorable robe woven from thine own blood.[^1243]

Thou didst show forth a new and marvelous way of suffering, having been nailed upon the Tree for us; for Thou, O Master, wast the beginning of confession and strength for the martyrs.[^1244]

*Theotokion:*
We mystically call thee the gate of Thy condescension unto us, O Lord, the east, the sun, and the light; for He Who is twofold in nature, the Lover of mankind, shone forth supernaturally.[^1245]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The rod is taken as an image of the mystery, for by its budding it designates the priest; and for the Church that formerly was barren, the Tree of the Cross has now blossomed forth, for dominion and confirmation.[^1246]

*Troparia:*
As the flinty rock struck forth water for the disobedient and hard-hearted people, it prefigured the mystery of the divinely called Church, whereof the Cross is the dominion and confirmation.[^1247]

When the most pure side was pierced with a spear, water flowed with blood, renewing the covenant and washing away sin; for the Cross is the boast of the faithful, and the dominion and confirmation of kings.[^1248]

*Another. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and confirmation![^1249]

*Troparia:*
With firmness of soul thou didst endure the threats of the tormentors, O glorious martyr of Christ, being empowered by divine strength.[^1250]

Having endured the laceration of thy flesh and the severing of thy limbs, O all-praised martyr of Christ, thou hast attached thy soul unto God.[^1251]

The assembly of the martyrs of Christ rejoices in Thee beholding thy memory celebrated today.

*Theotokion:*
O Mary, pure virginity and honorable dwelling, heal the cruel sores of my heart![^1252]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will, O Christ God, bestow Thy compassions upon Thy new commonwealth named after Thee. Rejoice our right-believing king with Thy power,[^1253] granting him victories over adversaries, having Thine alliance, the weapon of peace, an invincible trophy![^1254]

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into Paradise, and heard unspeakable and divine words, which it is not lawful for human tongues to utter: what does he write to the Galatians? As lovers of the Scriptures, ye have read and known: Far be it from me to boast, he says, save only in the Cross of the Lord, whereon having suffered He slew the passions! This then let us also firmly hold, the Cross of the Lord, all our boast; for this saving Tree is unto us a weapon of peace, an invincible trophy![^1255]

*Sessional Hymn of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
Having shown thyself an invincible soldier, thou didst overcome barbarian wiles, O glorious one, and having suffered, thou didst most mightily defeat the host of invisible enemies. Therefore thou didst also receive the diadem of victory, praying without ceasing for us, O blessed Nicetas, who sing unto thee in faith.[^1256]
*Twice.*

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast, in the same tone:*
Stretching out his hands unto the height of heaven, Moses prefigured the divine weapon of the faithful, the Cross, whereon Christ nailed our sins. Therefore the enemy also wept bitterly, suffering in his senses, and said: A wooden spear has pierced me in the midst of my heart! Christ releases all from the bonds of Hades.[^1257]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have considered Thy works, and I have glorified Thy Divinity.[^1258]

*Troparia:*
Of old Moses with a tree changed the bitter springs in the wilderness, manifesting beforehand through the Cross the transition of the nations unto piety.[^1259]

The Jordan gave up the axe-head that had sunk into the depth unto the wood, signifying through the Cross and baptism the cutting down of delusion.[^1260]

Sacredly the fourfold people encamp, marching in advance according to the pattern of the tabernacle of testimony of the tabernacle of testimony, glorified in cross-shaped order.[^1261]

Marvelously stretched out, the Cross emitted sun-like rays, and the heavens declared the glory of our God![^1262]

*Another. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her station, crying out worthily: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1263]

*Troparia:*
Redeemed by the Master's blood, the sufferer Nicetas rejoicing brings his own blood unto Christ; therefore, as He was slain, He cried out: Glory to Thee, my God![^1264]

Kindled with good desire, O martyr, thou didst trample down the idolatrous flame and all the power of demons, crying unto the Creator: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1265]

Enjoying the sight of the Lord and satisfied with His radiance, the martyr while suffering felt it not, and rejoicing cried: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1266]

*Theotokion:*
Adorned with various outpourings of light, Thy living heaven, O Christ King of kings, the all-pure Virgin, is now glorified as the Birthgiver of God.[^1267]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ was crucified, the King and Lord! Through thee he who deceived by a tree has fallen, being caught in the snare by Thee, God nailed in the flesh, Who grantest peace unto our souls![^1268]

*Troparia:*
Unto thee, O ever-hymned Tree, whereon Christ was stretched out, the turning sword that guarded Eden showed reverence; and the dread Cherub withdrew before Christ Who was nailed upon thee, Who grantest peace unto our souls![^1269]

The adverse powers beneath the earth are terrified of the Cross, when the sign is traced in the air; according whereto the generations of the heavenly and of mortals walk, bending the knee unto Christ, Who grantest peace unto our souls![^1270]

Having shone forth with incorruptible beams, the divine Cross, shining with divine light upon darkened and errant nations, joins them unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grantest peace unto our souls![^1271]

*Another. Heirmos:*
Thou, O my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning those who sing unto Thee in faith from the gloom of ignorance.[^1272]

*Troparia:*
Who can recount thy struggles, O Nicetas, all- -praised one, and the crowns which Christ granted unto Thee who didst suffer for Him?[^1273]

Having accomplished their struggles on earth, the martyrs received from Thee, O Giver of life, their heavenly reward in the highest.[^1274]

Now thou shinest as a luminary, O all-praised Nicetas, becoming a second light, standing gloriously before the Great Light.[^1275]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bear for us, O Mother of God, the Timeless Light Who became subject to time for those who are in the darkness of this life, and thou hast enlightened the whole world.[^1276]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
In the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah, stretching out his hands crosswise, clearly prefigured the saving Passion; therefore coming forth after three days, he depicted the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God nailed in the flesh, Who through His three-day Resurrection has enlightened the world.[^1277]

*Troparia:*
Bowed down with old age and weighed down by sickness, Jacob was uprighted when he crossed his hands, manifesting the operation of the life-bearing Cross; for God, Who was nailed upon it in the flesh, wrote anew the obsolescence of the shadowy script of the Law, and drove away the soul-destroying disease of delusion.[^1278]

Laying his hands crosswise upon the heads of the youths, divine Israel revealed that the older glory belonged to the people serving the Law; therefore, though supposed to have been mistaken, he did not change the life-bearing sign, for he cried: The newly established people of Christ God shall excel, being protected by the Cross![^1279]

*Another. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries out unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that for mercy's sake flowed from Thy side.[^1280]

*Troparia:*
Having desired the beauty of the Creator, O glorious one, and having received radiance from thence, O martyr, thou wast winged with longing; and taking no heed of death, thou didst draw near unto Him.[^1281]

Perceiving passing things with chaste understanding, and surmounting the raging tormentor, O martyr Nicetas, thou didst deliver thy body unto torments with gladness, rejoicing.[^1282]

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee alone as an apple tree in the woods, and as the purest lily and the flower of the valley, O Mother of God, the noetic Bridegroom took up His abode in thee.[^1283]

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 2, Podoben:*

*Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Having cut down the dominion of delusion by thy endurance, and having received the crown of victory in thy sufferings, O glorious Nicetas, named after victory, thou rejoicest with the angels, praying with them unceasingly unto Christ God for us all.[^1284]

*Ikos:*
Planting Thy knowledge within my soul, cleanse my thoughts and make me a doer of Thy commandments, O Savior, that I may be able to overcome the various assaults of my passions, receiving the victorious prize of dispassion through the prayers of Thy noble passion-bearer Nicetas, O Lover of mankind; for He Himself has gathered us together to commemorate him in his memorial, who prays unceasingly for us all.[^1285]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The mad command of the impious tormentor, breathing threat and God-hated blasphemy, shook the people; yet the bestial fury did not terrify the three youths, nor the consuming fire; but when the dew-bearing wind blew against it, being in the midst of the fire, they sang: Blessed art Thou, the supremely hymned God of our fathers and our God![^1286]

*Troparia:*
Having tasted of the tree, the first among men took up his dwelling in corruption; for being condemned by a most dishonorable rejection of life, a certain bodily corruption befell his whole race as an affliction of disease. But having found restoration through the Tree of the Cross, we the earthborn cry: Blessed art Thou, the supremely hymned God of our fathers and our God![^1287]

Disobedience broke the commandment of God, and the tree brought death unto men, having been unseasonably partaken of; and for the confirmation of what was most honorable, the tree of life was thenceforth forbidden, which was opened unto the thief of evil faith when he wisely cried: Blessed art Thou, the supremely hymned God of our fathers and our God![^1288]

Israel, embracing the top of Joseph's staff, foreseeing the future, manifested the majesty of the kingdom, showing forth how the most glorious Cross would prevail; for it is the victorious boast of kings, and a light unto those who cry in faith: Blessed art Thou, the supremely hymned God of our fathers and our God![^1289]

*Another. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, the Abrahamic youths, inflamed rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1290]

*Troparia:*
Illumined now with unapproachable radiance, O martyr, enlighten with thy light those who now sing of thy festival, as thou criest: Blessed art Thou, my God and Lord![^1291]

The angelic hosts were astonished at thy courage, O blessed one, beholding thee suffering patiently and saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of all and Lord![^1292]

*Theotokion:*
With the choir above, the bodiless Gabriel rejoicing cried out unto thee: Rejoice, O pure Mother of God; blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady![^1293]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Bless God the Father, the Creator, O ye youths equal in number to the Trinity; hymn the Word Who came down and changed the fire into dew; and supremely exalt unto the ages the all-holy Spirit Who gives life unto all![^1294]

*Troparia:*
Hymn the Wood being elevated, sprinkled with the blood of the incarnate God the Word, O heavenly hosts! Celebrating the restoration of the earthborn, O ye people, worship the Cross of Christ, through which resurrection came to the world unto the ages![^1295]

O ye earthborn, ministers of grace, elevate with your hands in sacred manner the Cross whereon Christ God stood, and the spear that pierced the body of God the Word, that all nations may see the salvation of God, glorifying Him unto the ages![^1296]

Rejoice, ye who were pre-elected by divine judgment! Boast, ye faithful Christian kings, in the victorious weapon, having received from God the precious Cross; for by this the tribes of wars seeking boldness are scattered unto the ages![^1297]

*Another. Heirmos:*
Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1298]

*Troparia:*
Thou didst offer thyself as a whole and acceptable sacrifice, O unconquerable martyr, and wast a sweet-smelling whole offering unto thy Master Who was crucified for our sake, crying with gladness: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1299]

Lawfully, as a divine warrior, having overthrown the enemy hosts, thou didst worthily receive an unfading crown of victory from the life-bearing right hand before which thou now standest, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord![^1300]

Thou didst immeasurably love Christ, and didst mingle Thy blood with His blood, being crushed by wounds and slain in diverse manners; therefore now, as His imitator, thou reignest together with Him, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1301]

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth to Christ, the only most pure One, thou hast clearly washed away the defilement of our nature, O pure and all-immaculate Mother of God; and thou wast higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim, who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1302]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Mother of God, who untilled didst bud forth Christ, by Whom the life-bearing Tree of the Cross was planted on earth; therefore now that it is being elevated, worshiping it, we magnify thee.[^1303]

*Troparia:*
Let all the trees of the forest rejoice, for their nature is sanctified by Him by Whom they were planted in the beginning, when Christ was stretched out upon the Tree; therefore now that it is being elevated, worshiping it, we magnify thee.[^1304]

The sacred horn is raised up, the Cross, head unto all the divinely wise, by which all the horns of sinners are spiritually shattered; therefore now that it is being elevated, worshiping it, we magnify thee.[^1305]

*Another. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out from thee without hands, O Virgin, from the uncut mountain, even Christ Who united the divided natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God.[^1306]

*Troparia:*
I offer my whole self unto thee, O divinely blessed Nicetas, that I may find thee an intercessor before the Master, able to save from every tribulation, and an advocate of divine salvation.[^1307]

Thou wast a true witness of the Truth, O passion-bearer; now rejoicing thou standest before the hypostatic and venerable Truth, receiving with boldness the rewards of the struggles of thy contest.[^1308]

Having reached the tranquil harbor, thou didst rest from afflictions; and crowned, thou rejoicest in Paradise with the martyrs of Christ; therefore we now worthily glorify thee, as thou art divinely glorified.[^1309]

*Theotokion:*
Apart from the laws of nature, thou didst give birth to the Lawgiver, Who for His ineffable compassion immutably became flesh, O blessed and pure one, being recognized in two natures.[^1310]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ оу҆слы́шите):*

Being protected by the weapon of Thy precious Cross, Thy passion-bearer, O Word, mightily overcame the adverse powers and put the tormentors to shame, and suffered for Thee; and with Thee, O my Christ, King of all, Nicetas reigns. Twice.[^1311]

*Glory, Both now, of the Cross:*
The Cross is elevated today, and the world is sanctified; the angelic ranks hymn Him Who was crucified for our sake, and they triumph with us and rejoice together, crying twice: The Master has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth![^1312]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Today the Cross of Christ is elevated, the life-bearing Tree, whereon He was nailed in the flesh, calling all.[^1313]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [LXX Ps. 98:5].*

Rejoice, divine guardian of the faithful, unconquerable wall, Cross of the Lord, through which we were lifted up from the earth![^1314]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [LXX Ps. 73:12].*

Come with gladness, let us all kiss the life-bearing Tree, whereon Christ, our deliverance, was stretched out.[^1315]

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 2:*
Today the whole universe rejoices in the sufferings of the passion-bearer; and the Church of Christ, adorned with flowers, cries out unto thee, O martyr of Christ: O favorite of Christ and most fervent advocate, cease not to pray for thy servants![^1316]

*Both now, in the same tone:*
Today the garden of life comes forth from the subterranean depths of the earth, certifying the Resurrection of Christ Who was nailed upon it; and being elevated by priestly hands, it proclaims His ascension into heaven, through which our compound nature, from its fall unto the earth, now dwells in the heavens. Therefore let us cry out with thanksgiving: O Lord Who wast lifted up upon it, and thereby hast raised us up together with Thee, vouchsafe unto us Thy heavenly joy, as Thou art the Lover of mankind![^1317]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 4 on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance: "Save us, O Son of God, Who wast crucified in the flesh, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia." Thus we sing even until the Apodosis. Prokeimenon of the Feast, and until the Apodosis. And of the Saint, Tone 7: "The righteous shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in Him." Verse: "Hear, O God, my voice..." [LXX Ps. 63:2, 11]. Epistle to Timothy, pericope 292.*[^1318]

*Alleluia, Tone 4: "The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree." Verse: "Those that are planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of our God" [LXX Ps. 91:13–14]. Gospel from Matthew, pericope 36. Communion hymn of the Feast, and until the Apodosis; and of the Saint: "The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance" [LXX Ps. 111:6].*[^1319]

*Note: Saturday after the Exaltation. Epistle to the Corinthians, pericope 125 from the midpoint. Gospel from John, pericope 30.*[^1320]

*Sunday after the Exaltation. Note: Prokeimenon of the Feast; Epistle to the Galatians, pericope 203. Gospel from Mark, pericope 37. Communion hymn of the day, and of the Feast.*[^1321]

*Note: It is proper to know: If the Exaltation of the Precious Cross falls on a Saturday:*
*On the Sunday after the Exaltation, the Epistle and Gospel are read on the morrow of the Feast, on Sunday.*
*On the following Saturday, at the Apodosis of the Feast, the Epistle and Gospel of the Saturday after the Exaltation are read first, and then the daily reading.*[^1322]

*It is proper to know: If the after-feast of the Exaltation of the Precious Cross falls on a Sunday, and the Saint is sung on 4 or on 6:*
*On Saturday at Small Vespers: Resurrectional Stichera, and of the Mother of God, as usual. Resurrectional Troparion; Glory, Both now, its Theotokion.*[^1323]

*At Great Vespers. Note: After the usual Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," Resurrectional Stichera, 3; and 1 Anatolian; and of the Feast, 3 of that day; and of the Saint of the Menaion, 3. But if the Saint is sung on 6, or if he has a Polyeleos, then we sing: Resurrectional Stichera, 3; and of the Feast, 3; and of the Saint, 4. Glory, of the Saint; Both now, Dogmatic Theotokion of the tone. At the Liti, the Stichera of the Feast of that day from the Aposticha. Glory, Both now, of the Feast, written at Matins at the Aposticha; but if the Saint has a Glory: Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Stichera. Glory, of the Saint, if there be one; Both now, of the Feast; but if not: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At the blessing of the loaves, the Troparion "O Mother of God and Virgin," twice; and of the Feast, once.*[^1324]

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Resurrectional Troparion, twice; Glory, of the Saint, if there be one; Both now, of the Feast. But if not: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. After the Kathismata, Resurrectional Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia; and a reading from the Commentary Gospel for the Sunday after the Exaltation. And the Evlogitaria with troparia; Hypakoe of the tone; and a reading from the Commentary Gospel for the Sunday in course. But if the Saint has a Polyeleos, after the two Kathismata we sing the Polyeleos of the Saint* and after the Polyeleos, the troparia: "The angelic assembly"; and the Hypakoe of the tone, and all the Sessional Hymns of the Saint, and a reading. The Graduals, and the Prokeimenon of the tone; and "Let every breath"; the Resurrection Gospel; and the Resurrection Sticheron, and the rest as on Sunday. The Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Mother of God on 2; and of the Feast on 4; and of the Saint on 4; Katavasia of the Feast. But if the Saint has a Polyeleos or Doxology, then we sing: the Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Feast on 4; and of the Saint on 6. After Ode 3, the Kontakion of the Feast, and of the Saint; and if he has also an Ikos, and the Sessional Hymn of the Saint; Glory, Both now, of the Feast, and a reading. After Ode 6, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Prologue. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." The Resurrection Exapostilarion; Glory, of the Saint, if he has one; but if not: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera, 4; and of the Saint, if he has them, 3 Prosomoia; and the Idiomelon which is for the Glory, we sing with its refrains. But if the Saint does not have Praises, then we sing: Resurrectional Stichera, 4; and of the Feast, 4, from the Aposticha of that day at Matins, with the refrains of the Feast. Glory, Evangelical Sticheron; Both now: "Thou art most blessed." The Great Doxology; and thereafter, only the Resurrection Troparion. Litanies and Dismissal; and the Catechesis, and the usual procession into the narthex. Then the First Hour. At the First Hour, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory, of the Feast; Both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After the Our Father, the Kontakion of the Feast. Likewise also at the other Hours we say the Kontakion of the Feast and of the Resurrection alternately; and if there is a Polyeleos, also of the Saint.[^1325]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the tone on 6, and the Ode of the Feast in course on 4. But if the Saint has an Ode: the Resurrection Beatitudes on 4; and the Ode of the Feast in course on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Troparion of the Resurrection and of the Feast; then of the church, and of the Saint if he has one. Glory, Kontakion of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. But if the Saint does not have a Troparion and Kontakion: Glory, of the Resurrection; Both now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Sunday after the Exaltation; then of the Saint, if he has them; but if not, of the day in course; and the Prokeimenon of the tone is omitted. Communion hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens"; another of the Saint, if he has one; but if not, of the Feast.*[^1326]

*The 16th Day of the Same Month: The Holy Great-Martyr Euphemia the All-Praised. On the same day, the Holy Hieromartyr Josaphat, Archbishop of Polotsk. His service is written after this service.*[^1327]

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Today Thy precious Cross, O Christ, shines forth luminously as the sun, being set fast upon the place of the skull, a place most glorious; and being elevated, O Savior, upon Thy most holy mountain, it shows forth most clearly that thereby, O Almighty One, Thou hast exalted our nature unto the heavens, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.[^1328]

Today the heavens declared Thy glory, incomprehensible unto men; for having shone forth the sign of the luminous Cross with unapproachable light, it exposed the furious and cruel disposition of the deicides; therefore we glorify Thy dispensation of love for mankind, O Jesus Almighty, Savior of our souls.[^1329]

By the stretching out of his hands, Moses conquered Amalek, prefiguring the sign of the Cross; and we, now worshiping the Tree of the Cross, trample down the wiles and stratagems of the enemy, having Christ as our Champion, Who was elevated upon it in the flesh, and put the serpent to death, and saved man.[^1330]

*Other Stichera of the Saint, in the same tone, Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́бля):*
Having adorned thy soul with the beauties of virginity and the blood of martyrdom, O glorious martyr, thou wast betrothed unto the Creator, Who truly preserves thee incorrupt forever; therefore thou makest choral dance with the hosts of the archangels and the choirs of angels, apostles, prophets, and martyrs, O all-praised one![^1331]

Being bound unto wheels, torn by wild beasts, and tried by fire and water, having sharpened thy mind with the divine Spirit, thou didst manly drown the ruler of darkness in streams of blood, and didst ascend unto the noetic bridal chambers, offering thy suffering as an eternal dowry unto thy Bridegroom, O virgin.[^1332]

Though dead, yet ever living, thou didst pour forth shedding of blood unto the praise of the Lord, O martyr refreshing the faithful and enlightening them with knowledge, but drowning the faithless enemies therein; therefore the divine scroll of church dogmas was entrusted unto thee, which thou keepest and holdest unto the ages.[^1333]

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Thou who didst blossom forth with virtues and wast enlightened in understanding, pouring forth myrrh into the hearts of the faithful, who didst shine forth from the East as a radiant star, and didst assemble the gathering of the divine Fathers by the descent of the Holy Spirit: cease not to pray unto the Lord for us, O all-praised Euphemia, that our souls may be saved![^1334]

*Both now, of the Cross, in the same tone:*
The four-cornered world is sanctified today when Thy four-part Cross is elevated, O Christ our God, and the horn of our faithful King is exalted together with it; thereby do we crush the horns of the enemies. Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous in Thy works; glory to Thee![^1335]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Тридне́венъ):*
We worship the place where the feet of Christ stood, elevating the thrice-blessed Cross, whereon was poured forth the Master's blood, Who poured forth resurrection for the world.[^1336]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [LXX Ps. 98:5].*

Having put to death the passions of the flesh and of the spirit, O divinely wise ones, let us make haste to be lifted up from earthly things into the heavenly resting-places by the elevation of the Cross, having been saved by the goodness of Christ.[^1337]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [LXX Ps. 73:12].*

The never-failing fountain from the divine ribs clearly boiled forth the Word, watering the souls of those who worship His divine passions, and Cross, and Resurrection in faith.[^1338]

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 8. By Byzantios:*
Let every tongue be moved unto the praising of the all-praised Euphemia; let every tribe and every age, young men and virgins, crown the virgin-martyr of Christ with praises! For having acted manly according to the Law, and cast off womanly weakness, by martyr's pains she cast down the tormentor enemy; and adorned with a heavenly and divine crown, she prays unto her Bridegroom and God to grant us great mercy.[^1339]

*Both now, of the Feast, in the same tone. By the Studite Monk:*

...Him Whom Moses of old prefigured in himself, casting down Amalek and conquering him; and David the psalmist, crying aloud, commanded to worship at Thy footstool, Thy precious Cross, O Christ God: today we sinners worship with unworthy lips, singing unto Thee Who wast pleased to be nailed upon it, we pray: O Lord, with the thief vouchsafe us Thy Kingdom![^1340]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy lamb, O Jesus, Euphemia, cries with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking Thee I endure suffering, and am crucified with Thee, and buried with Thee in Thy baptism, and I suffer for Thy sake that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may also live with Thee; but as an unblemished sacrifice accept me who with love have sacrificed myself unto Thee. By her prayers, as Thou art merciful, save our souls![^1341]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast:*
Save, O Lord, Thy people...

*At Matins, after the first Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "At the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
Thou didst deign to suffer the Cross and death, having set this up in the midst of creation, when Thou wast pleased, O Savior, to have Thy body nailed; then also the sun hid its rays. Beholding these things upon the Cross, the thief also sang unto Thee, crying: Remember me, O Lord; and having believed, he received Paradise.[^1342]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*After the second Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "Hope of the world" (Надѣ́жда мі́ра):*
Upon the Tree of the Cross, O Savior, for the compassions of Thy mercy, having been wounded in the side and pierced with a spear, Thou didst tear up the cruel handwriting of our sins, as Almighty God; therefore we piously sing of Thine ineffable dispensation, O Word![^1343]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*The Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Saint on 6.*

*The Canon of the Feast, Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Moses, having traced the Cross directly with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel who went on foot; and striking it reversely, he brought it together upon the chariots of Pharaoh, having inscribed the invincible weapon. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1344]

*Troparia:*
Moses of old prefigured the image of the most pure Passion in himself, standing in the midst of the sacred ones; and shaping the Cross, he raised up victory with outstretched palms, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God unto our God, for He has been glorified![^1345]

Moses placed upon a pillar a remedy against the venomous bite, deliverance from corruption; and unto the tree in the form of the Cross he bound the serpent that crawls upon the ground, in this exposing the malice of the deceitful one. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1346]

Heaven showed forth the victory of the Cross unto the ruler of piety and God-wise King, in which the ferocity of malignant enemies was cast down, and deceit was overturned, and the divine faith was spread abroad unto the ends of the earth. Therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1347]

*Another Canon of the Saint.*
*Whose acrostic is:*
*I praise the all-praised maiden.*
*A creation of John. Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone has been gloriously glorified.[^1348]

*Troparia:*
The all-praised maiden draws the hosts of the supramundane and the choirs of earthly ones unto song by her wonders.[^1349]
