Having despised noble birth and the splendor that comes from riches, the venerable Euphemia acquired Christ instead of all things.[^1350]

Having desired the beauty of the Good One of all, of thy most beautiful heart, O all-praised one, He accounted thee worthy of the heavenly bridal chambers.[^1351]

*Theotokion:*
O most pure Mother of God, who beyond nature gavest birth unto the incarnate, co-eternal, and super-divine Word: we sing of thee.[^1352]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The rod is taken as an image of a mystery, for by its budding it predetermines the priest; and for the Church that was previously barren, now the Tree of the Cross has blossomed forth, for her strength and confirmation.[^1353]

*Troparia:*
As the rock, being struck, poured forth water for a disobedient and hard-hearted people, it manifested the mystery of the God-called Church, whereof the Cross is the strength and confirmation.[^1354]

When Thy most pure side was pierced with a spear, water with blood flowed forth, renewing the testament and washing away sin; for the Cross is the boast of the faithful, and the strength and confirmation of kings.[^1355]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Thou art the confirmation of those that flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of those darkened, and my spirit sings of Thee.[^1356]

*Troparia:*
Thou didst appear in the judgment hall bearing a manly soul, and didst vanquish the enemy as unmanly, O all-praised one There was no blemish in thy beauty, nor wrinkle in thy soul; and Christ received thee as a bride into the incorruptible bridal chambers.[^1357]

Heal the wounds of my soul, O all-praised martyr of Christ, and calm the tempest of my life by thy prayers.[^1358]

*Theotokion:*
We Christians have all acquired thee as a refuge and our wall, and we ceaselessly glorify thee, O unwedded one.[^1359]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на кре́стъ):*
O Thou Who of Thine own will wast lifted up upon the Cross, bestow Thy compassions upon Thy new commonwealth named after Thee, O Christ God; gladden by Thy power [our faithful king],[^1360] granting him victories over adversaries, having Thine aid as a weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy.

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into Paradise, and heard unspeakable and divine words which it is not lawful for human tongues to utter, what writes he unto the Galatians, as lovers of the Scriptures have read and known? God forbid, he says, that I should boast, save only in the Cross of the Lord [Gal. 6:14], upon which having suffered, He slew the passions. That Cross of the Lord, therefore, let us all assuredly hold fast as our boast; for this saving Tree is unto us a weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy.[^1361]

*Sessional Hymn of the Saint, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
By the streams of thy blood, O martyr of Christ, thou dost ever work a deluge for the ungodly, O all-praised one; and by the outpourings of grace thou dost always water the spiritual fields, in which thou makest the wheat-ear of faith to grow. Therefore, most gloriously even after death thou didst appear as a cloud pouring forth the witness of life, O all-praised passion-bearer. Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who with love honor thy holy memory. Twice.[^1362]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast, in the same tone:*
In the midst of Eden a tree sprouted death, but in the midst of all the earth a Tree blossomed forth life; for having tasted of the first, though being incorruptible, we became corruptible; but having obtained the second, we enjoyed incorruption. For by the Cross, as God, Thou savest the human race.[^1363]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy divinity.[^1364]

Moses transformed with wood the bitter-producing springs in the wilderness of old, manifesting through the Cross the transformation of the nations unto piety.[^1365]

The Jordan, having embedded within its depth the axe, yielded it unto the wood, through the Cross and baptism signifying the cutting down of deceit.[^1366]

The four-part host of the people holy encamp, marching before the image of the tabernacle of witness, being glorified in cross-formed ranks.[^1367]

Being wondrously stretched out, the Cross shed forth sunbeams, and the heavens declared the glory of our God [LXX Ps. 18:2].[^1368]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. The same Heirmos.*

*Troparia:*
Having fashioned thyself as an undefiled mirror of divine understandings, as a most radiant beacon among the female sufferers, O martyr, thou didst shine forth.[^1369]

Thou didst not offer sacrifices unto the baneful demon, O unconquerable martyr; for thou didst love to receive a life-bearing death for the sake of piety.[^1370]

As one bearing a body fearlessly with the passion-bearers, O blameless one, thou didst remain insensible to wounds through the love of divine longing.[^1371]

Patiently suffering, thy face, O martyr, was radiantly adorned with wounds, and by the lightning of the divine Spirit it darkened the thoughts of the enemies.[^1372]

*Theotokion:*
Grant us cleansing of our ignorance, as Thou art sinless, and give peace unto Thy world, O God, through the prayers of her who gave Thee birth.[^1373]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ the King and Lord was crucified, through which he who deceived by the tree fell, being deceived by Thee, God nailed in the flesh, Who grantest peace unto our souls![^1374]

*Troparia:*
Unto thee, O ever-hymned Tree, whereon Christ was stretched out, the turning flaming sword that guarded Eden gave way in shame, O Cross; and the dread Cherub yielded unto Christ Who was nailed upon thee, Who grantest peace unto our souls.[^1375]

The subterranean contrary powers are terrified when the sign is traced in the air, wherein the generations of the heavenly and the earthly walk, bending the knee unto Christ, Who grantest peace unto our souls.[^1376]

With incorruptible rays the divine Cross appeared unto the darkened nations that were wandering in deceit, having flashed forth the divine light appropriates unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grantest peace unto our souls.[^1377]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Rising at dawn we cry unto Thee, O Lord: Save us! For Thou art our God; besides Thee we know none other.[^1378]

*Troparia:*
Having recognized the contrariety of day and of the world, thou didst not desire to love the war-loving demon.[^1379]

Thinking to weaken thy divine fortitude, O martyr, the all-crafty one became a laughing-stock by his wiles.[^1380]

Grant me enlightenment and peace, O all-praised one, resolving the much-troubled confusion by thy prayers.[^1381]

*Theotokion:*
We hymn thee as Mother of God after childbirth, for thou in the flesh hast borne the God-Word unto the world.[^1382]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
In the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah stretched out his hands in the form of a cross, clearly prefiguring the saving Passion; thence emerging on the third day, he depicted the supramundane Resurrection of Christ God nailed in the flesh, Who enlightened the world by His three-day Resurrection.[^1383]

*Troparia:*
Bent by old age and weighed down by infirmity, Jacob straightened himself up, having crossed his hands, manifesting the operation of the life-bearing Cross; for God, Who was nailed in the flesh upon it, wrote anew the antiquity of the shadowed writing of the Law, and drove away the soul-destroying disease of deceit.[^1384]

Having laid his hands crosswise upon the youths, the divine Israel showed forth their heads, as the elder glory, the people serving the Law; therefore, seeming thus to be deceived, he changed not the life-bearing image; for the newly established people of Christ God, they cried, shall abide, being walled about by the Cross.[^1385]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Grant me a robe of light, O Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment [LXX Ps. 103:2], O most merciful Christ our God![^1386]

*Troparia:*
Bearing a divine disposition of soul in female flesh, O glorious one, thou didst take no heed of the beasts that were in the waters.[^1387]

Thou didst overcome the pride of the tormentors without harm in the waters, O unconquerable martyr, abiding with the beasts like Jonah.[^1388]

Having heard thy prayers, the Lord delivered Thee from the corruption of the beasts, O all-praised one, as Daniel from the den.[^1389]

*Theotokion:*
O thou who alone by a word gavest birth unto the Word in the flesh, deliver we pray, our souls from the snares of the enemy.[^1390]

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
In thy suffering thou didst contest well, and after death thou sanctifiest us with outpourings of wonders, O all-praised one. Therefore we sing of thy holy dormition, fleeing with faith unto thy divine temple, that we may be delivered from soul-afflicting ailments, and may draw forth the grace of wonders.[^1391]

*Ikos:*
The temple of the all-praised one appeared as a paradise, having in the midst as a tree of immortality her honorable body. Those who gather its fair-flowering fruits are quickly sanctified; for beholding it, they marvel: How does the dead body, as if alive, pour forth blood, making all things fragrant? Therefore with diligence come with me, all ye humble ones, and let us cleanse ourselves of every defilement, kissing this, and let us draw forth the grace of wonders![^1392]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The mindless decree of the impious tormentor shook the people, breathing threatening and God-hated blasphemy; yet the three youths were not terrified by bestial rage, nor by the devouring fire; but when the dew-bearing Spirit blew against it, being with the fire they sang: O God of our fathers, and our God, blessed art Thou![^1393]

*Troparia:*
Having tasted of the tree, the first among men settled in corruption; for being condemned by the most dishonorable rejection of life, he transmitted to all his race a certain bodily corruption, as the harm of a disease; but having found restoration through the Tree of the Cross, we earthly-born cry: O God of our fathers, and our God, blessed art Thou![^1394]

Disobedience dissolved the commandment of God, and the tree brought death unto men, which was unseasonably partaken of; but for the confirmation of the greatly honored, the Tree of Life was forbidden from thence; which He opened unto the ill-believing thief who cried prudently: O God of our fathers, and our God, blessed art Thou![^1395]

Israel, seeing things to come, embraces the top of the staff of Joseph, manifesting the mighty power of the kingdom, as the most glorious Cross shall prevail; for this is the victorious boast of kings, and light unto those that cry with faith: O God of our fathers, and our God, blessed art Thou![^1396]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
The youths who went down from Judea to Babylon of old trampled down the flame of the furnace by faith in the Trinity, singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^1397]

*Troparia:*
The good courage of the divine martyrs appeared beyond mind; for the Creator of all subdues creation unto those who cry in sufferings: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^1398]

The most renowned maiden stopped the hungry mouths of the tormentors and the pride of the lawless by the Holy Spirit, divinely singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^1399]

The furnace heated of old burned up the three venerable ones; but now the God-wise one, singing of the three trials, caught the servants who sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^1400]

Mystically the Bridegroom, having come into the furnace unto the all-honorable bride, by the dew of the Spirit and the good pleasure of the Father, preserved her as she sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^1401]

*Theotokion:*
As Thou wast pleased to establish our salvation, O Savior, Thou didst dwell in the womb of the Virgin, whom Thou didst show forth as an advocate unto the world: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^1402]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
O youths equal in number to the Trinity, bless God the Father, the Creator; hymn the Word Who came down and changed the fire into dew; and supremely exalt the all-holy Spirit Who gives life unto all, unto the ages![^1403]

*Troparia:*
Hymn the heavenly Hosts the Wood being elevated, sprinkled with the blood of God the incarnate Word; O ye people celebrating the restoration of the earthly-born, worship the Cross of Christ, through which is the resurrection of the world unto the ages![^1404]

Ye earthly-born, ministers of the grace of the Cross, upon which Christ God stood: with your hands hierarchically elevate also the spear that pierced the body of the God-Word, that all the nations may see the salvation of God, glorifying Him unto the ages![^1405]

Rejoice, ye faithful Christian kings, pre-chosen by divine judgment; boast in the victorious weapon, having received from God the precious Cross; for in this the tribes of battles, seeking boldness, shall be scattered unto the ages![^1406]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
The King of heaven, Whom the angelic hosts hymn: praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1407]

*Troparia:*
O most blessed among women, having the reward of the grace of the Most High, singing, praise Christ unto all ages![^1408]

Strengthened by the thought of the Bridegroom, through immaterial longing thou didst surrender thy body thou didst surrender thy body unto death, and thou livest unto all ages.[^1409]

*Troparia:*
Armed with the Holy Spirit against deceit as against wild beasts, O martyr, thou didst receive the reward unto all ages.[^1410]

Thou didst not receive a soul-corrupting death, O pure one, but with good boldness by the bite of the beasts, O blameless one, thou didst exchange this for an ageless life unto all ages.[^1411]

*Theotokion:*
Thou drivest away the assaults of misfortunes and the attacks of passions, O Virgin; therefore we sing of thee unto all ages.[^1412]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Death, which came upon the race through the eating of the tree, has been abolished today through the Cross; for the universal ancestral curse has been loosed through the budding forth of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly Hosts magnify.[^1413]

*Troparia:*
Not having left the murderous bitterness that was from the tree, O Lord, for Thou didst utterly destroy it through the Cross; for this reason Thou didst also sweeten of old with wood the bitterness of the waters of Marah, prefiguring the operation of the Cross, which all the heavenly Hosts magnify.[^1414]

Those continually plunged in the darkness of the forefather, O Lord, Thou hast exalted today through the Cross; for as nature was completely and unrestrainedly brought low through deceit, so the light of Thy Cross has restored us again universally, which we the faithful magnify.[^1415]

That Thou mightest show unto the world an image to be worshiped, O Lord of the Cross, Thou hast depicted in all things as most glorious in the heavens, illumined with measureless light, an unconquerable panoply for the king; therefore all the heavenly Hosts magnify Thee.[^1416]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Thee, the Mother of the Most High God unwedded, Thee who beyond understanding hast given birth by a word unto the true God, higher than the most pure Hosts: with unceasing hymnody do we magnify.[^1417]

*Troparia:*
The stream of living blood, a sign of the incorruptible life granted unto thee from on high, O all-praised martyr, has appeared as an unceasing treasury of healings unto those who draw it forth in faith.[^1418]

Death touched thee by the law of nature, O divinely wise one, but dispassionately thou didst clothe thyself in life-bearing mortification, wherein having laid thy most honorable body as though animate, thou livest incorruptibly, and thy blood-streamings bear witness.[^1419]

Crowned with the laws of suffering, O martyr, proclaimer of Christ proclaimer of Christ, the scroll of the honorable dogmas of piety was entrusted unto thee from the hands of the Council, O Euphemia, which holding as a living pillar of Orthodoxy thou showest forth.[^1420]

*Theotokion:*
O unwedded Bride, vessel of sweet fragrance, as the true and undefiled one, and cloud of divine light, who received the heavenly rain within thy womb: O Virgin Mother, we magnify thee.[^1421]

*Exapostilarion:*
Having endured death, thou livest in God, and thou abidest alive, O all-praised Euphemia; and holding His scroll in thine embrace, thou wast a fore-pillar of the Orthodox who celebrate thy precious and all-sacred memory in faith. Twice.[^1422]

*Glory, Both now, of the Cross:*
With radiant splendors the Cross of the Lord, set forth for its elevation, summons all with divine longing: come, let us all kiss it faithfully with joy and love and fear, and let us glorify the only Creator and Master.[^1423]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 3. Idiomela:*
Seeing the suffering triumph celebrated in divine wisdom, O faithful, let us sing a thanksgiving song unto our God Who is marvelous in counsel; for He conquered the invisible power of the contrary force in female nature, and perfected His divine power in the weakness of the victoriously triumphant one: by her prayers He saves our souls. Twice.[^1424]

Having mingled a cup of truth from her own suffering blood, the all-praised martyr of Christ offers this ever unto the Church, wherein with the voice of wisdom she summons the foster-children of the Church, saying: Draw ye the drink that witnesses to the Resurrection, driving away the unfaithful, cleansing passions, and preserving pious souls, crying unto the Savior: O Thou Who hast refreshed us with the torrent of the sweetness of the Spirit, save our souls![^1425]

Having sealed our souls with the blood of Christ on the day of redemption, let us prophetically draw forth with spiritual joy the holy blood that gushes abundantly for us from the martyr's spring, figuratively representing the life-flowing passions of the Savior and His co-eternal glory. Therefore let us cry unto Him: O Lord Who art glorified in Thy saints, through the prayers of Thine all-praised passion-bearer, save our souls![^1426]

*Glory, Tone 6:*
At the right hand of the Savior stood the virgin and passion-bearer and martyr Euphemia, clothed with virtues, unconquered, and adorned with the oil of purity and the blood of suffering, and crying unto Him, joyfully holding a lamp: Unto the fragrance of Thy myrrh have I run, O Christ God, for I am wounded by Thy love; separate me not, O heavenly Bridegroom! By her prayers send down upon us Thy mercies, O almighty Savior.[^1427]

*Both now, in the same tone:*
Today the Cross of the Lord comes forth, and the faithful receive it with longing, and take healings of soul and body and of every disease. Let us kiss it with joy and fear: with fear, because of sin, as we are unworthy; but with joy, because of the salvation which Christ God, Who was nailed upon it, grants unto the world, as He has great mercy.[^1428]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
With mystical songs let us concordantly hymn the Cross of the Lord, whereon the Savior was crucified, the Resurrection of all.[^1429]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [LXX Ps. 98:5].*

Come, ye multitudes of monastics, having assembled, let us divinely hymn the life-bearing Tree whereon Christ was stretched out.[^1430]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [LXX Ps. 73:12].*

Let us, the faithful, glorify the Cross of the Lord, whereon the Master's blood was poured forth for the deliverance of all.[^1431]

*Glory, Tone 4. By Byzantios:*
Today the choirs of the Fathers, having assembled for Christ's sake, bring unto thee the scroll of the Orthodox faith, O all-praised one, which receiving into thy precious hands thou keepest unto the end. Therefore the assemblies of men, having come together, honor thy suffering, crying out piously: Rejoice, O all-praised one, who didst transform female nature into a manly array! Rejoice, O all-praised one, who didst preserve unharmed the Orthodox faith handed down by the Fathers! Rejoice, as thou prayest for our souls![^1432]

*Both now, in the same tone. By Andrew of Jerusalem:*
Today truly the hundred-fold voice of David has received its end; for behold, clearly we worship the footstool of Thy most pure feet [LXX Ps. 98:5, 131:7], and hoping in the shadow of Thy wings [LXX Ps. 16:8], we cry unto Thee, O all-bountiful One Let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us [LXX Ps. 4:7]. Exalt the horn of Thy faithful people by the elevation of Thy precious Cross, O Christ, O most merciful One![^1433]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast, Ode 3 on 4; and of the Martyr, Ode 6 on 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel." Verse: "In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel" [LXX Ps. 67:36, 27]. Epistle to the Corinthians, pericope 181 [2 Cor. 6:1–10]. Alleluia, Tone 6: "With patience I waited for the Lord, and He gave ear unto me" [LXX Ps. 39:2]. Gospel from Luke, pericope 33 [Luke 7:36–50]. Communion hymn: "The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance" [LXX Ps. 111:6].*[^1434]

*On the Same Day: The Holy Hieromartyr Josaphat, Archbishop of Polotsk.*[^1435]

*If it happens on a Sunday: On Saturday at Vespers, we sing the kathisma: "Blessed is the man," the whole kathisma. And at "Lord, I have cried," we sing: Resurrectional Stichera of the tone on 3; and of the Feast of the Exaltation on 3; and of the Saint on 4. But if on another day, we sing "Blessed is the man," the first Glory; and Stichera of the Feast of the Exaltation on 3; and of the Saint on 5.*[^1436]

*Stichera of the Saint, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-praised martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*
Having dyed thy sacred vestment with martyr's blood, thou didst enter into the Holy of Holies, O praiseworthy one, where the voices of those who feast resound, from whom thou receivest the victories of thy labors: an unfading crown, and everlasting beauty, and paradise-life, O Josaphat, hieromartyr! And now pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and peace, and great mercy unto our souls.[^1437]

Having first offered the bloodless sacrifice unto God as a divine hierarch, as a whole fruit-offering, an acceptable sacrifice, thou didst bring thyself in blood as a true hieromartyr unto Christ, O divinely speaking, all-venerable one! And now pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and peace, and great mercy unto our souls.[^1438]

Having cast down the schismatic arrogance by thy hierarch's word, and established with faith the unconfirmed hearts,[^1439] thou didst depart unto eternal life, having suffered for the Union; thou wast the Lord's witness, O hieromartyr Josaphat. And now pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and peace, and great mercy unto our souls.

Having dyed thy sacred vestment with the blood of thy sacred flesh, O holy father, thou didst receive a twofold crown from Christ, O exceedingly rich one,[^1440] and thou dancest with the angels in the heavens, standing before the Holy Trinity: by Whom do thou now pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and peace, and great mercy unto our souls.

O hieromartyr Josaphat, thou didst purely desire an honorable life, having become a worshiper of Jesus the Almighty;[^1441] and thou didst guide the people unto unity by thy precious words and by grace; thou didst pass unto things not temporal, having washed thyself with martyr's blood, O divinely blessed one. And now pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and peace, and great mercy unto our souls.

Having spiritually ascended into the unwaning cloud of unutterable Light, the hieromartyr and pastor learned the unutterable mysteries of Christ; for as a martyr he was enlightened, and as a pastor he was mystically taught; therefore he was also bound with twofold crowns from the glory on high.[^1442] And now pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and peace, and great mercy unto our souls.

*Glory, Tone 2:*
A lawful priest wast thou even unto thy demise, O hieromartyr Josaphat; for celebrating the divine, unutterable mysteries, thou didst pour forth thy blood for Christ God: thou didst bring thyself as an acceptable sacrifice. Therefore, having boldness toward Him, fervently pray for those who with faith celebrate thy most honored memory and revere it: that thy flock and all the world be delivered from misfortunes, from every foreign enemy, and from all tribulations and distresses.[^1443]

*If on Sunday: the Dogmatikon of the Tone. If on another day: Both now, of the Feast, Tone 6:*
Today the four-cornered world is sanctified as Thy four-part Cross is elevated, O Christ our God, and the horn of our faithful King is exalted together with it;[^1444] therefore we crush the horns of our enemies. Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous and marvelous in Thy works, glory to Thee!

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. Then, the Readings:*

*The Reading from Proverbs (composite of Chapters 10, 3, and 8):*
The memory of the righteous man is with praises, and the blessing of the Lord is upon his head [LXX Prov. 10:7, 6]. Blessed is the man that finds wisdom, and the mortal that knows understanding [LXX Prov. 3:13]. For the buying of it is better than treasures of gold and silver. And it is more precious than costly stones; and no precious thing is worthy of it. For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory. Out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and she bears law and mercy upon her tongue [LXX Prov. 3:14–16]. Hear me then, O children, for I speak honorable things; and blessed is the man that shall keep my ways. For my outgoings are the outgoings of life, and the will is prepared from the Lord [LXX Prov. 8:32, 35]. For this cause I entreat you, and put forth my voice to the sons of men: for I, wisdom, have set up counsel, and understanding, and knowledge have I called. Mine is counsel and safety, mine is understanding, and strength is mine. I love them that love me, and those that seek me shall find grace [LXX Prov. 8:4, 12, 14, 17]. Understand therefore, ye simple ones, subtlety, and ye uninstructed, lay it to your heart. Give ear unto me yet again, for I will speak honorable things, and I will open right things from my lips; for my throat shall meditate truth, and lying lips are an abomination before me. All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing in them crooked or perverse. They are all straight to them that understand, and right to them that find knowledge. For I teach you truth, that your hope may be in the Lord, and that ye may be filled with the Spirit [LXX Prov. 8:5–10].[^1445]

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (composite of Chapters 4, 6, 7, 10, 2, and 16):*
When the righteous man is praised, the people shall rejoice; for his memory is immortality, because it is known with God and with men, and his soul was pleasing unto the Lord [Prov. 29:2; Wis. 4:1, 10]. Love wisdom, therefore, O ye men, and ye shall live. Desire her, and ye shall be instructed; for the beginning of her is love, and the keeping of laws [Wis. 6:21, 12, 17–18]. Honor wisdom, that ye may reign unto the ages. I will declare unto you, and will not hide from you the mysteries of God [Wis. 6:21, 22]. For He is the guide of wisdom and the director of the wise; and in His hand is every understanding and knowledge of works, and wisdom will teach all understanding [Wis. 7:15–16]. For in her is an understanding and holy spirit, and the brightness of the everlasting Light, and the image of the goodness of God [Wis. 7:22, 26]. She makes friends of God and prophets. She is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of the stars; being compared with the light, she is found prior. She delivered from pain those who served her, and guided them in straight paths. She gave them holy knowledge, and kept them from them that lay in wait, and gave them a mighty conflict, that they might know that godliness is stronger than all [Wis. 7:27, 29; 10:9–10, 12]. And never shall malice prevail against wisdom, neither shall judgment pass over the wicked to convict them [Wis. 7:30; 1:8]. For they said within themselves, reasoning unrighteously: Let us oppress the righteous man, and let us not spare his holiness, nor let us reverence the ancient gray hairs of the aged [Wis. 2:1, 10]. But let our strength be the law; and let us lie in wait for the righteous, because he is not for our turn, and he is contrary to our doings, and upbraids us with our offending the law, and objects to our infamy the transgressions of our education [Wis. 2:11–12]. He professes to have the knowledge of God, and calls himself the servant of the Lord. He was made to reprove our thoughts, and he is grievous unto us even to behold; for his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion [Wis. 2:13–15]. We are esteemed of him as counterfeits; he abstains from our ways as from filthiness; he pronounces the end of the just to be blessed [Wis. 2:16]. Let us see if his words be true, and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him. Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness and prove his patience. Let us condemn him with a shameful death, for by his own words there shall be a visitation [Wis. 2:17, 19–20]. Such things they did imagine, and were deceived; for their own malice blinded them. And they knew not the mysteries of God, neither did they judge that Thou art the only God, Who hast the power of life and death, and savest in time of tribulation, and deliverest from all evil: Who art compassionate and merciful, and givest grace unto Thy holy ones, and with Thine own arm resistest the proud [Wis. 2:21–22; 16:13, 15].[^1446]

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapters 4 and 5):*
Though the righteous man happen to die early, yet shall he be in rest [Wis. 4:7]. And the righteous that is dead shall condemn the ungodly who are living [Wis. 4:16]. For they shall see the end of the wise, and shall not understand what God in His counsel has decreed of him; for the Lord shall dash them speechless to the ground, and shake them from the foundations, and they shall be utterly laid waste in grief, and their memory shall perish [Wis. 4:17, 19]. For they shall come with fear to the thought of their sins with fear, and their iniquities shall convict them to their face [Wis. 4:20]. Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him and made no account of his labors [Wis. 5:1]. When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation [Wis. 5:2]. And they, repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit, shall say within themselves: This was he whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach, fools that we were! We accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honor [Wis. 5:3–4]. How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints? Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined unto us, and the sun rose not upon us [Wis. 5:5–6]. We filled ourselves with the paths of lawlessness and destruction, and we have gone through deserts where there lay no way, but as for the way of the Lord, we have not known it [Wis. 5:7].[^1447]

*At the Litiya, Sticheron of the Feast, Tone 1:*
Today truly the hundred-fold voice of David has received its end [LXX Ps. 98:5, 131:7]; for behold, we worship the place of the footstool of Thy most pure feet, and hoping in the shadow of Thy wings [LXX Ps. 16:8], we cry unto Thee, O all-bountiful One: Let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us [LXX Ps. 4:7]. Exalt the horn of Thy Orthodox people by the elevation of Thy precious Cross, O Christ, O most merciful One![^1448]

*Stichera of the Saint, Tone 1:*
With divine sacred praises, come, all ye people, let us spiritually celebrate the memory of the hieromartyr Josaphat; for he cut down the thorns of schism, and planted for our souls saving doctrines, abundant with the fruit of sanctification through the virtues.[^1449]

Having ministered the divine Gospel, and sealed the divine doctrines with blood shed by schismatic sheep, O hieromartyr Josaphat: thou didst also enrich the Kyivan see, and didst ascend as a victor into the heavenly realms, having received the crown of victory.[^1450]

A ladder of ascent has doubly acquired thy sacred labors, O hieromartyr Josaphat: which thou also keepest unshaken and unassailed by hostile wolves, as it proclaims thy valors and magnifies thee, O blessed one.[^1451]

*Glory, Tone 5:*
This thy radiant solemnity the Church celebrates rejoicing, O hieromartyr Josaphat, faithfully honoring thee: which cease not as a shepherd to bless, offering prayer for all offering prayer for all.[^1452]

*Both now, in the same tone:*
Come, ye peoples, seeing the most glorious miracle, let us worship the power of the Cross: for as the tree in paradise budded forth death, so this one blossomed forth life, having the sinless Lord nailed upon it. From Whom all nations taking incorruption, we cry: O Thou Who by the Cross didst abolish death and set us free, glory to Thee![^1453]

*If it happens on a Sunday: we sing at the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichera; Glory, to the Saint; Both now, to the Feast. But if on another day, we sing:*
*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Like a radiant sun, thou didst spiritually shine forth upon the firmament of the Church; and the souls darkened by the malice of the enemy thou didst enlighten with the brilliance of thy words, and with divinely wise teaching, and with an angelic life; and thou didst guide the erring onto the true path, and didst bring them unto the unity of the Orthodox Catholic Church; therefore today rejoicing, we celebrate thy radiant and holy memory.[^1454]

*Verse: Thy priests, O Lord, shall be clothed with righteousness, [and Thy saints shall rejoice; LXX Ps. 131:9].*

Equal in honor to the Apostles wast Thou, O hieromartyr Josaphat, having received an equally zealous mind; Thou didst not fear the cruelty of the impious tormentors, but manfully with boldness preaching the unity of the faith, Thou didst endure manifold wounds and tortures; and now Thou hast received a great reward for thy longsuffering from the one Master of the contest, Christ our God: Whom do Thou fervently pray for all who with faith honor thy holy memory.[^1455]

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints [LXX Ps. 115:6].*

Offering an honorable ministry, O hieromartyr Josaphat, and a spotless sacrifice unto the Master Christ God, thou didst bring thine own self unto Him as a whole burnt offering, having suffered manfully for the sake of His love; and thou didst pour out thy blood, and like a true pastor and heir of Christ, thou didst not cease crying: Father, keep them all in Thy name, that they all may be one [John 17:11, 21]. And now, O all-blessed Josaphat, pray that unity be granted unto the Churches, and that all of us who are in the Union may be saved.[^1456]

*Glory, Tone 4:*
 Thy good works have shone like the sun, in heaven and on earth, O pleasing servant of Christ, O all-blessed hieromartyr Josaphat; for orthodoxly thou didst preach unto us the true and spotless faith of Christ, for whose sake thou didst also lay down thy life like a good shepherd, as a true heir of the Chief Shepherd, Christ our God: Whom do thou pray, O all-blessed hierarch, in thy commemoration, O God-bearer, that all who celebrate with love the all-venerable memory of thy suffering may be saved.[^1457]

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 8:*
The Cross which Moses of old prefigured in himself, when he cast down and conquered Amalek [Ex. 17:11]; and which David the psalmist commanded to worship, crying out unto Thy footstool [LXX Ps. 98:5]: unto Thy precious Cross, O Christ God, we sinners bow down today with unworthy lips, and hymning Thee Who didst deign to be nailed upon it, we pray: O Lord, vouchsafe us Thy Kingdom together with the thief![^1458]

*If on Sunday: the Resurrectional Troparion; Glory, to the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. But if on another day, Troparion of the Saint, Tone 4:*
A radiant beacon didst thou appear, O hieromartyr Josaphat; for as a good shepherd thou didst lay down thy life for the sheep, slain by most ferocious enemies; and thou didst enter into the Holy of Holies, taking up thine abode with the bodiless powers. Therefore we pray thee, O longsuffering one: Entreat Christ, the Chief of Shepherds, to number us also among the sheep standing on His right hand, and to save our souls.[^1459]

*Glory, both now: "O Lord, save Thy people..." [Troparion of the Cross, Tone 1].*[^1460]

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma:*
*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*
Having forsaken all earthly things, and lived in the world like an angel in bodily purity, in spirit thou wast a partaker with the angels; thou didst mortify the unclean bodily passions, showing thyself a servant pleasing unto the Holy Trinity, O all-blessed one. Therefore thou also healest the afflictions of the sick, and drivest away evil spirits by the grace of Christ, O God-bearing father, our hieromartyr Josaphat: entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory.[^1461]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast* Joshua, the son of Nun, mystically prefigured of old the image of the Cross, when he stretched out his hands crosswise, O my Savior, and the sun stood still until he cast down the enemies who opposed Thee, O God; for now it set seeing Thee upon the Cross, and having destroyed the dominion of death, Thou didst raise up the whole world together with Thyself.[^1462]

*After the 2nd Kathisma:*
*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ їѡ́сифъ):*
Having made thy heart a fair altar, and ministering the bloodless sacrifices, thou didst offer them unto God; and having suffered steadfastly from impious enemies, and endured diverse torments, thou wast brought as an acceptable sacrifice unto Christ our God Who sacrificed Himself for our sake, O all-blessed hieromartyr Josaphat, all-praised one: Whom do thou fervently pray always, that all who with love hymn thee may be saved.[^1463]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast:*
Moses, stretching out his hands to the height of heaven, prefigured the Cross, the divine weapon of the faithful, whereon Christ nailed our sins; therefore the enemy wept as he suffered, saying painfully in his senses: A wooden spear has pierced me through the midst of my heart; Christ looses all from the bonds of hades.[^1464]

*If it happens on Sunday: the Resurrectional Sessional Hymns. Then: "Praise ye the name of the Lord" [The Polyeleos]; after this:*
*Magnification:*
We magnify thee, O hieromartyr of Christ Josaphat, and we honor thy venerable sufferings which thou didst endure for the Union.[^1465]

*Verse 1: Hear this, all ye nations [LXX Ps. 48:2].*
*Verse 2: My mouth shall speak of wisdom [LXX Ps. 48:4].*
*Verse 3: O Lord, I have loved the beauty of Thy house [LXX Ps. 25:8].*
*Verse 4: The mouth of the righteous will meditate wisdom [LXX Ps. 36:30].*
*Verse 5: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance [LXX Ps. 111:6].*
*Verse 6: Blessed are they that dwell in Thy house [LXX Ps. 83:5].*

*Glory, both now: Alleluia, thrice.*

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4:*
Having cast down the haughtiness of schismatic enemies, as a good shepherd and a mighty, pious warrior, thou didst receive the crown of victory from the right hand of the Most High, Christ our God, the Chief of Shepherds; therefore we praise thee today as a good shepherd and a victorious sufferer, celebrating with faith thine all-festive memory, in which pray that we may be saved from enemies visible and invisible, O hieromartyr of Christ Josaphat, much-suffering one.[^1466]

*Glory, both now, of the Feast, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*
Of old the tree stripped me bare in paradise, the enemy bringing mortification through tasting; but the Tree of the Cross, bearing the garment of life unto men, was planted upon the earth, and the whole world was filled with all manner of joy. Seeing it elevated, let us, the peoples, with faith cry concordantly unto God: Full of glory is Thy house![^1467]

*If it is not Sunday: the Anavathmoi (Hymns of Ascent), Tone 4, 1st Antiphon. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints" [LXX Ps. 115:6]. Verse: "What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?" [LXX Ps. 115:3]. Gospel from John, pericope 35 from the middle: "He that enters not by the door..." [John 10:1–9]. After Psalm 50: Glory: "Through the intercessions of the blessed hieromartyr Josaphat, O merciful One, blot out the multitude of my transgressions." Both now: "Through the prayers of the most holy Birthgiver of God, O merciful One..." Then, Sticheron of the Saint, Tone 2: "A lawful priest wast thou even unto thy demise, O hieromartyr Josaphat..." (as given at Vespers).*[^1468]

*If it happens on a Sunday: the Resurrectional Antiphons are sung; Prokeimenon, Gospel, and the rest. After this, the Resurrectional Canon with its heirmoi and theotokia, then of the Feast and of the Saint according to the Typikon. Katavasia of the Feast. But if on another day: we sing the Canon of the Feast and of the Saint.*[^1469]

*Canon to the Hieromartyr Josaphat.*
*Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought out of the bondage of Egypt, for He has been glorified.[^1470]

*Refrain: Blessed hieromartyr Josaphat, pray unto God for us.*
The noetic Sun revealed thee as a divinely radiant star on the height on the height of His Church; for thou didst illumine the universe with thy sufferings and miracles.[^1471]

*Troparion:*
From youthful age having become divinely blessed unto God, O Josaphat, by the virtues given thee by God thou didst clearly illumine thy soul, and didst make the world bright by thy venerable sufferings for the Union.[^1472]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shine radiantly in the Church of Christ with a twofold luster, O newly appeared hieromartyr; therefore with a twofold crown the Benefactor of all has venerably crowned thee.[^1473]

*Theotokion:*
O most pure Birthgiver of God, who beyond nature didst bear the incarnate, ever-existing, and supernatural Word: we hymn thee.[^1474]

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
Tracing a cross upright with his rod, Moses divided the Red Sea for Israel who went on foot; then striking it crosswise, he brought it together again over Pharaoh's chariots, inscribing the invincible weapon; therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified.[^1475]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit rejoiced when singing: There is none holy like unto our God, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord![^1476]

*Troparion:*
Offering unto the Lord a spotless, fearful, and bloodless sacrifice, thou didst also bring thine own self unblemished unto slaughter with blood, O hieromartyr Josaphat.[^1477]

*Troparion:*
Imitating Christ, thou didst surrender thy life for the Union, O hieromartyr Josaphat, and didst break down the walls of schism.[^1478]

*Troparion:*
By wisdom thou didst destroy the ranks of the schismatics, O blessed Josaphat, having the divine Wisdom established in thy heart, with which thou didst crash down with a noise the arrogance of those foolish ones.[^1479]

*Theotokion:*
Grant us help by thy prayers, O most pure one, driving away the assaults of grievous tribulations.[^1480]

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
The rod is accepted as a figure of the mystery, for by its budding it chooses the priest; and for the Church that before was barren, now the Tree of the Cross has blossomed forth, unto power and steadfastness.[^1481]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Thou Who of Thine own will wast lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God, bestow Thy compassions upon Thy new commonwealth called by Thy name; gladden our faithful King by Thy power, granting him victories over adversaries may he have as help Thine alliance, a weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy![^1482]

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into paradise [2 Cor. 12:2–4], and heard unutterable and divine words which it is not lawful for human tongues to utter: what writes he unto the Galatians, which ye, lovers of the Scriptures, have read and known? God forbid, he says, that I should glory, save only in the one Cross of the Lord [Gal. 6:14], whereon suffering He slew the passions. That Cross of the Lord, then, we also firmly hold as all our boast: for this saving Wood is unto us a weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy.[^1483]

*Sessional Hymn of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Thou didst burn up the deception of the schismatics, O hieromartyr Josaphat; thou didst rightly clarify the faith by the Union, and didst enlighten the world; therefore thou didst appear as a sign-bearing sufferer, a pillar of the Church, and a true pastor: pray unceasingly unto Christ, that we all may be saved.[^1484]

*Glory, both now, in the same tone and same podoben:*
In thee, O thrice-blessed and life-giving Cross, the peoples, feasting, celebrate together with the immaterial choirs; the hierarchal orders devoutly sing hymns, and the multitude of monastics and fasters bow down in worship; and all of us glorify Christ Who was crucified.[^1485]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard the report of Thy coming, O Christ, that without seed Thou wast conceived in the Virgin's womb, and I cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1486]

*Troparion:*
Guiding the flock of Christ unto the light of the Union, O hieromartyr, thou didst drive away the darkness of schism; and having suffered for the Union, receiving the crown of martyrdom, thou criest: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1487]

*Troparion:*
The unwaning Light of the thrice-radiant Godhead having shone within thee, O all-blessed one, made thee a pure receptacle of divine gifts, O hieromartyr Josaphat; therefore thou singest: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1488]

*Troparion:*
Treading the path of virtue, O Josaphat, thou didst reach the mansions on high, O blessed one, adorned with the anointing of priesthood and with the holy blood of martyrdom.[^1489]

*Theotokion:*
Illumine my darkened soul with thy light, O most pure one, as thou didst bear the consubstantial Light.[^1490]

*Katavasia [Tone 8]: "I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation"*[^1491] I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead.[^1492]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, O Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for other than Thee we know no god.[^1493]

*Troparion:*
"God is light unto me, and the Giver of understanding," cried Josaphat before the schismatics, not fearing their threats; therefore, having been struck upon the head with an axe,[^1494] he now rejoices in the Lord in the everlasting light.

*Troparion:*
Riches and radiant glory, length of days and incorruptible life did Christ the true Wisdom grant thee, O hieromartyr Josaphat, as thou didst singularly love Him.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst escape the snares of those who hunt thee unto the heavenly nests, and thou didst unite thyself with the ranks of the martyrs; remember us who are in the Union,[^1495] who joyfully celebrate thy memory, O blessed Josaphat.

*Theotokion:*
Calm the restless storm of my passions, O Birthgiver of God, who didst bear God, our Pilot and Lord.

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ the King and Lord was stretched, by which he who deceived by the tree fell, caught by thee when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1496]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I am held fast in the depth of sins, O Savior, and tossed about in the tempest of this life; but like the prophet Jonah from the deep, lead me up from passions, and save me.[^1497]

*Troparion:*
Into the depths of the river Dvina the foolish schismatic people cast thy holy relics; but while they thought to conceal them, a pillar appeared from heaven, showing them unharmed; and the people of the Union, having found thee and taken thee up with joy, thanked God for the great signs and wonders.[^1498]

*Troparion:*
Come, all ye united ones, let us solemnly honor the divine zither of the Spirit, the trumpet plainly proclaiming the divine mysteries of the Union, the hierarch of Polotsk, the glory of the Belarusian land.[^1499]

*Troparion:*
The guide of the Union and the fountain of healings do we understand thee to be, O hieromartyr Josaphat, the church's foundation and citizen of heaven.

*Theotokion:*
A temple of God, an ark, an animate bridal chamber, and a heavenly gate do we, the faithful, proclaim thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
Stretching out his hands in the form of a cross in the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah clearly prefigured the saving Passion; and having come forth on the third day, he depicted the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God nailed in the flesh, Who enlightened the world by His three-day Resurrection.[^1500]

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 4:*
Enlightened in thy youth with a fiery ray from the crucified Christ, resembling the angels in monastic life, thou didst live piously in the hierarchal office; clearly preaching the Union, thou didst extinguish with martyr's blood the hearts of the schismatics inflamed with dissension,[^1501] and didst receive a crown from Christ. Therefore remember us who cry unto thee: Rejoice, unshakable pillar of the Union![^1502]

*Ikos:*
As an angel didst Thou appear upon earth clad in flesh, proclaiming the unutterable mysteries of God; and Thou didst persuade us, O fair-speaking one, to cry these things unto thee:
Rejoice, through whom the darkness of the schismatics was darkened!
Rejoice, through whom the light of the Union arose!
Rejoice, angel of the uncreated Godhead!
Rejoice, true reprover of created things and of divine matters!
Rejoice, for thou didst well declare the glory of God!
Rejoice, lamp that showed forth the sun!
Rejoice, chalice that dispenses divine drink!
Rejoice, for thou didst receive the martyr's crown!
Rejoice, for standing in the heavens before the Holy Trinity, thou dancest with the angels!
Rejoice, for thou makest merry with the martyrs!
Rejoice, through whom truth shines forth!
Rejoice, unshakable pillar of the Union![^1503]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
He Who of old extinguished the bubbling furnace, and cooled the children in it with spiritual dew: Blessed art Thou, O Lord![^1504]

*Troparion:*
With drops of thy blood, O all-glorious one, thou didst quench the seductive furnace of the schismatics; and thou didst dwell upon the water of life, crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The sword and arrows of the ill-renowned thou didst break, and the foolish pride of the schismatics thou didst truly scatter, as a great stone scatters the waves, O hieromartyr, crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^1505]

*Troparion:*
By thy words and doctrines the united Faith was sealed, and the fury of schism ceased, O glorious Josaphat;[^1506] and the overthrow of the Union was destroyed, as was the strength of the foolish.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst sprout a rod from the root of Jesse, O all-blessed Virgin, bearing a saving fruit of flower-bearing blossom unto those who cry with faith to thy Son: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
The foolish command of the impious tyrant shook the people, breathing threats and God-detested blasphemy; yet the bestial rage and consuming fire frightened not the three children; but when the dew-bearing wind blew against the fire, they sang in the midst thereof: O supremely praised God of our fathers, and our God, blessed art Thou![^1507]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The furnace of fire once in Babylon divided its operation by the divine command, burning the Chaldeans, but cooling the faithful who sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1508]

*Troparion:*
Thy memory is celebrated with praises, O fair-speaking one, for thou didst learn the understanding of future things by divine inspiration; and having known thy suffering and thy departure unto the Highest, the angels escorted thy soul into the heavens, joyfully singing unto the Creator: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Now thou hast stood before the theologians at the throne of the Almighty, as one like unto them and of one mind, O all-blessed Josaphat, first hierarch of Polotsk, unconquerable champion of the united Church; therefore by canonical assurance and peace thou hast sealed her unto the ages.[^1509]

*Troparion:*
Plainly defeated and in distress is the assembly of the schismatics by thy hand and by thy wise sayings, O hieromartyr Josaphat; and like smoke their corrupt folly vanished through thy loud-sounding and theological tongue.

*Theotokion:*
Preternaturally didst thou bear the Creator and Savior, God the Word, O Virgin, Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
Bless, O youths equal in number to the Trinity, the Creator, God the Father; hymn the Word Who came down and changed the fire into dew; and supremely exalt the all-holy Spirit, Who grants life unto all, unto the ages![^1510]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word from God, Who by unutterable wisdom came to renew Adam who had fallen grievously into corruption through eating, and Who was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin for our sake: Him do we, the faithful, with one mind magnify in hymns.[^1511]

*Troparion:*
Having become wholly filled with the highest wisdom, O all-glorious one, thou didst shine forth the light of the Union unto the world; thou didst conceive divine fear, and didst bring forth the words of the Spirit; whence thou wast the most radiant dwelling of the Holy Trinity: therefore we call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
Armed with love and hope, and protected by faith, thou didst dismantle the subtleties and crafts of the enemy; and having become a victor, thou now livest as a crown-bearer with the divine choirs of angels and monastics, around the throne of the King of all in heaven.

*Troparion:*
As thou hast boldness toward God, remember, O all-blessed Josaphat, those who joyfully celebrate this thy divine festival, O hieromartyr, and who praise with faith thy venerable and holy suffering; and deliver us from storm, misfortunes, and distresses.

*Theotokion:*
Crush the arms of those who oppose Thy Church, O Christ, for the sake of the Birthgiver of God, and strengthen our King, that we may unceasingly magnify Thee.[^1512]

*Katavasia [Tone 8]:*
Thou art a mystical paradise, O Birthgiver of God, who untilled didst bud forth Christ, by Whom the life-bearing tree of the Cross was planted upon earth; therefore, worshiping Him as it is now exalted, we magnify thee.[^1513]

*Exapostilarion:*
Mercilessly did the enemy cleave thy head, O blessed hierarch, which Christ God in the highest crowned with the crown of victory, O much-suffering crown-bearer, lamp of the universe, adornment of archpastors, glory of martyrs, and praise of all the venerable![^1514]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast of the Exaltation:*
The Cross is the guardian of the whole universe; the Cross is the beauty of the Church; the Cross is the might of kings; the Cross is the confirmation of the faithful; the Cross is the glory of angels and the plague of demons.[^1515]

*At the Praises, Stichera, Tone 6:*
Having dedicated thyself wholly from youth unto Christ, thou wast outside the flesh and worldly love, having become preeminent among monastics, O most sacred father Josaphat, and a receptacle of the Holy Spirit, having preserved purity of soul and body, living as an angel among monastics upon earth, in obedience and poverty, in love toward God and neighbor, in prayers and all-night vigils, thou wast an example unto all monastics, and a mirror of every virtue: thou didst wing thy mind unto the heavenly things, to behold the unutterable beauty of Christ the King and God, Whom having loved with all thy heart, and strengthened by His power, thou didst endure many afflictions and torments: unto Whom pray with boldness for our souls.

*Sticheron:*
Sitting upon the hierarchal throne, O all-blessed one, thou didst adorn thyself with every virtue, and by teaching and works didst guide unto repentance and salvation. Therefore armed with purity and diligent prayers, with fasting and all-night vigil, and as the Master Christ was approaching His Passion and death on the Cross, lying cross-wise upon the ground making prayer, thou didst prepare thyself for suffering, O hieromartyr Josaphat. Therefore the impious enemies, coming upon thee like merciless beasts, dragging thee like a guileless lamb, tore thee unrighteously, who didst suffer steadfastly and pray with boldness for our souls.

*Sticheron:*
The impious people, thine enemies, as David said psalmodically in the Psalms: "Those that hate thee made a tumult, they lifted up the head against thee,"[^1516] O blessed Josaphat; they dealt wickedly by their will, and having taken impious counsel, they said: "Come, and let us destroy him from the nations, and his name shall be remembered no more."[^1517] And as they took counsel together with one consent, the violent fell upon thee and cleaved thy venerable head, beating thee unmercifully, and dragging thee harshly, they poured out thy blood like water throughout the whole city. Having tied heavy stones to thy neck and to thy holy feet, they mockingly cast thee from the hill into the swift river.[^1518] O thy courage and long-suffering! for which thou didst receive, O much-suffering Josaphat, an unfading crown.

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Having loved Christ God from infancy, O all-blessed Josaphat, having forsaken the world for the sake of His love, and all the beautiful things that are in the world, thou didst evangelically follow Him in monastic obedience, purity, and poverty, all the days of thy life pleasing Him monastically, Christ God Who became poor for our sake. And furthermore, having manfully prepared thyself as a good shepherd for suffering, and for the Union of the Church of God, thou didst patiently endure many afflictions from impious people; beaten and slashed, and wounded with many wounds all over thy body throughout the whole day, and having thy head cleaved, thou wast accounted worthy of crowns from Christ God. Pray unto Him, O all-blessed one, for those who with love celebrate thine ever-honored memory, that we may be delivered from enemies visible and invisible, from passions and temptations of the evil one, and from the future judgment, and that our souls may be saved.

*Both now, Tone 6:*
Today the Cross of the Lord comes forth, and the faithful receive it with longing, and receive healings of soul and body and of every disease. We kiss it with joy and fear: with fear, on account of sin, as we are unworthy; but with joy, on account of the salvation which Christ God, Who was nailed upon it and possesses great mercy, grants unto the world.[^1519]

*Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His holy ones.[^1520]
*Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?[^1521]
*Epistle:* To the Hebrews, Pericope 334 [Heb. 7:26–8:2].[^1522]
*Alleluia, Tone 2:* Thy priests shall clothe themselves with righteousness, and Thy holy ones shall rejoice with joy.[^1523]
*Verse:* The righteous man shall flourish like a palm tree, and shall be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon.[^1524]
*Gospel:* From John, Pericope 36 [John 10:9–16].[^1525]
*Communion Hymn:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous man be [LXX Ps. 111:6b]. Alleluia.[^1526]

*SEPTEMBER 17:*
*Commemoration of the Holy Martyr Sophia and her three daughters: Faith, Hope, and Love.*[^1527]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, 3, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Ranks" (Нбⷭ҇ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
The Cross is exalted, and the demons are driven away; the thief opens the gates of Eden; death is slain and is now shown empty; Christ is magnified: therefore rejoice, all ye earth-born; the curse is destroyed![^1528]

Come, all ye lovers of God, beholding the precious Cross being exalted, let us magnify it together, and give glory unto the one Deliverer and God, crying: O Thou Who wast crucified upon the Tree of the Cross, despise not us who pray unto Thee!

Moses of old, sweetening the bitterness, delivered Israel, prefiguring the Cross by a type; and all of us faithful, divinely and mystically forming it always in our hearts, are saved by its power.[^1529]

*Other Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Hast Given a Sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Ye maidens, bound by the law of nature, and clearly strengthened by love of the Creator, broke the bond of error by faith; and having acted manfully, ye trampled underfoot the impotent enemy; and ye were radiantly adorned with the crown of victory, and rejoicing, took up your dwelling in the noetic bridal chamber.[^1530]

Faith all-praised, and glorious Love, and divinely wise Hope, being shown as namesakes of the most radiant virtues, by their martyrdom cast down the evil one who craftily deceived our first mother; and having become deified, they received the dwelling of paradise, praying for all.[^1531]

Caring not for the fire, and for the multifaceted torments, and for death, O all-honored ones; for seeking by faith the beauty of the most fair Bridegroom, and having been adorned with diverse wounds, the offshoots of Sophia—Faith, Hope, and Love—were betrothed unto Him: for whose sakes, O Lord, deliver us from cruel distresses.

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
The Tree of true life planted in the Place of the Skull, whereon the eternal King wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, being exalted today, sanctifies the ends of the world, and the house of the Resurrection is renewed; the angels rejoice in heaven, and men make merry upon earth, crying like David and saying: "Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy,"[^1532] Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
With deifying water and with Thy blood, O Word, the Church is radiantly adorned as a bride, singing the glory of the Cross.[^1533]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [LXX Ps. 98:5].
The lance with the Cross, the nails, and the other instruments by which the life-bearing body of Christ was pierced, let us worship as we exalt them.

*Verse:* God is our King before the ages; He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [LXX Ps. 73:12].
When Moses conquered Amalek, having his hands raised on high in the form of a cross, he prefigured the most pure Passion of Christ.[^1534]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4:*
Prefiguring Thy Cross, O Christ, the Patriarch Jacob, bestowing a blessing upon his grandsons, made his hands crossed upon their heads [Gen. 48:13–14].[^1535] Which Cross we, O Savior, exalting today, cry aloud: Grant victories unto our Christ-loving King, as Thou didst grant overcoming unto Constantine![^1536]

*Troparion of the Feast [Tone 1]:*
"Save, O Lord, Thy people..."[^1537]

*At Matins, after the 1st Poetic Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2. Podoben: "Since Thou Art Compassionate" (Бл҃гоꙋтро́бїа сꙋ́щи):*
When Thou wast crucified, O Master Christ, the dominion and strength of death were destroyed, and the tyrannical power was trampled underfoot, all that belonged to the enemy; and we, who of old were deadened through the tree of transgression, were made alive by the Tree of the Cross; therefore we hymn Thy Passion.[^1538]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Poetic Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily Anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Feasting concerning thee, O thrice-blessed and life-giving Cross, the people celebrate together with the incorporeal choirs; the ranks of hierarchs reverently sing praises; the multitude of monastics and fasters bow down; and all of us glorify Christ Who was crucified.[^1539]

...all of us glorify [Christ Who was crucified].

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*The Canon of the Feast, with its Heirmos to 8; and that of the Saints to 4.*

*The Canon of the Feast, Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Moses, having traced the Cross directly with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel walking on foot; and striking it oppositely, he united it over Pharaoh's chariots, depicting the unconquerable weapon: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1540]

*Troparion:*
Standing in the midst of the sacred priests, Moses of old prefigured in himself the image of the most pure Passion: for having formed the Cross, with outstretched hands he raised a trophy of victory, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1541]

*Troparion:*
Moses set a remedy upon a pillar, deliverance from corrupting and venomous biting; and by the figure of the Cross he bound the snake that crawls upon the ground to the wood, thereby exposing the evil harm: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1542]

*Troparion:*
Heaven showed the victory of the Cross unto the sovereign of piety and divinely wise King; wherein the fury of the malice-hearted enemies was cast down, deceit was turned back, and the divine Faith was spread unto the ends of the earth: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1543]

*Another Canon, of the Martyrs, the acrostic whereof is: "I hymn the radiant and most beloved children of Sophia." By Theophanes, Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Thy victorious right hand has in God-befitting manner been glorified in strength; for it, O immortal One, as all-powerful, shattered the adversaries, fashioning a new path through the deep for the Israelites.[^1544]

*Troparion:*
Grant unto me, O Master, the radiance of Thy transcendent and ineffable wisdom, unto Thine honorable and all-glorious martyrs, that I may hymn the offshoots of Sophia.[^1545]

*Troparion:*
Thy naming, O divinely wise one, was clearly adorned by thy manner of life; for thou didst pass all thy life in the desire of wisdom, O glorious Sophia, being illumined by the grace of wisdom.[^1546]

*Troparion:*
Thy all-blessed fruit, adorned in martyrdom by the number of the all-divine Trinity, contended for Her sake, O all-wise Sophia, namesake of the divine Wisdom.

*Troparion:*
Having purified body and soul with virtues, three virgin maidens were brought unto Thee as unto a noetic bridegroom, Christ, in martyrdom: Faith, with Hope, and glorious Love.[^1547]

*Theotokion:*
Having assumed my whole form, He Who of old was seen in the form of God, renewed the whole man in thy womb, having made His dwelling in God-befitting manner, O most pure one; therefore, we, the faithful, all glorify thee as the Birthgiver of God.[^1548]

*Ode 3 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
The rod is received as an image of the mystery, for by its budding it selects the priest; and for the Church which was previously barren, the Tree of the Cross has now blossomed, unto strength and confirmation.[^1549]

*Troparion:*
As the rock, being struck, gushed forth water for a disobedient and hard-hearted people, it manifested the mystery of the divinely called Church, whereof the Cross is the strength and confirmation.[^1550]

*Troparion:*
When Thy most pure side was pierced with a spear, water with blood flowed forth, renewing the covenant and washing away sin: for the Cross is the praise of the faithful, and the strength and confirmation of kings.[^1551]

*Another [Heirmos, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]:*
O Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and didst mercifully take form therein, gird me with power from on high, that I may cry unto Thee, O Holy One: The animate temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind![^1552]

*Troparion:*
Having listened unto the voice of Christ calling unto immortal and dispassionate life, the crown-bearing virgin martyrs followed, crying unto Thee, O Holy One: The animate temple of Thy most pure glory, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Christ granted strength unto you as ye stood in martyrdom before the judgment seat, as He promised, and filled you with divinely inspired wisdom, and showed you forth as radiant, victorious martyrs, shining with the grace of virginity.[^1553]

*Troparion:*
Ye blunted the mind of the enemy, O all-praised virgins, and cast down his pride, having contended with high resolve; and him who previously boasted to destroy the sea, ye drowned in the streams of your blood.

*Troparion:*
Having richly fed upon the highest wisdom of Christ, three chosen, wise, and prudent daughters put to shame the fierce rage and unbridled madness of the tormentors, confirming the divine doctrines.[^1554]

*Theotokion:*
Holily didst thou bear Christ, the Holy of Holies, O holy dwelling of holiness, Who rests in the saints; unto Whom we cry: Holy is the animate temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind![^1555]

...neffable glory, O Lover of mankind!

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thy Tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
Having been shown forth as the most sacred branches of honorable Sophia, Faith, Hope, and Love made foolish the Greek wisdom through grace; and having suffered, and been revealed as victory-bearers, they were crowned with an incorruptible wreath by Christ, the Master of all.[^1556]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "The Angelic Choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):*
As noetic lambs of the Lamb and Shepherd, ye were surrendered unto fire and cruel torments, and were shown forth as equal in honor unto the angels; therefore we all celebrate your sacred memory in gladness of heart, O divinely wise virgins.[^1557]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast. Podoben: The same:*
The weapon of the Cross was shown forth of old in warfare unto the pious Emperor Constantine, an invincible victory over the enemies for the sake of the faith; whereat the adverse powers tremble: this was both the salvation of the faithful and Paul's boast.[^1558]

*Ode 4 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and glorified Thy Godhead.[^1559]

*Troparion:*
Moses of old transformed the bitter-watered springs in the wilderness with the wood [Exod. 15:25], manifesting the conversion of the Gentiles unto piety through the Cross.[^1560]

*Troparion:*
Jordan yielded to the wood the iron axe-head that had sunk into the deep [2/4 Kings 6:5–7], signifying the cutting away of error by the Cross and by baptism.[^1561]

*Troparion:*
The four-part host of the people holily encamps, marching ahead after the pattern of the tabernacle of testimony [Num. 2:1–34], glorified in cross-shaped ranks.[^1562]

*Troparion:*
Marvelously stretched out, the Cross cast forth solar rays, and the heavens declared the glory of our God [LXX Ps. 18:2].[^1563]

*Another [Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]. Heirmos:*
Beholding with prophetic eyes thee as the mountain overshadowed by the grace of God, Habakkuk proclaimed that from thee should come forth the Holy One of Israel [LXX Hab. 3:3], for our salvation and renewal.[^1564]

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by divine grace, the noble-victorious Faith, Love, and Hope manfully put to shame the threats of the tormentors, being consumed with fire as whole-burnt offerings, all-wise ones, and brought unto Christ the Bridegroom.[^1565]

*Troparion:*
Having protected themselves with the full armor of the Cross, Faith, Love, and Hope, the holy ones, prevailed manfully to endure the wounds of torments, even unto blood most steadfastly resisting against sin [Heb. 12:4].

*Troparion:*
Lamps shining with threefold wisdom: Faith, Love, and Hope, clearly gleaming with the illumination of the Trinity, most radiantly enlighten the Church unto our salvation and defense.[^1566]

*Theotokion:*
Holy of holies, all-hymned Birthgiver of God, expectation of the Gentiles and salvation of the faithful: from Thee shone forth the Deliverer, the Giver of life, and the Lord, unto the salvation of us who hymn Thee.[^1567]

*Ode 5 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ the King and Lord was crucified, through which he fell who deceived through the tree, being deceived by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1568]

*Troparion:*
The revolving sword that guarded Eden reverenced thee, O ever-hymned Tree, whereon Christ was stretched out, O Cross; and the dreadful Cherubim gave place to Christ Who was nailed upon thee, Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1569]

*Troparion:*
The adverse subterranean powers dread the Cross, whose sign is traced in the air, through which the races of heavenly and earthly beings walk, bowing the knee unto Christ [Phil. 2:10], Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1570]

*Troparion:*
Having appeared with incorruptible beams, the divine Cross, shining with divine light upon the darkened Gentiles who had strayed in deception, unites them unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1571]

*Another [Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]. Heirmos:*
O Christ Who didst enlighten the ends of the world with the radiance of Thy coming, and didst illumine them by Thy Cross: enlighten with the light of Thy divine knowledge the hearts of those who hymn Thee in Orthodox faith.[^1572]

*Troparion:*
With endurance of their reasonings they took up torments, uttering the mysteries of wisdom that are in God; three God-bearing virgins, bound by faith and nature, put the ruler to shame.[^1573]

*Troparion:*
The foremother rejoices, beholding the deceiver who of old expelled her from Eden being overcome by divinely wise women, by Hope, Faith, and Love, the offspring of Sophia.[^1574]

*Troparion:*
The honorable maidens fled the venomous flattery of the tormentors, and willingly endured the wounds of torments, wounded by Thy love, O Christ, and by Thy divine desire.[^1575]

*Theotokion:*
The heavenly powers are glad beholding thee; with them the estates of men rejoice: for through thy childbearing they were united, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, Whom we worthily glorify.

*Ode 6 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
Stretching out his hands in the form of a cross in the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah clearly prefigured the saving Passion; therefore coming forth after three days, he depicted the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God Who was nailed in the flesh, and Who by His three-day Resurrection enlightened the world.[^1576]

*Troparion:*
Bowed down by old age and weighed down by sickness, Jacob straightened himself, crossing his hands, manifesting the operation of the life-bearing Cross [Gen. 48:14]; for God, Who was nailed in the flesh upon it, wrote anew the antiquity of the legal shadowy scripture, and drove away the soul-destroying sickness of deception.[^1577]

*Troparion:*
Laying his hands upon the young ones, divine Israel cross-wise revealed their heads [Gen. 48:13–19], as elder glory, the people serving the law; therefore, though thought to be mistaken, he altered not the life-bearing image: "For the newly established people of Christ God shall excel," they cried, protected by the Cross.[^1578]

*Another [Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]. Heirmos:*
The lowest abyss has compassed us about, and there is none to deliver; we were accounted as sheep for the slaughter [LXX Ps. 43:23]: save Thy people, O our God! For Thou art the strength of the weak and their restoration.[^1579]

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing, into Thy most pure hands, O Master, the three maidens placed their hopes, honored and praised by the quantity and number of the Trinity.[^1580]

*Troparion:*
Shining with the beauties of virginity, they were adorned with crowns of martyrdom, and worthily received a twofold wreath from on high, from Christ the Life-giver and all-bountiful.[^1581]

*Troparion:*
Brought into Thy temple, O Master, King of all, were the honorable virginal treasures, to partake of Thy kingdom: for Thou art their light and gladness.[^1582]

*Theotokion:*
The forefathers of our race rejoice in thee, O most pure Virgin, having through thee regained Eden, which they lost through transgression; for thou art pure both before childbearing and after childbearing.[^1583]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who Wast Lifted Up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ во́лею):*
O Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will, grant Thy compassions unto Thy new community called after Thy name, O Christ God; make glad make glad by Thy power our faithful King,[^1584] granting him victories over adversaries, as he possesses Thine alliance, the weapon of peace, an invincible victory.

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into paradise [2 Cor. 12:2–4], and heard unutterable and divine sayings which it is not lawful for human tongues to utter, what writes he unto the Galatians, which ye, as lovers of the Scriptures, have read and known: "God forbid that I should boast," he says, "save in the Cross of the Lord alone [Gal. 6:14], whereon having suffered, He slew the passions." This Cross of the Lord we also assuredly hold as our whole boast: for this saving Tree is unto us the weapon of peace, an invincible victory.[^1585]

*Ode 7 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
The senseless decree of the impious tyrant shook the people, breathing threat and God-detested blasphemy [Dan. 3]; yet the beast-like rage terrified not the three Children, nor did the consuming fire: but as the dew-bearing Spirit breathed contrary against the flame, they sang together: O most praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1586]

*Troparion:*
Having tasted of the tree, the first among men dwelt in corruption [Gen. 3:6]; for being condemned by a most dishonorable rejection of life, he passed on unto his whole race a certain bodily corruption, as the harm of a disease; but we earthborn beings, having found restoration through the Tree of the Cross, cry aloud: O most praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1587]

*Troparion:*
Disobedience destroyed the commandment of God, and the tree brought death unto men, having been unseasonably partaken of; and for the confirmation of that which was exceedingly precious, the Tree of Life was thenceforth barred [Gen. 3:24], which was opened unto the dying thief as he wisely cried: O most praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1588]

*Troparion:*
Israel embraced the top of Joseph's rod [Gen. 47:31; Heb. 11:21], beholding the future things, manifesting beforehand that the most glorious Cross should possess sovereign dominion in the kingdom; for this is the victorious boast of kings, and light unto those who cry with faith: O most praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1589]

*Another [Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]. Heirmos:*
