Thee, O Birthgiver of God, we faithful consider as a noetic furnace; for even as the Supremely Exalted One saved the three Children, He wholly renewed the world in thy womb: the praised and supremely glorified God of our fathers![^1590]

*Troparion:*
Clearly illuminated by the tri-radiant grace of the Unity, the virgins destroyed the demonic dark madness, theologizing and singing the tri-hypostatic Light: Praised and supremely glorified is the God of our fathers![^1591]

*Troparion:*
Possessing chambers in the heavens, O sacred souls, ye now gladly dance with the angels, beholding the ever-existing glory and saying: Praised and supremely glorified is the God of our fathers![^1592]

*Troparion:*
Having patiently shown resistance as the Children, they manfully trampled the fire; for, being equal in number to them, the God-bearing virgins acquired equal understanding, ever praising the God of our fathers and the Supremely Glorified One.[^1593]

*Theotokion:*
Thou, O pure one, grantest remission of transgressions unto those who faithfully hymn thee, delivering them from misfortunes and every tribulation; for thee have we now acquired as a refuge, O Bride of God, as thou didst bear in thine arms the praised God of our fathers.[^1594]

*Ode 8 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
Bless God the Father and Creator, ye Children, equal in number to the Trinity; sing praise unto the Word Who descended and transformed the fire into dew, and supremely exalt unto all ages the all-holy Spirit, Who grants life unto all![^1595]

*Troparion:*
Sing, ye heavenly powers, unto the Tree being exalted, sprinkled with the blood of the incarnate Word of God; and ye people, celebrating the restoration of the earthborn, bow down before the Cross of Christ, through which the resurrection is granted unto the world unto all ages.[^1596]

*Troparion:*
Ye earthborn stewards of grace, with your hands holily exalt the Cross whereon Christ God stood, and the spear that pierced the body of God the Word: that all the Gentiles may see the salvation of God, glorifying Him unto all ages.[^1597]

*Troparion:*
Be glad, ye faithful Christian kings, forechosen by divine judgment; boast in the victorious weapon, having received from God the precious Cross: for through this, the tribes seeking warfare's daring are scattered unto all ages.[^1598]

*Another [Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]. Heirmos:*
Out of the furnace the children of Israel, as in a crucible, shone purer than gold with the beauty of piety, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1599]

*Troparion:*
The divinely radiant virgins—Faith, Hope, and Love—shone purer than gold with the beauty of piety, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The shining virgins who were manifested through light-formed martyrdom, let us faithful hymn, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1600]

*Troparion:*
Abundantly, sufficiently, and richly, the shrines of the passion-bearers ever pour forth a stream of healings unto those who cry with faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1601]

*Theotokion:*
A holy land wast thou, O pure one, who didst bear the life-bearing ear of grain, Christ, the Mediator of ever-existing life; unto Whom we all cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1602]

*Ode 9 [of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
Thou art a mystical paradise, O Birthgiver of God, who untilled didst bud forth Christ, by Whom the life-bearing Tree of the Cross was planted upon earth; therefore at its being exalted now, worshipping Him, we magnify thee.[^1603]

*Troparion:*
Let all the trees of the forest rejoice [LXX Ps. 95:12], their nature having been sanctified by Him by Whom they were planted from the beginning, when Christ was stretched out upon the Tree; therefore at its being exalted now, worshipping Him, we magnify thee.[^1604]

*Troparion:*
A sacred horn has arisen, and the head unto all the divinely wise: the Cross, whereby all the horns of sinners are noetically shattered [LXX Ps. 74:11]; therefore at its being exalted now, worshipping Him, we magnify thee.[^1605]

*Another [Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 1]. Heirmos:*
The bush that burned with fire yet remained unconsumed showed forth the image of thy pure childbearing [Exod. 3:2]; and now we pray thee to extinguish the raging furnace of temptations that besets us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.[^1606]

*Troparion:*
Being filled with tri-hypostatic light, and now taking your fill of divine radiance, ye namesakes and companions of the virtues: Love, Hope, and Faith: strengthen us by hope, love, and faith![^1607]

*Troparion:*
Pray unceasingly with your supplications, O noble-victorious ones, that the power on high may now tame the heresy that assails the faith, O invincible passion-bearers, and grant like-mindedness unto the faithful.[^1608]

*Troparion:*
Having passed through the night of this life, O all-wise ones, ye attained unto the day that knows no evening, rejoicing in martyrdom, and virgins boasting in grace, accounted worthy of the incorruptible divine kingdom.[^1609]

*Theotokion:*
O how did the Virgin bear the ever-existing Word and hypostatic radiance of the Father's hypostasis, our Benefactor and Lord, Who took flesh from her: Whom we worthily magnify.

*Exapostilarion:*
The Cross is the guardian of the whole universe; the Cross is the beauty of the Church; the Cross is the might of kings; the Cross is the confirmation of the faithful; the Cross is the glory of angels and the plague of demons.[^1610]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6. Podoben: "Having Risen on the Third Day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Where the feet of Christ stood [LXX Ps. 131:7], we worship the place, exalting the thrice-blessed Cross, whereon the Master's blood was shed, Who poured forth resurrection unto the world.[^1611]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [LXX Ps. 98:5].
Having slain the passions of the flesh and of the spirit, O divinely wise ones, let us hasten to lift ourselves up from earthly things unto heavenly rest, through the Exaltation of the Cross, having been co-crucified with the Master Christ.[^1612]

*Verse:* God is our King before the ages; He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [LXX Ps. 73:12].
The life-flowing spring that gushed forth together from the Savior's divine ribs [John 19:34] waters the souls of those who worship with faith His divine Passions, His Cross, and His Resurrection.[^1613]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 2:*
Come, all ye Gentiles, let us bow down before the blessed Tree, through which everlasting righteousness came to be; for he who deceived the forefather Adam through the tree is deceived by the Cross, and falls cast down by a strange fall, he who held tyranny over the royal creation: by the blood of God the serpent's venom is washed away, and the curse of the righteous condemnation was destroyed, when the Righteous One was condemned by an unrighteous judgment. For by wood it was fitting to heal wood, and by the passion of the Impassible One upon the wood to loose the passions of the condemned one. But glory, O Christ King, unto Thy wise dispensation concerning us, whereby Thou hast saved all, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind.[^1614]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 4, on 6.*

*SEPTEMBER 18:*
*Commemoration of our Venerable Father Eumenius, Bishop of Gortyna, Wonderworker.*[^1615]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4. Podoben: "As One Valiant among Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
When Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, O Master, Thou didst lift up together with Thyself all fallen Adam's nature; therefore as we exalt Thy most pure Cross, O Lover of mankind, we ask from Thy strength on high, crying aloud: Save us, O Highest, as Thou art a merciful God, who honor the precious and light-bearing, divine Exaltation of Thy Cross![^1616]

*Sticheron:*
Psalmodically foreseeing now Thy footstool, O Master, where Thy most pure feet stood [LXX Ps. 98:5; 131:7], today with love we honor Thy most pure Cross; and exalting it piously, we pray unto Thee, crying aloud: O Thou Who didst exist before the ages, having sanctified all things by Thy divine Cross, show us forth as partakers of Thine ineffable tender compassion and of Thy grace![^1617]

*Sticheron:*
As an invincible weapon, an insurmountable shield, and as a divine scepter, we bow down before Thy Cross, O Christ, Thy throne: through which the world was saved and Adam dances for joy; we, the assemblies of earthborn beings, honor it with songs, praising it well, and accomplishing its divine Exaltation, we ask for purification.[^1618]

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 8. Podoben: The same:*
Having purified thy soul and body from passions, thou wast a house of the Holy Spirit, and didst adorn thyself with the anointing of sacred things; thou wast an excellent protector, O Eumenius, and a converser with the holy angels, and an heir of the glory of the Lord, and an intercessor for those who praise thee.[^1619]

*Sticheron:*
Thy most glorious life, illumined with virtues, shone with the brightness of wonders, and made thee renowned unto the ends of the earth, O all-blessed one, an unfailing luminary, a co-dweller of the saints, and a hierarch who is a citizen of the Holy City, a fellow-citizen of the angels, O wonderworker worthy of glory![^1620]

*Sticheron:*
The adornment of Crete, the prelate of Gortyna, the unshakable foundation of the Church the hierarch Eumenius, greatest in wonders, and most glorious in many mighty deeds, who enlightened the hearts of those that were in darkness, as a luminary of the faithful, coming together let us honor with loud voices.[^1621]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 2. Idiomelon:*
The divine treasure hidden in the earth, the Cross of the Life-giver, appeared in the heavens unto the pious Emperor, and clearly manifests the title of victory over the enemies; whereat rejoicing with faith and love, having divinely ascended unto the height of contemplation, by his zeal he brought it forth from the bowels of the earth, unto the deliverance of the world and the salvation of our souls.[^1622]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Today the Cross of Christ is exalted, the life-bearing Tree, whereon He was crucified in the flesh, calling all unto Himself.[^1623]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [LXX Ps. 98:5].
Rejoice, divine guardian of the faithful, insurmountable rampart, O Cross of the Lord, through which we were lifted up from the earth.[^1624]

*Verse:* God is our King before the ages; He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [LXX Ps. 73:12].
Come, let us all gladly kiss the life-bearing Tree, whereon Christ our Deliverance was stretched out.[^1625]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4:*
Prefiguring the operation of the precious Cross, O Christ, Moses conquered the adverse Amalek in the wilderness of Sinai [Exod. 17:11]; for when he stretched out his hands, making the form of the Cross, the people were strengthened; and now the fulfillment of the things has been accomplished in us: today the Cross is exalted, and the demons flee; today the whole creation is set free from corruption, for on account of the Cross all gifts have shone forth unto us; therefore rejoicing, we all fall down before Thee, saying: "How magnified are Thy works, O Lord [LXX Ps. 103:24]; glory to Thee!"[^1626]

*Troparion of the Feast [Tone 1]:*
"Save, O Lord, Thy people..."[^1627]

*At Matins: Troparion of the Feast, thrice.*

*After the 1st Poetic Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Joseph Was Amazed" (Оу҆диви́ся і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Stretching out his hands unto the height of heaven, Moses prefigured the Cross, the divine weapon of the faithful, whereon Christ nailed our sins [Col. 2:14]; therefore the enemy wept in suffering, painfully crying with his senses: "A wooden spear has pierced me in the midst of my heart; Christ has loosed all from the bonds of hades!" looses all from the bonds of hades![^1628]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Poetic Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6. Podoben: "Hope of the World" (Наде́жда мі́ра):*
Upon the wood of the Cross, O Savior, Thou wast lifted up through the tender compassions of mercy, and having had Thy side pierced with a spear [John 19:34], Thou didst tear up the harsh handwriting of our sins [Col. 2:14], as almighty God; therefore we piously hymn Thine ineffable dispensation, O Word.[^1629]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*The Canon of the Feast, with its Heirmos on 8; and that of the Saint on 4.*

*The Canon of the Feast, Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Moses, having traced the Cross directly with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel walking on foot [Exod. 14:21–22]; and striking it oppositely, he united it over Pharaoh's chariots, depicting the unconquerable weapon: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1630]

*Troparion:*
Standing in the midst of the sacred priests, Moses of old prefigured in himself the image of the most pure Passion [Exod. 17:11–12]: for having formed the Cross, with outstretched hands he raised a trophy of victory, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1631]

*Troparion:*
Moses set a remedy upon a pillar, deliverance from corrupting and venomous biting; and by the figure of the Cross he bound the snake that crawls upon the ground to the wood [Num. 21:8–9], thereby exposing the evil harm: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1632]

*Troparion:*
Heaven showed the victory of the Cross unto the sovereign of piety and divinely wise King; wherein the fury of the malice-hearted enemies was cast down, deceit was turned back, and the divine Faith was spread unto the ends of the earth: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1633]

*Another Canon, of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "By thy prayers grant me Christ to be propitious, O blessed one." By Joseph, Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt [Exod. 14], for He has been glorified![^1634]

*Troparion:*
Having Christ, O divinely wise father Eumenius, Who gives ear unto thy divine prayers, make Him propitious, O blessed one, unto those who praise thee with love.[^1635]

*Troparion:*
Having loved from youth the high-exalting humility, O venerable one thou didst humble the proud serpent, and wast manifestly enriched with the gift of healings.[^1636]

*Troparion:*
A receptive instrument of the Spirit wast thou, having through many fasts subjected the carnal mind of the soul, subjecting that which is worse unto that which is better.[^1637]

*Theotokion:*
The prophecies concerning thee have now been fulfilled, O Sovereign Lady, Birthgiver of God; for Him Whom the high-speaking prophets proclaimed, thou didst hold in thy womb, in two perfect natures.[^1638]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The rod is taken as an image of the mystery, for by its budding it designated the priest [Num. 17:8]; and for the Church that formerly was barren, the Tree of the Cross has now blossomed forth [Isa. 54:1], unto strength and confirmation.[^1639]

*Troparion:*
As the flinty rock struck with the rod poured forth water for the disobedient and hard-hearted people [Num. 20:11], it manifested the mystery of the divinely-called Church, whereof the Cross is the strength and confirmation.[^1640]

*Troparion:*
From the most pure side pierced with a spear, water with blood flowed forth [John 19:34], renewing the covenant and cleansing away sin; for the Cross is the boast of the faithful, and the strength and confirmation of kings.[^1641]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing of Thee.[^1642]

*Troparion:*
Diligent as a bee, O hierarch, thou didst traverse the spiritual meadows, gathering sweet honey and placing it into the combs of the heart.[^1643]

*Troparion:*
Having ordered a pure life and speech seasoned with divine salt [Col. 4:6], O Eumenius, thou showest forth, O glorious one, thy hidden grace and brightness.[^1644]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with virtues thou wast exalted, and didst ascend unto the highest thrones, being anointed with the chrism of the divine Spirit, and art known as the sweet fragrance of Christ [2 Cor. 2:15].[^1645]

*Theotokion:*
O Mary, golden censer, drive away the foul stench of my passions, and establish me who am shaken by the assaults of the deceitful warrior.[^1646]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Illumined with divine light, O all-blessed one, thou dost enlighten us who with love sing of thy honorable, glorious, and holy falling asleep, O father, hierarch Eumenius, praying unceasingly for us all.[^1647]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-beginningless" (Собезнача́лное):*
Shining with orthodox teachings, O father, thou didst diminish all dark heresies, and showing thyself a worker of wonders, O Eumenius, thou wast renowned in all things through divine providence; therefore with faith we honor thee as a hierarch of equal honor with the angels.[^1648]

*Glory, Both now, Podoben, the same:*
Thou Who by Thy voluntary counsel didst endure the Cross and didst deliver men from corruption, O Savior: we the faithful hymn and worship Thee, for Thou hast enlightened us by the power of the Cross; and we all bless Thee, O Lover of mankind and compassionate One, as the Giver of life and the Lord.[^1649]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I considered Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity.[^1650]

*Troparion:*
Of old, Moses changed with wood the bitter-producing springs in the wilderness [Exod. 15:23–25], prefiguring through the Cross the grafting of the Gentiles unto piety.[^1651]

*Troparion:*
The Jordan surrendered the axe to the wood which penetrated into the depth [2 Kings 6:5–7], signifying through the Cross and baptism the cutting off of deceit.[^1652]

*Troparion:*
Sacredly do the people encamp in four divisions [Num. 2], going before in the pattern of the Tabernacle of witness, glorified in cruciform ranks.[^1653]

*Troparion:*
Marvelously outstretched, the Cross cast forth rays like the sun, and the heavens declared the glory of our God [Ps. 18:2; LXX Ps. 18:1].[^1654]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, Who alone art the Lover of mankind.[^1655]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a house of the Spirit, keeping thyself at leisure in the divine temples, O hierarch, and adorned with honorable teachings.[^1656]

*Troparion:*
Having become a God-pleasing hierarch, O wise father, and the primate of Gortyna, thou didst flash forth the ray of miracles.[^1657]

*Troparion:*
With the rays of thy prayers, O most sacred one, thou didst burn up the gaping mouth of the great serpent that rushed against thee.[^1658]

*Theotokion:*
The sacred voices of old proclaimed the depth of thy childbearing, whose fulfillment we have now seen, O pure one.[^1659]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ the King and Lord was crucified, through which he who deceived by the tree fell, being deceived by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1660]

*Troparion:*
Thee, the ever-hymned Tree, whereon Christ was stretched forth, the turning sword that guarded Eden reverenced thee, O Cross [Gen. 3:24]; and the fearsome Cherub yielded unto Christ Who was nailed upon thee, Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1661]

*Troparion:*
The adverse underworld powers dread the sign of the Cross traced in the air; according to which the generations of the heavenly and earthly walk, bowing the knee unto Christ [Phil. 2:10], Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1662]

*Troparion:*
Having appeared with incorruptible beams, the divine Cross, shining divine light upon the darkened Gentiles who had strayed in deceit, unites them unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1663]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Lord, Giver of light and Creator of the ages, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for other than Thee, no other God do we know.[^1664]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst possess understanding, O venerable one, having put to death mind and soul from passions; therefore thou dost resolve the quarrels of those who reign faithfully and who rightly obey thee.[^1665]

*Troparion:*
Inclining his ears unto thee, the faithful ruler dissolved the long-standing enmity that bore destruction, and came to love brotherly concord of mind, O divinely wise Eumenius.[^1666]

*Troparion:*
Having arrived as a beacon, thou dost enlighten Rome by performing miracles, and dost manifestly call those plunging in the depth of passions unto the calm haven of healing, O blessed one.[^1667]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bear for us the pre-eternal Son as a young child, Who is twofold with two volitional operations, as both man and God together, O all-immaculate one.[^1668]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Stretching out his hands in the form of a cross in the belly of the aquatic beast [Jonah 2:1], Jonah manifestly prefigured the saving Passion; therefore coming forth after three days, he portrayed the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God Who was nailed in the flesh and by His three-day Resurrection enlightened the world.[^1669]

*Troparion:*
Bowed down by old age and weighed down by infirmity, Jacob straightened himself up when he crossed his hands [Gen. 48:14], manifesting the operation of the life-bearing Cross; for God Who was nailed in the flesh upon it rewrote the antiquity of the shadowy legal writing [Col. 2:14], and drove away the soul-destroying infirmity of deceit.[^1670]

*Troparion:*
Laying his hands in the form of a cross upon the youths, divine Israel revealed the heads, as the elder glory was that of the law-serving people; therefore, though he seemed to be mistaken, he changed not the life-bearing figure; for he cried that the newly confirmed people of Christ God shall excel, being protected by the Cross.[^1671]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Rolling in the deep abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion: bring me up from corruption, O God![^1672]

*Troparion:*
Having Christ as an active, inviolable treasure in thy heart, O Eumenius, thou didst account gold, which the emperor gave unto thee, as clay.[^1673]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst sit upon a high throne, O father, having borne the word of peace unto the Church, which now boasts in thine invocation.[^1674]

*Troparion:*
Without being wetted by sins, thou didst sail across the grievous storm of life and didst reach the havens where the assembly of the venerable rejoices.[^1675]

*Theotokion:*
The heavenly rain descending upon thee, having watered with the waters of divine knowledge the parched earth of piety, showed it to be abundant in fruit.[^1676]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ):*
Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will, grant Thy compassions unto Thy new commonwealth named after Thee, O Christ God; gladden by Thy power our faithful King,[^1677] granting him victories over adversaries, having Thine aid, a weapon of peace, an invincible trophy.[^1678]

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into Paradise [2 Cor. 12:2–4] and heard unspeakable and divine words which human tongues are not permitted to speak, what wrote he unto the Galatians, as lovers of the Scriptures have read and known? 'Far be it from me,' he says, 'to boast, save only in the Cross of the Lord [Gal. 6:14],' whereon having suffered, He slew the passions. That same Cross of the Lord, then, let us all firmly hold as our boast; for this saving Tree is unto us a weapon of peace, an invincible trophy.[^1679]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The senseless decree of the wicked tyrant shook the people [Dan. 3], breathing forth threat and God-abhorred blasphemy; yet the three youths were not dismayed by the bestial fury nor by the consuming fire, but when the dew-bearing Spirit breathed against it, being in the midst of the fire they sang: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1680]

*Troparion:*
Having tasted of the tree, the first among men settled into corruption; for by the rejection of life, he was condemned to a most dishonorable rejection, and imparted unto all the race a bodily corruption as the harm of a disease [Gen. 3:19; Rom. 5:12]; but we the earthborn, having found recall through the Tree of the Cross, cry aloud: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1681]

*Troparion:*
Disobedience destroyed the divine command, and the tree, partaken of unseasonably, brought death unto men [Gen. 3:6]; but for the confirmation of that which is exceedingly precious, the Tree of Life was thenceforth forbidden [Gen. 3:24]; which was opened unto the malefactor who cried wisely [Luke 23:42]: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1682]

*Troparion:*
Foreseeing the future, Israel embraced the top of Joseph's staff [Gen. 47:31; Heb. 11:21], prefiguring how the most glorious Cross should possess sovereign power over the kingdom; for this is the victorious boast of kings, and light unto those who cry with faith: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou![^1683]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The three youths neglected the godless decree to worship the golden image in the plain of Dura [Dan. 3:1]; but cast into the midst of the fire, being refreshed with dew they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^1684]

*Troparion:*
Boasting in the fervor of thy soul above dead reasonings, in deepest old age, O venerable one, thou didst undertake journeys for the beneficence of those who receive thee with faith, O Eumenius, as a sower of sacred and honorable teachings.[^1685]

*Troparion:*
Rome, having enjoyed thy good deeds, sent thee, a beloved gift, against thy will unto the Thebaid, O father Eumenius; where having arrived, thou didst remedy the ruin of drought by the raining down of thine honorable prayers, O venerable one.[^1686]

*Troparion:*
Nourished at the breasts of abstinence, thou didst suck the milk of purity and didst attain unto full stature [Eph. 4:13], ascending unto the height of virtues, O father, and shining more radiantly than the sun with divine tokens unto those held by the night of passions.[^1687]

*Theotokion:*
Thy womb became the dwelling of the immaterial Light, Who by the brightness of divine knowledge diminished godlessness, O all-pure Maiden, Bride of God [Luke 1:42]; singing of Whom, we cry aloud: Blessed is the fruit of thy womb![^1688]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Ye youths equal in number to the Trinity, bless God the Father, the Creator; hymn the Word Who descended and transformed the fire into dew [Dan. 3]; and highly exalt the all-holy Spirit, Who gives life unto all, unto the ages![^1689]

*Troparion:*
Ye heavenly powers, sing of the Tree that is exalted, sprinkled with the blood of God the Word incarnate; and ye people, celebrating the recall of earthly beings, worship the Cross of Christ, whereby resurrection is given to the world unto the ages![^1690]

*Troparion:*
Ye stewards of grace, with your hands sacredly lift up the Cross whereon Christ God stood, and the spear that pierced the body of God the Word [John 19:34], that all the Gentiles may see the salvation of God, glorifying Him unto the ages![^1691]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, ye foreordained by divine judgment; ye faithful Christian kings, boast in the victorious weapon, having received from God the precious Cross; for by this the tribes of wars seeking insolence shall be scattered unto the ages![^1692]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths and changed the flame into dew [Dan. 3], praise Him as Lord, ye works, and highly exalt Him unto all ages![^1693]

*Troparion:*
Having conquered the enemy and finished the good course [2 Tim. 4:7], in deepest old age thou didst pass unto thy fathers like ripe wheat [Job 5:26], receiving the end of life in a foreign land.[^1694]

*Troparion:*
By no means remembering thy good deeds, O father, the insolent children were sent beforehand by those who fittingly held thy sacred hand for their homeland and flock; by whose return they gush forth the grace of miracles.[^1695]

*Troparion:*
The shrine that formerly contained the honorable and much-suffering body of Cyril now also hides thine, O wise one, joined in life by like-mindedness; both of whom the heavenly homeland possesses unto the ages.[^1696]

*Theotokion:*
The most sacred choir of the prophets prefigures thee as the Ark, the unhewn mountain, the rod, and the gate through which, as He knew, the Most High passed [Ezek. 44:2], leaving thee shut again, O Virgin.[^1697]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The death that came upon mankind through eating of the tree has been abolished today through the Cross [Gen. 3:6; Rom. 5:12]; for the universal ancestral curse of the foremother has been dissolved by the offspring of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly powers magnify.[^1698]

*Troparion:*
Leaving not the murderous bitterness which came from the tree, O Lord, for Thou didst utterly destroy it by the Cross; therefore by wood didst Thou of old sweeten the bitterness of the waters of Marah [Exod. 15:23–25], prefiguring the operation of the Cross, which all the heavenly powers magnify.[^1699]

*Troparion:*
Us who were unceasingly plunged in the darkness of the forefather, O Lord, Thou didst lift up today through the Cross; for as nature was formerly completely cast down without restraint through deceit, the light of Thy Cross has restored us of all generations, which we the faithful magnify.[^1700]

*Troparion:*
That Thou mightest show unto the world the adored image of the Cross, O Lord, Thou didst portray it in all things as most glorious in the heavens, illumined with boundless light, an invincible whole-armor for the king; therefore all the heavenly powers magnify Thee.[^1701]

*Another Canon [of the Saint]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam who had grievously fallen into corruption through eating [Gen. 3:6], and Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin, with one mind we the faithful magnify in hymns.[^1702]

*Troparion:*
As a hierarch of Christ, O father, thou didst pass marvelously from strength to strength [Ps. 83:8; LXX Ps. 83:7], where the most sacred choirs serve the honorable Trinity in fear with all the heavenly powers, O all-blessed Eumenius.[^1703]

*Troparion:*
Quell the present tempest of our homeland, rendering the Godhead propitious by thy prayers; cast down the barbarian onslaught that afflicts us, O blessed one, and the temptation that plunges the wicked into the depth of ruin, O ever-memorable Eumenius.[^1704]

*Troparion:*
Thy most sacred memory convenes pastors of the venerable and pious people, bearing sanctification unto all; richly enlighten us who celebrate it with the radiances of the graces that are in thee, O all-lauded Eumenius.[^1705]

*Theotokion:*
Thou bearest Him Who upholds all things by divine power [Heb. 1:3], and from thy breasts, O all-pure one, thou dost nourish Him Who nourishes all breath; thy wonder, surpassing understanding, amazes angels and men who ever hymn thee and with love call thee blessed [Luke 1:48].[^1706]

*Exapostilarion:*
With luminous radiances, the Cross of the Lord, set forth for its exaltation, convenes all with divine longing: Come, let us all kiss it faithfully with joy, love, and fear, and let us glorify the only Creator and Master.[^1707]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
With mystical hymns let us harmoniously sing of the Cross of the Lord, whereon the Savior was crucified, the Resurrection of all.[^1708]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [Ps. 98:5; LXX Ps. 98:5].*

Come, ye multitudes of monastics, having assembled together, let us divinely sing of the life-bearing Tree whereon Christ was stretched forth.[^1709]

*Verse: But God is our King of old, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [Ps. 73:12; LXX Ps. 73:12].*

Let us the faithful glorify the Cross of the Lord, whereon the good blood was poured forth [John 19:34] for the deliverance of all.[^1710]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4:*
The Cross, an image radiant with stars, prefigured the victory of triumph unto the great and pious King. Which his mother Helena, having found, made manifest unto the world; and lifting it up today, we choirs of the faithful cry aloud: Enlighten us by thy brightness, O life-bearing Cross; sanctify us by thy might, O all-honorable Cross; and strengthen us by thine exaltation, being lifted up against the host of enemies![^1711]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Odes 5 and 6, on 6.*[^1712]

*On the nineteenth day of the same month [September 19], the Holy Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Dorymedon:*[^1713]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
The all-holy Cross, an invincible victory, appearing from the earth comes forth today as a hidden treasure, enriching the universe with the rays of its worldwide goodness; therefore we glorify the most good dispensation of Christ our God Who was well-pleased to be crucified upon it.[^1714]

Of old, the Cross, prefigured by God through Moses the servant and faithful seer of God, the divine prophet, turned back the regiments of foreigners [Exod. 17:11]; and now, prefigured by God through sacred hands in its divine elevation, it drives away the hosts of demons and the gatherings of the Jews, and exposes the audacity[^1715] of the ungodly.

Thy Cross, O our Savior, is an invincible stronghold unto us Christians, whereby the multitudes of foreign nations are cut down, and peace is bountifully granted unto Thy Church, O Christ, for those who glorify Thee in orthodox manner; kissing it now, we beseech Thee, O Lover of mankind: Vouchsafe us the portion of Thy saints![^1716]

*Other Stichera, of the Saints, Tone 8, Podoben: "Thy martyrs" (Мꙋ́чєницы твоѝ):*
Desiring to inherit unfailing food, O martyr Trophimus, thou didst feed upon bodily pains, and didst pass from corruption unto incorruption rejoicing, adorned with martyrdom; therefore by thy prayers entreat for all, O blessed one, great mercy.[^1717]

Having endured many torments, glorious Sabbatius was counted worthy to feast most joyfully in the heavenly courts today; having received the prizes of his contests, he is numbered among the angelic choirs; by his prayers, O Christ, grant unto Thy people great mercy.[^1718]

Having rejected the counsel of the godless, Dorymedon strengthened his mind with divine counsels; and thou didst courageously step forward unto the trials of torments, receiving the prizes of victory, thou reignest ever with Christ, praying for us all.[^1719]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4:*
Let us clap our hands today in hymnic triumph, and with radiant countenance and clear tongue let us cry aloud: O Christ, Who for our sake didst receive judgment, spitting, and stripes, and wast clothed in purple, and didst ascend the Cross [Matt. 27:28–31], seeing which the sun and moon hid their light, and the earth shook with fear, and the veil of the temple was rent in two [Matt. 27:45, 51]! Do Thou even now grant us Thy precious Cross as a guardian and keeper, and a driver-away of demons; that kissing it, we may all cry unto it: Save us, O Cross, by thy power; sanctify us by thy brightness, O precious Cross; and strengthen us by thine exaltation, for thou hast been given unto us as light and the salvation of our souls![^1720]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинẃвъ):*
The Cross is exalted, and demons are driven away; the thief opens the gates of Eden [Luke 23:43]; death is put to death and now shown to be despoiled; Christ is magnified: therefore rejoice, all ye earthborn, for the curse is dissolved![^1721]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [Ps. 98:5; LXX Ps. 98:5].*

Come, all ye lovers of God, seeing the precious Cross being exalted, let us magnify it together, and give glory unto the only Deliverer and God, crying aloud: O Thou Who wast crucified upon the Tree of the Cross, despise not us who pray unto Thee![^1722]

*Verse: But God is our King of old, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [Ps. 73:12; LXX Ps. 73:12].*

Sweetening the bitterness of old [Exod. 15:23–25], Moses delivered Israel, portraying the Cross in figure; and we the faithful, divinely and mystically portraying it in our hearts at all times, are saved by its power.[^1723]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 5:*
The voice of Thy prophets Isaiah and David has been fulfilled, O God, saying: All nations shall come, O Lord, and shall worship before Thee [Ps. 85:9; LXX Ps. 85:9; Isa. 66:18, 23]; for behold, the people who have been filled with Thy grace, O Good One, are in Thy courts in Jerusalem [Ps. 121:2; 134:2; LXX Ps. 121:2; 134:2]. O Thou Who didst endure the Cross for our sake and dost quicken us by Thy Resurrection, preserve and save us![^1724]

*Troparion of the Martyrs, Tone 8:*
God, praised in Trinity, glorified the trinity of martyrs: Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Dorymedon; for having believed in Him, they cast down the enemy: by their prayers, O Christ our God, have mercy on us.[^1725]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast.*

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 7:*
The Church cries unto Thee, O Christ God, worshiping Thee in the pine, the cedar, and the cypress [Isa. 60:13]: Grant victories from God unto our rulers, and have mercy on us![^1726]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4:*
Thy Cross, O Lord, shining like light, drives away the dark regiments and enlightens the faithful who sing: The Cross is the boast of the world![^1727]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*The Canon of the Feast, with its Heirmos on 8; and that of the Saints on 4.*

*The Canon of the Feast, Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Moses, having traced the Cross directly with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel walking on foot [Exod. 14:21–22]; and striking it oppositely, he united it over Pharaoh's chariots, depicting the unconquerable weapon: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1728]

*Troparion:*
Standing in the midst of the sacred priests, Moses of old prefigured in himself the image of the most pure Passion [Exod. 17:11–12]: for having formed the Cross, with outstretched hands he raised a trophy of victory, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1729]

...unto the destruction of the might of the all-destroying Amalek: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Moses placed upon a pillar the remedy, deliverance from the pestilential and venomous bite [Num. 21:8–9]; and to the wood, in the figure of the Cross, he bound the serpent that creeps upon the earth, exposing the malicious harm therein: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1730]

*Troparion:*
The heaven showed forth the victory of the Cross unto the ruler of piety and God-wise emperor [Constantine], wherein the rage of malicious enemies was cast down, deceit was overturned, and the divine faith was spread unto the ends of the earth: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1731]

*Another Canon, of the Saints, whereof the Acrostic is: "I sing the thrice-radiant splendor of the martyrs. Joseph." Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The chariot-driver Pharaoh was plunged into the deep of old by the wonderworking rod of Moses, which struck in the figure of the Cross and divided the sea [Exod. 14:21–28]; but it saved fugitive Israel, fleeing on foot, who sang a song unto God.[^1732]

*Troparion:*
Illumined by the bright lightning-flashes of the Spirit, dispel the dark clouds of my soul, enlighten my mind, and open my lips to sing your praise, O renowned martyrs of Christ![^1733]

*Troparion:*
With steadfastness of mind, O martyrs, ye opposed the vain-minded tyrant who forced you to give honor unto alien gods; and through various torments ye offered yourselves as a perfect sacrifice unto the King of all.[^1734]

*Troparion:*
Strength was granted unto you from God the Almighty to cast down all the might of the serpent, O honorable great martyrs, warriors of the Trinity: marvel-worthy Sabbatius, divine Dorymedon, and Trophimus.[^1735]

*Theotokion:*
Radiantly illuminated by the pouring-forth of thy luminiferous graces, O thou who alone art rejoiced by God, door of the Light, the valiant martyrs, singing thy praises, passed through the deepest darkness of intolerable sufferings.[^1736]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The rod is accepted as a figure of the mystery, for by its budding it chooses the priest [Num. 17:1–8]; and for the Church, formerly barren, the Tree of the Cross has now blossomed forth, for her power and confirmation.[^1737]

*Troparion:*
As the struck rock poured forth water for a disobedient and hard-hearted people [Exod. 17:6; Num. 20:11], it manifested the mystery of the God-called Church, whereof the Cross is the power and confirmation.[^1738]

*Troparion:*
When His most pure side was pierced with a spear [John 19:34], water and blood flowed forth, renewing the covenant and washing away sin: for the Cross is the boast of the faithful, and the strength and confirmation of kings.[^1739]

*Canon of the Saints, Tone 8. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and founded the earth upon the waters [Ps. 135:5–6; LXX Ps. 135:5–6]: establish me upon the rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, for there is none holy besides Thee, O only Lover of mankind.[^1740]

*Troparion:*
With most noble counsel and steadfast conscience ye came unto the trial of martyrdom: severely scraped and wounded with stripes, ye remained unshaken with an unconquerable resolve.[^1741]

*Troparion:*
Having dyed a most sacred purple robe with the outpourings of your blood, O valiant warriors, ye now stand before the immortal King and Lord, making ceaseless supplication for us.[^1742]

*Troparion:*
Ye denied not Christ when subjected to torments, scraped variously in body, cruelly stretched on the rack, and given over to wild beasts, O all-glorious warriors, holy great martyrs.[^1743]

*Theotokion:*
Submitting to the ordinances of the Master Who took flesh from thee, O all-immaculate Maiden, the valiant sufferers conquered the lawless, having thee as helper who savest our souls.[^1744]

*Kontakion of the Martyrs, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*
As the foundation of sufferers and the confirmation of piety, the Church honors and glorifies thy light-bearing suffering, O ever-praised, blessed sufferer, valiant-minded, glorious Trophimus: together with those who suffered with thee, ask cleansing for those who sing of thee, as one unconquered.[^1745]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*
Having manfully endured the pains of torments, ye have now passed together unto painless life, O Dorymedon, Trophimus, and glorious Sabbatius: therefore today Christ's Church, celebrating your sacred memory, divinely rejoices.[^1746]

*Glory, Both now, of the Cross, the same Tone:*
On high, as God having heaven as Thy throne and the earth as Thy footstool [Isa. 66:1; LXX Isa. 66:1], O Christ Savior, Thou hast shown forth the Cross unto us as the footstool of Thy feet [Ps. 98:5; LXX Ps. 98:5]: we all worship this in Davidic fashion, having it as a guardian and helper, and faithfully glorify Thee.[^1747]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I considered Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity.[^1748]

*Troparion:*
Moses of old changed the bitter-springing fountains in the wilderness with wood [Exod. 15:23–25], prefiguring the conversion of the nations unto piety through the Cross.[^1749]

*Troparion:*
The Jordan surrendered to the wood the cutting axe that was buried in its depth [2 Kings 6:5–7; LXX 4 Kings 6:5–7], signifying by the Cross and Baptism the cutting down of deceit.[^1750]

*Troparion:*
The four-part host of the people sacrosanctly encamped, going before in the figure of the tabernacle of testimony [Num. 2:1–34], glorified in cross-formed ranks.[^1751]

*Troparion:*
Marvelously extended, the Cross emitted sun-like rays, and the heavens declared the glory of our God [Ps. 18:1; LXX Ps. 18:1].[^1752]

*Canon of the Saints, Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who leaving not the bosom of the Father, didst visit our poverty: therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee [Hab. 3:2]: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind![^1753]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by the endurance of torments, O martyrs, ye were hanged upon a tree, and scraped along your ribs with iron claws, O glorious ones; by the stripping off of the body ye were clothed in divine incorruption, ever standing before the throne of the Trinity.[^1754]

*Troparion:*
In wounds for Christ, O Martyr Trophimus, thou wast sweetened by surpassing pains, looking upon the divine recompenses in heaven and the inexhaustible delight, whereof thou hast now been accounted worthy, having finished the struggle and attained unto goodly pasture.[^1755]

*Troparion:*
Having endured torments with youthful vigor, O Sabbatius, rejoicing thou didst deliver thy soul into the hands of God [Luke 23:46; Wis. 3:1], and hast well rested in the heavenly mansions, having conquered the one wretchedly cast down from thence, and received the prizes of victory.[^1756]

*Theotokion:*
Calling upon thee as helper, O most pure Virgin, as upon a pure royal palace, the threefold company of the martyrs destroyed the temples of the demons, and transferred unto the temple of heavenly glory, ever honoring thee with praises.[^1757]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ the King and Lord was crucified, through which he that deceived by a tree fell, caught in the snare by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1758]

*Troparion:*
O Cross, ever-hymned Tree whereon Christ was stretched out, the revolving sword that guarded Eden stood in awe before thee [Gen. 3:24]:

...the fearsome Cherubim gave way unto Christ nailed upon thee, Who grants peace unto our souls!

*Troparion:*
The adverse powers beneath the earth are terrified at the figure of the Cross traced in the air, beneath which the races of heaven and the earthborn walk, bowing the knee unto Christ [Phil. 2:10], Who grants peace unto our souls![^1759]

*Troparion:*
Appearing with incorruptible rays, the divine Cross, having shone forth divine light upon the darkened nations that wandered in deceit, unites them unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1760]

*Canon of the Saints, Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy countenance, O unwaning Light [Ps. 42:2; LXX Ps. 42:2], and an alien darkness has covered me, a wretch? But turn me back, and direct my ways unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee.[^1761]

*Troparion:*
Having estranged yourselves from bodily love, O all-lauded ones, by many pains and wounds ye united yourselves unto the all-bountiful God, Who loved you in mercy and by His Passions slew the passions.[^1762]

*Troparion:*
Thy steps were guided, O all-wise Martyr Trophimus, unto the paths of martyrdom, wherein being beautified and nailed into iron boots, thou didst crush the head and stings of Belial.[^1763]

*Troparion:*
Officiating the divine mysteries, O much-suffering Trophimus, thou didst trample down the tormentor, and walking in thy blood thou didst sanctify the earth; and rejoicing thou dost pass into paradise, asking salvation for us.[^1764]

*Theotokion:*
Calling upon the holy, God-rejoiced, and all-immaculate Virgin for help, the mighty warriors passed through the heaviness of torments and the surge of wounds with unswerving mind.[^1765]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
In the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah, stretching forth his hands in the form of a cross, clearly prefigured the saving Passion [Jonah 2:1–10]; and coming forth on the third day, he depicted the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God nailed in the flesh, Who illumined the world by His three-day Resurrection.[^1766]

*Troparion:*
Bowed down with old age and weighed down by infirmity, Jacob straightened himself, crossing his hands, manifesting the operation of the life-bearing Cross [Gen. 48:13–14]: for the God nailed in the flesh upon it rewrote the antiquity of the shadowy legal scripture:

...and drove away the soul-destroying disease of deceit.[^1767]

*Troparion:*
Placing his hands upon the youths, divine Israel revealed their heads in the form of a cross [Gen. 48:14], that the people serving the law possessed elder glory: though supposed to have been mistaken, he altered not the life-bearing figure; for the newly established people of Christ God cried aloud that they would surpass them, being protected by the Cross.[^1768]

*Canon of the Saints, Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and bring me up from the depth of evils, I pray Thee [Ps. 129:1–2; LXX Ps. 129:1–2]; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou hear me, O God of my salvation![^1769]

*Troparion:*
Quietly traversing the gulf of torments by the pilotage of the Spirit, the glorious sufferers sacrosanctly reached the painless haven of salvation.[^1770]

*Troparion:*
Beholding thy limbs falling upon the earth, O Trophimus, and receiving vinegar into thy nostrils, thou didst all the more perceive the sweet-smelling fragrances of Christ's love [2 Cor. 2:15].[^1771]

*Troparion:*
Having become a counselor of Christ's ordinances, thou didst utterly reject the counsels of godless enemies; and thou didst surrender thyself unto torments, being beaten, O Martyr Dorymedon.[^1772]

*Theotokion:*
Quickened by the powers sent forth from thee, O Christ, Thy passion-bearers suffered lawfully, singing the praises of Thy pure Mother who ineffably gave birth unto Thee.[^1773]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ во́лею):*
Thou Who of Thine own will wast lifted up upon the Cross, bestow Thy compassions upon Thy new commonwealth named after Thee, O Christ God; gladden our orthodox king by Thy power, granting him victories over adversaries, having Thy help, the weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy.[^1774]

*Ikos:*
He that was caught up into paradise unto the third heaven, and heard ineffable and divine words which it is not lawful for human tongues to speak [2 Cor. 12:2–4], what writes he unto the Galatians, as ye lovers of the scriptures have read and known? "Far be it from me to glory," he says, "save only in the Cross of the Lord [Gal. 6:14], whereon having suffered, He slew the passions." That same Cross of the Lord we all therefore steadfastly hold as our boast; for this saving Tree is for us the weapon of peace, an unconquerable trophy.[^1775]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The senseless decree of the blasphemous tyrant shook the people, breathing forth threat and God-abhorred arrogance [Dan. 3:1–23]; yet neither the bestial rage nor the consuming fire terrified the three youths: but when the dew-bearing Spirit blew against it, being in the midst of the fire they sang: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned God of our fathers and of us![^1776]

*Troparion:*
Having tasted of the tree, the first among men dwelt in corruption [Gen. 3:6, 19]; for condemned by a most dishonorable expulsion from life, he imparted unto the whole race a bodily corruption as the harm of a disease: but we earthborn, having found recall through the Tree of the Cross, cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned God of our fathers and of us![^1777]

*Troparion:*
Disobedience annulled the divine commandment, and the tree brought death unto men, being unseasonably partaken of; but for the confirmation of that which is exceedingly honorable, the Tree of Life was withheld from thence [Gen. 3:22–24], which was opened unto the thief who cried with good understanding: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned God of our fathers and of us![^1778]

*Troparion:*
Beholding things to come, Israel grasped the top of Joseph's staff [Gen. 47:31; Heb. 11:21], revealing beforehand the royal power, and manifesting how the most glorious Cross shall prevail; for it is the victorious boast of kings, and light unto those who cry in faith: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned God of our fathers and of us![^1779]

*Canon of the Saints, Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The fire was ashamed of the condescension of God in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, dancing with rejoicing foot as in a meadow of flowers, sang [Dan. 3:24–28]: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^1780]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with most divine impulses toward God, O blessed one, though burned with glowing skewers and unrighteously scraped along thy ribs, O Dorymedon, thou didst steadfastly endure.[^1781]

*Troparion:*
Desiring to behold the ineffable glory of God, thou wast blinded in thine eyes with glowing irons, and didst thankfully cry unto the Lord, O Trophimus: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^1782]

*Troparion:*
Kindled with love for the honorable Trinity, ye three accomplished the greatest struggles, and now rejoice with the heavenly myriads [Heb. 12:22]: with them remember us, ever asking for us remission of transgressions.[^1783]

*Theotokion:*
Being the Sovereign Lady, purer than all creation, thou didst receive the Word Who was ineffably born of thee:

...whom the valiant martyrs having loved, endured multitudes of torments.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Bless God the Father and Creator, ye youths equal in number to the Trinity; hymn the Word Who came down and turned the fire into dew; and supremely exalt the all-holy Spirit Who gives life unto all, unto the ages![^1784]

*Troparion:*
When the Tree is exalted, sprinkled with the blood of God the Word incarnate, sing, ye heavenly hosts! Ye peoples, celebrating the recall of the earthborn, worship the Cross of Christ, through which resurrection is given to the world unto the ages![^1785]

*Troparion:*
Ye earthborn, stewards of grace, with your hands hieratically exalt the Cross whereon Christ God stood, and the spear that pierced the body of God the Word [John 19:34]: that all nations may see the salvation of God [Luke 3:6; Isa. 52:10], glorifying Him unto the ages![^1786]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, ye who were fore-chosen by divine decree! Ye faithful Christian rulers, boast in the victorious weapon, having received the precious Cross from God: for through it the tribes that seek boldness in warfare are scattered unto the ages [Ps. 67:31; LXX Ps. 67:31].[^1787]

*Canon of the Saints, Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Chaldean tyrant madly kindled the furnace sevenfold for the pious [Dan. 3:19]; but seeing them saved by a better power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1788]

*Troparion:*
Exposing your naked bodies unto wounds, ye received the adornment of incorruption; having clothed the enemy in shame [Ps. 108:29; LXX Ps. 108:29], O crowned ones of eternity, having passed unto the divine resting-places, ye cry: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1789]

*Troparion:*
Following after Christ's Passions, O witnesses, ye were bound to trees and endured lacerations with valiant mind; and with streams of your blood ye drowned the most malicious regiments of demons, divinely singing: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1790]

*Troparion:*
Let Trophimus be praised, let Sabbatius be glorified, and let Dorymedon be magnified today: the unshakable pillars, ramparts of the faithful, light-like lamps of the Church, who honorably illumine her with the rays of their greatest struggles unto all ages.[^1791]

*Theotokion:*
As a young child, O most pure Virgin, thou didst bring forth Christ our God, Who is understood to be consubstantial with the Father and the Spirit:

...Whom confessing, the valiant martyrs sacrosanctly suffered; with them, O all-holy one, peoples, tribes, and tongues bless thee in faith unto all ages.[^1792]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thou art a mystical paradise, O Birthgiver of God, who without tilling didst blossom forth Christ, through Whom the life-bearing Tree of the Cross was planted upon earth [Gen. 2:9]: therefore as it is now exalted, worshiping it, we magnify thee![^1793]

*Troparion:*
Let all the trees of the wood rejoice, for their nature has been sanctified by Him by Whom they were planted in the beginning [Ps. 95:12; LXX Ps. 95:12], when Christ was stretched out upon the Tree: therefore as it is now exalted, worshiping it, we magnify thee![^1794]

*Troparion:*
The sacred horn and head has arisen for all the God-wise, even the Cross, through which all the horns of sinners are spiritually broken [Ps. 74:10; LXX Ps. 74:10]: therefore as it is now exalted, worshiping it, we magnify thee![^1795]

*Canon of the Saints, Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Heaven was astonished at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men in the flesh [1 Tim. 3:16], and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens: therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.[^1796]

*Troparion:*
By the might of the Creator of all, ye bound the rushing of wild beasts; and ye remained unharmed by them, being greatly admired for your immutable resolves: therefore ye were numbered among the flocks of martyrs; pray ever for us.[^1797]

*Troparion:*
As sacrifices for the mystical table, ye were most gloriously beheaded with the sword, and now most joyfully dwell in the mansions of the firstborn [Heb. 12:23], beholding the glory of God, receiving the fruits of your pains and the prizes of suffering.[^1798]

*Troparion:*
Come, ye faithful, having gathered together in harmony, let us praise Dorymedon, Sabbatius, and glorious Trophimus: the steadfast witnesses of truth, clusters of the spiritual vine, from which the true wine of gladness trickles forth for us by divine grace.[^1799]

*Troparion:*
The all-festal memory of the wise sufferers, having dawned today, truly enlightens all more than the rays of the sun, driving away the darkness of passions and the clouds of despondency: by their prayers, O Christ, grant Thy mercies unto us all.[^1800]

*Theotokion:*
The truly unwaning Sun Who preserved thee a Virgin and shone forth from thy side, O Virgin, brightly illuminated the sufferers who struggled patiently: with them pray unto Him to have compassion upon us who piously magnify thee![^1801]

*Exapostilarion of the Feast:*
The Cross is the guardian of the whole world; the Cross is the beauty of the Church; the Cross is the might of kings; the Cross is the confirmation of the faithful; the Cross is the glory of angels and the plague of demons.[^1802]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
We worship at the place where the feet of Christ stood [Ps. 131:7; LXX Ps. 131:7], exalting the thrice-blessed Cross, whereon the Master's blood poured forth, of Him Who poured forth resurrection for the world.[^1803]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy [Ps. 98:5; LXX Ps. 98:5].*

*Troparion:*
Having put to death the passions of the flesh and of the spirit, O God-wise, let us hasten to be lifted up from earthly things unto heavenly rest by the exaltation of the Cross, being co-crucified with the Master Christ [Rom. 6:6; Gal. 2:20].[^1804]

*Verse: But God is our King of old, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [Ps. 73:12; LXX Ps. 73:12].*

*Troparion:*
The life-flowing fount from the divine side of the Savior waters the souls of those who in faith worship His divine Passions, Cross, and Resurrection.[^1805]

*Glory, Both now, Tone 5:*
The voice of Thy prophets Isaiah and David has been fulfilled, O God, saying: All nations shall come, O Lord, and shall worship before Thee [Ps. 85:9; LXX Ps. 85:9; Isa. 66:18, 23]; for behold, the people who have been filled with Thy grace, O Good One, are in Thy courts in Jerusalem [Ps. 121:2; 134:2; LXX Ps. 121:2; 134:2]. O Thou Who didst endure the Cross for our sake and dost quicken us by Thy Resurrection, preserve and save us![^1806]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast: Ode 7, on 6.*[^1807]

*The same month, on the 21st day. The Holy Great-martyr Eustathius and those with him.*[^1808]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast on 3; and of the Saints on 3.*

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Today Thy precious Cross has dawned light-like as the sun, O Christ, being established upon the most glorious Place of the Skull [Matt. 27:33; John 19:17]; and being exalted, O Savior, upon Thy most holy mountain, it manifests most brightly that thereby, O Almighty One, Thou hast lifted up our nature unto the heavens as the Lover of mankind.[^1809]

*Troparion:*
Today the heavens declared Thy glory unto men, O Incomprehensible One [Ps. 18:1; LXX Ps. 18:1]; for shining brightly with unapproachable light, the figure of the Cross exposed the mad and harsh disposition of the God-slayers: therefore we glorify Thy dispensation of love for mankind, O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls![^1810]

*Troparion:*
By stretching forth his hands, Moses conquered Amalek, prefiguring the form of the Cross of old [Exod. 17:11–12]; and we, now worshiping the Tree of the Cross, trample down the wiles and snares of the enemy, having Christ as our subjugator, Who was lifted up upon it in the flesh, and slew the serpent, and saved man.[^1811]

*Other Stichera, of the Saints, the same Tone and Podoben:*
Thy calling was from on high, not from men, O Eustathius [Gal. 1:1]; but Christ Himself, the Lover of mankind, appeared unto thee, and caught thee with the nets of faith, O blessed one; and having cleansed thy sins through thy baptism, as Master He extended patience unto thee through the trials of life, and showed thee forth as a renowned victor.[^1812]

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing in thy youth, thou didst receive the training of virtues, O Eustathius: deprived of thy children and valiantly enduring the captivity of thy spouse, thou didst suffer dishonorable servitude; but thy courage in warfare, O ever-memorable one, made thee beloved and restored thee in brightness.[^1813]

*Troparion:*
As a divine, most sweet-smelling incense in the fire, and a fair whole-burnt offering, an acceptable sacrifice, a living and most perfect oblation [Rom. 12:1; Eph. 5:2], thou didst offer thyself unto God with all thy house, bearing fruit: therefore the heavenly mansion has now received thee with thine own, O Eustathius, worthy of wonder, together with the armies of the saints.[^1814]

*Glory, of the Saints, Tone 6. By Ephrem of Caria:*
A second Job, Eustathius, by his life, sufferings, and struggles, sets himself before us as an example of virtues and a pillar of endurance, having truly surpassed Job in virtue, together with his spouse and children: faithful in life, unshakable in temptations, and victorious in suffering; whom we bring in prayer unto Christ, that He may grant unto our souls illumination and the cleansing of sins.[^1815]

*Both now, of the Feast, the same Tone:*
The crossing of the hands of the Patriarch Jacob in blessing his children [Gen. 48:13–14] foreshowed the mighty sign of Thy Cross: holding fast to it as a firm protector, we mightily drive away the demonic legions, and cast down the pride of Belial therein, defeating the all-destroying power of the most hostile Amalek [Exod. 17:11–12]. This Cross, now being exalted, do we the faithful with pious mind offer unto Thy goodness for the cleansing of sins, crying aloud with manifold voice: Lord, have mercy! O Thou Who wast incarnate of the Virgin, have compassion, O Good One, upon the wise creation of Thy hands![^1816]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
With deifying water and Thy blood, O Word [John 19:34], the Church is radiantly adorned as a bride, singing the glory of the Cross.[^1817]

*Verse: Exalt the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy [Ps. 98:5; LXX Ps. 98:5].*

*Troparion:*
Exalting the spear with the Cross, the nails, and the other instruments whereby the life-bearing body of Christ was pierced, let us worship![^1818]

*Verse: But God is our King of old, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth [Ps. 73:12; LXX Ps. 73:12].*

*Troparion:*
When Moses conquered Amalek [Exod. 17:11–12], having his hands lifted up on high in the form of a cross, he prefigured the most pure Passion of Christ.[^1819]

*Glory, of the Saints, Tone 6. By Ephrem of Caria:*
O diamond in soul, how shall we praise thee worthily? For Thou didst surpass nature, being deprived of possessions, children, and companion of life, O blessed one; and Thou didst cry aloud that ever-remembered voice of Job: The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; as it pleased the Lord, so it came to pass [Job 1:21]! But God Whom Thou didst love, and Whom Thou didst ardently desire, again granted unto thee thy dearest[^1820] ones, having provided that they should be fellow-sufferers with thee; with whom, having accomplished a blessed end through various torments, receiving them as thy fellow-intercessors, O patient-souled Eustathius, pray that we may be delivered from our iniquities.[^1821]

*Both now, of the Feast, the same Tone:*
O Cross of Christ, hope of Christians, guide of the wandering, haven of the tempest-tossed, victory in battles, foundation of the universe, physician of the ailing, resurrection of the dead: have mercy on us![^1822]

*Troparion of the Martyrs, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors and crushed the powerless boldness of the demons: by their prayers save our souls![^1823]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast.*

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Stretching forth his hands unto the heavenly height, Moses prefigured the Cross, the divine weapon of the faithful, whereon Christ nailed our sins [Col. 2:14]; therefore the enemy wept in suffering, painfully crying out in his senses: A wooden spear has pierced me through the midst of my heart; Christ releases all from the bonds of hades![^1824]

*Glory, Both now, the same Tone.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma reading, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "He is risen from the dead" (Воскре́се и҆з̾ ме́ртвыхъ):*
In the midst of Eden a tree sprouted death, but in the midst of all the earth a Tree blossomed forth life [Gen. 2:9; LXX Ps. 73:12]; for having tasted of the first, though we were incorrupt, we became corruptible; but having attained unto the second, we have enjoyed incorruption: for by the Cross Thou, as God, dost save the human race.[^1825]

*Glory, Both now, the same Tone.*

*Canon of the Feast, with the Heirmos on 6, Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Tracing a cross with his rod, Moses divided the Red Sea in a straight line for Israel walking on foot [Exod. 14:21–22]; and striking it again crosswise, he united it over Pharaoh's chariots [Exod. 14:26–28], portraying an invincible weapon: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1826]

*Troparion:*
Of old, Moses prefigured in himself the image of the most pure Passion [Exod. 17:11–12], standing in the midst of the consecrated ones: and forming a cross with his outstretched palms, he raised up victory, destroying the power of the all-destroying Amalek: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God for He has been glorified![^1827]

*Troparion:*
Moses set upon a pole a remedy, deliverance from the corrupting and venomous biting, and upon the tree in the likeness of a cross bound the serpent crawling on the earth [Num. 21:8–9], in this exposing the subtle harm: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1828]

*Troparion:*
Heaven showed the victory of the Cross unto the ruler of piety and God-wise emperor, wherein the fury of the malicious enemies was cast down, delusion was overturned, and the divine faith was spread abroad unto the ends of the earth: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He has been glorified![^1829]

*Another Canon, of the Holy Eustathius, on 6. Whose acrostic is: "Praise unto him who is named after steadfastness." By Theophanes, Tone 4:*[^1830]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the watery deep of the Red Sea with unwetted feet [Exod. 14:21–22], ancient Israel conquered the might of Amalek in the wilderness by Moses' hands stretched forth in the form of a cross [Exod. 17:11–12].[^1831]

*Troparion:*
Subduing the surging play of my passions by thy prayers, O martyr of Christ, enable me to praise well the sacred solemnity of thy struggles, O all-blessed one![^1832]

*Troparion:*
Thy calling was not from men, O most excellent one [Gal. 1:1], but Christ called thee from heaven as of old He called Paul [Acts 9:3–6], appearing as a stag, rescuing thee from the venomous serpents.[^1833]

*Troparion:*
Having been filled with highest wisdom, O martyr, instead of corruptible riches and pleasure, thou didst most piously choose heavenly delight, being crowned with all thy house.[^1834]

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee purer than all creation, O all-immaculate one, the Creator of all and God was pleased to become incarnate, having providently willed to fashion man anew in the flesh from thee.[^1835]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The rod is taken as an image of the mystery, for by its budding it designates the priest [Num. 17:1–8]; and for the Church that formerly was barren [Isa. 54:1; Gal. 4:27], the Tree of the Cross has now blossomed forth, unto dominion and foundation.[^1836]

*Troparion:*
As when struck the flinty rock poured forth water for the disobedient and hard-hearted people [Exod. 17:6; Num. 20:11], it prefigured the mystery of the God-called Church, whereof the Cross is the dominion and foundation.[^1837]

*Troparion:*
When the most pure side was pierced by the spear, water with blood flowed forth [John 19:34], renewing the covenant and cleansing sin: for the Cross is the boast of the faithful and the dominion and foundation of kings.[^1838]

*Another Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and foundation [1 Sam. 2:2; LXX 1 Kings 2:2]![^1839]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst steadfastly endure the threefold waves of misfortunes, O glorious martyr of Christ, Eustathius, being deprived of children and wife.[^1840]

*Troparion:*
Having been saved by God from the snatching of wild beasts, thy children, O martyr of Christ, Eustathius, conquered the spiritual beasts.[^1841]

*Troparion:*
Passing through this life as through a river, O glorious one, through temptations thou didst preserve the God-like character of thy soul unshakable.[^1842]

*Theotokion:*
Come, ye faithful, let us praise with joyful songs the pure tabernacle of purity and venerable dwelling of virginity![^1843]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ во́лею):*
O Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will, bestow Thy compassions upon Thy new habitation called after Thy name, O Christ God; gladden our orthodox king with Thy power, granting him victories over adversaries, having for aid Thy weapon of peace, the invincible trophy![^1844]

*Ikos:*
He who was caught up unto the third heaven into paradise and heard unutterable and divine words which it is not lawful for human tongues to utter [2 Cor. 12:2–4], what writes he unto the Galatians, as lovers of the Scriptures have read and know? God forbid that I should boast, he says, save only in the Cross of the Lord, whereon He suffered and slew the passions [Gal. 6:14]! This then do we also steadfastly hold, the Cross of the Lord, our boast, all of us; for unto us this saving Tree is the weapon of peace, the invincible victory.[^1845]

*Sessional Hymn of Eustathius, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Upon the beast thou didst behold the form of the Cross, and upon it the form of Jesus: falling prostrate, thou wast amazed at the vision; and with all thy house thou didst come unto divine baptism, and becoming poor thou didst show thyself as a second Job. Therefore, being deprived of thy spouse and sons, thou didst cry aloud: The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away [Job 1:21]! O commander Eustathius, pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who with love celebrate thy holy memory! *Twice.*[^1846]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast, the same Tone and Podoben:*
The precious Cross of the Savior, hidden in the earth, came forth, and fills the fullness of the world with joy, and in the divine temple it proclaims to be exalted in deed, and bears the sceptre into the royal palaces. Therefore Helen cried unto her son: Stretch forth, O master, and receive with thy hands thy dominion and victories, O wise one, and teach the nations in grace to worship the Cross and the Passions of Christ![^1847]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I considered Thy works, and I glorified Thy divinity [Hab. 3:2].[^1848]

*Troparion:*
Moses transformed the bitter-producing fountains in the wilderness of old with a tree [Exod. 15:23–25], prefiguring through the Cross the transformation of the Gentiles unto piety.[^1849]

*Troparion:*
Having immersed the cutting axe-head into the depths, Jordan gave it back to the wood [2 Kings 6:5–7; LXX 4 Kings 6:5–7], signifying through the Cross and baptism the cutting down of deception.[^1850]

*Troparion:*
The fourfold people sacredly encamped, advancing before the type of the tabernacle of witness [Num. 2:1–34], being glorified by cruciform ranks.[^1851]

*Troparion:*
Marvelously stretched forth, the Cross emitted sun-like rays, and the heavens declared the glory of our God [Ps. 18:1; LXX Ps. 18:1].[^1852]

*Another Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her station, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord [Hab. 3:11]![^1853]

*Troparion:*
Preserved by the divine hand from the enemy's torment, thy companion who kept chastity remained crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1854]

*Troparion:*
Having been assailed and variously tried, O martyr of Christ, Eustathius, thou didst run unto the arena of martyrdom, crying unto thy Master: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1855]

*Troparion:*
Guided by the Master's command, adorned with martyric blood, thou didst appear, O ever-memorable, glorious Eustathius, together with thy wife and children...[^1856]

*Theotokion:*
Without knowing wedlock thou didst give birth, O Virgin, and after childbirth thou didst appear still virgin again; therefore with unceasing voices we cry unto thee with unwavering faith: Rejoice, O Lady![^1857]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O thrice-blessed Tree whereon Christ was crucified, the King and Lord, through which he who deceived by a tree fell, himself deceived by Thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls![^1858]

*Troparion:*
The revolving sword that guarded Eden [Gen. 3:24] was put to shame by thee, O ever-hymned Tree whereon Christ was stretched forth, O Cross: and the fearsome cherubim yielded unto Christ Who was nailed upon thee, Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1859]

*Troparion:*
The adverse powers of the nether regions are terrified of the Cross, the sign being traced in the air; therefore the races of the heavenly and of the earthborn walk, bowing the knee unto Christ [Phil. 2:10], Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1860]

*Troparion:*
Having appeared with incorruptible rays unto the darkened nations who had wandered in deception, the divine Cross, shining forth the divine light, unites them unto Christ Who was nailed upon it, Who grants peace unto our souls.[^1861]

*Another Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning from gloomy ignorance those who praise Thee in faith [John 12:46].[^1862]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as a Job, O Eustathius: blameless and pious [Job 1:1], thou wast found sailing through this life with long-suffering.[^1863]

*Troparion:*
Who can hymn thy pains, O blessed Eustathius, which thou didst endure, being deprived of spouse and children, O martyr?[^1864]

*Theotokion:*
O Mother of God, heal the affliction of my soul, who didst give birth unto the all-good Word Who appeases all things.[^1865]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Stretching forth his palms in the form of a cross in the belly of the aquatic beast, Jonah clearly prefigured the saving Passion [Jon. 2:1–10]; therefore coming forth on the third day, he portrayed the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God Who was nailed in the flesh and illumined the world by His three-day Resurrection.[^1866]

*Troparion:*
Bent down with age and weighed down by infirmity, Jacob straightened up by crossing his hands [Gen. 48:13–14], revealing the power of the life-bearing Cross; for God, Who was nailed in the flesh upon it, wrote anew the antiquated shadowed writing of the law, and drove away the soul-destroying infirmity of deception.[^1867]

*Troparion:*
Placing his palms crosswise upon the heads of the youths, divine Israel revealed that the older glory belonged to the people serving the law; therefore, though he seemed to be mistaken, he did not change the life-bearing image; for the newly established people of Christ God shall excel, they cried, being fortified by the Cross.[^1868]

*Another Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of thanksgiving, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from the demonic blood by the blood which for mercy's sake flowed from Thy side [Jon. 2:9; John 19:34].[^1869]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst desire Christ Who appeared unto thee, O glorious one, and didst unite thyself unto Him in love; for thou didst appear, O martyr, adorned, made fair with the purple robe of thy blood.[^1870]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst hasten, following the divine footsteps of Christ, and didst show thyself a partaker of His Passions and of His Kingdom, being all-perfectly crowned with all thy house, O martyr.[^1871]

*Theotokion:*
Now having the words of Gabriel, O all-immaculate Virgin, we cry aloud: Rejoice, only blessed Mother! Rejoice, O portal having the Sun of righteousness [Luke 1:28; Mal. 4:2]![^1872]
