*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Въ вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Having manifestly imitated the Passions of Christ and zealously drunk His cup [Matt. 20:22], O Eustathius, thou becamest a partaker and fellow-heir of His glory [Rom. 8:17], receiving divine remission from on high from the very God of all.[^1873]

*Ikos:*
Grant me a song, O my God, to hymn and tell now the struggles of Thy passion-bearer, O Lord, that I may decently praise the good Eustathius in his sufferings: who was always a victor in the enemy's battles, great in piety, and shone forth in the choir of martyrs; with whom the all-wise one unceasingly sings unto Thee with the angels, receiving divine remission from on high.[^1874]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The senseless command of the impious tormentor shook the people, breathing forth threats and God-hateful blasphemy [Dan. 3:1–28]; yet the beast-like fury and the consuming fire frightened not the three children; but when the dew-bearing Spirit blew against it, being in the midst of the fire they sang: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and of us, blessed art Thou![^1875]

*Troparion:*
Tasting of the tree, the first among men dwelt in corruption [Gen. 3:6]; for being condemned by a most dishonorable rejection of life, he transmitted a bodily corruption unto all the race, as the hurt of a disease: but we earthborn, having found recall through the Tree of the Cross, cry aloud: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and of us, blessed art Thou![^1876]

*Troparion:*
Disobedience broke the divine commandment, and the tree brought death unto men, being unseasonably partaken of [Gen. 3:6, 17]; and for the preservation of what was exceedingly precious, the Tree of Life was thenceforth barred [Gen. 3:22–24]: which was opened unto the thief who died a thief, wisely crying aloud [Luke 23:42–43]: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and of us, blessed art Thou![^1877]

*Troparion:*
Seeing future things, Israel embraced the top of Joseph's staff [Gen. 47:31; Heb. 11:21] revealing that the most glorious Cross should possess the dominion of the kingdom: for this is the victorious boast of kings and the light of those who cry with faith: O exceedingly praised God of our fathers and of us, blessed art Thou![^1878]

*Another Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, the children of Abraham, inflamed by love of piety rather than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord [Dan. 3:52]![^1879]

*Troparion:*
Shut up as in a furnace within the burning brazen bull, ye martyrs of Christ cried out with thanksgiving: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1880]

*Troparion:*
United by the law of love and of nature, O glorious martyrs, suffering ye showed one endurance, singing: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^1881]

*Theotokion:*
Thou art truly higher than the heavenly divine powers, the only one from all ages: for thou didst ineffably give birth unto their Creator, O all-pure Lady Birthgiver of God.[^1882]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Bless God the Father, the Creator, ye children equal in number unto the Trinity; praise the Word Who descended and transformed the fire into dew; and exceedingly exalt the All-holy Spirit Who gives life unto all, unto the ages![^1883]

*Troparion:*
Sing, ye heavenly powers, when the Tree sprinkled with the blood of the incarnate Word of God is exalted; ye people celebrating the recall of the earthborn, worship the Cross of Christ, through which the resurrection of the world has come unto the ages![^1884]

*Troparion:*
Ye earthborn ministers of grace, with your hands sacredly exalt the Cross whereon stood Christ God, and the spear that pierced the body of God the Word [John 19:34], that all nations may see the salvation of God [Luke 3:6; Isa. 52:10], glorifying Him unto the ages![^1885]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, ye Christian faithful kings chosen by divine judgment; boast in the victorious weapon, having received the precious Cross from God: for therein the tribes that seek boldness in warfare shall be scattered unto the ages [Ps. 67:31; LXX Ps. 67:31].[^1886]

*Another Heirmos:*
Stretching forth his hands, Daniel shut the mouths of the lions in the pit [Dan. 6:16–22]; and girded with virtue, the children, lovers of piety, quenched the power of the fire [Dan. 3:19–27], crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord [Song of the Three Children 1:35]![^1887]

*Troparion:*
Let us all now piously praise the choir of true witnesses, radiantly united by the laws of nature and by the word of faith, as lovers of piety, and let us sing with faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1888]

*Troparion:*
Beautifully were ye reunited, O honorable ones, who formerly were separated by a higher providence; having dyed the purple robe of bridal adornment with your blood, ye fervently hastened unto the heavenly bridal chamber, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1889]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst piously offer unto God the fruit of thy womb, O blessed Eustathius, and thy rejoicing spouse; having partakers in suffering according to nature, who sing unto Christ: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1890]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast a rod from the root of Jesse, O Virgin [Isa. 11:1], having blossomed forth the flower, the almighty Lord, Who fills us with sweet fragrance and grants His aroma unto all who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1891]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Death, which came upon the race through eating of the tree, has been abolished today through the Cross [Gen. 3:6; Rom. 5:12]; for the ancestral curse upon the whole race has been loosed through the budding forth of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly powers magnify![^1892]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst not leave the murderous bitterness that came from the tree, O Lord, for through the Cross Thou didst utterly destroy it: therefore a tree sweetened of old the bitterness of the waters of Marah [Exod. 15:23–25], prefiguring the power of the Cross, which all the heavenly powers magnify.[^1893]

*Troparion:*
Those who were unceasingly plunged in the gloom of the forefather, O Lord, Thou hast exalted today through the Cross; for as human nature had formerly been utterly led astray through deception, the light of Thy Cross has again restored us all together, which we the faithful magnify.[^1894]

*Troparion:*
That Thou mightest show unto the world the worshipful form of the Cross, O Lord, Thou didst portray it on the heavens as most glorious among all things, illumined with boundless light, an invincible panoply for the emperor: therefore all the heavenly powers magnify Thee.[^1895]

*Another Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out of thee without hands, O virgin mountain [Dan. 2:34, 45], even Christ, Who united the separated natures: therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God![^1896]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast passed in joy into all the light of the Trinity, and now rejoicest together with the angelic hosts, O martyr Eustathius: with whom unceasingly pray that all who praise thee may be saved.[^1897]

*Troparion:*
On earth were thy struggles and various tribulations, but from on high in the heavens thou hast now received joy with the righteous: whereof grant those who praise thee to partake, O glorious one![^1898]

*Troparion:*
I fervently offer this hymn unto thee, O martyr Eustathius, that through thee I may be enriched with an intercessor before the Master, who is able to protect from every tribulation, and a mediator of divine salvation.[^1899]

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth without knowing wedlock unto the Giver of life and Savior, we all earnestly pray unto thee, confessing thee as the Birthgiver of God: deliver us from every sorrow by thy prayers, O Virgin Mother![^1900]

*Exapostilarion of the Saint, Podoben: "In spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*
Thou didst attain unto immortal glory and endless life, having forsaken worldly pleasures, O all-blessed Eustathius, with thy God-wise children and all-blessed wife: therefore with love we celebrate thy most sacred and divine memory! *Twice.*[^1901]

*Glory, Both now, of the Feast:*
Hoping in thee, O Birthgiver of God, we utterly conquer double-dealing foes, having the Cross of Thy Son as our weapon and victory, a shield, sword, and spear, and an arrow against Belial![^1902]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 4, Automela. By Andrew of Pyrgos:*
Who would not call thy most blessed disposition blessed, O Eustathius? For thou didst valiantly endure the assaults of the primordial evil enemy: for the loss of thy spouse and children thou didst endure not heavily, but didst cry out the thankful voice of Job: Naked came I forth from my mother's womb, and naked shall I depart [Job 1:21] unto the only Creator and Savior of our souls! *Twice.*[^1903]

*Tone 6:*
Being the dwelling of the incorruptible offspring of Mary, O martyr, unceasingly abiding in the immaterial light, thou dost make the uncreated Trinity propitious unto us.[^1904]

*Tone 8:*
Having entered the out-going cloud, and united unto the Sun of righteousness, spiritually appearing from on high, touching the divine form through the beast, thou becamest an odor of sweet-smelling form, O all-blessed Eustathius: therefore illumined from the Spirit and water by operation [John 3:5], and washed with martyric blood, thou wast vouchsafed to dance together in heaven with the angelic choirs: together with whom number us also unto Christ the Savior and our God![^1905]

*Glory, Tone 8. By Germanus:*
Having cast aside the military command of the earthly kingdom, and [cleaving] unto Him Who appeared unto thee upon the beast in the likeness of our Savior, thou now dancest together with the heavenly hosts with thy wife and children, O all-blessed Eustathius: therefore we pray thee, pray unto the Lord for our souls.[^1906]

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 8:*
Whom of old Moses, prefiguring in himself, cast down Amalek and conquered; and David the psalmist, crying aloud, commanded [us] to worship Thy footstool, even Thy precious Cross, O Christ God: today we sinners worship with unworthy lips, and singing praise unto Thee Who wast well pleased to be nailed upon it, we pray: O Lord, vouchsafe us Thy Kingdom together with the thief![^1907]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Today the Cross of Christ is exalted, the life-bearing Tree, whereon He was nailed in the flesh, calling all [unto Himself].[^1908]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy.[^1909]
*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, divine treasury of the faithful, irreproachable wall, O Cross of the Lord, whereby we have been exalted from the earth!

*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages, He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^1910]
*Sticheron:*
Come with gladness, let us all kiss the life-bearing Tree, whereon Christ our redemption was outstretched!

*Glory, Tone 8:*
Even as Paul, receiving thy calling not from men, O martyr Eustathius, and growing in God through the hope of the Cross, thou didst manly put to shame the wickedness of the tormentors and the cruelty of the tortures: therefore thou didst resist unto blood against sin, contending against invisible enemies; and thou unceasingly prayest unto the King and God, to grant peace unto the universe, and great mercy unto our souls.[^1911]

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 8:*
The voice of Thy prophet Moses, O God, is fulfilled, which says: Ye shall see your Life hanging before your eyes! Today the Cross is exalted, and the world is set free from deception. Today the Resurrection of Christ is renewed, and the ends of the earth rejoice, offering a song unto Thee with cymbals after the manner of David, and saying: Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O God, even the Cross and the Resurrection: for the sake whereof Thou hast saved us, O Good One and Lover of mankind[^1912] O Almighty Lord, glory be to Thee![^1913]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 5 on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6 on 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made wonderful all His desires in them. *Verse:* I beheld the Lord ever before me, for He is at my right hand, that I might not be shaken. *Epistle to the Ephesians, pericope 233 [Eph. 6:10-17]. Alleluia, Tone 4:* The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them. *Gospel according to Luke, pericope 106 [Luke 21:12-19]. Communion Verse:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.[^1914]

*The same month, on the 21st day. The holy Apostle Quadratus of Magnesia. His service is sung on the 22nd day of this month, together with the Hieromartyr Phocas.*[^1915]

*On this day the Feast of the Precious Cross is given back (the Apodosis).*[^1916]

*At Vespers: The usual kathisma. On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast on 6, sung as on the feast itself: Glory, Both now, of the Feast.*

*Note: If it be Saturday, Glory of the Feast, and Both now, the Dogmatic Theotokion of the current Tone. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Feast. Ektenia, and dismissal.*[^1917]

*At Compline, after the Trisagion, Kontakion of the Feast. The Midnight Office we sing according to custom with the daily troparia.*

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast, thrice. After the kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Feast. Canon of the Feast on 12. Heirmoi twice, the final heirmos being the same, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn, twice. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but sing the refrains of the Feast: of the first canon with the heirmos on 8; of the second canon with the heirmos on 6: the heirmoi of both canons of the ninth ode twice. Then at the Katavasia we sing with the refrain* the heirmos: "Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Birthgiver of God"; and thereafter the refrain, and the heirmos: "Through the eating of the tree"; and a prostration. Exapostilarion of the Feast, twice. At the Praises, Stichera on 4: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Feast. Then the ektenias, and dismissal. At the Hours, Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.[^1918]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the canon, Ode 9 on 8. After the Entrance, Troparion of the Feast. Glory, Both now, Kontakion of the Feast. Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Verse of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel of the day.*[^1919]

*After the dismissal of the Liturgy, the priest comes forth with the censer, and the deacon with a candle, and censes the precious Cross; and thus the priest takes the precious Cross with the tray upon his head, and carries it into the holy altar through the Royal Doors, the deacon going before him with a candle, and censes the precious Cross. Then the priest places the precious Cross upon the holy table, and censes it cruciformly. And thus the Feast of the Precious Cross is given back (the Apodosis is accomplished).*[^1920]

*It is fitting to know: If the Apodosis of the Exaltation of the Precious Cross fall on a Sunday.*[^1921]

*On Saturday at Small Vespers, the Resurrection Stichera. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron, and the Aposticha of the Feast with its own verses from Great Vespers: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. Resurrection Troparion: Glory, Both now, of the Feast.*

*At Great Vespers: After the usual kathisma, on "Lord, I have cried," 3 Resurrection Stichera, and 1 Anatolian; and of the Feast 6, sung as on the feast itself: Glory of the Feast: Both now, the first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. At the Litya, the Stichera, and Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichera: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At the Blessing of the Loaves, the Troparion: "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin," twice; and of the Feast, once. And a reading in the Epistles of the Apostles.*

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Resurrection Troparion, twice: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. After the kathismata, the Resurrection Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia. And a reading in the Commentary Gospel for the Sunday after the Exaltation, and the Blameless (Kathisma 17); and the Hypakoe of the Tone; and the appointed Sunday reading. The Graduals (Gradual); and the Prokeimenon of the Tone; and "Let every breath praise the Lord"; and the Resurrection Gospel.*

*"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50; the Resurrection Sticheron; and the rest according to custom. The Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Birthgiver of God on 2; and of the Feast on 8. Katavasia of the Feast. After Ode 3, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and the Sessional Hymn, twice; and a reading of the Feast. After Ode 6* After Ode 6, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Prologue. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable." Resurrection Exapostilarion: Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At the Praises, 4 Resurrection Stichera, and of the Feast on 4 with the Doxasticon, with the refrains of the Feast. Glory, the Gospel Sticheron: Both now, "Most blessed art thou": Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Resurrection Troparion, and the ektenias, and the Studite Catechesis. The usual procession into the narthex, and the First Hour, and the final dismissal. At the Hours, the Resurrection Troparion: Glory, of the Feast; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast and the Resurrection Kontakion we say alternately.[^1922]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and of the Feast, Ode 4 on 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Troparion and of the Feast. Glory, the Resurrection Kontakion; Both now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon of the day, and of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel for the Sunday after the Exaltation, and of the day. Alleluia, and Communion Verse of the Feast, and of the day.*[^1923]

*Note: The service of the holy Apostle is sung on the 22nd day.*[^1924]

*Be it known: That after the Apodosis of the Feast of the Precious Cross, from the 22nd day of the month of September, we begin to recite at Matins 3 kathismata. We make also 4 readings, besides the Prologue. At Vespers we recite Kathisma 18: "Unto the Lord, when I was in affliction" [Ps. 119].*[^1925]

*If there be a great saint having a polyeleos, we recite at Matins 2 kathismata, and at Vespers the third in sequence.*

*Be this known: that from Sunday the Psalter takes its beginning; and this is done from Monday, 3 kathismata each day, until the 20th day of the month of December. But on Sundays at Matins we recite 2 kathismata, and we append also the polyeleos on all Sundays until the 20th of December.*[^1926]

*And from the 20th of December the polyeleos is not sung until the 14th of January, until the Feast of the Theophany is given back, except for a great saint having a polyeleos.*

*And from the 14th of January, we sing the polyeleos on all Sundays until Cheesefare Sunday. The Katavasia from today is sung: "I shall open my mouth," until the 21st of November.*[^1927]

*The same month, on the 22nd day. The holy Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope; and the holy Prophet Jonah; and the Venerable Jonah the Presbyter, father of Theophanes the hymnographer and Theodore the Branded. On this day we sing to the holy Apostle Quadratus.*[^1928]

*At Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Apostle on 3, Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
As a hierarch, as a divine preacher, as a God-chosen witness of the passions of Christ, and a co-heir of the ineffable glory that is to be revealed, O glorious Quadratus, thou didst most wisely preach the sacred Gospel most sacredly, and didst guide into light those who were in the darkness of ignorance: therefore with joy we honor and celebrate thy most sacred and holy memory, O blessed God-bearer![^1929]

Illumined with divine rays most gloriously, thou didst pass through like the sun, enlightening the earth with the lightnings of preaching, O initiate of sacred mysteries, and didst enlighten souls that were in darkness; and thereby thou didst drive away the ruler of darkness and his gloomy demons, who could not endure the brightness dwelling within thee, even divine grace and the operation of the all-effecting Spirit, O blessed hierarch Quadratus, intercessor for those who praise thee!

Strengthened by divine confession, and adorned with the beauties of wounds, driven away from thy flock by lawless men, O all-blessed one, like a saving spring thou didst water the earth, and didst show fruitful the hearts that formerly had grown barren through the gloom of vanity: as an apostle and as a most true disciple of Christ, O hierarch Quadratus, intercessor for those who praise thee!

*Other Stichera of the Hieromartyr, Tone 1, Podoben: "Of the heavenly ranks" (Небⷭ҇ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
Having cast down the deception of idols by thy sacred word, thou didst establish by faith the unstable hearts, and didst guide them unto life, O hierarch; and having suffered lawfully, thou becamest the martyr of the Lord, O Phocas![^1930]

Having dipped thy sacred vesture in the blood of thy sacred flesh, O most sacred father, thou didst truly receive a twofold crown from Christ, O all-blessed one; and thou dancest together with the angels in heaven, praying that we may be saved.

With rays of miracles thou dost enlighten the whole earth, ever helping those who are at sea, O father; thou drivest away every disease of souls and bodily infirmities, having received grace from the Lord, O martyr Phocas, blessed of God![^1931]

*Glory, Tone 4. By Cyprian:*
From thy youth thou wast a lover of the Lord, O all-blessed and wise hieromartyr Phocas: for taking the weapon of the Cross upon thy shoulders, thou didst walk the path of salvation without turning aside; whereby thou becamest a companion of angels, an adversary of demons, and wast shown forth as a most radiant intercessor for the world.[^1932]

*Both now, Theotokion; or if it be Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding hanging upon the Tree thy Son and God, Who hung the earth unrestrained upon the waters, and created all creation: for I shall arise and be glorified, and will crush the kingdom of Hades with power, and destroy his might, and deliver the captives from his malice, for I am tenderhearted, and will bring them unto My Father, for I am the Lover of mankind.[^1933]

*At the Aposticha, from the Oktoechos.*

*Troparion of the Apostle, Tone 3:*
O holy Apostle Quadratus, entreat the merciful God, that He grant remission of transgressions unto our souls.[^1934]

*Glory, of the Hieromartyr, Tone 4:*
And having shared their character and succeeded to their thrones, as successor to the apostles, thou didst find action, O God-inspired one, as an ascent unto contemplation: therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, thou didst also suffer for the faith even unto blood, O hieromartyr Phocas: pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.[^1935]

*The service of the Prophet Jonah and of the Venerable Jonah is sung at Compline.*[^1936]

*Canon, whose acrostic is: "I sing the glory of Thy Prophet, O Christ." Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The all-conquering power of old laid low the entire host of Pharaoh in the deep; and the Word made flesh has consumed all-malicious sin, the most glorious Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified![^1937]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
Having preserved the dignity of the soul, O blessed Jonah, thou becamest a God-like image, and wast vouchsafed to prefigure the otherworldly Resurrection of Christ, which we all hymn, for gloriously has He been glorified!

With fatherly love thou didst incline unto God, O ever-memorable one, and illumined with the splendors proceeding thence, thou wast appointed by Him a loud-voiced prophet unto the nations, teaching the saving nuptials of repentance.[^1938]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Having become a servant of God, O father, as a priest thou didst preserve the commandments of the Savior: for thou didst forsake the worldly confusion, taking up thy cross, and didst follow His life-bearing footsteps, O all-blessed one![^1939]

*Troparion:*
An intercessor of salvation, knowing God-inspired understanding, thou didst piously search all the Scripture, learning the God-promised commandments, O venerable father Jonah, and thence didst receive the dignity of the priesthood.

*Theotokion:*
From thee, O Mother and Ever-Virgin, shone forth the Sun, Who before the ages was invisible from the Father, but was most gloriously circumscribed by a visible body, and enlightened mankind with the ray of piety.[^1940]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies, for my spirit rejoiced when singing: There is none holy as our God, and none righteous above Thee, O Lord![^1941]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
The Prophet, foreseeing by divine power the grace passing over unto the Gentiles, was cast down into the abyss of despondency, crying aloud unto Thee, O Master: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord![^1942]

*Troparion:*
Having proclaimed piety unto the mariners, and declared thyself the servant of the Most High, thou wast cast into the deep, crying aloud, O glorious Prophet: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord![^1943]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Receiving from us now this woven word of praise, O God-bearer, rejoice, enjoying thy labors, and crying aloud, O venerable one: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having heard the words of the Master, thou didst forsake the world and the things in the world, and didst bring thy offspring unto the Lord, crying aloud, O venerable one: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord![^1944]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone beyond all great ones from the ages wast vouchsafed supernatural things: for in thy womb thou didst bear God, Whom all creation cannot contain, and didst give Him flesh: therefore we all honor thee as the Birthgiver of God.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou camest from the Virgin, not an intercessor nor an angel, but Thyself incarnate, O Lord, and hast saved me, the whole man: therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1945]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
Unable to bear seeing the falling away of thy people, O God-proclaiming Jonah, therefore thou didst choose to flee, and wast taken by the sea monster, prefiguring the three-day burial of Christ, O blessed one![^1946]

*Troparion:*
Knowing the Master to be the Lover of mankind, he could not bear to see the prophetic gift reproached: therefore he deferred the divine command, fleeing away, O God-proclaiming one.[^1947]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Thou didst open thy doors, O God-wise Jonah, like unto Abraham, unto all who were in need, O venerable one: therefore Christ opens unto thee the heavenly gates, O all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst adorn the twofold dignity of the priesthood, O blessed Jonah; and unto the assembly of the monks thou didst hasten with joy, being brought with thine entire household, O all-blessed one.[^1948]

*Theotokion:*
Healing the ancient transgression of Eve, the most divine One took up His abode within thee, the all-immaculate and all-holy, remaking me, the whole fallen man.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Enlightenment of those lying in darkness, salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior, unto Thee I rise early, O King of peace: enlighten me with Thy radiance, for other than Thee I know no God.[^1949]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
The great Prophet Jonah became a prefiguration of Thy three-day burial in the rock, O Christ, whereby Thou hast saved, O Word, those who cry unto Thee with faith and love: Other than Thee we know no God![^1950]

*Troparion:*
Unable to bear overlooking the Ninevites lying in the pit of sin, O my Christ, but having compassion, Thou didst send unto them the Prophet Jonah as preacher, O Master, plainly proclaiming repentance.[^1951]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Illumined with a Christ-like life, O blessed Jonah, thou wast shown honored unto all: for virtue truly knows how to make glorious those who possess it; for thou wast shown a well-pleasing priest of Christ.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by divine power, O blessed one, thou didst firmly reject worldly love; and with thy voluntary disposition thou camest rejoicing unto the Master, and having kept the faith uninjured, thou didst receive the crown of glory, O God-wise one.[^1952]

*Theotokion:*
 Thou alone, O blessed one, ineffably givest birth unto the hypostasis visible unto us in two essences, the Word of God, Who took flesh for the sake of ineffable mercy: pray unto Him to preserve those who praise thee.[^1953]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion: Lead me up from corruption, O God![^1954]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
As Thou didst save Jonah from the whale, O Savior, unharmed beyond all understanding: so now also save my soul from the snares of the serpent![^1955]

*Troparion:*
Thou becamest an intercessor of salvation, O glorious prophet, unto the Ninevites who believed thy preaching, having proclaimed aloud the preaching of repentance.[^1956]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Knowing the fleeting nature of worldly things, O father, thou didst forsake these, and didst hasten unto the reward of the heavenly portion, O most wealthy one!

*Troparion:*
Piously nourishing the multitudes of monks, thou didst not forsake them, O blessed father: therefore thou wast vouchsafed the better sweetness in the heavenly mansions.[^1957]

*Theotokion:*
Without knowing wedlock, O all-pure Virgin, thou didst give birth, and remainest a Virgin forever, showing forth the images of the true Divinity of thy Son and God.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Having become a prophet of the coming of Christ, thou didst plainly foretell His three-day rising, O blessed one, spending three days unharmed in the belly of the whale, crying aloud: Now let my life ascend from corruption unto Thee, Who art well pleased to deliver the earthly from corruption![^1958]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The God-opposing decree of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame; but Christ spread spiritual dew upon the pious children, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified![^1959]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
Unable to bear seeing thee tormented with grief and sorrow, O all-honored prophet, He forthwith most gloriously spread over thee a shade that brought relief, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified![^1960]

*Troparion:*
From thy youth thou wast dedicated unto thy Creator, O all-praised, God-wise, and all-blessed Jonah: for having become an offshoot of prayer, thou wast vouchsafed to receive the grace of the prophetic Spirit, O most wealthy one![^1961]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Adorned by the choice of judgment, having become a priest, O venerable father Jonah: therefore having become thou art within the highest temple, beholding unapproachable things, having reaped the fruit of thy sacred ministry.[^1962]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst love the choral standings of the sanctuary, and in the choirs of the fathers thou wast joyfully glorified: standing early before Him, O all-blessed venerable one, thou receivest the recompense of all thy ministry.

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin cloud, O Christ, gave birth unto Thee, the Sun of righteousness, while remaining a Virgin, Who didst partake of the thickness of the flesh and becamest man: whom we hymn as most glorious![^1963]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God, Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and turned the flame into dew: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1964]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
As in a bridal chamber within the beast, O God-proclaiming Jonah, stretching forth thy hands, thou didst cry aloud, saying unto the all-seeing God: My Savior, lead me up from corruption, that my life may now ascend again unto Thee![^1965]

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed the noetic part of thy soul from defilement, thou wast mingled with the Desired One, O blessed one; and thou becamest God-like, being deified by divine understanding, singing: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
With perfect, pure love thou didst desire Christ, O father, initiate of sacred mysteries, and with unceasing voices didst cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Forsaking worldly beauty, thou camest willingly unto Christ, O blessed one: desiring to behold His splendor, taking up thy dwelling in the holy mansions, supremely exalting Christ unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*
With most sacred voices the most sacred prophets of God clearly proclaimed thee, O pure one, as the future Mother of Him Who rules over all, O all-immaculate one: Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin has appeared unto us, to enlighten those in darkness, and to gather the dispersed: therefore we magnify the all-hymned Birthgiver of God![^1966]

*Troparion of the Prophet:*
Illumined with rays of grace, thou becamest, O Jonah, a prefiguration of the manifestation of Christ: therefore as a prophet we all, who piously enjoy thy all-wise teachings, praise thee with blessings, O wonder-worthy one!

*Troparion:*
With divine hymns in all piety we sing unto thee, as having manifested the prefiguration of the burial of Christ, and having become the sign beyond understanding of His Resurrection, O blessed one[^1967] which may we enjoy through thine intercessions, O accepted of God.[^1968]

*Of the Venerable Jonah:*
*Troparion:*
Having learned orthodox understanding fittingly from thy youth, thou didst clearly explain the Son Who shone forth from the Father before the ages, and the co-worshiped Spirit ineffably proceeding thence, having become a hierarch, O venerable one.[^1969]

*Troparion:*
The Creator has settled thee in the heavenly mansions as an honored minister of His mysteries, O father Jonah, God-bearer; and now look down upon us, thy children, O all-blessed one, who ever praise thee.[^1970]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast a bridal chamber of the incarnation of the Word beyond understanding, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, clothed and adorned with the glory of virtues: therefore we the faithful magnify thee, the all-immaculate one.

*Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Illumined with the radiance of the tri-sunned Divinity, O most wealthy Jonah, as a prophet of God with a pure heart, thou didst plainly receive the gift of prophecy, and didst foretell things to come, and didst prefigure the three-day Resurrection of the Word, being received by faith, and not receiving corruption.[^1971]

Foreseeing the illumination about to come upon the Gentiles, O blessed one, hiding thyself wisely, thou didst flee from the presence of the King of all, lest they should be saved by divine preaching; and thou wast delivered unto the whale, which harmed thee not at all, and wast cast forth upon dry land by divine beckoning.[^1972]

Prefiguring the three-day Resurrection of Christ, thou camest forth after three days from the whale, O blessed one; and crying aloud, O Jonah: "Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be given over to final destruction!" and seeing through their repentance that thy preaching would not come to pass, thou didst grieve, marveling at the love of God for mankind.[^1973]

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the most righteous Judge, O pure one, pray, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, that He condemn me not, who have lived prodigally, condemned and perplexed, at the future fearful judgment, O Virgin; but that He number me among the chosen who shall stand at His right hand, according to His mercy and abundant goodness.[^1974]

*If it be Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Christ put to death, Who puts the deceiver to death, the all-pure Sovereign Lady, weeping, sang praise unto Him as Master Who came forth from her womb, and marveling at His long-suffering, cried aloud: O most beloved Child, forget not thine handmaid; tarry not, O Lover of mankind my consolation![^1975]

*At Matins, one Canon of the Oktoechos, and two of the Saints.*

*Canon of the Apostle, the acrostic whereof is: "Unto thee, O great Quadratus, I weave a hymn of praise." Tone 2.*[^1976]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea, and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He is glorified![^1977]

*Troparion:*
Standing crown-bearing before the King of hosts, pray that He illumine those who brightly celebrate this thy memory, O blessed apostle.[^1978]

*Troparion:*
Building upon the foundation of the faith the fullness of the pious by thy most mighty teachings, O God-proclaimer, Thou didst overthrow all the deceit of idols.[^1979]

*Troparion:*
Ministering the sacred Gospel with thy most sacred words, thou didst sanctify souls unto thy Creator through faith, O ever-memorable Quadratus, by the strength of the Spirit.[^1980]

*Theotokion:*
The Creator of creation is born in the flesh from a Maiden that knew not wedlock; after birthgiving He preserves her a Virgin, even as before birthgiving, as He was well pleased.[^1981]

*Another Canon of the Hieromartyr,*
*The acrostic whereof is: "May God grant the gift to hymn thee, O Phocas." Joseph. Tone 4.*[^1982]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Traversing the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet of old, Israel conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness by the cross-shaped hands of Moses.[^1983]

*Troparion:*
Unto me who eagerly strive today to hymn thy divine memory, illumine my soul with the lamp-bearing rays of the Spirit, O glorious shepherd and martyr, manifested of the Almighty.[^1984]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst brightly enrich the divine glorious praise of the martyrs, adorning it with pastoral beauties, and having dyed the vesture of thy sacred suffering with blood, O God-blessed one.[^1985]

*Troparion:*
Having established thy mind upon better hopes, O all-wise one, thou didst utterly enfeeble him that is strong in malice, and as a most excellent victor thou didst ascend unto heavenly realms, O Phocas.[^1986]

*Theotokion:*
The condemnation of our forebears is loosed, O pure one: for thou givest birth unto the pre-eternal God, Who appears as a young Child, and truly renews the whole nature of man.[^1987]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death; and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing unto Thee.[^1988]

*Troparion:*
Performing awesome miracles, O Quadratus, thou didst bring the unbelieving unto the divine faith, as an apostle accepted of God, as an honored hierarch, O most sacred one.[^1989]

*Troparion:*
By divine teachings thou didst enlighten many, for thou wast shown forth as a minister of the Light that illumines the ends of the earth with divine rays, O hierarch Quadratus.[^1990]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast an intercessor of better goods unto thy flock, delivering it from the darkness of ignorance, and enlightening it by the display of most glorious miracles.[^1991]

*Theotokion:*
The unendurable Fire took up His abode within thee, O Birthgiver of God, without burning thy womb; and He burns up our passions, and reduces to ashes the mire of deception.[^1992]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and refuge, and foundation![^1993]

*Troparion:*
Performing healings by the invocation of Christ, O venerable one, thou didst save city and people from the enemy's deceit by the grace of God.[^1994]

*Troparion:*
Being a temple of God, O martyr, thou didst cast down the idol shrines, having the all-effective power as helper and fellow-worker.[^1995]

*Troparion:*
An angelic host was seen, O Phocas, and the unmeasured divine light, when the Lord glorified Thee before the judicial tribunals.[^1996]

*Theotokion:*
Incarnate of thee, God was united unto men in His tender mercy, and destroyed the curse, O only all-blessed Sovereign Lady.[^1997]

*Kontakion of the Hieromartyr, Tone 6, Podoben: "Fulfilling the dispensation" (Є҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ):*[^1998]
As a hierarch offering sacrifices, O father, at the end thou didst offer thyself as a living sacrifice [Rom. 12:1], testifying lawfully concerning Christ God, strengthened by angels, and choosing death, abiding with those who cry unto thee: Come, O Phocas, be with us, and none is against us![^1999]

*Ikos:*
Desiring life in heaven, trampling underfoot the sweetness upon earth, let us purify our lips and make clear our tongues for songs and thanksgiving, that we may worthily weave praise for the hierarch Phocas. For having entered unto the heavenly gates, he found unhindered entrance into the innermost sanctuary, and beholds the Desired One Who is glorified by angels: for thence he is also able to propitiate for our soul's infirmities the only Compassionate One, as having borne witness concerning Him let us sing praise unto him therefore and cry aloud: Look down upon us, come, O Phocas, be with us, and none is against us![^2000]

*Sessional Hymn of the Apostle, Tone 3, Podoben: "Awed by the beauty" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*[^2001]
Wounded by the beauty of the sacred One Who is fair beyond the sons of men [Ps. 44:3], thou didst preach the pre-unoriginate Word incarnate beyond understanding, O Quadratus. Therefore thou didst enlighten those who were in darkness, having become a light of the Gentiles as a divine hierarch. Therefore, celebrating thy light-bearing festival with faith, we hymn thee.[^2002]

*Glory, of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*[^2003]
As a martyr and shepherd thou wast sacredly glorified, having dyed the garment of priesthood with blood most radiantly, and thou standest before the Lord. Therefore today the Church of God celebrates thy most glorious memory, O all-blessed Phocas.[^2004]

*Both now, Theotokion:*
O most holy Virgin, hope of Christians, unceasingly pray together with the heavenly powers unto God Whom thou didst bear beyond understanding and word, that He grant remission of sins unto us all, and amendment of life, who ever glorify thee with faith and love.[^2005]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee dead, outstretched upon the Cross, O Christ, the all-immaculate Mother cried aloud: O My Son, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, what is this ineffable dispensation whereby Thou hast saved, O Bountiful One, the creation of Thine all-pure hands?[^2006]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard the report of Thy dispensation, O Lord, and I glorified Thee, the only Lover of mankind.[^2007]

*Troparion:*
Having tilled the field of thy heart, with the sickle of thy words thou didst uproot all the thorns of malice.[^2008]

*Troparion:*
Thy tomb pours forth gifts of healings unto all of us who praise thee, O sacred Quadratus.[^2009]

*Troparion:*
Bending down in prayer, thou deliverest from bitter and grievous afflictions those who entreat thee, O sacred Quadratus.[^2010]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast enlightened with the torches of thy words, and didst enlighten those darkened by deceit, and burned up all the brushwood deception.[^2011]

*Theotokion:*
The Creator was incarnate of thy pure blood, O Birthgiver of God, and renewed all that was corrupted.[^2012]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
Beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her place, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^2013]

...the Master placed thee as a most radiant star upon the height of the Church, O most sacred Phocas, through thy sufferings, and enlightening the hearts of all with the rays of miracles.[^2014]

*Troparion:*
Confessing the incarnation of the Master before the judgment seat of the tormentors, O passion-bearing martyr, thou didst brightly put to shame the shrines of the Hellenes and their polytheistic godlessness.[^2015]

*Troparion:*
When the sea of deceit was tossed by the tempest of polytheism, thou didst pass through it by divine pilotage, O glorious one, having become a most calm haven unto all that sail.[^2016]

*Theotokion:*
O blessed Virgin who knewest not wedlock, praise of hierarchs and crown of all passion-bearers: deliver from afflictions and sorrows those who hymn thee.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Lord, Giver of light and Maker of the ages: guide us in the light of Thy commandments, for other than Thee we know no God.[^2017]

*Troparion:*
Finding thy pure soul to be a dwelling place of His glory, the most pure God cleanses through thee the souls defiled by bitter falls into sin.[^2018]

*Troparion:*
The Hellenic sages, vanquished by thy wise dogmas, submitted to confess Christ the Creator, the Wisdom and Power of the unoriginate Father, O blessed one.[^2019]

*Troparion:*
Sacredly proclaiming unto men the radiance from the Father of lights, O Quadratus, thou didst enlighten the people to honor and glorify the undivided Trinity.[^2020]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bear for us the Son incarnate in two natures, O pure one, Who was begotten of the Father before all ages without seed and timelessly, as He alone knows.[^2021]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning back from gloomy ignorance those who sing unto Thee with faith.[^2022]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst clearly burn up the paths of the enemy, directing thy steps unto the paths of the divine will, O most sacred one.[^2023]

*Troparion:*
Torn with wounds, thy much-suffering body rent asunder the bonds of godlessness by divine power, O God-blessed Phocas.[^2024]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst offer thyself as a sacred slaughter unto God Who was sacrificed for our sake, O all-praised one, and Who destroyed the bloody sacrifices of idols.[^2025]

*Theotokion:*
The Wisdom of God built for Himself a temple from thy holy and pure blood, O Sovereign Lady, as He was well pleased.[^2026]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion: Lead me up from corruption, O God![^2027]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a high heaven declaring the saving glory of God [Ps. 18:2]: as a divine hierarch, as a glorious apostle, O Quadratus.[^2028]

*Troparion:*
Preaching the one unoriginate nature of the Godhead, the one Lordship, O all-wise one, thou didst destroy the gloomy folly of polytheism, O Quadratus.[^2029]

*Troparion:*
Though by the law of nature thy body now lies in the tomb, O blessed and most sacred one, it works most glorious miracles beyond nature, O ever-memorable Quadratus.[^2030]

*Theotokion:*
He Who stretched out the heaven by His will [Ps. 103:2] showed thee forth as another heaven upon earth, O Sovereign Lady Birthgiver of God, and through thee illumined those who were in darkness.[^2031]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed in mercy from Thy side.[^2032]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst dry up the sea of godlessness, O all-wise one, pouring forth teachings of the Spring of life unto the pious; and now with showers of miracles thou washest away every foul stench of passions.[^2033]

*Troparion:*
Bound upon the tree, grievously broken and exhausted, O blessed one: thou didst perceive a voice from on high strengthening thee, O hierarch and much-suffering martyr.[^2034]

*Troparion:*
Having dispassionately conformed thyself unto the Passion [of Christ], O Phocas, thou healest diverse passions, and deliverest from tempest and swell those who sail, by thy divine prayers unto God.[^2035]

*Theotokion:*
Like rain the saving Word of the Spring [descended] into thy incorrupt womb, O all-holy Maiden, and dried up the evil currents by divine power.[^2036]

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*[^2037]
As an honored hierarch and a most steadfast sufferer, the universe brings unto Thee, O Lord, the Apostle Quadratus, and with hymns honors his precious memory, ever asking remission of transgressions: that this may be granted unto those who sing praise unto him, O Bountiful One.[^2038]

*Ikos:*
Let us honor the wise hierarch as a faithful shepherd and teacher: for in the garden of suffering a most sacred rose blossomed forth and filled us, the faithful, with sweet fragrance; and with the rays of miracles and virtuous deeds he filled the whole earth with the illumination of the brightness of healings: for God marvelously glorified Him unto all who honor his precious memory with hymns, as He is compassionate.[^2039]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
When the golden image was worshiped in the plain of Dura [Dan. 3:1], Thy three children despised the godless decree; cast into the midst of the fire, bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2040]

*Troparion:*
Having lifted up thy mind unto the primal Good, thou becamest a most God-like temple of the Trinity; and thou didst raise up the sheep from the depth of affliction by thy most exalted teachings, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2041]

*Troparion:*
Having crushed the idol shrines by the excavations of thy prayers, thou didst build temples of God by the Divine Spirit, O most sacred father, and didst bring multitudes of the saved, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2042]

*Troparion:*
Being fire-inspired, O all-wise one, having ever in thy heart the divine spiritual fire: thou wast seen as a torch burning up all the brushwood deception, and enlightening those who cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2043]

*Theotokion:*
Delivered through thee from the ancestral curse, O thou who hast found favor with God, we know thee as the cause of good things, as having given birth unto the all-causing Word beyond understanding and wonder; and we cry unto thee, O all-pure one: Blessed art thou who didst bear God in the flesh![^2044]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
In the Persian furnace the Abrahamite children, burned rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^2045]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast not terrified by the fury of the tormentors, O glorious one, but pasturing the rational flock, thou didst offer thyself as a lamb unto the Chief Shepherd Christ, being martyrologically glorified, O Phocas.[^2046]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast tried like gold in the furnace, O martyr, cast into the midst of the flame-like bath, and was not burned at all, crying: Blessed art Thou, my God, in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^2047]

*Troparion:*
Divine love inflaming thy heart, with divine dew it preserved thee unharmed in the fire, O glorious hierarch, burning up the mire of godlessness burning up the mire of godlessness, O hierarch.[^2048]

*Theotokion:*
The house of my soul being consumed, O all-pure Maiden: as thou art good, renew it with patterns of repentance, thou who didst renew all mankind by thy childbearing.[^2049]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God, Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and turned the flame into dew: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^2050]

*Troparion:*
Having the footsteps of thy soul established upon the noetic Rock, thou didst burn up the enemies of the Lord, O blessed one; and thou didst establish all, O Quadratus, who sing and supremely exalt Christ unto all ages.[^2051]

*Troparion:*
Having thy soul and heart adorned with virtues, thou didst adorn souls with the word of teaching, delivering them from the ugliness of all idol madness, O God-proclaiming Quadratus.[^2052]

*Troparion:*
As a disciple of Jesus, as a radiant apostle, as a light-resembling lightning of the Sun of righteousness, O Quadratus: enlighten and sanctify those who celebrate thy holy memory.[^2053]

*Theotokion:*
With most sacred voices the most sacred divine prophets clearly proclaimed thee, O pure one, as the future Mother of Him Who rules over all, O all-immaculate one: Whom we bless unto all ages.[^2054]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
Stretching forth his hands, Daniel shut the lions' mouths in the den [Dan. 6:22]; and the children, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire [Dan. 3], crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2055]

*Troparion:*
Grace was poured forth into thy lips, O all-wise Phocas [Ps. 44:3]; therefore thou didst turn back the people wandering by the serpent's counsel, and as a true shepherd didst bring them unto Christ, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2056]

*Troparion:*
The assembly of the faithful possesses thee as an unstinting intercessor, O wise one, calming the fierce waves of the sea, subduing assaults, and delivering us who are in grievous perils, as we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2057]

*Troparion:*
Thy temple ever pours forth streams of healings unto those in need, being shown forth as a storm-free haven, driving away passions unto those who honor thee and cry unto Christ, O martyr: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2058]

*Troparion:*
That we may honor thy precious memory, O Phocas, celebrating festival fervently beseech the all-good Lord to grant deliverance from misfortunes unto us who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2059]

*Theotokion:*
The things of the Law prefigured thee, O all-pure one: the Ark, the urn containing the manna, the divine table, and again the golden lampstand [Heb. 9:4; Exod. 25:31], as having given birth unto the Light for the revelation of the Gentiles [Luke 2:32], Who enlightens the ends of the earth with the knowledge of God.[^2060]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who by eating had grievously fallen into corruption, Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: we the faithful with one accord magnify with hymns![^2061]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with understanding, thou ever standest most radiant before the fair Master, as a hierarch accepted of God, as a divine apostle, truly entreating peace for the world with all the apostles, O Quadratus.[^2062]

*Troparion:*
Possessing the shrine of thy relics like a divine ark, Magnesia draws every benefit thence with love, O Quadratus; and the heavenly mansions, possessing thy soul, rejoice with all the saints.[^2063]

*Troparion:*
Thy radiant day, thy light-bearing memory, thy truly glorious festival has shone forth unto all like the sun: which we celebrate with faith, O Quadratus, praying that through thy prayers we may find cleansing of sins and great mercy.[^2064]

*Theotokion:*
Spare me, O Lord, spare me when Thou shalt judge me; and condemn me not unto the fire, nor rebuke me in Thy wrath [Ps. 6:2]: for the Virgin who bore Thee entreats Thee, O Christ, together with the multitude of apostles, and the martyrs with the prophets.[^2065]

*Another Heirmos [Tone 4]:*
A cornerstone was cut out from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin, not cut by hands of man [Dan. 2:34]: even Christ, Who united the divided natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God![^2066]

*Troparion:*
With divine sacred hymns, come, all ye people, let us most sacredly celebrate the all-holy memory of the sacred shepherd, who entreats God the Benefactor for us.[^2067]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown forth inflamed with the zeal of the Master, when, O martyr, thou didst enter into the heated bath, wherein rejoicing, O martyr, thou didst commit thy spirit into the hands of God.[^2068]

*Troparion:*
The choirs of hierarchs, the assemblies of martyrs, and the company of sacred apostles, and the souls of all the righteous rejoice, having thee in their midst, O martyr Phocas.[^2069]

*Troparion:*
Thy memory has spread throughout the world, enlightening the souls of those who praise with faith thy struggles, thine endurance, and thy valiant suffering, O shepherd and wonder-worthy martyr.[^2070]

*Theotokion:*
Enlighten, O pure one, my soul that is darkened by sin; and deliver me by thine intercession from eternal fire and darkness: that rejoicing, I may praise thy greatness.[^2071]

*Exapostilarion of the Apostle, Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃и́лище):*[^2072]
Having turned the course of thy beautiful feet [Rom. 10:15; Isa. 52:7] unto the heavenly journey, thou didst ascend rejoicing, O Apostle Quadratus; and standing before the Trinity, in the Father thou beholdest the Son and the Divine Spirit: therefore with faith we celebrate thy most sacred and divine memory.[^2073]

*Glory, of the Hieromartyr, Podoben: "The sky with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^2074]
Thou wast shown forth as the glory of hierarchs, the protector of the poor, and the pillar of virtues, O God-wise father: therefore remember all who sing unto thee, O Phocas.[^2075]

*Both now, Theotokion:*
We sinners all have thee as our protectress, O all-immaculate Virgin: make thy Son well-disposed unto us through thy maternal prayers.[^2076]

*At the Liturgy:*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones [Ps. 115:6; LXX Ps. 115:6]. *Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me? [Ps. 115:3; LXX Ps. 115:3]. *Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 334 [Heb. 13:7–16]. Alleluia, Tone 2:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice [Ps. 131:9; LXX Ps. 131:9]. *Gospel according to John, pericope 36 [John 10:9–16]. Communion Verse:* The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance [Ps. 111:6; LXX Ps. 111:6].[^2077]

*(Ornamental woodcut tailpiece: IHS Christogram cartouche with Cross, Instruments of the Passion, and floral motifs)* [Fol. 145r]
*The month of the same, on the 23rd day.*
*The Conception of the Honorable, Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist of the Lord, John.*[^2078]
*At Vespers, the customary Kathisma.*[^2079] *On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

*Sticheron 1:*
Serving as a priest, the godly Zechariah, and being within the most divine temple, and offering the petitions of the people unto the Benefactor and All-Merciful One, beheld a most divine angel crying unto him: "Thy prayer and supplication have been heard; take courage, elder, and disbelieve me not, for thou shalt have as a child the divine Forerunner, who is greater than those born of women, who in the power of Elijah precedes Christ."[^2080]

*Sticheron 2:*
"Thou appearest strange unto me in vision and in word, strange both in speeches and in announcements," Zechariah replied, speaking against him; "for I have come to ask salvation for the people, and not to receive a child as thou proclaimest. I find these things contrary to my petitions, and I consider that thou speakest not the truth. For how shall that which thou sayest manifestly come to pass? For Elizabeth is barren, and I, as thou knowest, am an old man."

*Sticheron 3:*
"Why dost thou not believe my words, O Zechariah? Dost thou say that I bring false tidings unto thee? I am God's Archangel; those things which were commanded me I speak unto thee, standing with thee. Because thou hast not believed, and hast not faith, thou shalt be deaf and dumb until thou seest the divine fulfillment of my words. But when Elizabeth shall bear unto thee the voice of the Word, the great Forerunner, thy tongue being loosed, thou shalt bless the God of Israel."

*Glory..., Tone 6. By Byzantius:*
From a barren womb today, the fruit of prayer has budded forth, John the Forerunner! Rejoice, O wilderness, and dance, O mankind; for behold, the preacher of repentance comes to be fashioned in his mother's womb. Come, ye lovers of the feast, let us exult with joy at his glorious conception, crying aloud: O thou who art the greatest among those born of women, cease not to pray for those who in faith celebr- [Fol. 145v]
-ate thy divine conception, that we may find cleansing of sins and great mercy.

*Both now..., Theotokion:*
*Who will not call thee blessed...*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

*Sticheron 1:*
For He Who sits above the two [Cherubim] of the Holy of Holies,[^2081] unto the consecrated prophet, in the Holy of Holies, as it is written, an angel appeared and cried aloud, saying: "Thy prayer has been heard, and Elizabeth's barrenness is now dissolved; she shall bear unto thee, O elder, a son, John the Forerunner, a lamp of the Sun, the highest prophet, and a voice proclaiming the Word from the Virgin Maiden of God!"

*Verse: And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest [LXX Luke 1:76].*[^2082]

*Sticheron 2:*
"Speak unto me most clearly: whereby shall I know this?" again the most blessed elder said unto the angel; "for as thou seest, I am advanced in days, and Elizabeth is barren. How then dost thou speak these words unto me? I marvel beyond nature! I consider that thou speakest not the truth at all, O man, depart! For I ask deliverance for the people, and not to receive a child, a thing inconceivable!"

*Verse: To serve Him in holiness and righteousness before Him, all the days of our life [Luke 1:74–75].*[^2083]

*Sticheron 3:*
"I am the Archangel of God the Almighty, Gabriel is my name," the bodiless one said unto the elder; "and now be thou deaf, and learn silence, because thou hast not believed my words. But when thy spouse shall bear unto thee the trumpet of the Word, the Spirit taking away thy dumbness, thou shalt cry out most clearly:[^2084] 'O child, thou shalt be called the prophet of the Most High, to prepare His paths by grace, as He was well pleased!'"

*Glory..., Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
As an angel[^2085] hast thou come forth from a barren womb, O Baptist; from thy very swaddling clothes thou didst dwell in the wilderness, and thou wast shown forth as the seal of all the prophets. For Him Whom they foresaw in manifold ways and darkly proclaimed, Him wast thou counted worthy to baptize in the Jordan. And thou didst hear the Father's voice from heaven bearing witness to His Sonship, and didst behold the Spirit in the form of a dove, drawing the voice upon the One baptized. But O thou who hast been above all the prophets,[^2086] cease not to pray for us who faithfully celebrate thy memory.

*Both now..., Theotokion:*
No one who flees unto thee departs from thee put to shame, O most pure Virgin Birthgiver of God; but he asks [Fol. 146r]
for grace, and receives a gift unto the profit of his petition.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Rejoice, O barren one who formerly didst not bear, for behold, thou hast manifestly conceived the lamp of the Sun, who is to enlighten the whole inhabited earth which is ailing with blindness. Exult, O Zechariah, crying aloud with boldness: "The prophet of the Most High is he that is to be born!"

*Glory... Both now..., Theotokion:*
*The mystery hidden from all ages...*[^2087]

*At Compline, after the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Forerunner.*

*At Matins, after the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лное сло́во):*
Elizabeth was freed from barrenness, yet the Virgin remained a Virgin when at Gabriel's voice she conceived within her womb; but in the womb the Forerunner John leaps beforehand, having recognized God and Master in the virginal womb, being incarnate for our salvation.[^2088] *Twice. Glory... Both now...:*

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O holy mountain trodden by God! Rejoice, O living bush unconsumed! Rejoice, O only bridge of the world unto God, who leadest mortals across unto eternal life! Rejoice, O incorrupt Maiden, who without knowing man didst give birth unto the salvation of our souls!

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
The wilderness-loving turtledove, the sacred Baptist, who preached repentance and made manifest Christ become man, is born as an advocate for all sinners, and continually aided all that are storm-tossed. By his supplications, O Christ, save Thy world. *Twice.*

*Glory... Both now..., Theotokion:*
O thou who alone didst bear the Creator of all, who alone didst adorn mankind by thy childbearing, O most pure one: deliver me from the snares of deceitful Beliar; set me upon the rock of the desires of Christ, earnestly imploring Him Whom thou didst incarnate.

*Both Canons of the Octoechos without the hymns to the martyrs, and that of the saint on 6, the composition of John of Damascus, Tone 6.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Traversing the deep as on dry land with footsteps, and beholding Pharaoh the pursuer drowning, Israel cried aloud: "Unto God let us sing a song of victory!"*[^2089]

*Troparion:*
Pluck out the barren thoughts of my barren soul, O offshoot of a barren woman, as I begin to praise in hymns thy holy conception in thy mother's womb.

[Fol. 146v]
*Troparion:*
Having entered into the temple, the sacred Zechariah beheld the divine angel manifestly proclaiming unto him: "O priest, in thine old age thou shalt receive a son, the Forerunner!"

*Troparion:*
A radiant lamp of the Sun of glory, the great Forerunner is conceived to shine forth in his mother's womb, whereby the darkness of passions and the bonds of barrenness are loosed.

*Theotokion:*
Beholding the Master, Who was carried in thy womb, carried in His mother's womb, O most pure Birthgiver of God, John manifestly leapt, as being His Forerunner.

*Katavasia: I shall open my mouth...*[^2090]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession.*[^2091]

*Troparion:*
Today the barren woman conceives the sacred fruit, who at the last is to cut down all the barrenness of souls with the spiritual axe by grace.[^2092]

*Troparion:*
Having become deaf within the temple, O great Zechariah, he receives the voice of the Word by a terrible announcement, and brightly magnifies the compassionate Lord.

*Troparion:*
Having shown forth a firm path of repentance unto the faithful, the glorious Forerunner budded forth in his mother's womb by the command of the angel, through the divine counsel beyond hope.

*Theotokion:*
When he that was from a barren woman recognized Christ borne in the Virgin's womb, he leapt, proclaiming the joy that had come upon the earth, to deliver all from mourning.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
While the sacred Zechariah was censing in the temple, Gabriel appeared from heaven and said unto him: "In thine old age thou shalt have a blessed fruit; and the former barrenness of Elizabeth shall now immediately be loosed, as well as the childlessness of barrenness; and having conceived, she shall bear the preacher of Jesus and His Forerunner." By their supplications, O Savior of the world, save our souls. *Twice.*

*Glory... Both now..., Theotokion:*
O pure, all-immaculate, and unwedded one, who alone in time didst bear the ageless Son and Word of God: with the holy and honorable apostles, martyrs, prophets, and venerable ones, entreat Him to grant us cleansing and great mercy.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Christ is my power, God and Lord, the honorable Church divinely sings, crying aloud from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.*[^2093]

[Fol. 147r]
*Troparion:*
The voice of angels sacredly proclaimed unto the priest that thou, being an angel of Christ's coming, shouldest bud forth from a barren womb, O blessed Forerunner.

*Troparion:*
She that formerly was childless and did not bear now rejoices in her barrenness, for thou, O Elizabeth worthy of wonder, shalt all-gloriously bear fruit: Christ's Baptist and Forerunner!

*Troparion:*
With the axe of thy prayer, O Forerunner, cut down the thorns of my passions, and pull up the stumbling-blocks of my thoughts, and make my mind fruitful with virtues, O all-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
The womb of the Virgin bore Thee Who bearest all things, when the Baptist, carried in the womb, bowed down unto Thee, O Christ, and leapt with joy.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray Thee, with love the souls of those who rise early unto Thee, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who callest them from the darkness of sin.*[^2094]

*Troparion:*
As he was going into the sanctuary and offering the legal services unto the Creator, the holy angel appeared unto the prophet, announcing the divine conception of the Forerunner.

*Troparion:*
"How shall this be manifest unto me? For I am an old man, as thou seest, and I have a barren wife," Zechariah said unto the Archangel; "thou speakest words contrary to nature unto me!"

*Troparion:*
"Look unto Sarah, Abraham's wife, and see how she bore Isaac in old age, O man; and ever believe the things spoken," the great angel cried unto the elder.

*Theotokion:*
"Blessed art thou among women, O thou who hast been gladdened by God!" Elizabeth manifestly cried unto thee when she recognized thee as giving birth without a man, who alone didst remain incorrupt after childbirth.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, and fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly-Merciful One!*[^2095]

*Troparion:*
"I have a doubting thought, and I do not believe thy words," the priest said unto the Archangel; "for I ask the salvation of the people, not fruit from my loins."

*Troparion:*
"The Creator of nature, the King of angels," the minister replied, "was well pleased that an angel of His coming should be born unto thee; disbelieve not my words, O man!"

*Troparion:*
"Thy look is fiery, and thy countenance is terrible, and [Fol. 147v]
thy word is marvelous,"[^2096] Zechariah said unto the minister; "yet therefore I do not believe, since thou speakest strange words unto me beyond nature."

*Theotokion:*
The lamp of the Sun, concealed in the cloud of his mother's womb, having recognized the Son in the dark dwelling of the womb, bowed down, rejoicing and leaping.

*Kontakion, Tone 1. Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):*
The great Zechariah rejoices brightly with his all-glorious spouse Elizabeth, worthily conceiving John the Forerunner, whom the Archangel announced with joy; and let us mortals worthily honor him as a minister of grace.

*Ikos:*
Let us unfold the holy Gospel which Luke, the sacred and marvelous, wrote for us, and let us behold the bright and honorable conception of the Forerunner; for he says: When the elder and righteous Zechariah entered into the Holy of Holies to offer incense during the time of his division, Gabriel appeared unto him, bringing good tidings and saying: "O leader of the priests, in thine old age thou shalt have a son, a prophet and Forerunner, a voice and preacher, an ever-luminous lamp, and an initiate of grace."[^2097]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The angel made the furnace shed dew for the venerable youths, while the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tyrant to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*[^2098]

*Troparion:*
"Because thou hast not believed my words, receive deafness most manifestly; and when thou seest the voice of the Word being born, receive again thy voice, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of Israel!"

*Troparion:*
Having been united unto the youthful Elizabeth,[^2099] Zechariah, all-luminous as the sun, gave birth to a light-bearing, bright lamp, shining upon us who are held fast cruelly in the darkness of passions.

*Troparion:*
Tremblingly making clear his leapings like words, O Christ, the great Forerunner worshipped Thee in the virginal womb, while he himself was borne by the womb of Elizabeth: O Jesus, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*
Elizabeth, being the moon carrying within the star of the divine Forerunner, bowed down unto the bright cloud, Mary, who was bearing Christ the Sun, Who took flesh from her for our salvation.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable ones, and with water Thou didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous man;*[^2100]

[Fol. 148r]
*...and with water Thou didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous man; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, merely by willing them: Thee do we exalt supremely unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
The Friend of the Bridegroom is being prepared, and the voice of the Word receives a beginning; and in a barren womb now is nourished the great soldier of the King of all.

*Troparion:*
For barren hearts a husbandman has blossomed forth, the axe of passions already blooms, the honorable calf of temperance is being nourished, the great Forerunner: O ye peoples, be glad!

*Troparion:*
As Thou didst loose of old the bonds of the barren woman, so loose the petrification of my thoughts, O Baptist, and make me yield fruits of repentance, that I may live unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*
When Elizabeth saw thee bearing child within thy womb, O Maiden, she rejoiced divinely, the infant having leapt within her, as having recognized his Master.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word Incarnate appeared unto men, Whom magnifying with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed.*[^2101]

*Troparion:*
Christ's great and divine Forerunner, having now opened the barren gates, takes up dwelling, as in royal palaces, in his mother's side, that he may come forth as a soldier, preparing the paths of the King of all.

*Troparion:*
O elder, prophet of God, dance with joy, for thou shalt beget a son greater than whom none has arisen among men, John the Lord's Forerunner! Leap for joy, O Elizabeth! Rejoice, all the earth, offering praise unto God the Creator of all!

*Troparion:*
Remember us now who in faith praise thee with hymns, O prophet and Forerunner of the Lord, delivering us from passions of the soul; save us from afflictions, divinely guiding us unto the heavenly path, O ever-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
Elizabeth manifestly recognized thee as the pure Mother, when she felt herself loosed from the bonds of barrenness, and the Forerunner whom she bore felt the One Who had taken up abode within thy womb, O pure Virgin Mary gladdened by God.

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "With the disciples" (Со ꙋ҆чени́ки):*
The glorious conception of the Forerunner proclaims beforehand the King Who is to be born of the Virgin; for this one is from the barren and childless Elizabeth, and from the elder and great priest Zechariah: by their supplications, and of the Birthgiver of God, and of John Thy Baptist, O Lord, save and have compassion upon all. *Twice.*

*Glory* [Fol. 148v]
*Glory... Both now..., Theotokion:*
The pre-eternal Son by the Father's counsel has truly wrought great things with thee; for thou didst bear the immortal Life without passion, and didst remain as before birthgiving, having escaped maternal pangs; and after birthgiving, a Virgin didst thou remain, O Virgin.[^2102]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

*Sticheron 1:*
Creation makes merry at thy conception, O prophet and Forerunner, Baptist John; for thy divine birth prefigures unto us the Master's birth; and therefore with one accord, we that are upon earth worthily praise thee.

*Sticheron 2:*
Having found the conception of the barren woman as a marvelous testimony, the angel brings it unto Mary, presenting it for assurance; therefore we also praise the barrenness of Elizabeth, and Zechariah her spouse, and John.[^2103]

*Sticheron 3:*
The divinely-fashioned lamp of the Ever-Existing Light, the friend of the Bridegroom, the great light-bearer of the Sun of glory, the living voice of God the Word, the forerunner of the Lord's coming, is now conceived by the angelic annunciation.

*Sticheron 4:*
Having received the standing on the right of the divine altar of the sweet savor of Christ and the knowledge of His good pleasure, thou art signally known, O Forerunner, by the angel's intercession, being prefigured on the right of the holy place.[^2104]

*Glory... Both now..., Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
Elizabeth conceived the Forerunner of grace, and the Virgin conceived the Lord of glory. Both mothers greeted one another, and the babe leapt; for within, the servant praised the Master. Marvelling, the mother of the Forerunner began to cry aloud: "Whence is this to me, that the Mother of my Lord should come unto me? That He may save the alienated people, having great mercy!"[^2105]

*The Great Doxology, and the Troparion of the saint. Glory... Both now..., Theotokion: The mystery hidden from all ages... Litanies, and Dismissal.*

*Note: Wonder not concerning the Great Doxology; for it is indeed possible, as the Typikon explains, when the Octoechos is chanted and "Lord, I have cried" is sung, to perform also the Great Doxology.*[^2106]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon, Odes 3 and 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him [Ps. 63:11, LXX Ps. 63:11].*
*Verse: Hear my voice, O God [Ps. 63:2, LXX Ps. 63:2].*
*Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 210 from the midpoint [Gal. 4:22–31]: Brethren, Abraham—* [Fol. 149r]
*—had two sons.*
*Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous man shall flourish like a palm tree [Ps. 91:13, LXX Ps. 91:13].*
*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 2 [Luke 1:5–25]: At that time, there was in the days of Herod the king... The end: ...my reproach among men.*
*Communion Verse: The righteous man shall be in everlasting remembrance [Ps. 111:6, LXX Ps. 111:6].*

*The month of the same, on the 24th day.*
*The Holy Protomartyr and Equal-to-the-Apostles Thekla.*[^2107]
*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 8. Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и, а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*

*Sticheron 1:*
O Lord, though Thekla leaned toward the window for the love of Thee,[^2108] yet standing spiritually before Thy throne in the highest, she was amazed at Thine unapproachable majesty, which appeared in love toward mankind that Thou mightest save our souls.

*Sticheron 2:*
O Lord, though Thekla was separated involuntarily from her teacher,[^2109] yet she had Thee abiding with her at the time of suffering; and being stripped of clothing, she was covered with Thy glory; and having been crowned by Thy hand, she protects our souls.

*Sticheron 3:*
O Lord, though Thekla ran bound unto the stake,[^2110] yet she cast away the attachment to earthly bonds, and by the cord of the love of Thy strength was firmly bound unto Thee, O Savior of our souls.

*Sticheron 4:*
O Lord, though Thy pure one and protomartyr was given over to fire, yet was she not consumed in it, having Thee as a refresher; and she remained unharmed among many wild beasts, guarded by Thy hand, O Savior of our souls.

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
By the roots of passion-bearing, thou didst trample down the enemy, O all-blessed Thekla, and having crushed his wiles by suffering, thou didst flee from Thamyris,[^2111] and didst betroth thyself unto Christ, the true Lover.
