O converser with Paul, and fellow-sufferer with Stephen, having boldness as Christ's protomartyr among women: deliver from afflictions by thy prayers those who faithfully celebrate thine all-festal memory.

*Both now..., Theotokion:*

[Fol. 149v]
*Or if it be Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
A sword, as Simeon said, pierced thy heart, O most pure Sovereign Lady, when thou didst behold the ineffable Word Who shone forth from thee, condemned by the lawless and lifted up upon the Cross, tasting vinegar and gall, His side pierced, His hands and feet nailed; and with weeping thou didst cry aloud, shouting maternally: "What is this, O sweet Child, this new mystery?"[^2112]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory... of the saint, Tone 8. By Anatolius:*
Thou didst trample down the rush of lions, and didst put Thamyris to shame, O much-suffering protomartyr. Thou didst follow after thy Bridegroom, crying: "Unto the fragrance of Thy myrrh have I run, O Christ!" Therefore, seeking also Paul, thou didst receive a gift from heaven, and didst obtain a crown from God the Arbiter of combats; and thou prayest unceasingly that forgiveness of sins may be granted unto those who in faith celebrate thy sacred memory.

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
"What is this sight seen, which is beheld by mine eyes, O Master? Thou Who upholdest all creation wast suspended upon the tree, and art put to death, Thou Who givest life unto all!" the Birthgiver of God said weeping, when she beheld lifted up upon the Cross Him Who ineffably shone forth from her, God and Man.[^2113]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Instructed by the words of Paul, O Thekla bride of God, and strengthened in the faith by Peter,[^2114] called by God as protomartyr, thou wast shown forth as the first passion-bearer among women: thou didst ascend the flame as into a place in fair bloom, and wild beasts and bulls were afraid of thee, for thou wast armed with the Cross. Therefore, O all-lauded one, entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos, without the hymns to the martyrs, and the Canon of the saint on 6, whose acrostic is: "The Protomartyr is divinely glorified." The composition of John the Monk, Tone 8.*[^2115]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone has been gloriously glorified.*[^2116]

*Troparion:*
The voice of the tongue cannot recount the all-glorious sufferings of the protomartyr, for it fails before her worthy praise.

*Troparion:*
The proud savagery of the tormentor has ceased, for against him women contended gallantly in Christ with piety.

*Troparion:*
Instructed evangelically by thine ineffable words, O all-blessed Paul, the virgin betrothed herself unto Christ.

*Theotokion:*
As a life-bearing cluster pouring forth the sweetness of universal salvation, the Virgin bore Thee, O Christ.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou art the affirmation of those who run unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee.[^2117]

*Troparion:*
Oh, the love of thine that surpasses understanding, O all-honorable one, whereby in Christ thou didst cleave unto Paul, being joined in spirit!

*Troparion:*
The enjoyment of earthly things could not wound thee in mind, O glorious one, who wast already wounded with spiritual desire.

*Troparion:*
Forsaking all carnal attachments, thou wast not softened by maternal entreaties, O all-praised passion-bearer.[^2118]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the restoration of our foremother Eve, O Birthgiver of God, having borne unto the world the Author of life.

*Kontakion, Tone 8. Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Я́кѡ нача́тки):*
Thou didst shine forth with the beauty of virginity, and wast adorned with the crown of martyrdom; having entrusted thyself unto the apostolate, O virgin, as most glorious, thou didst turn the flame of fire into dew, and by thy prayer didst tame the fury of the bull, as the first-sufferer.[^2119]

*Then the Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having transformed womanhood into manhood through virtues by the love of Christ, thou wast alive on either side: for having diminished the darkness of passions through fasting, thou didst show forth the martyr's praise of suffering. Therefore thou shinest twofold unto the world as a luminary, radiating the beams of the Spirit, O all-praised protomartyr. Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor thy holy memory with love. *Twice.*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
As a virgin and the only one among women who without seed didst bear God in the flesh, all generations of mankind call thee blessed: for the fire of the Godhead made its abode in thee, and as an infant thou didst nurse the Creator and Lord. Therefore, both the angelic and human race worthily glorify thy most holy childbearing, and with one accord we cry unto thee: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who worthily hymn thy glory.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

*Stavrotheotokion (continued):*
Beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer upon the Cross, the ewe-lamb exclaimed weeping, and bitterly lamenting cried out: "The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee, but my heart burns within me, beholding Thy crucifixion, which Thou endurest for the tender mercy of Thy loving-kindness. O longsuffering Lord, abyss of mercy and inexhaustible fountain, have compassion, and grant remission of transgressions unto those who in faith hymn Thy divine passions."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have understood Thy works, and I have glorified Thy Godhead.[^2120]

*Troparion:*
Turning thee from betrothal unto Thamyris, Paul the bridesman united thee unto the heavenly Bridegroom as one undefiled, O all-honorable virgin.[^2121]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst cling unto the love of piety by Paul's words, and as idle babble, O martyr, didst thou revile the words of Thamyris.

*Troparion:*
By the sprinkling of divine blood the race of Adam was blessed; Eve rejoices, beholding the deceitful serpent falling indeed through women.

*Troparion:*
Having loved purity, the protomartyr rejected all the fair things of life: riches, noble lineage, beauty, and the sweetness of a betrothed.

*Theotokion:*
All we who are enlightened know thee as the Birthgiver of God, O all-pure one: for thou thyself hast borne the Sun of righteousness, O Ever-virgin.[^2122]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Rising early, we cry unto Thee: O Lord, save us; for Thou art our God, and beside Thee we know no other.[^2123]

*Troparion:*
By exceedingly grievous suffering thou didst contend in the arena, O all-blessed virgin, and wast accounted worthy of the prize.

*Troparion:*
The crafty serpent was despoiled, for the virgin was taught obedience by the divine sufferings.

*Troparion:*
Thy bashfulness was overcome by divine boldness: for the cloud that appeared kindled a saving fire for thee.[^2124]

*Theotokion:*
O Mary, unwedded Birthgiver of God, confound the hopes of enemies, and make glad those who hymn thee.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows, for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn nigh unto hades; and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God![^2125]

*Troparion:*
The maiden, having strengthened the weakness of her nature by the might of the Cross, youthful adornment having rejected youthful adornment through divine love, for boldly by night she ran, seeking the fragrant teachings of the Desired One.[^2126]

*Troparion:*
The glorious and first martyr Thekla supernaturally exchanged bridal chambers through voluntary love: for perceiving the embrace of evildoers, desire for the Creator conquered desires for creatures.

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing, the martyr kissed the chains of the divine teacher; in prison as in a divine flower-garden, watered by his words, she truly brought forth most beautiful fruit unto the Master.[^2127]

*Theotokion:*
As a rose, as a purest lily, as a fragrant perfume, O Maiden, the Creator, having chosen thee from the fair valleys of the world, made His abode in thy womb, and having been born, filled all things with fragrance.

*Kontakion, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Having wounded thy heart with the love of Christ, O virtuous virgin, thou didst despise the temporal betrothed as negligible, and didst dare the fire, and shut the mouths of wild beasts; and being saved from them, thou didst diligently seek Paul, O first-suffering virgin.[^2128]

*Ikos:*
Having learned the way of truth from Paul, along which thou didst tread unswervingly, O most marvelous one, and having forsaken thine own kin as a stranger, thou didst follow a stranger with manly mind and countenance. Therefore the Master showed thee forth unto the ends of the earth as the first-sufferer among women passion-bearers; having gone forth unto them, thou didst abide seeking Paul, O first-suffering virgin.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Children coming from Judea in Babylon of old trampled down the flame of the furnace by their faith in the Trinity, chanting: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2129]

*Troparion:*
Unto Paul as a prisoner thou wast bound by love, O all-blessed one, with indissoluble bonds, consenting in faith with piety, and chanting together: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst stand with Paul when judged by the unjust, O virtuous virgin! and through desire for the Master, casting away fear and shame, thou didst cry out: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
For divine love, O martyr, thou didst give over thy body unto the furnace, and by the power of the Desired One didst remain unconsumed, crying aloud:

...crying aloud: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
A rain-bearing cloud, having quenched the flame with rain and hail, justly burned the foolish, and saved the hymn-singing martyr: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast a rod from the root of Jesse, O all-blessed Virgin, budding forth the fruit of salvation unto those who in faith cry unto thy Son: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2130]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Whom the hosts of angels hymn, the King of heaven, praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2131]

*Troparion:*
Strangely manifested was thy mind: for into the tomb as into Eden thou didst enter, O virgin martyr, hymning Christ unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
Not enduring that the comeliness of the brightness of virginity should be darkened, through thy beauty thou didst choose to die and live unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
Having been united unto Christ the Bridegroom, Who gives life and is supernatural, O protomartyr, thou didst choose wild beasts to be the guardians of thy virginity.

*Troparion:*
Having put off the garment of corruption, O beautifully clad runner of Christ in the stadium, Thou hast arrived unto the ageless life unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*
Supernaturally thou didst bear the Creator and Savior, God the Word, O Virgin; therefore we honor thee, O pure one, unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thee, the unwedded Mother of God the Most High, thee who beyond understanding hast in truth through the Word borne God, who art higher than the all-pure hosts, with unceasing doxologies do we magnify.[^2132]

*Troparion:*
Who would not marvel at thy unconquerable courage, O protomartyr? For having tamed the noetic beasts, the passions of the soul, thou didst not fear the unrestrained rushes of wild beasts, but didst remain undefiled in the midst of them.

*Troparion:*
By divine command the impassable, hard rock split open for thee, the God-bearing martyr, sealed with the bath of regeneration, and reverently received the divine bride within as a bridal chamber.[^2133]

*Troparion:*
Heal, O protomartyr, the wounds of my soul; grant peace unto the world, granting victories over barbarian enemies unto our faithful King,[^2134] and peace unto the churches through thy prayers.

*Theotokion:*
Thee, the all-glorious and most holy Birthgiver of God, all we faithful glorify with unceasing hymns, and we chant unto thee who hast borne the Lord of all, for salvation for the salvation of those who hymn thee.

*Exapostilarion:*
Let us praise in hymns the glory of women, the instructor of sufferers, who opened the paths of martyrdom unto all, the virgin equal-to-the-apostles and first-sufferer.

*Theotokion:*
By thy strong protection, O pure one, preserve all of us thy servants unharmed from the assault of enemies: for thee have we acquired as our only refuge in necessities.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4. Tone 2. By Anatolius:*
Having the Bridegroom Christ God in the heavens, thou didst despise a temporal bridegroom and suitor, O first-suffering virgin. For sensibly disobeying thy mother's enticements, thou didst follow Paul. Taking the sign of the Cross upon thy shoulders, thou wast not afraid of fire, and the savagery of wild beasts thou didst turn into meekness. Thou didst slay the sea-monsters by the burial in Christ of holy baptism;[^2135] but as one who has shone forth valiantly in sufferings, cease not to pray unceasingly unto the Lord for those who in faith celebrate thine all-honorable memory.

*Tone the same:*
Having committed thyself unto the all-powerful nod, being strengthened as Christ's protomartyr, having forsaken earthly love, thou didst clothe thyself in the light of eternal life: being in the blessed chamber, wherein the flocks of women rest, having found entrance unto eternal life. With them pray, O equal-to-the-apostles virgin, for our souls.

*Tone 4:*
Form a choir, ye lovers of the martyrs, for the season of contests is at hand, and the annual memory of the protomartyr, urging all unto the doxology of God. For Thekla, the first martyr among women, having accomplished the course of suffering, was shown forth as the first crown-bearer, praying with boldness for our souls.

*Tone the same:*
At thy suffering surpassing man, O protomartyr of Christ, not only human nations were amazed, but even fierce wild beasts were struck with awe. The flames were accounted as no flames unto thee, O virtuous virgin Thekla, for the sake of thy Bridegroom Christ. Thou didst rejoice therefore, suffering for His sake and being separated from the world, that thou mightest attain heavenly blessedness, praying with boldness for our souls.

*Glory, Tone 2. By Anatolius:*
A martyr's contest *Glory, Tone 2. By Anatolius (continued):*
A martyr's contest lies before us today, O people, let us rejoice, and in it we shall behold accomplished and all-glorious things: for the undefiled ewe-lamb lies ready for slaughter after Christ God Who was slain for us, the virtuous virgin Thekla and bride of God. Therefore by faith in the Trinity she destroyed the godlessness of the tormentors, and dancing with the angels, she prays unto the Savior that our souls may be saved.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льніи мꙋ́ченицы):*
"A sword has pierced my heart, * O Son," the Virgin said, * when she saw Christ hanging upon the Tree, * "and it rends me, O Master, * even as Simeon foretold unto me of old.[^2136] * But arise and glorify together with Thyself, * O Immortal One, * Thy mother and handmaid, I pray."

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory of the martyr, Tone 2. By Anatolius:*
Come, ye lovers of the martyrs, let us honor in songs the praise of women, the protomartyr Thekla: for she trampled down the adversary enemy by the power of the Cross, and having taken the victory, was worthily crowned. Therefore the much-suffering one prays that those who celebrate her memory with faith and love may be delivered from misfortunes and from the future judgment.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Many pangs didst thou endure at the crucifixion of thy Son and God, O all-pure one, groaning, weeping, and crying out: "Woe is me, O sweetest Child, how dost Thou suffer unjustly, wishing to deliver the earthborn of Adam's race?" Therefore, O all-pure Virgin, in faith we pray thee: make Him merciful unto us.

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4; and of the saint, Ode 3 on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.[^2137]  
*Verse: In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel.*[^2138]  
*Epistle to Timothy, Pericope 296 [2 Tim. 3:10–15].*[^2139]  
*Alleluia, Tone 1: With patience I waited for the Lord, and He gave ear unto me.*[^2140]  
*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 101 [Matt. 25:1–13].*[^2141]  
*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*[^2142]

*The same month, on the 25th day. Memory of our venerable mother Euphrosyne:*[^2143]

*Stichera of the Octoechos, 3; and of the saint, 3. Tone 5. Podoben: "O venerable father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́тче):*
O venerable mother Euphrosyne, worthy of marvel, desiring the true joy, thou didst walk the path mediating it: for thou didst exchange riches for much poverty; a carnal betrothed for Him Who lives unto the ages; corruptible food for abstinence; rest for painful afflictions in ascetic struggle; life in the world for otherworldly life: which also thou hast obtained with the wise virgins,[^2144] having kept thy lamp unquenched, and being accounted worthy of the bridal chamber as a virgin, as a bride of Christ, O all-praised one.

Having watered thy mind with the labors of tears, through fasting thou didst make rich the fruits of virtues, and like a most beautiful vine thou didst bring forth fair clusters, O honorable one; manifestly satisfying our spiritual senses with their divine must, we are truly delighted by thy likeness, and we rejoice with divine gladness, having found sobriety from sin.[^2145] Crying unto thee, O all-honorable one: Pray ever unto Christ to grant the universe oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

A strange sight, and hard for nature to accept: how didst thou escape the cruel cunning of the old supplanter of Eve? Having dwelt in the midst of men with a perfect mind,[^2146] how didst thou pass through the midst of fire unburned? How didst thou conceal the weakness of womanhood, being strengthened by the divine power of Him Who took upon Himself our weakness, and Who shone forth from the unwedded Maiden? Pray thou Him, as thou dancest with the angels, to grant the universe oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 6. By the Studite:*
The pure treasury of thy purity thou didst preserve blameless from men, having become the bride of Christ, O all-blessed Euphrosyne: for having withered bodily beauty through ascetic labors, and having adorned the soul with the fair countenance of grace: for having manifestly hidden womanhood in manhood, thou didst escape *Glory, Tone 6. By the Studite (continued):*
...the snares of Beliar, having lived angelically. But ask peace for those who praise thee with love, as one eponymous of gladness, O divinely blessed one.[^2147]

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
O pure one, when thou didst see hanging upon the Tree the fully ripened Cluster, Whom without cultivation thou didst bear in thy womb, weeping thou didst exclaim, crying aloud: "O Child, drop down sweetness, whereby all intoxication of the passions is taken away, O Benefactor, for the sake of me who bore Thee, with divine consolations, as Thou art tender-hearted."

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Come, all ye lovers of virtue, and lovers of purity! Come, ye monastic pair, and choir of venerable women, let us all with one accord hymn the all-blessed Euphrosyne: Rejoice, thou who in a womanly body didst manfully contend! Rejoice, thou who through chastity didst put the enemy to shame and didst love Christ! Rejoice, precious stone, eponymous of gladness![^2148] But, O venerable mother, cease not to pray for those who honor thy memory.

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
Of old the undefiled ewe-lamb * and spotless Sovereign Lady, * when she saw her Lamb * lifted up upon the Cross, * exclaimed as a mother, * and marveling cried aloud: * "What sight is this, O sweet Child, * novel and most glorious? * How do the ungrateful people * deliver Thee unto the judgment seat of Pilate, * and condemn unto death the Life of all? * Yet I hymn Thine ineffable condescension, O Word!"

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
In thee, O mother, was preserved with certainty that which is according to the image; for taking up the cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thine actions didst teach us to despise the flesh, for it passes away, but to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Therefore also thy spirit rejoices together with the angels, O venerable Euphrosyne.[^2149]

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos; and of the saint, on 4. Whose acrostic is: With songs I praise thee who art worthy of gladness. By Joseph, Tone 5:*[^2150]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The steed and rider into the Red Sea: Christ Who shatters warfare with a high arm shook them off; but He saved Israel, as they sang a song of victory![^2151]

*Troparion:*
Unto me who today hymn in God-befitting songs Thy holy and truly all-praiseworthy memory, illumine me with the light of Thy prayers, O all-honorable one, who art eponymous of divine gladness.

*Troparion:*
Having loved the sole divine beauty of Christ, and being inflamed by His immaterial loveliness, thou didst abhor bodily beauty, O glorious one, exercising thyself in divine visions.

*Troparion:*
As a bride adorned with the beauties of virtues, thou wast truly betrothed unto Christ, Who is fair in beauty, having forsaken a temporal betrothed, O Euphrosyne, and all the beauty of life.

*Theotokion:*
He Who is all desire and sweetness and life has shone forth from thee through the transcendence of goodness, O all-undefiled Virgin: Whom pray Thou to save those who unceasingly call thee blessed.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing by Thy command, and didst suspend its unsupported weight: upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, establish Thy Church, O Thou Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind![^2152]

*Troparion:*
Having endured great struggles, thou didst cast down the enemy's crafts; thou didst conquer the demonic assaults; thou wast made like unto the angels, having practiced immortality, O mother, in thy mortal body.

*Troparion:*
Thy life makes glad the hearts of monastics, being an affirmation and instruction unto the saving commandments, and unto the paths of incorruption, and unto the uttermost limit of love for the Creator, O Euphrosyne.

*Troparion:*
Thy radiant and worthy of glory memory enlightens the divine gatherings of the faithful, sweetens the choirs of the venerable, and gladdens the angels: with whom thou art housed, O Euphrosyne, as one who has emulated the life equal to the angels.

*Theotokion:*
The grievous surging of passions overwhelms me; the abyss of evil spirits holds me fast; a tempest of sin shakes my heart: O Parent of God, establish me who purely praise thee!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лное сло́во):*
Having strengthened womanly weakness with heavenly hopes, with an unwavering mind thou didst dwell in the midst of men, O divinely inspired one *Sessional Hymn (continued):*
...having brought into subjection Eve's deceiver through thy fasting, O Euphrosyne, in vigils and meditations: therefore in faith we call thee blessed.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Having found thee, O Birthgiver of God, to be a haven and wall, a refuge and hope, a protection and fervent intercessor, we the faithful flee unto thee, and diligently cry out, and call aloud with faith: Have mercy, O Birthgiver of God, on those who hope in thee, and deliver us from transgressions.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee, O Christ, hanging willingly upon the Cross in the midst of thieves, Thy mother, torn in maternal affection, said: "O sinless Son, how dost Thou hang unjustly upon the Cross as an evildoer, wishing as the All-good One to bring the human race to life?"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Perceiving Thy divine condescension with prophetic insight, O Christ, Habakkuk cried aloud unto Thee in trembling: Thou art come for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones![^2153]

*Troparion:*
When thou didst take heed unto the heavenly Bridesman of souls, neither a father's love nor that of a temporal bridegroom hindered thee from walking the saving path.

*Troparion:*
Like a palm tree thou didst divinely blossom with the sweetness of righteousness, and like a cedar beside the waters of abstinence, O divinely wise one, thou didst multiply the fruits of virtues.[^2154]

*Troparion:*
By the fire of abstinence Thou didst reduce brushwood-like pleasures to ashes, and kindled by the ember of the Lord's love, Thou didst shine forth rays of miracles.

*Troparion:*
Torn in pieces and lying before thy fair feet is seen the former adversary of Eve, through the power and grace of Him Who was born of the Virgin, O Euphrosyne.[^2155]

*Theotokion:*
Show compassion, as thou art compassionate, unto my most wretched soul, O all-undefiled Parent of God, which is grievously darkened by the passions of sin and groans aloud.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, unto Thee I rise early and unto Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, as the only Merciful One![^2156]

*Troparion:*
By the radiance of divine deeds, like the emerald stone, O pure one, thou wast seen in the midst of men: showing forth manly roots and making glad the Lord.[^2157]

*Troparion:*
Pouring forth tears, thou wast perfumed as with spices, and thou wast magnified as myrrh costly myrrh, and thou wast offered unto God as an incorrupt virgin.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst offer all thy desire unto God, desiring Him, seeking Him, following His saving legislation, O virgin.

*Theotokion:*
O pure one, in youth thou didst bear as an infant Him Who timelessly shone forth from the unoriginate Father before the ages: Whom implore for the world, O bride of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Calm the sea of passions raging with a soulish storm, O Master Christ, and lead me up from corruption, as Thou art compassionate![^2158]

*Troparion:*
As pure and undefiled, as fair, as exceedingly good, thou wast betrothed unto the Bridegroom Word, Who preserves thee incorrupt unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
Seeking the Creator with groanings and tears, thou wast accounted worthy of the vision of Him as one chosen with the chosen, O thou worthy of marvel.

*Troparion:*
An image of abstinence, an animate likeness of chastity wast thou shown forth unto the faithful who rightly praise thy sacred memory, O Euphrosyne.

*Theotokion:*
Beyond understanding, beyond speech, O all-pure one, thou didst bear the timeless Creator, Who delivers from all corruption those who hymn thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Kontakion, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Desiring to obtain the life on high, thou didst diligently forsake earthly sweetness, and mingled thyself in the midst of men, O most fair one; for the sake of Christ thy Bridegroom thou didst despise a temporal betrothed.[^2159]

*Ikos:*
Gladdened in gladness and joy of soul, let us arise diligently to hear the most glorious word: for this narrative surpasses every mind, and strikes with awe, how a woman, dwelling in the midst of men, conquered Beliar, and trampled down the fire of pleasures, and was not burned at all; for desiring Christ, the undefiled one despised a temporal betrothed.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The supremely exalted Lord of the fathers quenched the flame, and bedewed the youths as they sang in unison: Blessed art Thou, O God![^2160]

*Troparion:*
Light shone forth for thee, his spouse, O glorious Euphrosyne:[^2161] for thou didst have an upright mind, chanting in song: Blessed art Thou, O God!

*Troparion:*
Having the Cross as a staff strengthening thee, thou didst pass through the demonic chasms unharmed, O venerable one, chanting in song: Blessed art Thou, O God Blessed art Thou, O God!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst make thy heart a dwelling of the Holy Spirit, O venerable one, Who strengthened thee and showed thee forth stronger than the evil spirits.

*Theotokion:*
O all-undefiled one, thou didst bear the incorporeal God clothed in the body, Who delivers us as with fear we chant in song: Blessed art Thou, O God!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the youths in the furnace, having woven a universal choir, sang: All ye works, hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^2162]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shake off the darkness of the passions, O maiden, having emulated the immaterial life of the angels: with whom also thou singest: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The Guardian of life gives thee life, for thou didst follow His footsteps: desiring His divine beauty, with Him also thou art glad unto all ages.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast ascended unto the everlasting mansions in truth, having obtained the desire Whom thou didst love, delighting as it were in the tree of life, and supremely exalting Christ unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*
All-chosen, all-adorned, whom God loved, whom He chose, wast thou shown forth, O Virgin ever most glorified: therefore we hymn thee always as the Birthgiver of God.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Rejoice, O Isaiah! The Virgin had in womb, and bare a Son, Emmanuel, both God and man; Orient is His name: Whom magnifying, we call the Virgin blessed.[^2163]

*Troparion:*
The assembly of monastics praises the sacred celebration, accomplishing thy divinely radiant memory; the choir of nuns rejoices, for thou, O pure one, wast shown forth as the brightness of all, O Euphrosyne worthy of marvel.

*Troparion:*
As an honorable offering of the heavenly temple wast thou, as a lily thou didst blossom in the courts of God, as a sweet-smelling rose thou didst offer thyself unto the King of all, as precious myrrh, O all-blessed Euphrosyne.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst enlighten thyself with the radiant adornment of thy virtues, and wast brought unto the spiritual bridal chamber, O pure one; and now ineffably thou beholdest the beauty of Christ, and receivest most perfect deification.

*Troparion:*
Thy radiant memory shines forth today upon the faithful, pouring out enlightenment and holiness in it we pray thee, as the chosen bride of Christ: Save us always by Thy prayers, O Euphrosyne!

*Theotokion:*
With the light of thy countenance enlighten me lying in the darkness of passions, O spiritual door of light, lest the night of death overtake me, O pure and good one, cutting off the despair of my salvation.

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "By the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Having hidden thyself from the prince of shame, thou didst show him forth as foolish in his crafty-minded form: being a virgin in soul and body, thou wast a man in understanding and faith, O venerable Euphrosyne, the adornment of virgins, and the beauty of nuns.[^2164]

*Theotokion:*
Make the day of spiritual gladness dawn upon me: for thou art, O pure one, light and life unto those in darkness. For thou art powerful in thy desire, and hast the power to accomplish it, as thou art the Sovereign Lady of all: deliver all from misfortunes and afflictions, and from the stumbling-blocks of the alien.

*The same month, on the 26th day. The Falling Asleep of the Holy Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian:*[^2165]

*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Come, ye faithful, let us today crown with divine songs the writer of the depths of wisdom and orthodox dogmas, the glorious and beloved John; for he thundered forth: In the beginning was the Word.[^2166] Whence he was shown forth as a son of thunder, having wisely preached the Gospel unto the world, the ever-memorable one. *(Twice)*

In truth thou wast shown forth as a true friend, a great bosom companion unto the Teacher Christ: for reclining upon His breast,[^2167] thence didst thou draw forth the dogmas of wisdom, wherewith thou enrichest all the earth round about, as a divine speaker of God. Therefore holding fast unto these, the fair Church of Christ now rejoices and is glad.

Rejoice, O theologian in truth! Rejoice, most beloved son of the Mother of the Lord! For standing by the Cross of Christ, thou didst hear the divine voice of the Master crying aloud unto thee: Behold now thy mother![^2168] Whence worthily do all of us call thee blessed, as the great and beloved apostle of Christ.

*Glory, Tone 2. Idiomelon (Самогала́сенъ):*
Come, ye faithful, let us call blessed the summit of the apostles, the trumpet of theology, the spiritual commander who subjected the universe unto God, the ever-memorable John, who departs from the earth, yet departs not from the earth, but lives and awaits the awesome Second Coming of the Master;[^2169] entreat that we may meet it uncondemned, O beloved one, initiate of mysteries, bosom companion of Christ, for those who accomplish thy memory with love.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1. Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льніи мꙋ́ченицы):*[^2170]
O glorious theologian, by thy divine teachings * and the manifestations of miracles * thou didst drive away all the mist of delusion, * and didst enlighten the people * unto the knowledge of the true faith: * and now pray that unto our souls * peace be granted, and great mercy.

*Verse: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^2171]

O all-wise John, * constant beloved of Christ, * delivering me from the love of the flesh, * establish me in deeds of piety * by thy divine supplications unto the Birthgiver of God of all, * and pray that there be given unto me * the remission of transgressions, * and great mercy.

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.*[^2172]

O all-sacred eyewitness, * deliver from passions and misfortunes, * and from diseases and afflictions, * those who rightly praise thee, * and honor thee with love, * and flee unto thee with faith, * coming unto thy divine protection; * and entreat that unto our souls * peace be granted, and great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 2:*
O theologian and virgin, beloved disciple of the Savior: by thy prayers save us, we pray, from every harm: for we are thy flock.

*Both now... Theotokion:*
All my hope I place upon thee, O Mother of God: keep me under thy protection.

*Troparion, Tone 2:*
O beloved apostle of Christ God, hasten to deliver a defenseless people: He accepts thee falling down before Him, Who received thee reclining upon His breast; pray Him, O theologian, to dispel the impending mist of the heathen, asking for us peace and great mercy.[^2173]

*Glory... Both now... Resurrection Theotokion:*

*At Great Vespers, we chant the Kathisma: "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*[^2174]

*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 8, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
The beholder of ineffable revelations * and teller of the exalted mysteries of God, * the son of Zebedee, * having written for us the Gospel of Christ, * has taught us to theologize * the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

The well-attuned lute of heavenly songs, * the writer of mysteries, * the lips inspired by God, * sweetly sings the song of songs; * moving his lips like strings, * moving his tongue like a plectrum, * he prays that we may be saved.

With thy voice like thunder, * making known the hidden word * of the wisdom of God, * O beloved of God, * thou criest aloud ever, purely moving thy lips: * In the beginning was the Word; * and thou teachest every man unto the knowledge of God.[^2175]

*Glory, Tone 2. Idiomelon (Самогала́сенъ):*
The son of thunder, the foundation of the divine words, the chief of theology, and the first preacher of the truth of the dogmas of the wisdom of God, the beloved John and virgin, let the human race duly praise with hymns. For having unceasingly within himself the divine utterance: In the beginning was the Word, he said, united without beginning unto the Father, and equal according to the Father's essence, he showed forth unto us in himself the orthodoxy of the Holy Trinity; and being co-Creator with the Father, bearing life and the true Light, he likewise showed Him forth unto us. O awesome wonder, and thing full of wisdom! For being full of love, he was also filled with theology, being by glory, honor, and faith the founder of our pure faith: through which we shall obtain eternal blessings on the day of judgment.[^2176]

*Both now... Theotokion. Podoben: "The shadow of the Law has passed" (Пре́йде сѣ́нь зако́ннаѧ):*

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*

*Readings, 3.*

*Reading from the General Epistle of John [1 John 3:21–4:6]:*[^2177]
Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, we have boldness toward God; and whatsoever we ask, we receive of Him, because we keep His commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in His sight. And this is His commandment, that we should believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, as He gave us commandment. And he that keeps His commandments dwells in Him, and He in him: and hereby we know that He abides *Reading 1 (continued):*
...in us, by the Spirit Whom He has given us. Beloved, believe not every spirit, but prove the spirits, whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. Hereby know ye the Spirit of God, and the spirit of delusion: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God; and every spirit that confesses not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it comes, and even now already is in the world. Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is He that is in you, than he that is in the world. They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world hears them. We are of God: he that knows God hears us; he that is not of God hears not us.[^2178]

*Reading from the General Epistle of John [1 John 4:11–16]:*[^2179]
Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another. No man has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwells in us, and His love is perfected in us. Hereby know we that we dwell in Him, and He in us, because He has given us of His Spirit. And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Savior of the world. Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwells in him, and he in God. And we have known and believed the love that God has to us. God is love; and he that dwells in love dwells in God, and God in him.[^2180]

*Reading from the General Epistle of John [1 John 4:20–5:5]:*[^2181]
Beloved, if a man say: I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he that loves not his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God Whom he has not seen? And this commandment have we from Him, That he who loves God love his brother also. Whosoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God; and every one that loves Him that begat loves him also that is begotten of Him. By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God, and keep His commandments. For this is the love of God, that we keep His commandments; and His commandments are not grievous. For whatsoever is born of God overcomes the world: and this is the victory that overcomes the world, even our faith. Who is he *Reading 3 (continued):*
...that overcomes the world, but he that believes that Jesus is the Son of God?[^2182]

*At the Litiya, the Stichera of the temple. Then of the apostle, Tone 1. By Germanus:*
Rivers of theology flowed forth from thine honorable lips, O apostle, wherewith the Church of God being watered, orthodoxly worships the consubstantial Trinity: Whom do thou also now implore, O John the Theologian, to establish and save our souls.

*By Andrew Pyros:*
A garden of purity, sweet-smelling myrrh has shone forth again unto us in the present festival, to cry aloud unto him: Reclining upon the Master's breast, and having rained down the Word upon the world, O apostle John, who didst keep the Virgin as the apple of thine eye, entreat for us great mercy from Christ!

O disciple of the Savior, virgin and theologian: unto thee as a virgin, Christ God when crucified delivered the Virgin and Birthgiver of God; and her thou didst preserve as the apple of thine eye.[^2183] Therefore pray that our souls may be saved.

As an eyewitness of ineffable mysteries, thou didst cry aloud, proclaiming the eternal Word to be in the beginning with God, and that He is God, O apostle John, bosom companion of Christ and constant friend, sweetness of the Trinity, unshakable affirmation of Ephesus and Patmos, and our help: pray, O all-blessed theologian, that the people who faithfully accomplish thy memory may ever be delivered from impious enemies, visible and spiritual.

*Glory, Tone 4:*
Reclining upon the breast of the Teacher Christ at the Supper of the Lord, O beloved disciple, thence didst thou learn ineffable things, and thundered forth unto all a heavenly voice: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God;[^2184] the true Light that enlightens every man coming into the world: Christ God and the Savior of our souls.

*Both now... Theotokion:*
The Son Who with the Father and the Spirit is doxologized in the highest by the Cherubim, desiring to fashion anew the first-created, ineffably emptied Himself wholly in thy womb, O all-hymned Birthgiver of God: and having shone forth from thee, He enlightened the whole world with His divinity, delivering it from idol-madness, and having deified humanity in Himself, He led it up unto the heavens: Christ God and the Savior of our souls.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4. Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
Having theologized the Son of the Highest * co-everlasting with the Father * and consubstantial, * Light from Light immutable, * and the impress of the Hypostasis of the Father, timelessly shone forth and impassibly from Him, the Creator and Lord of all ages, O beloved one, thou didst preach Him unto the world: as having brought forth light out of darkness, Christ our God; Whom pray to save and enlighten our souls.

*Verse: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^2185]

Having received the Comforter's light, * whereby also being enlightened thou didst theologize * Him Who proceeds from the Father * and through the Son is manifested unto mankind, * equal in honor, * enthroned together, * and consubstantial * with the unoriginate Father and the Word of God, * O beloved one, thou didst proclaim unto all.[^2186] * Therefore in hymns we honor thee * as the divine foundation of the faith: * which do thou keep unshaken * by thy prayers unto the Lord.

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.*[^2187]

Having ascended unto the heights of theology, * thou wast taught the ineffable mysteries of God: * concerning the one essence of the Godhead, * the one glory, * and kingdom, and dominion, * ever distinguished in three Hypostases, * essentially undivided and united * in unconfused divine unity: * thus with glory thou didst proclaim the undivided Trinity, O theologian. * Whom pray to save and enlighten our souls.

*Glory, Tone 6. By John the Monk:*
O apostle of Christ, evangelist and theologian, having become an initiate of ineffable mysteries: thou didst thunder forth unto us the unutterable teachings of wisdom, explaining unto the faithful: In the beginning was the Word; and casting aside: He was not,[^2188] thou didst cut off the words of heretics. Shown forth as a bosom companion and beloved friend: like Isaiah the loud-voiced and Moses the God-seer, having boldness toward God, diligently pray for our souls.

*Both now... Theotokion. Podoben: "My Maker and Redeemer" (Творе́цъ и҆ и҆зба́витель мо́й):*

*At the Blessing of the Loaves, Troparion:*
O beloved apostle of Christ God: *(Twice)*. Written at Small Vespers. And Birthgiver of God and Virgin: *(Once)*.

*And a Reading.*

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the saint, (Twice); Glory... Both now... Theotokion: "All surpassing understanding" (Всѧ̑ па́че смы́сла):*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Thou wast called a son of divine thunder,[^2189] so as to sound forth *Sessional Hymn (continued):*
...unto the ears of the impious; and proclaiming sweeter than a trumpet, O all-wise one: The incarnation of the Word is the righteousness of the heart; and reclining upon His breast as an intimate friend, whence thou didst draw forth the revelation of understanding: thou didst proclaim unto all Him Who is co-unoriginate with the Father, O apostle John: pray Christ God to grant the remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love. *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Having conceived Wisdom and the Word in thy womb without being consumed, O Mother of God, thou didst bear unto the world Him Who holds the world; and in thine arms thou didst hold Him Who upholds all, the Nourisher of all, and Creator of creation. Therefore I pray thee, O all-holy Virgin, and in faith I glorify thee, that I may be delivered from transgressions; and in the day of judgment, when I am to stand before the face of my Creator, O Sovereign Lady, pure Virgin, then grant me thy help; for thou canst do all things whatsoever thou desirest, O all-hymned one.

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having left the depths of catching fish, with the rod of the Cross thou didst openly catch all the nations unto the faith like fish; for as Christ said unto thee, thou wast shown forth as a fisher of men,[^2190] catching them unto piety. Therefore thou didst sow the understanding of the Word throughout all Patmos, and didst acquire Ephesus by thy words, O theologian and apostle: pray Christ God to grant the remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love. *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
O all-pure Virgin Mother of God, heal the grievous passions of my soul, I pray thee, and grant me forgiveness of my transgressions, which in foolishness I have committed: my soul and body have I defiled, wretched that I am. Woe is me! What shall I do in that hour, when the angels shall separate my soul from my passionate body? Then be thou my helper and most fervent intercessor: for thee do I have as hope, I thy servant.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Reclining upon the breast of Jesus, thou didst obtain boldness, as a disciple inquiring: Lord, who is Thy betrayer?[^2191] Being greatly beloved, O all-lauded one, He openly showed him unto thee with the bread. Therefore, having become an initiate of ineffable things, thou teachest *Sessional Hymn (continued):*
...the ends of the earth the incarnation of the Word, O theologian and apostle: pray Christ God to grant the remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love. *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Let us hymn the heavenly door and ark, the all-holy mountain, the radiant cloud, the unburnt bush, the rational paradise, the recall of Eve, the great treasure of the whole universe; for salvation has been wrought in her for the world, and remission of ancient transgressions. Therefore we cry aloud unto her: Pray thy Son to grant remission of transgressions unto those who piously worship thy most holy Nativity.

*The Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.[^2192]  
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God.*  
*Let every breath praise the Lord.*  
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 67 [John 21:15–25].*[^2193]  
*After Psalm 50. Glory: Through the prayers of the apostle...*  
*Both now: Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God...*  
*Sticheron, Tone 2:*
O theologian and virgin, beloved disciple of the Savior: by thy prayers save us, we pray, from every harm: for we are thy flock.

*Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the Heirmos on 6; and of the apostle, both canons on 8.*

*Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The weapon-bearing power of old overwhelmed the whole army of Pharaoh in the deep; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin: the supremely glorified Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified![^2194]

*Troparion:*
As fair, as wholly exceedingly good, as undefiled among women, God chose thee and dwelt in thine undefiled womb; Whom pray, O all-undefiled one, to deliver from the defilement of sins all who hymn thee.

*Troparion:*
In the manner of the Psalms, O pure one, as queen thou hast stood at the right hand of the King Who shone forth from thy womb;[^2195] Whom pray, O all-undefiled one, that He show me forth a beholder of the right hand in the day of recompense, O Bride of God.

*Troparion:*
Having dried up human nature by every kind of unseemliness, having borne the heavenly rain, thou didst renew all things; but I pray thee: show forth the parched furrow of my soul fruitful, O Bride of God!

*Troparion:*
Having been slain by the orchard of knowledge, by the Tree of life, O pure one, we have been called unto eternal life, through Christ Who has blossomed forth from thee beyond understanding from thee, Christ our God; Whom do thou entreat with boldness, that our souls may be saved.

*Canon of the Apostle, whose acrostic is: "I sing the Son of Thunder in beauty worthy of Christ."[^2196] The composition of Theophanes. Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. The same Heirmos.*

*Troparion:*
Having received the heavenly adoption as a son, O blessed one, which thou didst proclaim, and having become a converser with the true Word: by thy prayers preserve those who believe in thy honorable preaching and theology.

*Troparion:*
Having a steadfast mind, thou didst disregard all things that are upon the earth and the bonds of nature; and dwelling with the Word, O all-wise one, both rationally and spiritually, thou didst deliver from irrationality those who lived irrationally.

*Troparion:*
Having received the understanding of heavenly things, O most divinely-inspired theologian, thou didst proclaim God the Word: *"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with His Parent, and the Word was God"*; thus didst thou teach the Gospel.

*Theotokion:*
The choir of divine maidens most divinely sings of thee in thy beauty among women, O Virgin Sovereign Lady, adorned with the beauties of the Godhead; for beyond word thou didst give birth to the beneficent Word.

*Another Canon of the Apostle, whose acrostic is: "I offer supplications to the divine initiate of mysteries."[^2197] The composition of Joseph. Tone 6.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel, seeing the pursuer Pharaoh drowned, cried out: Let us sing a song of victory unto God!

*Troparion:*
Illumined in mind by the lightnings of the Spirit, having stooped down, thou didst clearly declare unto us the awesome Nativity, O theologian of God: *"In the beginning was the Word of God."*

*Troparion:*
Bowed down by a multitude of assaults, and passions, and afflictions, and by the onsets of cruel misfortunes, with faith we flee unto thee, O theologian: be a helper unto thy servants.

*Troparion:*
Having healed the cruel passions of our souls as an excellent physician, O wise one, deliver us from eternal condemnation and the fire by thy mediation.

*Theotokion:*
O pure one who didst conceive God Who became man for our sake: entreat Him, in the day of judgment, to show mercy upon us who have sinned greatly against Him.

*Katavasia:*
*"I shall open my mouth..."*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The desert blossomed as the lily, O Lord, the barren church of the Gentiles, by Thy coming by Thy coming, wherein my heart is established.

*Troparion:*
The Creator, coming forth from thy womb, O all-immaculate one, clothed Himself in me, a man, granting a garment of incorruption unto him who was stripped naked by many unseemly deeds.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst give birth to the most pure One, God the Word, O Birthgiver of God: Whom do thou fervently entreat to have mercy on my humble soul, grieving in the dishonor of pleasures.

*Troparion:*
Heal the wounds of my soul, O most pure one, and my humble heart, embittered by the venom of the serpent, do thou cure with thy effective remedy.

*Troparion:*
As a Mother possessing boldness toward thy Son, O Birthgiver of God, ask help for the afflicted people, and cast down the insolence of the lawless.

*Another [Troparion]. The same Heirmos:*[^2198]
Thou didst appear as a trumpet by thy theological tongue, [proclaiming] the mystery beyond understanding, O divinely-blessed John, wherein my heart is established.

*Troparion:*
Thy tongue became the pen of a scribe, of the All-Holy Spirit, divinely inscribing Thy honorable and divine Gospel.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst draw forth the abyss of wisdom, O all-wise one, having reclined with divinely-wise boldness upon the fountain of Wisdom; and of Him thou didst become a divine preacher.

*Theotokion:*
We honor thee who alone art both virgin and mother, as having become the mediatress of salvation for us, O all-immaculate one, and having delivered the world by thy prayers.

*Another. Heirmos:*
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

*Troparion:*
With a luminous and pure mind, having conversed with the Word, O thrice-blessed theologian: thou wast mystically instructed by Him wisely in things that are beyond word, and thou didst enlighten the whole creation.

*Troparion:*
Deliver me from the cruel bonds of sin, O thrice-blessed one, binding me with the love of the Master and God, Whom thou didst warmly love, and Whose theologian thou wast named.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast appeared as our defender, and mediator, and deliverer, and intercessor before the Lord, and worker of wonders, and a fountain of healings, O theologian; therefore we honor thee.

*Theotokion:*
When the Word Who was ineffably incarnate of thee, O Birthgiver of God, was lifted up upon the Tree of the Cross, He entrusted thee, as a virgin maiden, unto the virgin disciple.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Having reclined upon the breast of Wisdom, and having been taught the knowledge of existing things, thou didst divinely thunder forth: *"In the beginning was the Word."* Having well written first of the unoriginate Nativity, thou didst proclaim unto all the Incarnation of the Word. Therefore, having caught the nations with thy tongue as with a net, by the grace of the Spirit thou dost instruct the ends of the earth and enlighten them with wonders, O theologian and apostle: entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love. *(Twice)*

*Glory..., both now... Theotokion:*
Having fallen into manifold temptations from enemies visible and invisible, and held fast by the tempest of my countless sins: as unto my fervent protection and shelter, and a haven, O pure one, I flee unto thy goodness. Therefore, O most pure one, fervently pray unto Him Who was incarnate of thee without seed, for all thy servants who unceasingly pray unto thee, O most pure Birthgiver of God, entreating Him ever to grant remission of sins unto those who worthily hymn thy glory.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou hast come from the Virgin, not an envoy nor an angel, but Thyself incarnate, O Lord, and hast saved me, the whole man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Rain down upon me a drop of compunction, O Birthgiver of God, taking away all the filth of my heart, and my sorrow, and driving away harmful assaults.

*Troparion:*
Despise me not, O most pure one, wounded by the weapon of pleasure and lying in wounds, but heal me by the spear and Blood of Thy Son and our God Who was crucified.

*Troparion:*
O thou who hast been enriched with the dominion over every creature, make me, who am grievously impoverished, worthy of divine grace: that I may magnify thee as my good protectress, O all-immaculate one.

*Troparion:*
From thy womb, O unwedded Maiden, Christ the ray of the Sun shone forth, and being crucified He enlightened the universe and destroyed the demonic darkness.

*Another. The same Heirmos:*

*Troparion:*
The Word worthily showed thee forth as a theologian, having most excellently initiated thee into the mysteries of His Godhead, and having taught thee His ineffable dispensation according to man.

*Troparion:*
Having acquired a divine mind and a virginal body, thou wast a living and animate temple, O glorious one, and a most sacred dwelling of the all-hymned Trinity.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast honored with the adoption of the most pure Virgin, O blessed virgin disciple, and thou didst appear as a brother unto Him Who chose thee and perfected thee as a theologian.

*Theotokion:*
Healing the ancient transgression of Eve, the transcendent God dwelt within thee, the all-immaculate and most pure one, to re-create me, a man, who had fallen in every way.

*Another. Heirmos:*
"Christ is my power, God and Lord," the venerable Church sings in divine manner, crying out from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.

*Troparion:*
With the drops of the word, O glorious one, thou didst water the whole universe, and thou didst piously dry up the turbid waters of impiety; therefore we honor thee.

*Troparion:*
With strength and boldness, I pray thee, O all-wise one: gird my soul, weakened by all manner of assaults from unclean enemies, as I flee beneath thy shelter.

*Troparion:*
Having become a temple of the Divine Spirit, by thy mediation, O theologian, show forth as temples of God those who with faith attend in thy divine temple.

*Theotokion:*
Let us sing of the divine temple of God: let us all call the holy Virgin blessed, having been divinized through her and delivered from cruel misfortunes.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou hast become a Mediator between God and men, O Christ God; for through Thee, O Master, from the night of ignorance we have access unto Thy Father, the Prince of Light.

*Troparion:*
O most pure one who didst give birth to the Way of Life: guide me now into the right path, who have been irrationally cast down into tracklessness and the abyss of cruel falls.

*Troparion:*
Having estranged my mind from the knowledge of God, I have lived prodigally, wandering in the far country of passions; but turn me back, O pure Virgin, and save me by thy consolations.

*Troparion:*
With thy living waters, water thy servant who is consumed by the flame of sins and scorched by the demonic assaults, O most pure Virgin-Mother.

*Troparion:*
Behold, in thy womb, O most pure Birthgiver of God, thou didst hold Christ God beyond word, as Isaiah proclaimed, and beyond nature thou didst give birth unto Him, O Mother of God.

*Another. The same Heirmos:*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as a heavenly mind by grace, O theologian, having become wholly light through drawing near unto the Primal Light, and by thy pure vision being divinized in drawing near unto Him.

*Troparion:*
With a pure mind, and with holy lips, O divinely-inspired one, and with most pure speech thou didst proclaim thy Gospel, and didst set forth common salvation unto all the faithful.

*Troparion:*
Dwelling with Christ from youth, Thou wast appointed an instrument of grace by Him, instructed in the mysteries of theology and taught the thrice-holy glory beyond nature.

*Theotokion:*
Remembering thy generations, we now call thee blessed: through thee, O all-immaculate one, we have truly received ineffable blessedness and unending life.

*Another. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray, the souls of those who lovingly rise early unto Thee: that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, calling them forth from the darkness of sin.

*Troparion:*
As the dawn thou didst shine forth upon those on earth, O apostle, clearly proclaiming to the world the Spiritual Dayspring Who came in the flesh and destroyed the darkness of polytheism.

*Troparion:*
With thy sacred words of theology, thou didst water every soul, O sacred preacher and apostle; therefore I cry unto thee: with grace water my heart, which is parched by sins.

*Troparion:*
I have been wounded by the arrows of the enemy: heal me completely, O wise one, I pray, by thy intercession; and direct me into the paths of God, who am ever going astray in iniquities.

*Theotokion:*
When thou didst stand with the beloved disciple at the Cross of thy Son, O all-immaculate one, thou didst groan weeping, and didst marvel at His great compassion toward men.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender mercy: lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
Show me not forth as a joy unto demons at the future judgment, O Sovereign Lady; but looking with compassion upon me, entreat the Judge and thy Son.

*Troparion:*
With my thoughts and with my evil and lawless deeds I have angered Thee, O Lord; I bring unto Thee Thy Mother in prayer: have compassion and save me!

*Troparion:*
Deliver me from condemnation, O Sovereign Lady, who am self-condemned by transgressions: for thou didst give birth to the Judge and God of all, O all-hymned one.

*Troparion:*
Entreat Jesus the Savior, Whom beyond nature thou didst bear in the flesh, O Virgin-Mother most pure, that thy servants may be delivered that thy servants may be delivered from tribulations.

*Another. The same Heirmos:*

*Troparion:*
Jesus, my God and Lord, accepting thy purity and all-perfect holiness, received thee as a brother, O theologian.

*Troparion:*
As a disciple, thou didst liken thy life holily unto the disciple; thou didst recline upon the breast of Wisdom, O glorious one, and from thence didst draw forth grace.

*Troparion:*
The great and divine splendors of thy theology, O glorious one, enlightened the whole universe and illumined it with the tri-hypostatic light.

*Theotokion:*
He Who stretched out the heaven by His will, stretched thee forth, O pure Mother of God, as another earthly heaven, and shining forth from thee He appeared.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!

*Troparion:*
Thy theological tongue truly became as the pen of a ready scribe, inscribing true understanding, and the very new law upon the tablets of our hearts, O theologian.

*Troparion:*
Having radically withered the shoots of impiety as a most excellent cultivator: plant in my soul the fear of God, O glorious one, blossoming with the good fruit of virtues.

*Theotokion:*
He Who came forth from the Virgin manifestly named thee the son of the Virgin: with her, pray, O ever-memorable one, that all who do what is well-pleasing unto Him may become sons of God by adoption.

*Theotokion:*
In the likeness of flesh, God was made known unto men from thee, O all-immaculate one: Whom do thou ever entreat, O most pure one, to put to death the ruinous wisdom of our flesh.

*Kontakion, Tone 2:*
Who shall tell of thy majestic deeds, O virgin disciple? For thou dost pour forth miracles and pour out healings, and thou prayest for our souls as the theologian and friend of Christ.

*Ikos:*
To learn the heights of heaven and to search the depths of the sea is audacious and incomprehensible; for just as it is utterly impossible to number the stars and the sand of the seashore, so likewise is it impossible adequately to recount the things of the theologian: with so many crowns did Christ, Whom he loved, crown him; upon Whose breast he reclined, and at the Mystical Supper ate with Him, as the theologian and friend of Christ.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The god-opposing decree of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame. But Christ spread a spiritual dew upon the pious children, He Who is blessed and supremely praised.

*Troparion:*
Being my strength, and song, and salvation, and firm defense, and an unconquerable wall, O Birthgiver of God: subdue the demons that war against me, who ever seek to put me to death.

*Troparion:*
Having incarnated God, by thy active blood, O Virgin, thou didst divinize mankind. Therefore I pray thee: by thy prayers deliver me, defiled by passions and corrupted by the wiles of the enemy.

*Troparion:*
The furnace prefigured thy childbirth, O all-immaculate one; for neither did it burn the children, nor did the unbearable Fire burn thy womb. Therefore we pray thee: deliver thy servants from the eternal fire.

*Troparion:*
A most pure conception and an incorrupt childbirth thou alone didst show forth, remaining a virgin; for thou didst conceive God Who is above all, O pure one, Who became man for the salvation and deliverance of the faithful.

*Another. The same Heirmos:*

*Troparion:*
Shining with divine radiance, thou didst clearly theologize the Holy Spirit, as proceeding from the unoriginate Father and abiding in the Son unceasingly,[^2199] as consubstantial.

*Troparion:*
In thee, O blessed one, Christ, the supremely glorified and beloved One, placed the dwelling of the Sun of righteousness, having made thee ever-moving and being proclaimed by thy theological tongue.

*Troparion:*
The power of thy words, the divine utterance, went forth, O all-blessed and wonder-worthy one, and thy other-worldly Gospel encompassed the whole earth by the grandeur of its dogmas.

*Theotokion:*
A most pure conception and an incorrupt childbirth thou alone didst show forth, remaining a virgin; for thou didst conceive God Who is above all, O pure one, Who became man for the salvation and deliverance of the faithful.

*Another. Heirmos:*
The angel made the furnace shed dew for the holy children, but the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tyrant to cry out: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Let us hymn the theologian as the thunder resounding unto all the ends of the earth, by which every hearing truly thunderstruck is lifted up from the earth, and Christ the Creator of all is magnified.

*Troparion:*
The sightly beauty of thy house enlightens every mind; wherein ever gathering together we sing in divine manner to the Creator of all, and faithfully praise thee as our protector.

*Troparion:*
Knowing thee as a star shining brightly unto all, we pray, O disciple of Christ: that we may be enlightened by thy radiant beams, being delivered from the darkness of passions and manifold temptations by thy mediation.

*Theotokion:*
We bless thee, O all-immaculate one, who didst bear the blessed Lord, Who by divine blessings broke the curse of human nature, and renewed us who had grown old through corruption.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The fiery furnace in Babylon of old divided its actions by the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, but moistening the faithful with dew, who sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Emulate good things, having departed from evil ones, by care for divine deeds, O my soul, having the Mother of God praying for thee, the unashamed protectress of all, as she is merciful and full of love for mankind.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst loose mankind from the bonds of the ancient condemnation, O Mother of God. Therefore I pray thee: loose every wicked bond of my heart, binding me, O most pure one, with the divine love of the Creator.

*Troparion:*
Having given birth to the Ray of the Father's glory, O Birthgiver of God, make clear my heart, which grieves in the dishonor of transgressions, and show me forth as a partaker of the everlasting glory, that with faith I may glorify thee.

*Troparion:*
The true Sun of righteousness appeared unto us from thee, O Mother of God, Who was incarnate and enlightens all things with the rays of the Godhead: Whom we hymn with songs.

*Another. The same Heirmos:*

*Troparion:*
As a bright lightning traversing the world thou didst appear to the universe, O blessed one: by the brightness of purity, the radiance of virginity, and the dogmas of piety enlightening the world, O beloved of Christ God.

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed body, and soul, and mind, thou didst preach the heavenly Gospel of Christ; and having become a co-dweller with the angels in the heavens, thou dost now cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
A luminous pillar and a divine offering of the heavenly temple wast thou, and a throne of perception, and a vessel of wisdom, an instrument of theology singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
That Thou mightest destroy the first curse and the deathly condemnation of the ancestral mother of old, O Word of God, Thou wast born of the Virgin Mother of God, granting indestructible immortality unto all.

*Another. Heirmos:*
From the flame Thou didst shed dew for the holy ones, and with water Thou didst burn up the sacrifice of the righteous man; for Thou dost accomplish all things, O Christ, simply by willing them: Thee do we supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Troparion:*
With an eloquent tongue, O blessed one, thou didst proclaim the good tidings, and all who were dead through malice thou didst catch alive, receiving thy sacred preaching; therefore we honor thee as an initiate of ineffable mysteries.

*Troparion:*
Thy divine church was shown forth as another paradise, gladdening the souls of all with miracles like flowers, O apostle, and driving away the foul stench of passions.

*Troparion:*
O God, my God, give ear unto me, and deliver me from the enemies who daily attack me and crush my humble heart, having Thy divine disciple praying unto Thee.

*Theotokion:*
Entreat Jesus the Savior, Whom thou didst incarnate of thy pure blood, O woman full of divine grace, to have mercy upon us thy servants, and to take us away from eternal torment.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, having become incarnate of the Virgin, has appeared unto us,[^2200] to enlighten those in darkness, to gather the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Birthgiver of God do we magnify.

*Troparion:*
Adam, having tasted of the tree the food that was not fitting, bitterly found death from the tree; but Thy Son, O most pure one, nailed upon the Tree, poured forth the sweetness of immortality: therefore we honor thee.

*Troparion:*
Having beyond word given birth to the King of kings, Christ and Lord, Who destroyed the kingdoms of Hades: fervently entreat Him, O Maiden, to make all who honor thee worthy of the heavenly Kingdom.

*Troparion:*
Show goodness, O Sovereign Lady, unto my humble heart, afflicted and submerged by pleasures, as thou didst give birth to the Good One, and art thyself all-good: and lead me unto the good gates of repentance.

*Troparion:*
Having become dead upon the Cross, by divine power Thou didst put the serpent to death. Therefore I cry unto Thee: have mercy, O Word, and make alive my soul which is deadened by wicked deeds, through the prayers of her who bore Thee.

*Another. The same Heirmos:*

*Troparion:*
Now not in riddles, but face to face, the torrent of delight thou wast accounted worthy to behold the torrent of delight, and the river of peace, and the fountain of immortality: being now watered by which, thou dost enjoy divinization.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst ask to receive an earthly seat from Christ, but He grants thee His own breast: reclining upon which, O theologian, thou wast enriched with a firm and abiding good session, O adornment of the apostles.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst extinguish the godless error of Hellenic wisdom, O wise one, proclaiming: *"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and truly the Word was God; by Whom all things were made, both visible and invisible."*

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast found as the morning dawn in the night of life, flashing with the rays of virginity, having shown forth unto us the Dayspring of the spiritual Sun of righteousness, O all-venerable Mother of God.

*Another. Heirmos:*
It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word incarnate appeared unto men: Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
The Lord of hours and times, and the Redeemer, in the middle of the day hung upon the Cross, and unto thee as a virgin, O blessed one, He committed the Ever-Virgin, giving thee inextinguishable glory to magnify thee.

*Troparion:*
Being with the heavenly divine hosts, and crying aloud with them the divine hymnody: save by thy honorable intercessions those who sing in thy holy house and praise the All-Good One, O apostle of Christ.

*Troparion:*
Save us who ask of thee with faith from every affliction, O blessed theologian: directing our steps unto the Lord by the Spirit, and guide us into the way of peace, of the commandments of the Almighty.

*Theotokion:*
A voice of thanksgiving do we offer brightly unto the Mother of God, and we cry aloud: Rejoice, O most exalted throne of God; rejoice, O cloud of light; rejoice, O paradise, through whom we have been accounted worthy of the delight of paradise!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit" (Дх҃омъ):*
As virginal in soul and body, O blessed one, the Word chose thee, O virgin theologian, and showed thee forth as a marvelous scribe and servant of His Godhead: who also didst pass away from the earth, not dead, but alive in God, and abiding immortal.

*Glory..., Podoben: "Give Ear, Ye Women" (Же́ны оу҆слы́шите):*[^2201]
Having become a Son of Thunder, thou didst theologize unto men that the Word was in the beginning, O Apostle John; for having faithfully reclined upon the breast of thy Master, and having drawn forth from thence the streams of theology, thou dost water all creation.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Standing by the Cross of thy Son and God, O all-pure one, with the virgin disciple, thou didst hear the Creator say: Behold, thy son; and to the disciple He says: Behold, thy mother. With whom we all hymn thee, O Virgin Birthgiver of God.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 8. Podoben: "O Most Marvelous Wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

*Sticheron 1:*
O blessed John, all-wise one, through the fiery warmth of the love of Christ thou wast loved more than all the disciples by the all-seeing Word, Who judges the whole universe with measures of righteousness; having been illumined with the beauties of purity and virginity, both in body and in thoughts, O divinely blessed one.

*Sticheron 2:*
Blossom of virginity, pleasant dwelling of venerable virtues, instrument of wisdom, temple of the Spirit, light-bearing mouth of grace, most radiant Tserkovne Oko: let us now praise the all-venerable John with spiritual songs as a servant of Christ.

*Sticheron 3:*
Having reclined upon the breast, thou didst draw forth the waters of theology, of wisdom, and didst give drink unto the world, O most divinely excellent John; through knowledge of the Trinity thou didst dry up the sea of godlessness, having become a pillar and an animate cloud, guiding us unto the heavenly inheritance.

*Sticheron 4:*[^2202]
O pure and divine one: the fountain of good things, the unshakable Kingdom, eternal life, and ineffable joy, and the enjoyment of divine vision, and the bountiful gifts of Christ, surpassing the mind and human comprehension: proclaiming them in the Gospel to the world, O Son of Thunder, thou didst strike it with awe!

*Glory..., Tone 8. Idiomelon:*
O evangelist John, equal of the angels, virgin, theologian, taught of God: in Orthodox manner thou didst preach to the world the all-pure side that poured forth blood and water, through which we find eternal life for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
O Sovereign Lady, accept the prayers of thy servants...

*Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the apostle. Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion: All beyond comprehension... Litanies, and the Dismissal. And we sing the idiomelon sticheron of the saint, which the ecclesiarch desires. And the priest goes forth with the censer, a lamp-bearer going before him* bearer going before him, and he censes the icon of the holy apostle on the analogion; and having given back the censer, he stands on the right side of the analogion. And the hegumen comes to the analogion, makes two prostrations, and kisses the icon of the holy apostle. And after kissing it, he makes one prostration, and having taken the brush arranged for this, he anoints himself from the lamp with the holy oil crosswise upon his forehead. And the brethren likewise kiss the icon of the saint. And the hegumen anoints the priest and the rest of the brethren with the holy oil. After the anointing with the holy oil we sing the First Hour. At the First Hour, the Troparion and Kontakion of the apostle. And the final dismissal takes place. In this manner the anointing always takes place, and on all feasts of great saints on which vigils are kept.

*Note: At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes: from the Canon of Tone 2, Ode 3, on 4; and of Tone 8, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance, the Troparion of the temple of Christ, and of the Birthgiver of God, and of the apostle; but the troparia and kontakia of temples of the saints are not said. After this, the Kontakion of the temple of Christ; then Glory..., the Kontakion of the apostle; Both now..., of the temple of the Birthgiver of God. But if there be no temple of the Birthgiver of God: Both now..., of the temple of Christ. But if there be neither temple of Christ nor of the Birthgiver of God, we say the troparia thus: Troparion of the apostle; Glory..., his Kontakion; Both now..., Protection of Christians (*Предста́тельство хрїстїа́нъ*)... Prokeimenon, Tone 8: Into all the earth [His sound has gone forth] [LXX Ps. 18:4];*[^2203] *Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God [LXX Ps. 18:1].*[^2204] *The Apostle: From the General Epistle of John, Pericope 73 from the midpoint [1 John 4:12–19]: "Beloved, no one has seen God..." Alleluia, Tone 1: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord [LXX Ps. 88:5];*[^2205] *Verse: God is glorified in the council of the saints [LXX Ps. 88:7].*[^2206] *Gospel from John, Pericope 64 [John 19:25–27, 21:24–25]: "There stood by the Cross of Jesus..." Communion Verse: Into all the earth [His sound has gone forth] [LXX Ps. 18:4].*

## The Same Month, on the 27th Day. The Holy Martyr Callistratus, and His Companions

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 8. Podoben: "O Most Marvelous Wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

*Sticheron 1:*
O martyr and sufferer Callistratus, having enlightened thy mind with the light of piety, thou didst walk without turning aside on the path that leads unto the blessedness that is there, having overcome the wiles of the afflictions of the adversary. Therefore we praise thee, honoring thy sacred memory, O most blessed one.

*Sticheron 2:*
