O martyr Callistratus, wise in God, having been enriched with the Word of life, thou didst guide unto life those who previously were wretchedly dead through ignorance; who also, having zealously died, O glorious one, for the resurrection of us all, are believed most truly to live in Christ. With them remember us before the All-Good Lord.

*Sticheron 3:*[^2207]
O sacred martyr Gymnasius: for beheaded with the sword, by the flow of thy blood thou didst truly drown the deceitful Pharaoh, and now thou dost pour forth healings unto all that run with faith unto thy temple, and praise thy struggles therein, and celebrate thy venerable memory, O blessed one.

*Glory..., Tone 4. By Byzantios:*
Before Thy precious Cross, death was fearful unto men; but after Thy glorious Passion, man became fearful unto death. Thus was the passion-bearer made strong; thus did he make void all the enemy's power. By his prayers, O Christ, save our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "As One Valiant Among Martyrs" (Ꙗ́кѡ до́бля):*
When she saw Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the Tree, the Ewe-lamb who gave birth to Thee wept aloud, and maternally cried out unto Thee: O my most longed-for Son, how art Thou suspended upon the Tree of the Cross, O longsuffering One? How were Thy hands and Thy feet, O Word, nailed by lawless men, and how didst Thou pour forth Thy blood, O Master?

*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for possessing Thy strength for possessing Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless insolence of demons: by their prayers, save our souls.

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos; and the canon of the saints on 4. By Joseph. Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us send up a song, ye people, unto our marvelous God, Who delivered Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying: Let us sing unto Thee, the only Master.

*Troparion 1:*
Having walked without turning aside on the path of suffering, thou wast a way unto those who had strayed, leading them, O blessed one, unto divine repose. Therefore having gathered together, in faith we praise thee, Callistratus.

*Troparion 2:*
Having shone forth like a most radiant star, thou didst illuminate the Church of Christ with the light of the knowledge of God; and having driven away the darkness of ignorance, O martyr, thou didst cast down the deceitful temples.

*Troparion 3:*
Having patiently endured every wounding, O Callistratus, thou didst not refuse to die for the Life of all; therefore rejoicing thou hast passed over unto immortal rest, making merry with the angelic choirs.

*Troparion 4:*
A coal of the divine Spirit, the sacred Gymnasius was shown forth inflamed by fire, and he burned up the filth of deceit; and by miracles he bedews those burned by the flame of the passions.

*Theotokion:*
Alone among women thou dost bear One of the Trinity, supernaturally, O all-immaculate one, having known no man; therefore we glorify thee, for He Who was born of thee is beyond all cause and reason.[^2208]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou Who by Thy word didst establish the heavens, and didst found the earth upon many waters: establish me unto the singing of Thy praise, O Lord.

*Troparion 1:*
Not having sacrificed at all unto delusive gods, thou wast offered as a pure sacrifice unto the God of all, Who was sacrificed for us, O martyr and passion-bearer Callistratus.

*Troparion 2:*
Adorned with a purple robe dyed truly from thy sacred blood, O martyr, thou dost stand crown-bearing before the King of ages, O blessed one.

*Troparion 3:*
The enemy was shown forth stripped naked by thy divine glory and that of the sufferers with thee, who were clothed from on high, O valiant-minded martyr Gymnasius.

*Theotokion:*
Fervently make supplication unto thy Son, O Virgin, that He may save us from the afflictions that encompass us, and from eternal torment.

*Kontakion, Tone 4. Podoben:*

*Podoben: "Thou Hast Appeared Today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ):*
Celebrating every labor today, O holy ones, the Church mystically praises you who suffered for her, O divine martyrs, fair-victorious and all-wise.

*Then the Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The Word Co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*
Let us praise the sufferings of Callistratus, let us hymn the pains of Gymnasius; let us, the faithful, call blessed in love those who suffered patiently with them, and let us cry out unto them: O armor-bearers of piety, ask that peace and great mercy be granted unto us.

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*
Quickly heal the grievous passions of my soul and the infirmities of my flesh, stop the distractions of my mind, O all-immaculate one, and vouchsafe that in tranquility of thought I may still offer pure prayers unto the King of all, and ask remission of transgressions.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee, O Christ, hanging willingly upon the Cross between thieves, Thy Mother, tearing her maternal heart, cried aloud: O sinless Son, how art Thou unjustly crucified upon the Cross as an evildoer, desiring as the All-Good One to bring the human race to life?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead.

*Troparion 1:*
Like a most excellent general, O martyr, having drawn up in battle against the persecutor, thou didst capture for divine life those whom he previously held captive.

*Troparion 2:*
With showers of thy words thou didst water hearts, and didst guide them unto the water of life eternal, O ever-memorable sufferer of the Lord.

*Troparion 3:*
Like a ram is the ever-memorable Callistratus slaughtered, having as lambs slaughtered before him his strong and most zealous armor-bearers.

*Troparion 4:*
Having ripened like a vine, O martyr Gymnasius, through the word of thy suffering the cluster blossomed forth, pouring out the wine of piety.

*Theotokion:*
Purify my heart, defiled by passions, O Maiden, and make it a receptacle of pure and divine illuminations.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou Who from the night of ignorance didst enlighten the ends of the earth with the knowledge of God: enlighten me with the dawn of Thy love for mankind, O Lord.

*Troparion 1:*
Having zealously loved Christ our God, O martyr, thou didst suffer and destroy the powerless power of the enemy.

*Troparion 2:*[^2209]
With divine praise of warriors thou wast shown forth as the head, O Callistratus; thou wast numbered among the hosts of angels, O martyr, rejoicing.

*Troparion 3:*
Adorned with the glory of the martyrs' brightness, O Gymnasius, rejoicing thou hast now passed over unto the angelic splendors.

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast shown forth as the orient of the Sun of righteousness, O all-immaculate one: entreat Him to save those who in purity glorify thee.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation.

*Troparion 1:*
Thou didst crush the jaws of the invisible lions, O wise one, and those who were once the food of the enemy thou didst show forth as children of God and partakers of heavenly delight, O martyr Callistratus.

*Troparion 2:*
Beautifying in God the divine word, those who previously wretchedly served soulless gods thou didst reveal as divine, having suffered with them, O most glorious Callistratus.

*Troparion 3:*
Having bowed your necks unto Christ, O martyrs, ye received slaughter, and were offered as perfect sacrifices unto God, and adorned the Church of the firstborn.

*Theotokion:*
Cleanse my mind and enlighten my heart, O holy Mother of God, and deliver me from the cruel evils that beset me, that I may glorify thee, O Birthgiver of God, Ever-Virgin.

*Kontakion, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who Wast Lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йся на крⷭ҇тъ):*
Having endured manifold wounds and received crowns from God: pray unto Christ for us who celebrate your all-festive memory, O most great Callistratus with those who suffered with thee, O blessed ones, that He may bring peace unto the flock and the people; for He is the strengthening of the faithful.

*Ikos:*
Beholding the shrine of thy relics, O Callistratus, I sing and magnify the pains and sufferings which thou didst endure, suffering; therefore I pray thee, make Christ thy Master of the contest merciful unto me also, to give me a word by grace, that I may be able to praise thy struggles: for no one among men can theologically declare thy valiances, how thou didst enter manly into the judgment hall and refute the earthly creeping thoughts of the torturers. Christ is the strengthening of the faithful.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The children coming from Judea in Babylon of old, by faith in the Trinity trampled down the furnace flame, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Troparion 1:*
Having been purified like gold by the fire of tortures, thou wast shown forth as a sign of the sufferings of Christ, and now thou art laid up among divine treasures, O glorious one, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Troparion 2:*
Strengthened by sufferings, thou wast shown forth as an unsheathed sword, O all-blessed one, cutting down the legions of invisible demons, and crying, O Callistratus: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Troparion 3:*
Mighty wast thou shown forth against impiety, O martyr Callistratus, by the might of the Trinity; enlightened now by Whose radiances, thou dost cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Troparion 4:*
Having loved Christ with a firm mind, O martyr Gymnasius, thou wast slaughtered together with all thy fellow-zealots, singing in thanksgiving, O divinely inspired one: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Theotokion:*
Entreat Him Who was incarnate of thee beyond mind and word, O woman full of divine grace, that they may be saved who honor thee with love and cry in harmony: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The God-proclaiming children in the furnace, trampling down the flame together with the fire, sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.

*Troparion 1:*
Having uprooted the thorns of deceit, thou wast shown forth as a most beautiful garden of paradise, O martyr, bearing the fruits of piety by divine grace.

*Troparion 2:*[^2210]
Looking unto future hopes in perfect trust, thou didst train thyself for struggles, and having conquered lawfully, thou wast crowned, O Callistratus.

*Troparion 3:*
Having acquired healing from thy temple, those who come with piety are delivered from grievous afflictions, praising thee with faith, O glorious Gymnasius.

*Theotokion:*
As thou art higher than all creatures, O Maiden full of divine grace, make my mind higher than the scandals of the deceiver, O all-immaculate one.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Every ear was terrified at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High of His own will came down even unto the flesh, having become man from the virginal womb. Therefore we, the faithful, magnify the all-pure Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion 1:*

...the shrine of thy relics pours forth healing unto all that need it, O martyr Callistratus, and truly stays incurable passions, and drives away the darkness of evil spirits by the operation, power, and grace of the divine Spirit.

*Troparion 2:*
Ye appeared, O martyrs of Christ, like a divinely woven chain, bound to one another by grace, ascending unto the heights, and sanctifying the earth with the pouring out of blood. Therefore in faith we celebrate your memory, rejoicing.

*Troparion 3:*
Thou didst openly receive an unfading crown, and eternal glory and gladness, and joy having no end, and the heavenly Kingdom, O Callistratus wise in God, together with those who suffered with thee; with them remember us before the Lord.

*Troparion 4:*
The divine memory of the wise Callistratus and of Gymnasius today, and of those who suffered with them, having shone forth more than the sun with radiant splendors, enlightens the ends of the earth. By their prayers, O Christ, deliver us from condemnation.

*Theotokion:*
With joyful mind we cry unto thee the voice of Gabriel: Rejoice, O joy of the faithful! Rejoice, golden lampstand, and table, mountain, and spiritual gate! Rejoice, divine chariot of Christ the King! Rejoice, loosening of the curse, O all-blessed one!

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "Give Ear, Ye Women" (Же́ны оу҆слы́шите):*
O wonder, how did men of clay appear golden by nature? For neither fire, nor sword, nor the teeth of wild beasts, nor torments, nor wounds destroyed them; but having in the flesh cast down the bodiless foe, they pray unto the Lord for us.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, palace of God! Rejoice, overshadowing mountain! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, unburnt bush! Rejoice, throne of glory! Rejoice, all-golden jar! Rejoice, all-radiant lampstand! Rejoice, light cloud, O Virgin Mother Mary!

*The same month, on the 28th day. Our Venerable Father and Confessor Chariton:*

*At Vespers, we chant the Kathisma: "Blessed is the man..."*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Hast Given a Sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

*Sticheron 1:*
The bodily passions thou didst wither by abstinence, and with diligent supplication, by torrents of tears, thou didst drown the deceitful serpent, O blessed one; and thou didst exceedingly well-please God, O venerable Chariton; therefore Jesus, the Lover of mankind and Savior of our souls, adorned thee with heavenly gifts.

*Sticheron 2:*
With the sweat of fasting thou didst extinguish the coals of the passions, O ever-memorable one, being brought near unto fire by wounds and afflictions, having confessed before lawless tormentors the emptying of the incarnate Word; and thou wast a witness, adorned with the wounds of manifold torments, O God-bearing and most wealthy Chariton.

*Sticheron 3:*
Into wildernesses and mountains thou didst ever withdraw thyself, preserving thy soul spotless, O most sacred one, and wast shown forth as a house of the Trinity, O Chariton; by Whose power thou didst build sacred houses, O blessed one, and sheepfolds for the saving establishment of monks who honor thy holy memory, O ever-memorable one.

*Glory..., Tone 4. By John the Monk:*
O God-bearing Chariton, even after death thou dost live in the heavens in Christ, for Whose sake thou didst crucify thyself unto the world. For being outside the flesh and the world, thou didst truly live above visible things; for thou didst not live unto thyself, but rather Christ our God lived in thee: entreat Him that our souls may be saved.

*Both now, Theotokion / Dogmatikon: "Who for Thy sake..." (И҆́же тебѐ ра́ди):*

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*

*Three Readings:*

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon [Wisdom 5:16–6:3]:*[^2211]
The righteous live unto the ages, and in the Lord is their reward, and the care of them is with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of majesty, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord; for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He shield them. He shall take His zeal for armor, and shall arm the creature for the repulse of enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate and shall put on judgment without hypocrisy as a helmet; He shall take holiness as an invincible shield; and He shall sharpen severe wrath for a weapon, and the world shall fight with Him against the senseless. Right-aiming shafts of lightning shall go forth, and as from a well-drawn bow of the clouds they shall fly to the mark. And from a stony wrath hail shall fall in full measure; the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall drown them relentlessly. A spirit of power shall stand up against them, and like a whirlwind shall scatter them, and lawlessness shall make the whole earth desolate, and evil-doing shall overturn the thrones of the mighty. Give ear therefore, O kings, and understand; learn, ye judges of the ends of the earth! Give ear, ye that rule multitudes, and take pride in crowds of nations! For dominion is given unto you from the Lord, and power from the Most High.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon [Wisdom 3:1–9]:*[^2212]
The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was accounted an affliction, and their going from us destruction; but they are in peace. For though in the sight of men they be punished, their hope is full of immortality. And having been a little chastened, they shall be greatly benefited; for God tested them, and found them worthy of Himself. Like gold in a furnace He tested them, and as a whole burnt-offering sacrifice He accepted them. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and like sparks through stubble shall they run. They shall judge nations, and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord shall reign over them unto the ages. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth, and the faithful in love shall abide with Him; for grace and mercy are upon His holy ones, and visitation upon His elect.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon [Wisdom 4:7–15]:*[^2213]
Though the righteous happen to die early, he shall be in rest. For honorable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor is it measured by number of years; but wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is the stature of old age. Being well-pleasing unto God, he was beloved, and living among sinners he was translated. He was taken away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul. For the bewitching of wickedness darkens good things, and the roving of lust undermines the simple mind. Having been perfected in a short time, he fulfilled long years; for his soul was pleasing unto the Lord; therefore hastened He to take him away from the midst of wickedness. But the people saw and understood not, neither laying this up in their thought: that grace and mercy are in His holy ones, and visitation among His elect.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Venerable One, Tone 4, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*

O most praised Chariton, thou didst offer up Thy life through care for the virtues; for with hymnody and orthodox faith they praise Christ, obeying Thy teaching. Standing before Him, pray that we may be established in the peace of the Divine Spirit.

*Verse:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^2214]

O God-inspired Chariton, Thy life indeed appeared unto those on earth as equal to the angels; and unto the heavenly hosts Thy confession was offered as a sweet-smelling sacrifice and fragrant incense. And now pray, that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

*Verse:* Blessed is the man that fears the Lord; in His commandments he shall greatly delight.[^2215]

O most wealthy Chariton, thou wast the conqueror of passions, and thou didst overcome the robbers; rejoicing in choir with the crown-bearers, O blessed one, remember all who celebrate thy memory: pray now unto Christ, that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

*Glory, Tone 8:*

We honor thee, our father Chariton, as the instructor of multitudes of monks; for by thy path we have truly learned to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having labored for Christ, and having exposed the power of the enemy. Companion of angels, fellow-partaker with the venerable and the righteous: with them pray unto the Lord, that our souls may be shown mercy.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

*O unwedded Virgin (Безневѣ́стная дѣ́во), or:*[^2216]

*Troparion, Tone 8:*

With the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and with sighs from the depths thou didst bear fruit for thy labors an hundredfold, and didst become a luminary to the universe, shining with miracles, O Chariton our father: pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

*Thou Who for our sake wast born (И҆́же на́съ ра́ди рожде́йся):*

*At Matins, the troparion twice; Glory, and now, Theotokion.*

*After the 1st Kathisma: Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йся):*

Having disdained the enjoyment of earthly and corruptible things, thou didst follow Christ, and didst love desert dwelling above the beauty of the world and temporal sweetness; whence thou wast vouchsafed both martyrdom and to be united with the ranks of fasters: with them pray that thy servants may be saved. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

He Who sits upon the cherubic throne, and abides in the Father's bosom, sits as upon His holy throne in thy womb, O Sovereign Lady; God, having become incarnate, has truly reigned over all the nations, and with understanding we now sing unto Him: implore Him that thy servants may be saved.

*After the 2nd Kathisma: Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Guiding unto wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Emulating in fasting the manner of John the Baptist and the virtues of Elijah the Tishbite, thou didst live as one bodiless, glorifying with the angels the Trinity without beginning, and overcoming the assaults of the robbers with courage; therefore also in suffering thou didst contend valiantly, worshipping Christ's divine incarnation with His divinity, O blessed Chariton: pray unto Christ God that remission of sins be granted unto those who honor thy holy memory with love. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

As a virgin and unique among women, who didst bear God in the flesh without seed, all we human generations call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead made its dwelling in thee, and thou sucklest the Creator and Lord as an infant; therefore both the angelic and the human race worthily glorify thy all-holy birthgiving, and with one accord cry out unto thee: pray unto Christ God that remission of transgressions be granted unto those who worthily sing thy glory.

*After the Polyeleos: Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йся):*

Having disdained the enjoyment of earthly and corruptible things, thou didst follow Christ, and didst love desert dwelling above the beauty of the world and temporal sweetness; whence thou wast vouchsafed both martyrdom and to be united with the ranks of fasters: with them pray that thy servants may be saved. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

Under thy divine and good protection, O Mother of God, I the humble one flee, falling down in prayer: have mercy, O most pure one, for my sins have exceeded my head, and I fear torments, O Sovereign Lady, and tremble: make supplication, O pure one, unto thy Son, to deliver me from them.

*Gradual Antiphon, the first antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^2217]

*Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?[^2218]

*Let every breath:*

*The Gospel according to Matthew, zachalo 10 [Matt. 4:25–5:12]:*[^2219]

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*

Venerable father, into all the earth went out the sound of thy achievements; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors. Thou didst destroy the hosts of demons and didst attain unto the ranks of angels, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness toward Christ God, entreat peace for our souls.

*Canon of the Theotokos, with the Heirmos, to 6; and of the Venerable One to 8.*

*Canon of the Theotokos, whose acrostic is: "I sing praise unto the life-bearing Maiden."[^2220] Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Traversing the untrodden, unaccustomed sea-path with unwetted feet, the chosen Israel cried aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is glorified.

*Troparia:*

The immaterial ladder of old, and the pathway of the sea that strangely solidified, prefigured thy birthgiving, O pure one, which we all hymn: For He is glorified.

The Power of the Most High, the perfect Hypostasis, the Wisdom of God, having become incarnate from thee, O most pure one, has communicated Himself unto men: For He is glorified.

The Sun of righteousness, O pure one, passed through the impassable door of thy sealed womb, and shone forth unto the world: For He is glorified.

*Canon of the Saint.*

*A composition of John the Monk.*

*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Having traversed the deep of the Red Sea on foot with unwetted steps, Israel of old conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness through the hands of Moses stretched out crosswise.

*Troparia:*

Having sailed across the deep of the sea of passions with the life-bearing weapon of the Cross, O blessed one, thou didst drown the evil, noetic Pharaoh by divine power.

Offered unto the Lord from thy mother's swaddling bands, O blessed one, before the tribunal of the tormentor thou didst wisely proclaim Christ in a godly manner; for in the manner of Moses thou didst cast down the insolence of the adversaries.

Leaving behind the Egypt of delusion, O venerable Chariton, and having become a citizen of the desert, thou didst converse purely with the Honored One, and didst receive the heavenly inheritance.

*Theotokion:*

Seedlessly, by the Father's will, from the Divine Spirit thou didst conceive the Son of God, and in the flesh didst bear Him Who is without mother from the Father, and for our sake without father from thee.

*Katavasia: I shall open my mouth.*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

The bow of the mighty is broken by Thy strength, O Christ, and the weak are girded with power.

*Troparia:*

He Who is beyond all time, as Creator of the times, was voluntarily fashioned as an infant from thee, O Virgin.

Let us hymn the womb more spacious than the heavens, through which Adam rejoices and dwells in the heavens.

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying out: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and establishment.

*Troparia:*

Thy rational flock of disciples spiritually rejoices in thee, O venerable one, having been illumined by thy radiance.

The fleshly mind, as the cause of enmity against God, Thou didst subject unto the Spirit of life, O venerable Chariton.

In the manner of David thou didst cast down the alien Goliath, O venerable one, the power of the noetic foe, with the armor of the Spirit.[^2221]

*Theotokion:*

Thou alone among those on earth, beyond nature, wast the Mediatress of good things, O Mother of God; therefore unto thee we cry: Rejoice!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Guiding unto wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Having been tested by the pains of suffering, and established by the trials of fasting, thou didst shine forth brighter than gold in piety, and wast a pure receptacle of the Spirit: thou didst dispel the darkness of evil spirits; therefore, having gathered multitudes of monastics, thou wast their shepherd and a most radiant luminary, O blessed Chariton: pray unto Christ God that remission of sins be granted unto those who honor thy holy memory with love. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

Falling into manifold temptations from enemies visible and invisible, and held fast by the tempest of my countless sins, unto thy goodness do I run, O pure one, as unto my fervent protection and shelter. Therefore, O most pure one, pray diligently unto Him Who was incarnate from thee without seed on behalf of all thy servants who unceasingly pray unto thee, O most pure Mother of God: beseeching Him ever to grant remission of sins unto those who worthily sing thy glory.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

I have heard, O Lord, of Thy glorious dispensation, and I have glorified, O Lover of mankind, Thine incomprehensible power.

*Troparia:*

Lo, the divine mountain of the house of the Lord is exalted higher than the powers, appearing clearly as the Mother of God.

Outside the laws of nature, thou alone, O Virgin, didst give birth unto Him Who rules over creation: thou wast vouchsafed the divine calling.

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

For the sake of love of Thine image, O Compassionate One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away; for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and my praise.

*Troparia:*

Rejoicing in the Lord as a victor, the venerable one cried aloud against the bodiless enemies: My God is my strength and my Lord!

The graces crowned thee, O Chariton, with the martyr's crown of the kingdom of Christ, for thou didst uproot the drunkenness of delusion, O blessed one.

Teaching before thy repose, O Chariton, having put pleasures to death by the pains of abstinence: thou wast clothed with life-bearing mortification, O venerable one.

*Theotokion:*

Ineffably was thy birthgiving shown forth, O Mother of God, sole pure and blessed one; therefore falling down before thee, we cry aloud: Rejoice!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

The live coal shown unto Isaiah shone forth as a sun from the virginal womb, granting the illumination of divine knowledge unto those wandering in darkness.[^2222]

*Troparia:*

O clouds, drop down the sweetness of gladness unto those upon earth; for a child is given: the Son before the ages, our God incarnate from the Virgin.[^2223]

A light has shone forth unto my life and flesh, and has destroyed the infirmity of sin: the Most High has become incarnate at last from the Virgin without seed.

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

Thou, O Lord, hast come into the world as my Light: a holy Light turning from the gloom of ignorance those who hymn Thee in faith.

*Troparia:*

Thou, O venerable one, hast brightly appeared as an undefiled mirror of the Light of the illumination from on high, O all-blessed Chariton.

Thou shinest with twofold graces, O venerable one, for thou wast piously illumined by the wounds of suffering and by the pains of fasting.

Thou wast shown to be a physician of souls, O venerable one, having sought divine wisdom from an early age, O all-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*

Thee do we set forth as an invincible weapon against the enemies; thee as the defense and hope of our salvation have we acquired thee, O Bride of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Having heard the voice of suppliant words from an afflicted soul, O Master, deliver me from evil things; for Thou alone art the Author of our salvation.

*Troparia:*

Human nature, which was enslaved to sin, obtained freedom through thee, O pure Sovereign Lady; for thy Son is slain as a Lamb for all.

We all cry aloud unto thee, the true Mother of God: Deliver thy servants who have angered God; for thou alone hast boldness toward thy Son.

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries out unto Thee, having been cleansed from demonic blood by the blood which flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.

*Troparia:*

Not having laid sand, but Christ as the foundation, thou didst build virtue more precious than gold, O father; and thou didst become a house of the Most Holy Trinity.[^2224]

The serpent is known as the instrument of malice, but defeated by thy pleasing deeds to God, O God-bearer Chariton, he avenged the unjust through righteous Providence.[^2225]

Nothing separated thee from the love of Christ: neither thy body being wounded, nor the sentence of death threatening thee; in divine union thou didst delight, O blessed one.[^2226]

*Theotokion:*

O wonder newest of all wonders! For the Virgin, having conceived without knowing man Him Who upholds all things by His word, contained Him within her womb without constraint.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "In prayers" (Въ мл҃твахъ):*

Delighting in abstinence, O godly-wise one, and having bridled the lusts of thy flesh, thou wast shown to increase through faith, and didst blossom forth as a tree of life in the midst of paradise, O all-blessed and most sacred Chariton.

*Ikos:*

Open my mouth, O blessed servant of the Trinity, by thy acceptable prayers, standing before God, O all-glorious venerable-martyr, that I may sing of thy divine life and worthily proclaim thy virtues, which thou didst accomplish on earth with fervent love. For thou wast a most valiant confessor, and didst direct thy abstinence by faith, having loved vigilance and purity, O all-blessed and most sacred Chariton.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

In the furnace the Abrahamic youths of old, being most wise in philosophy, for possessing acceptable souls, theologizing with their lips, sang O pre-divine God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou.

*Troparia:*

Jacob indeed beheld God in the night as in a riddle; but incarnate from thee, He appeared in radiance unto those who sing: O pre-divine God of our fathers, Thou art supremely praised![^2227]

Foreshowing the signs of the ineffable union in thee, He wrestled with Jacob, through which He was voluntarily united unto men, O pure one: O pre-divine God of our fathers, Thou art supremely praised![^2228]

Abominable is he who does not proclaim Thee, the Son of the Virgin, to be of the one Godhead of the Trinity, crying aloud with unwavering mind and tongue: O pre-divine God of our fathers, Thou art supremely praised!

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, consumed more by love of piety than by flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord.

*Troparia:*

Emulating with zeal for piety those Abrahamic youths in the furnace, thou didst trample down the tormentor's command, O God-bearer, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord my God!

As in the furnace of trials from divine inflammation, cooling grace from heaven visited thee, O venerable one, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord my God!

As one wounded with the divine love of the Trinity, thou didst offer unto It spiritual folds equal in number singing: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*

Rejoice, O consecrated and divine dwelling of the Most High; for through thee joy was given, O Mother of God, unto those who cry: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Disregarding the golden image, the thrice-blessed youths, having beheld the immutable and living image of God, sang in the midst of the fire: Let all creation, having been brought into being, hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages.[^2229]

*Troparia:*

He Who is incomparable in goodness and power was seen upon earth through thee and lived among men; hymning Him, all we faithful cry: Let all creation, having been brought into being, hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Truly proclaiming thee pure, we glorify thee, O Mother of God; for thou didst bear One of the Trinity incarnate, unto Whom with the Father and the Spirit we all sing Let all creation hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages.

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

Stretching out his hands, Daniel shut the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2230]

*Troparia:*

Though thy breast was unjustly burned with fire, O venerable one, thou didst quench deception; and thou thyself didst remain unconsumed through the operation of the Holy Spirit, and didst raise up people to sing in piety: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

Thou didst truly put on Christ, having put off the old man; and having exposed the ruler of the darkness of this world by the wounds of torture, O venerable one, thou didst cry with gladness: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2231]

Having truly been a disciple of Paul, O Chariton, thou didst follow his footsteps, O venerable one; and thou wast shown to be a teacher of monastics, having become a rule of virtue for all who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*

Thou alone in all generations wast shown to be the pure Virgin Mother of God; thou wast the all-immaculate dwelling-place of the Godhead, unburned by the fire of the unapproachable Light: therefore we all bless thee, O Mary, Bride of God.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Thou art all desire, Thou art all sweetness, O Word of God, Son of the Virgin, God of gods, Lord, most holy of the saints: therefore with her who bore Thee we all magnify Thee.

*Troparia:*

A rod of strength was given unto corruptible nature: the Word of God within thy womb, O pure one; and He raised up this nature that had slipped toward hades: therefore as the Mother of God, O all-pure one, we magnify thee.[^2232]

Receive mercifully, O Master, her whom Thou didst choose as an intercessor on our behalf, Thine own Mother, and all things shall be filled with Thy goodness: that we all may magnify Thee as our Benefactor.

*Another Heirmos [Saint's Canon]:*

A cornerstone was cut out from thee, an uncut mountain, O Virgin, without hands: Christ, Who joined together the parted natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God.[^2233]

*Troparia:*

Not even the grave, that mediator of oblivion, was able to cover thy virtues, O venerable Chariton; for thy perpetual memory has shone forth like the sun, which we worthily magnify.

Come, let us spiritually celebrate the yearly memorial, emulating his life in virtues and having emulated the God-bearer, let us cry out with him: We magnify thee thrice-blessed!

*Troparia:*

Always preserve those who are shaken by passions and manifestly engulfed by the tempest of sin, as thou hast boldness toward Christ, who piously magnify thee.

*Theotokion:*

Rejoice and be glad, O bride of the Great King, beholding brightly the beauty of thy Bridegroom, which shines brighter than gold and radiates above the sun.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ оу҆слы́шите):*

Having first been well tested by suffering, and secondly by fasting, and having finished the divine course, thou didst ascend into the heavens and standest before Christ, O our venerable father Chariton, praying for us who warmly hymn thee. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

Having given birth unto the ineffable joy, the Lord: make us, who truly honor thee, O most pure one, partakers of heavenly joy, and who from our soul cry out unto thee: Forget not thy servants, O blessed Mary!

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

The grace of the Spirit, having shone upon thee, O father Chariton, brightly illumined thee: whence thou didst diminish the night of passions and didst reach the day of dispassion; purely thou wast united unto the purest Light: dwelling wherein, O God-voiced one, forget not those who in faith hymn thy sacred memory. *Twice.*

Bearing the heavenly grace desired by thee, O Chariton, thou didst disregard earthly things; therefore, as one bodiless, thou didst choose the life of suffering, desiring to piously enjoy the torrent of eternal sweetness, O God-receiver; and with tears thou didst dry up the turbid spring of passions, O venerable one, and didst water the soul-nourishing ears of grain.

Thou didst worthily receive the grace of healings from divine grace, O Chariton: whence the deceit of evil spirits is cast down by thee, and fleeing the corruption of grievous illnesses, thou didst pass over, O venerable one. For like waters thou pourest forth thy streams of grace, watered by which, we hymn thy memory.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Venerable father, having heard the evangelical voice of the Lord, thou didst leave the world, accounting wealth and glory as nothing; therefore thou didst cry out unto all: Love God, and ye shall find grace eternal grace; prefer nothing to His love, that when He comes in His glory, ye may find rest with all the saints: by whose prayers, O Christ, preserve and save our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

We bless thee, O Virgin Theotokos, and we faithful glorify thee as is meet: city unshakable, rampart unconquerable, steadfast intercessor, and refuge of our souls.

*The Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon, Odes 3 and 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* The venerable ones shall boast in glory, and shall rejoice upon their beds.[^2234]

*Verse:* Sing unto the Lord a new song.[^2235]

*The Epistle to the Corinthians, zachalo 176 [2 Cor. 4:6–15]:*[^2236]

*Alleluia, Tone 6:* Blessed is the man that fears the Lord.[^2237]

*Verse:* His seed shall be mighty upon earth.[^2238]

*The Gospel according to Luke, zachalo 24 [Luke 6:17–23]:*[^2239]

*Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^2240]

*The same month, on the 29th day. Our Venerable Father Cyriacus the Anchorite:*[^2241]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you, O holy ones" (Что̀ вы̀ нарече́мъ ст҃і́и):*

Having conquered bodily passions with the bridle of abstinence, O wonderworking Cyriacus: for thou didst put on the radiant robe of dispassion, O father, and didst expose all the malice of him who of old stripped our forebears; and now thou dwellest in paradise, ever rejoicing: pray that our souls may be saved.

Bearing the Cross upon thy shoulders, thou didst follow Christ with an unwavering mind, disregarding worldly pleasures, O Cyriacus; and having mortified bodily passions with prolonged vigils and prayers, thou didst receive grace, O venerable one, to heal infirmities: pray that our souls may be saved.

Thou didst settle in the desert, O venerable one, making bitter herbs thy food, O Cyriacus, and by mortifying sensation, the spiritual sweets thou didst pluck up by the roots, O blessed one; therefore unceasing delight received thee after thy repose, who lived like the angels: pray that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, Tone 8:*

The multitudes of monks honor thee as an instructor, O our father Cyriacus: for by thy path we have learned truly to walk rightly. Blessed art thou, having labored for Christ, and having exposed the power of the enemy, companion of the angels, partaker with the venerable and the righteous: with them pray unto the Lord, that our souls may be shown mercy.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

When the ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb stretched out willingly upon the wood of the Cross, she cried out maternally, lamenting with weeping: O my Son, what strange sight is this? Thou Who givest life unto all as Lord, how art Thou put to death, O longsuffering One, granting resurrection unto the earthly? I glorify Thy great condescension, O my God!

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Venerable father, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of thy righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors; thou didst destroy the hosts of demons, and hast attained the ranks of angels, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness toward the Lord, ask peace for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*

Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who bore Thee cried aloud: What strange mystery is this that I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die upon the wood, suspended in the flesh, O Giver of life?

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

A dweller of the desert, and in the body an angel, and a wonderworker thou wast shown to be, O our God-bearing father Cyriacus; by fasting, vigil, and prayer having received heavenly gifts, thou healest the sick, and the souls of those who in faith run unto thee. Glory to Him Who gave thee strength! Glory to Him Who crowned thee! Glory to Him Who works healings through thee for all!

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos, and of the Saint on 6. A composition of Stephen, of which the acrostic is: Cyriacus, be an intercessor unto God. Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Let us send up a song, O ye peoples, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory singing and crying: Let us sing unto Thee, the only Master![^2242]

*Troparia:*

Grant me, O Christ, the glory of divine understanding and grace, worthily to hymn the venerable Cyriacus by his prayers: for Thou art beyond word the treasury of wise teachings.

Having accepted with good favor him who now brings a song unto thee, O blessed Cyriacus: pray that I may partake of the divine ray and radiance of Christ, and holy obtain salvation.

Firmly strengthened by the Master's power, and having followed His footsteps, O father, thou didst conquer the rulers of darkness, O all-blessed Cyriacus, and didst attain the highest rest.

Thou didst show an equal zeal on earth unto the bodiless hosts, having subjected all carnal wisdom unto the life-bearing Spirit: therefore in the heavenly courts thou now dancest with them, O God-bearer.

*Theotokion:*

With hymns let us faithful praise the all-pure Mary, the graced Mother of God, the divine protection, the calm haven, the salvation of all the faithful.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

There is none holy as the Lord, and none righteous as our God, Whom all creation hymns: there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord.[^2243]

*Troparia:*

Having unceasingly traversed the path of life, for from thy youth thou didst love thy Creator, O venerable one: Whom thirsting thou didst seek, like a hart running to the fountains of waters.[^2244]

Having received upon the tablet of thy heart thy writing, O God-proclaiming one, by the finger of the Spirit, like an ensouled book thou didst actively preserve the life-giving commandments of Christ.[^2245]

Having restrained thy belly in fasts, O venerable one, thou didst put to death gluttonous desires and carnal pleasure, having lived with purity, O father, throughout all thy life.

Having purified mind, body, and spirit, O thrice-blessed one, thou didst make of the bodily dwelling an understanding temple for the Trinity: and thou becamest a receptacle of the thrice-radiant Light.

*Theotokion:*

As a virgin thou didst give birth, knowing no man, and a virgin thou didst remain, unwedded Mother, Mary Theotokos: pray Christ our God that we may be saved.

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the champion leader" (Взбра́нной):*

As a steadfast champion and defender, the sacred Lavra honors thee and ever celebrates thy yearly memory; but as thou hast boldness toward the Lord, preserve us from attacking enemies, that we may cry: Rejoice, O thrice-blessed father!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-beginningless" (Собезнача́льное):*

With temperance thou didst adorn thy life, and having mortified thy limbs, thou didst conquer the assaults of the enemy, O venerable father; and a dweller of the desert, an intellectual luminary of the world, O Cyriacus, thou wast shown to be: therefore pray unto the Lord to show mercy upon our souls. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

Having found thee a haven and a wall, a refuge and a hope, a protection and a warm intercessor, O faithful, we run unto thee, and we cry out diligently, and we call in faith: Have mercy, O Mother of God, upon those who hope in thee, and deliver them from transgressions.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

By the Cross of thy Son, O woman graced of God, all the deception of idols was abolished, and the power of demons was trampled down: for this cause, as is our duty, we faithful ever hymn thee and bless thee, and truly confessing thee to be the Mother of God, we magnify thee.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my joy, Who didst not leave the Father's bosom, yet didst visit our poverty; therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind![^2246]

*Troparia:*

The sun was amazed at thy temperance and endurance, which spending many years in the day could not at all see thee taking food by day, O venerable one: singing with good strength in unceasing vigils: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Meditating, O wise one, in the New Laws and the Old Testament with the understanding of holy men, O blessed one, having learned every form of virtue, emulating the character of the wise bee, and having become a chosen vessel, thou didst cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Thou art the wealth of sweetness, the praise and joy of the venerable, O Christ: for love of Thee, Cyriacus accounted all pleasurable things in the world as refuse; therefore in impassable deserts he lovingly delighted in Thy beauty.

The Prophet of old made sweet the bitter waters of Marah; and having transformed the bitter food of herbs, O Cyriacus, into sweet tasting, thou didst show boldness toward the Lord unto me, Who truly glorifies His servants by divine power.[^2247]

As a disciple and imitator of the Master Christ, thou didst heal by prayer the afflicted son of a servant, O father, having received grace to drive away illnesses and cast down the demonic legions by the sign of the divine Cross.

*Theotokion:*

Thou art the praise of the faithful, O unwedded one, thou art the intercessor, thou art also the refuge of Christians, the rampart and haven; for unto thy Son thou bearest supplications, O all-immaculate one, and from dangers thou savest those who with faith and love honor thee and glorify thee as the Mother of God.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy presence, O unwaning Light, and the alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But convert me, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my paths, I pray Thee.[^2248]

*Troparia:*

Having received from Christ the invincible grace of the Spirit, thou didst sovereignly cast down the cruel ruler of the world; having restrained carnal passions, O Cyriacus, thou wast crowned with the crown of dispassion.

Firm thou wast shown to be, patiently enduring with fortitude the afflictions of fasting, having remained unweakened unto deepest old age, O venerable one, living with great joy in the deserts as if in royal palaces and bridal chambers.

Performing all-night vigils, O blessed one, and ascending toward God without pride by prayer, thou didst converse with the immaterial Mind, and thou didst receive radiant rays of light, O Cyriacus, illumined in thy mind in a light-giving manner.

Filled with light-bearing radiance and the prophetic gift, O venerable one, thy pure tongue proclaimed the complete and utter destruction of the raving and soul-corrupting malady of Origen that afflicted men of old.[^2249]

*Theotokion:*

With understanding the assembly of the prophets perceived thy mysteries: for the Master showed thee, O pure one, to be the door of salvation, and was incarnate of thee, O Virgin, the Sun of righteousness having shone upon those in darkness.[^2250]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and from the depth of evils lead me up, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation![^2251]

*Troparia:*

Having become a god by adoption through the deification of Christ, the God by holy nature, thou didst heal natural wounds and weaknesses, O blessed one, curing the sick and straightway healing the demon-possessed by divine grace.

Thou didst flee from the multitude of people coming unto thee, and again thou didst attain the formidable torrents, turning away, O ever-memorable one, from the vain praises of human renown.

Beholding all the glory of the corruptible world as a shadow, Thou didst love to be a partaker of the better glory of the only living God: of which, O wise one, Thou wast righteously deemed worthy.

*Theotokion:*

As an ensouled ark thou didst receive the Word without beginning; as the Holy of Holies thou didst contain the Creator; as a fiery throne thou bearest the Master, O Mother of God of all creation.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*

Having divinely armed thyself with purity of soul, and grasping unceasing prayer in thy hand like a spear, thou didst mightily cut down the demonic hosts, O Cyriacus our father: pray unceasingly for us all.

*Ikos:*

How shall I, the wretched one, praise thy struggles, O venerable father? And how shall I pour forth a deep sea of tears? For in life thou didst excel, and didst attain the angelic choir. Truly by temperance thou didst mortify all passions, O wise one, and having enslaved the flesh, thou didst subject it unto the spirit; and having prayer as a sword, thou didst cast down the leader of darkness: pray unceasingly for us all.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Hebrew youths in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and changed the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages![^2252]

*Troparia:*

Thy most faithful servant, O Lord, sweetened his throat with the study of Thy laws and God-inspired words above honey, singing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages![^2253]

O blessed, God-proclaiming one, thou bringest those who hymn thee unto Christ, purified from the mire of passions by thy prayers, crying out, O Cyriacus, and saying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!

Daniel was glorified, having escaped the fierceness of the lions; and Cyriacus had their whelps obeying his command, crying unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages![^2254]

Install all the grace of the Spirit within me, O Christ: for Cyriacus was whole-souledly a lover of Thine all-pure beauty, crying unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!

*Triadikon:*

Having joined contemplation unto action, thou didst preach the three-hypostatic Essence in the Father, and the Son and the Holy Spirit, crying out, O God-pleasing Cyriacus: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!

*Theotokion:*

Extinguish the flame of my passions, and calm the storm of heresies, O Mother of God; for we Christians possess thee as our intercessor and helper, and we hymn thee in faith unto ages.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Having become victors over the tyrant and the flame by Thy grace, and cleaving exceedingly unto Thy commandments, the children cried: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2255]

*Troparia:*

With streams of tears, O blessed one, thou didst water the seed-bearing soil of thy soul with divine compunction, and didst show it forth as multi-fruitful, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto ages!

A dweller of old dried up fertile drops by drought; but thou, O all-blessed one, didst bring down an outpouring of rain for the growth of the harvest, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto ages![^2256]

By noble struggles thou didst expose the deception of the blasphemous, the disciples of the babbling and fable-speaking Origen, singing orthodoxly: Bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto ages![^2257]

*Triadikon:*

Piously thou didst teach the single Essence of the Trinity, O father: in three Suns as one radiance and brightness; saying: Bless the Lord orthodoxly, and exalt Him above all unto ages!

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast shown to be the daughter of the fallen Adam, but the Mother of God Who renewed my nature, Whom all creation hymns as Lord, and exalts above all unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Every ear was struck with fear at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High willingly descended even unto flesh, having become man from the virginal womb; therefore, O all-pure Mother of God, we faithful magnify thee.

*Troparia:*

A cave received thee, O wise one, who didst receive the fountain of grace; having emulated the marvels of the divine father of old, Chariton, in martyr-like manner, O Cyriacus, thou wast an unshakable wall and most steadfast guardian for his flock.[^2258]

With yearning for true life, taking up the Cross upon thy shoulders, O Cyriacus, thou didst make thy life a meditation upon death; therefore thou hast now departed unto unaging, incorruptible sweetness, and shining forth in the light together with the heavenly choirs shining together, kindled with the radiance of the Spirit, and thou wast shown to be bright unto the supreme choir-ranks; but illumine my mind, O blessed one, with the noetic and thrice-radiant Light of the Godhead by thy prayers, and save me from passions and transgressions.

Crowned with a victorious diadem, O God-proclaiming Chariton and blessed Cyriacus, and standing in the highest before Christ, fatherly delivering your flock from perils, now look down upon those who celebrate your memory.

*Theotokion:*

Prosper, proceed favorably, and reign, O Son of the Mother of God, subduing unto the Christ-loving sovereigns the Ishmaelite enemy who wars against us, through the prayers, we pray Thee, of her who bore Thee without knowing man, as Thou art God and the Lover of mankind.[^2259]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "By the Spirit" (Дꙋ́хомъ):*

Having cleansed thy soul of the darkening of passions, O venerable one, by severe fasting and unceasing prayer, thou becamest, O father, a mirror of divine splendors, sending down unto us now ascending paths, O luminary of monks, God-bearing Cyriacus.

*Theotokion:*

Truly we confess thee to be the Mother of God, O Sovereign Lady, who have been saved through thee; for thou didst ineffably give birth unto God, Who destroyed death by the Cross, and drew unto Himself the assemblies of the venerable: with them we praise thee, O Virgin.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Glory, Tone 5:*

Venerable father, thou didst not give sleep unto thine eyes, nor slumber unto thine eyelids, until thou didst free soul and body from passions, and preparedst thyself to be a dwelling-place for the Spirit; for Christ, coming with the Father, made an abode with thee; and having become a servant of the consubstantial Trinity, O our father Cyriacus, great preacher: pray for our souls.[^2260]

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйся):*

When she who like a vine put forth the uncultivated Cluster beheld Him hanging upon the wood, and His divine side pierced with a spear: What is this, she said, O my Son and God? How dost Thou, Who didst heal all infirmities and passions, accept passion, being passionless by nature as the Son in Godhead? Why have the ungrateful people rendered this unto Thee, the Benefactor, instead of benefits? cried the all-pure one; but pray unceasingly that by His sufferings I may be delivered from passions, that I may glorify thee.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4, and of the Venerable One, Ode 3 on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^2261]

*Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?[^2262]

*The Epistle to the Galatians, zachalo 213 [Gal. 5:22–6:2]:*[^2263]

*Alleluia, Tone 6:* Blessed is the man that fears the Lord.[^2264]

*Verse:* His seed shall be mighty upon earth.[^2265]

*The Gospel according to Luke, zachalo 24 [Luke 6:17–23]:*[^2266]

*Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^2267]

*The same month, on the 30th day. The Holy Hieromartyr Gregory of Great Armenia:*[^2268]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having set aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

Having dyed thy sacred vesture with the blood of martyrdom, thou didst enter into the Holy of Holies, O praiseworthy one, where is the ineffable Light, where is the divine glory, where is the voice of those who keep festival; wherein, O martyr, thou receivest the recompense of thy labors, the unfading crown, eternal blessing, and the dwelling of paradise, O wise Gregory: with boldness pray for our souls.

The surge of tortures did not shake thy soul, nor the long-lasting confinement hiding thee in the dark pit, O glorious sufferer; but like light thou didst shine forth upon those in distress in darkness, whom thou didst reveal as sons of the day by the laver of baptism, and by soulish and salvific rebirth, and truly by divine abiding, as a God-pleasing hierarch, O all-wise Gregory.[^2269]

Loving the immortal Bridegroom, the Master of all, Rhipsime received the flaying of her bodily skin, having first torn asunder the dark garment of passions by temperance; with whom the ever-memorable Gaiana also struggled, leading a company of virgins who suffered steadfastly, and cast down, alas, the ancient deceiver: worthily praising them, we glorify Thee, O Christ.[^2270]

*Glory, the same tone [Tone 6]:*

*By Sergius. Idiomelon:*

Who can worthily tell the victories of thy virtues? What mouth can recount the endurance of thy tortures? For in both thou didst act valiantly, O Gregory; but cease not to pray, O servant of Christ, to save our souls, as thou hast great boldness, O hieromartyr.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Having set aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

When the spotless ewe-lamb and immaculate Sovereign Lady of old beheld her Lamb lifted up upon the Cross, maternally crying aloud and marveling, she shouted: What sight is this, O sweet Child, new and glorious? How do the ungrateful people deliver Thee unto the judgment-seat of Pilate, and condemn unto death the Life of all? Yet I hymn Thine ineffable condescension, O Word!

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Having noetically entered into the unwaning cloud of ineffable Light, the martyr and shepherd was taught the unutterable things of the mysteries of Christ: illumined indeed as a martyr, and taught mystagogy as a shepherd; therefore he was crowned with twofold crowns from high glory, ever praying unto Christ for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*

Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who bore Thee cried aloud: What strange mystery is this that I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die upon the wood, suspended in the flesh, O Giver of life?

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

A sharer in the ways and a successor upon the thrones of the Apostles, thou didst find action, O God-inspired one, as an ascent unto contemplation; therefore dispensing the word of truth, thou didst suffer for the faith even unto blood, O hieromartyr Gregory: pray Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos, and of the Saint on 6. Of which the acrostic is: I hymn thee, O martyr, the vigilant shepherd. Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, drown, I pray Thee, the mighty captains, the three parts of the soul, in the depth of dispassion, that in the mortification of the body, as upon a timbrel, I may sing unto Thee a song of victory.[^2271]

*Troparia:*

Standing before the honored Trinity crowned as a victor, as a vigilant shepherd as a vigilant shepherd, as a sacred martyr, by thy sacred prayers put to sleep the dark illusions of my passions, for me who praise thee, O blessed Gregory.

The unwaning luminary, the great hierarch, the much-suffering shepherd, the testing of struggles, the praise of Armenia, has called the faithful unto hymnody today: having gathered together, let us call him blessed.

Thou wast filled with the living waters of the Spirit, O blessed one, like a river flowing forth from the spiritual Eden, watering the face of the Church, and drying up the abyss of idolatrous frenzy, O Gregory.

*Theotokion:*

Strengthened, O pure one, by the Cross of Him Who was incarnate of thee, the women suffered steadfastly, and virgins following after thee were brought unto Him, radiant with the brightness of virginity and with the blood of martyrdom.[^2272]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

The barren Church of the Gentiles has given birth, and the assembly populous with children has grown weak; unto our marvelous God let us cry aloud: Holy art Thou, O Lord![^2273]

*Troparia:*

By the wounds of thy struggles thou didst break the teeth of lions, and by outpourings of blood thou didst destroy the demonic blood; and thou didst overturn the idolatrous temples from their roots, O praiseworthy one.

Neither the onset of cruelties, nor bitter torments, nor the long-lasting confinement of the dark pit could shake thy adamantine mind, O praiseworthy martyr.

Thou didst not give slumber unto thine eyes, O martyr, until thou didst show those held by the evil slumber of impiety to be sons of the day, crying: Holy art Thou, O Lord![^2274]

*Theotokion:*

Knowing thee alone to be the Mother of God, O Maiden, the martyr Rhipsime desired thy beauty, and was brought after thee unto Christ, shining by her sufferings.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Lifted up" (Вознесы́йся):*

With most radiant splendors, O hierarch, having luminous-bearingly illumined thy soul with virtues, thou didst enlighten the face of the earth, having Christ within thy heart; and like an unwaning sun thou enlightenest the assemblies of the nations, adorning us with the beauties of martyrdom, O all-wise Gregory. *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

Being a lover of sin, I pray thee, who didst give birth unto the sinless God Who takes away the sin of the world, O all-pure one: have compassion on my much-sinning soul, and cleanse my many sins; for of sinners for of sinners thou art the cleansing, and the salvation of the faithful, and the defense.[^2275]

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Having in the last times given birth in the flesh unto Him Who was born of the unoriginate Father, beholding Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, she cried out: Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How is it that Thou, Who art glorified as God by the Angels, art now willingly crucified by lawless men, O my Son? I hymn Thee, O longsuffering One![^2276]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine came on a swift cloud with an incorrupt palm, and saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^2277]

*Troparia:*

The High Lord Most High in glory led thee up unto the conspicuous height of martyrdom, O glorious one; whose sufferings thou didst rejoice to depict, O hieromartyr, crying: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

By divine power thou didst cast down the destroyer, the godless enemy of all the Armenian land; and shining forth like a ray of dawn, thou didst enlighten those lying in darkness, O wise illuminator.

Many times multiplied hast thou brought thy talent unto the Creator through those saved by thy divine teachings, O Gregory; and thou hast received the kingdom that is in the heavens, and radiance.

*Theotokion:*

As good, as chosen, and as beautiful did the maiden-virgins who suffered with Rhipsime love thee, O Virgin-Mother Mary; and they were brought after thee, rejoicing unto thy Son.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Send down Thy enlightenment upon us, O Lord, and loose us from the gloom of transgressions, O Good One, granting Thy peace.[^2278]

*Troparia:*

Manifestly didst thou behold the cross-revealed sign visibly shining with light, and dissolving the night of idolatry, making the faithful children of light.

From the lowest pit Christ God saved thee, while thou wast with wild beasts through the course of years: intending by the light of the divine word to enlighten the senseless.

Having struggled as a martyr, thou wast crowned as a victor; and being anointed with the chrism of the high priesthood, thou didst anoint the people, having delivered them from foul-smelling deception, O Gregory.

*Theotokion:*

Having perceived the fragrance of the myrrh of the Word Who shone forth from thee, O pure Virgin, by struggles of martyrdom the virgins pleased Him well, rejoicing.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried aloud, praying in the sea-monster: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers![^2279]

*Troparia:*

By the power of thy words the heathen altars were destroyed, and the unstable demonic idols were overthrown, and the hearts of the faithful were established in divine desire.

Like a bound boar, thou didst lead Tiridates as a lamb unto the Lord, who before was a fierce wolf, now being saved through the great riches of the loving-kindness of God.[^2280]

Thou didst show unto the straying the divine path, having perfected them by undeceitful teachings as a shepherd, O hierarch, imitating the true Shepherd, O Gregory.

*Theotokion:*

When Rhipsime learned that He Who was incarnate of thee, O Birthgiver of God, was crucified, she hastened to be co-crucified with Him as a ewe-lamb unto the Shepherd, as a spotless sacrifice unto God.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The firm" (Тве́рдыя):*

Today let all us faithful praise in hymns and chants the glorious hierarch as a sufferer for the truth, the vigilant shepherd and teacher, Gregory, the universal luminary and champion: for he prays unto Christ, that our souls may be saved.[^2281]

*Ikos:*

Let us praise in songs this great one among sufferers, the divine luminary of Armenia, the faithful shepherd and teacher, and with divine hymns let us crown his head; for he destroyed the darkness of idolatrous godlessness, and together with it put to death all demonic working. Therefore having endured labors with a firm mind and by grace, he now prays unto Christ, that we may be saved.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

Of old in Babylon the Abrahamic children trampled upon the furnace flame, calling out with hymns: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2282]

*Troparia:*

Having endured manifold torments, O martyr, thou didst free many from torments and from future sorrow, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Having made thyself a dwelling of the Trinity, O blessed one, thou didst demolish the temples of idols, and didst erect temples unto the all-seeing Word, for the salvation of the people.

A celebrant of sacred rites wast thou shown to be, and having before fervently offered the mystic sacrifice unto thy Master, later sacrificing unto Him, thou dost give Him unto the pious, for the salvation of souls.

*Theotokion:*

...Adorned with crowns of martyrdom, the maidens were brought unto Christ Who shone forth from the Virgin, crying in hymnody: Blessed art Thou, O Christ![^2283]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

O almighty Redeemer of all, having descended into the midst of the flame, Thou didst bedew those who acted piously, and didst teach them to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works, sing praise unto the Lord![^2284]

*Troparia:*

Having suffered lawfully, thou didst put the lawless enemies most powerfully to shame, O sacred minister Gregory; and thou didst bring unto Christ a multitude of those who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord!

Having plowed the barren field, thou didst sow the rational seeds, and didst reap a hundredfold the spiritual harvest of ears of grain, having enriched it, O tiller of souls.

By the brightness of thy words thou didst enlighten and draw many from darkness unto Him Who for our sake willingly endured sufferings, unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord!

*Theotokion:*

Neither fearing the multitude of torments, nor submitting unto carnal pleasures, Rhipsime confessed the Son, the Lord born of the Virgin, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, through the burgeoning of childbearing, hast blossomed forth blessing unto the world: therefore we all magnify thee.[^2285]

*Troparia:*

Crowned with the power of Christ, thou didst endure the pains of torments, and didst destroy the demonic shrines, and didst dig up the idol temples; and those abiding in unbelief thou didst enlighten, O all-honored hieromartyr.

Like the dawn thy memory has shone forth upon us, bearing the radiance of graces; for thou wast shown to be a receptacle of the divine Light, and hast ascended unto the unwaning Light, richly illuminated with divine outpourings of light, O venerable one.

Thou wast shown to be a companion of the prophets, a fellow-partaker with the martyrs and the apostles, with hierarchs and venerable ones, equal in standing with angels and archangels; with them, O father, pray unto the Lover of mankind for us who honor thee.

The venerable women triumphed, setting right the fall of Eve; they endured the surging tempest of afflictions, and with their most beautiful feet crushed him who boasts himself exceedingly on high: whom we worthily call blessed.[^2286]

*Theotokion:*

...Illuminated by the light of the countenance of Him Who shone forth from thee, O Ever-Virgin, by unrestrained love Rhipsime depicted in her own flesh the sufferings and death of God; therefore together with thee, O Lady, she is now magnified.[^2287]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "With the disciples" (Оу҆ченика́мъ):*

Let us praise the glorious Gregory, who was steadfastly shut up in the pit with wild beasts, who transformed the persecutor Tiridates into a wild boar, and proclaimed the word of enlightenment unto all the earth.[^2288]

*Theotokion:*

Thou art the comfort of all creation, O Birthgiver of God, who didst give birth unto Christ; Him do thou pray, that this thy little flock may be preserved unharmed from every assault of the adversary.[^2289]

*At the Liturgy. The Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4, and of the Saint, Ode 6 on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^2290]

*Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?[^2291]

*The Epistle to the Corinthians, zachalo 136 [1 Cor. 6:20–7:12]:*[^2292]

*Alleluia, Tone 2:* Thy priests shall clothe themselves with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.[^2293]

*The Gospel according to Matthew, zachalo 103 [Matt. 24:42–47]:*[^2294]

*Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^2295]
